Snow fell thick out of a grey sky and lay deep on every roof and every street and every ledge, blanketing the whole city so completely that the towers looked carved from sugar.
And the streets were alive!
People moved everywhere down there, small at this height and busy.
Humans in heavy cloaks, carrying loads across a market square.

Beastmen among them, broad-shouldered and fur-maned, a wolf-headed guard leaning on a spear at a gate, a pair of horned children chasing each other through a drift, a bear-shouldered merchant shouting prices across the snow.
Smoke rose from a thousand chimneys.
Somewhere a smith’s hammer rang, steady and patient.
Noah stood very still.
He knew this place!
Or rather, he knew the place it was built from.
The Beast World.
It was not a copy, quite.
It was grander than the real thing had ever been, tidier, more beautiful, as if someone had taken the memory of it and spent years building it back up with love and very careful hands.
"I wondered when my husband would come see me in my dream."
The voice came from behind him.
"Years have passed, you know!"
Noah turned.
Adelaide stood in the doorway of the balcony, and she looked like an empress!
Her blue hair was bound up in a high crown of braids, a few loose strands falling past her cheek.
She wore a gown of deep sea-blue trimmed with white fur, heavy and imperial, the kind of dress meant to be seen from the far end of a throne rooom.
And around her, on every side, moved Mana.
Not a trickle.
Waves of it, boundless and slow, rolling off her in visible currents and swirling back, so thick that the snow falling near her melted before it could reach her shoulders!
She looked at him for one long moment.
Then she crossed the balcony in three strides and threw her arms around him, and held on hard!
Noah held her back.
And as he held her, he felt her existence against his, and he blinked.
She had grown.
A great deal!

Her Dimensionality had climbed past everything she had been when he laid her down on the shore, past the whole of the Finite Verse, and was just beginning to press into the first stages of the Transfinite.
Years of dreaming, all of them spent growing.
In a dream he had given her, she had simply refused to sit still.
He smiled into her hair.
"Sorry it took so long," he said.
"What have you been up to?"
Adelaide pulled back just far enough to look up at him.
Her eyes were pulsing, light moving in them in slow waves, blue and bright.
"Just trying to continue what you cast out," she said.
"Your First Infinite Scale, THE Genesis Scale.
Your Second, THE Source Scale.
I’ve been rebuilding them.
And I’ve started designing a Third.
THE Dimensional Scale!"Her mouth tightened.
"But forget all that.
Time is unforgiving in this place, do you know that?
It’s been so long I almost dreamed another version of you, just to have someone to... talk to!"
She did not wait for an answer.
Her hand closed on the front of his garment, and her pulsing eyes flashed, and there was something in them now that was not scholarly at all.
"Get over here," Adelaide said."I have missed you!"

And Noah, THE True Human Emperor, who could step through time and dream impossibilities into existence, was yanked bodily off the balcony and into the room behind her before he had the chance to say a single word!

chapters.title: Chapter 5785: Targets and Roots III
paragraphs: Time, Noah was learning, had stopped being a thing that happened to him.

Inside Adelaide’s dream, months went by. Snow came and went over her imagined Beast World, festivals were held and forgotten, and she built whole new Chapters of the Third Scale on paper covered in tight blue script. Outside, on the golden shore, barely an hour passed over her floating body.

And Noah, who stood in both places at once, felt neither of those clocks. His existence was anchored to itself. However fast or slow the room around him ran, his own perception ticked by at its own steady pace, and to him, the whole of those months felt like a few pleasant minutes.

He could not interfere with her dream too much. It was hers, and a dream steered too hard by someone else stopped being a dream and became a cage. But he could guide it. He could sit with her over her papers and point at a line and ask why it had to end there. He could tell her what he had learned about Infinity, the Absolute and Transcendent and Dialetheic kind, and watch her eyes widen and her pen start moving again. So he did.
Then he went visiting others.
Barbatos was fighting a war of necromancy in her dream, a glorious and completely unnecessary one, and winning it with great style.
Henry was running a farm as he looked happier than Noah had seen him before. Seo-yeon was forging one Observable Existence after another while designing new causes.
His mother sat in a garden and grew things, and when Noah sat down beside her she took his hand without saying anything, and they stayed there a long time.
Kazuhiko...well, the swordsman had pivotted entirely and had writen forty novels. All of them trash smut!
But at least they were his!
And then there was THE Emperor Penguin.

Noah stepped into that particular dream and stopped, because he was standing in a throne room of polished black ice, and it was full of soldiers. Tall, gleaming, robotic Dimensional Lifeforms, rank upon rank of them, standing at perfect attention. Every single one of them had... Noah’s face.
At the far end of the hall, on a throne carved from a glacier, sat a small, round, flightless bird with its flippers crossed importantly over its belly.
"Soldiers!" the penguin cried. "Polish my throne! Fetch new fish! Bow, Osmonts, bow!"
A thousand Noah-faced soldiers bowed.
The real Noah looked at this for a long, quiet moment.
Then he walked down the length of the hall, between the bowing copies of himself, and the penguin saw him coming and went pale under its feathers!
"RAA! Master!" THE Emperor Penguin flapped off the throne and hit the ice. "Master, this is just a dream! I would never dare think of you as a servant! Never! Ah! AH!"
THE Emperor Penguin received a correctional beating. A thorough one! It was, Noah felt, important that such a dream never be repeated.
Hours of his existence passed like that, and they were good. Almost relaxing!
HUUM!
Some hours later, a body of his stood in the Vasiliou Elsedimension, and the Vasiliou Elsedimension was empty.

The great halls were silent, and the gardens lay under snow. Every family of the Lineage had been relocated, one family after another, and all that remained of them here were their houses, standing quiet with their shutters closed, and the long white avenues between them.
Snow was falling even here. The Long Night had reached this sealed pocket like it had reached everywhere else.
It was beautiful, though.

The snow came down slow and silent, catching the pale gold light of the Elsedimension’s sky, and lay on the roofs in soft round drifts and along the garden walls in neat white lines. The bare trees were iced to the tips of their twigs, and the air smelled clean and sharp. It was the kind of snowfall that makes a person want to stand still and breath, the kind children remember for the rest of their lives.
In the middle of the main avenue stood three figures.

Thalia, and on either side of her, her parents. Aurelius and Rosalia Vasiliou. Thalia had used THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign on both of them, reaching into their existential genomes and remaking them, and now they were Elselifeforms. Their existences shone differently, rewritten from the root, their Provenance forever altered. They stood straighter. They glowed faintly in the falling snow.
Thalia looked at them both.
"I will take revenge on THE UNPAID COLLECTOR,"she said. "For our Lineage. For everything he took from us."
"But none of you can stay to witness it. Go, for now."
Aurelius looked at his daughter with nothing but love in his face, and nodded.

Rosalia did not look at her daughter. Rosalia looked at Noah, and glared, with the full weight of a mother who believed her daughter’s troubles had all started the day this man walked into her life. Which, to be fair, was not entirely wrong.
His mother-in-law was troublesome. Noah paid it no heed.
He lifted a hand, and the two of them vanished, carried away into THE Infiniverse where nothing that hunted the Vasilious could follow.
Then it was only him and Thalia, alone in the snow!

He crossed the white avenue to her. She wore a great heavy coat of Provenance authority, deep gold and crimson, turned up at the collar against the cold, and her red-gold hair had come loose and blown across her face. He brushed it aside. Snow was catching on her lashes. Her freckles stood out bright against her cheeks in the cold.
"So," Thalia said, looking up at him. "How do you plan to draw out an Immense One?"
"Simple." Noah did not lower his voice. "That fucker promised he would appear the next time I held you. To split us both in half. So that we would be afraid of so much as touching each other."

He slid his hand to the back of her neck. "So I am going to hold you. Loudly. And we will see whether THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, one of Those Who Remain, will do anything at all while the prize he promised himself is taken by someone else."

There was that, and there was also the fact that by having their records read, Immense Ones could know or sense something. If he directly adressed an Immense One and an obsession of theirs? He would definitely come!
And so he kissed her.

He kissed her there in the falling snow, slow and unhurried, and while he did, he let his voice go out with all his authority behind it, booming across every white avenue and silent house of the Vasiliou Elsedimension.
"THE UNPAID COLLECTOR,"Noah said, "must be a cluster of trash and worthlessness. The kind that sits on s couch and watches while what was his gets taken. What a bum of one of Those Who Remain!"
Thalia smiled against his mouth!

"An Unpaid Collector," Noah went on, still kissing her, his voice rolling off the snowbound roofs. "He cannot even collect. Some debt he is. He made a promise and then went back to sleep. I am holding her right now, you senile little shit. I am holding her and I will keep holding her. Where are you? Did you forget which Dimension you left your remnant balls in?!"
Not even a second passed.
HUUM!
The Vasiliou Elsedimension shook!

It shook to its foundations, the houses rattling on their stones, the iced trees shedding their snow all at once, the whole sealed pocket of existence groaning like a ship in a storm! And above Noah and Thalia, in the pale gold sky, two eyes opened.
They were utterly cold. Vast, and flat, and filled with a hatred so complete it had gone past anger into something quiet.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR looks down upon the two of you.|
|He says he has never once, in all his existence, been so insulted by an insect and a whore.|
|He says your deaths will not be light ones. Even if THE REMINISCING WIDOW comes here herself again, nothing will change.|
Noah looked up at the eyes, and went quiet.

There was nothing he could do about this. Not yet. Not right now! The weight of the thing above him currently was so grand that it made the Fiend’s grip over the frozen forest feel gentle. Even with his Root, even at six hundred and growing, he was nowhere near an Immense One, and he knew it.
At that very moment it was taking everything he had just to keep himself and Thalia from trembling under the pressure bearing down on them from above.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR notes your silence.|
|"No more words from you?"|
Noah held Thalia a little tighter.
"Well," he said."I am only buying as much time as possible."
The eyes above them blinked, once, in the middle of their rage.
And in the next instant, the snow thickened.

All at once it was everywhere, pouring out of the gold sky so densely the houses vanished behind it, heavy and white and driving, and a sound erupted out of the heart of it, a booming sound that did not come from anywhere Noah could point to. The cold eyes of THE UNPAID COLLECTOR were forced downward, dragged out of their height, and as they came, a body came with them!

A massive hazy form now stood in the skies above the Vasiliou Elsedimension. Noah could barely perceive it, a shape too vast and too grand for his sight to hold. But he could see one thing clearly on it now, and that thing was grimness.
The Collector raised both hands to the sky and pushed.

Above him, a thin film of white had appeared across the heavens, pale and smooth as frost on a windowpane. He pushed against it, and it did not break. He pushed harder, and the whole Elsedimension shuddered, and still it held. It was a barrier, and a terrible one, and it had not been put there to keep anything out. It had been put there to keep him in!
Then, directly above Noah, the snow began to gather.

It converged, spiraling in from every direction, thickening, taking shape. A figure formed out of it. Blue-white and jagged and never quite resolving, with two pale points of ice where its eyes should be, and a face Noah had seen twice now. Once in a Runestone’s memory, smiling at him across an age. Once rising out of a dead Immense One’s corpse above a frozen forest.
The frost-visage of Lucy!
It looked up, calmly, at the vast hazy form of THE UNPAID COLLECTOR held beneath the white.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR stares down at what has formed below him.|
|"What...the fuck is this?"|
Noah’s Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin beat faster in his chest!

His job was done. Draw the Collector out, hold him a few seconds. He had done exactly that. But he had not known what would come to finish it! This Hollow Night Lifeform wearing the image of Lucy herself, standing calm beneath an Immense One who was pushing at the sky and failing to get out.
He was curious!
Why did the Long Night want THE UNPAID COLLECTOR dead? What was this thing, really? And just what was he about to be allowed to witness?!
The snow began to wrap around him at this time.
It came in close around him and Thalia, thick and deliberate, and Noah frowned. From somewhere inside it, flat and quiet, came a voice he knew.
"Your task is complete," said the Caretaker. "Your presence here is not conducive to what needs to occur."
Motherfucker!

Before he could see a single thing more, the snow took hold of his existence and moved it. Just moved it, bodily, out of the Vasiliou Elsedimension and across existence and down, layering this body of his onto the one already sitting in the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity.
He was on the Glacial Mountain, in the snow outside the golden monastery.
And beside him, blinking and still flushed, stood Thalia!

chapters.title: Chapter 5786: Death and Progeny I
paragraphs: The snow on the Glacial Mountain came down as quietly as ever, as if nothing at all had happened anywhere.
Noah stood in it, solemn, with the Vasiliou Elsedimension still burning behind his eyes!
Somewhere across existence, an Immense One was being held under a white film of sky by a thing wearing Lucy’s face, and he had been moved out of the room before the first blow landed.
Thalia stood beside him, breathing hard. Her furry coat was still dusted with the snow of another Dimension.
"What happened?"She looked up at him, and there was frustration in her gaze. "We won’t be able to know his fate?"

He had told her the shape of the plan before they went. Not all of it, because he had not known all of it, but enough. That he meant to bait THE UNPAID COLLECTOR into showing himself. That when the Collector came, something else would come after him, something grand enough to handle an Immense One, and that their part ended the moment the trap closed. She had agreed at once, before he even finished the sentence.
Of course she had!
That being had hunted her Lineage. Thalia had not agreed because she wanted to watch him fall!
And instead, they had been swept out of the room like dust.

Noah did not like it either! He had stood there with his Root beating faster in his chest, staring up at a frost-visage and an Immense One and the beginning of something few had ever seen, and the Caretaker had simply decided he did not need to see it.
"I’ll try to keep track of exactly what happens,"he said. "For now, go and get your parents settled into THE Infiniverse..."
Thalia looked at him a moment longer. Then she nodded.
Noah waved his hand, and she was gone.
He stood alone in the snow outside the golden monastery for a little while after that. Then he sat down, closed his eyes, and reached for the cold!
The Cold Place received him without ceremony!

The frozen seas ran to every horizon, blue and white and shining. The Hollow Night Lifeforms sat in their thousands on the rivers, blank-eyed in their turning pillars, breathing the winter in and out.
Nothing here knew or cared that an Immense One was being brought down somewhere across existence. Nothing here had ever cared about anything.
And The Caretaker was already waiting, her pages turning slow around her in the air!
"I want to see it," Noah said in a very straightforward manner!
"You cannot."
"I still want to."
"Wanting has never once been a kind of sight."The Caretaker regarded him with those flat, cognizant eyes, and the pages turned.

"Your Dimensionality could not hold that battle if I laid the whole of it before your face. Two Immensities are touching. Where they touch, existence does not record the event so much as look away from it. You would perceive a pale smear and a sound with no source. You would learn nothing, and some part of you would tear in the effort of learning it anyway."
Her voice did not change at all.
"I will give you glimpses later. When it has ended, I will give you what remains. That is the measure your sight can hold, and so that is the measure you are given."
Noah’s eyes pulsed!

Well. She was not wrong! He had watched Vakochev and the Immense Ones clash over the sundered Train, and with an Infinite gaze turned on it he had caught an arm through a curtain and the sound of a breaking jaw and nothing else. Glimpses were all he had ever gotten. At least this time someone was offering a bit more.
"The page is finished," The Caretaker said. "What was owed for it is owed."
She lifted one pale hand!

Two slivers of crystal rose out of the frozen river at her feet, pale blue at the edges and white at the heart, their insides branched into snowflake paterns too fine to follow. They pulsed together, slow and cold, and Noah’s Root answered them before he had even reached out!
|LESSER KRYOS EXISTENTIAL CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN x2.|
|The reward for a page completed. It wasn’t that much work, anyways.|
Two more! He now had three sitting cold in his keeping, each one a quarter of a genuine unit of true Immensity, and none of them would ever disperse.
Then a third thing rose from the river!
A page. A sheet of ice, thin and clear and faintly glowing, and it drifted across the air toward him and turned once as it came.
"Here is the next," The Caretaker said. "Look at it for as long as you need."
Noah took it out of the air!
On its surface, letters formed! Not the crawling script of a Runestone but plain obsidian characters, black and sharp against the ice, and they spelled a name he knew.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW!
And beneath the name, an image. Eyes. He recognized them at once.
Noah stood in the frozen dark and said nothing for a long moment.
He thought about Atlas. Of course he did! She was Atlas’s widow, in every sense that counted.
And here she was on a frozen page in a dead place, handed to him by the winter.
"Is she marked for death?"Noah said. "Am I meant to lure her to her end, as I lured the Collector?"
"No."
The word came without weight and without reassurance.

"This page asks for a messenger, not a hunter."The Caretaker’s pages turned. "Carry what I give you to her, and bring her to a place. She holds a power that was made for exactly one lock, and there is exactly one thing behind that lock, and no other hand in existence can turn it. Deliver the message. Have her agree to go. Then the page is finished, and nothing further is asked of you. Of her, a great deal. Of you, nothing."
Beside her, the air thickened, frost gathered out of nothing, and a scroll formed. Ice and rime, bound closed, cold as the botom of the sea, and it floated across the space between them.
Noah took it, and his gaze was heavy!

"What does all of this mean?"Noah said. "What is the purpose here? I severed a thing from THE Sealed One. I held an Immense One in place so something could fall on him. Now I am to move another Immense One across existence to a place of your choosing."
He lifted the scroll slightly. "Three pages, and not one of them resembles the others. So what is the end goal?"
The Caretaker was quiet!
Around her the pages turned, and beneath her the thousands of Hollow Night Lifeforms sat in their cold, and somewhere far above, an Age went on freezing.
"You are basically asking what the winter is for," she said at last.
Her flat eyes did not leave him.
"A winter is not a tool. It does not lift, or carry, or strike. It comes, and it takes whatever cannot hold itself, and what remains, remains. No hand forged it to drive a nail."
The pages stilled around her, all at once, as if they were listening.

"And yet. Threads are being cut that were tied before the first of Those Who Remain ever drew breath. What was scattered is being gathered. What was gathered is being scattered. And a door that was shut a very long time ago has begun, in places, to be unshut. In these epochs and boundless others...the cold has always remained supreme."

sentences.text: The snow on the Glacial Mountain came down as quietly as ever, as if nothing at all had happened anywhere.
Noah stood in it, solemn, with the Vasiliou Elsedimension still burning behind his eyes!
Somewhere across existence, an Immense One was being held under a white film of sky by a thing wearing Lucy’s face, and he had been moved out of the room before the first blow landed.
Thalia stood beside him, breathing hard.
Her furry coat was still dusted with the snow of another Dimension.
"What happened?"She looked up at him, and there was frustration in her gaze.
"We won’t be able to know his fate?"
He had told her the shape of the plan before they went.
Not all of it, because he had not known all of it, but enough.
That he meant to bait THE UNPAID COLLECTOR into showing himself.
That when the Collector came, something else would come after him, something grand enough to handle an Immense One, and that their part ended the moment the trap closed.
She had agreed at once, before he even finished the sentence.
Of course she had!
That being had hunted her Lineage.
Thalia had not agreed because she wanted to watch him fall!
And instead, they had been swept out of the room like dust.
Noah did not like it either!

He had stood there with his Root beating faster in his chest, staring up at a frost-visage and an Immense One and the beginning of something few had ever seen, and the Caretaker had simply decided he did not need to see it.
"I’ll try to keep track of exactly what happens,"he said.
"For now, go and get your parents settled into THE Infiniverse..."
Thalia looked at him a moment longer.
Then she nodded.
Noah waved his hand, and she was gone.

"You cannot."
"I still want to."

Her voice did not change at all.

Noah’s eyes pulsed!
Well.
She was not wrong!

She lifted one pale hand!

|LESSER KRYOS EXISTENTIAL CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN x2.|

A page.

Eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 5787: Death and Progeny II
paragraphs: The Caretaker told him nothing more!

Whatever was happening in the Vasiliou Elsedimension was still happening, and the frozen underworld had nothing else to give him until it finished. So Noah opened his eyes on the Glacial Mountain and stood.
The snow that had gathered on him while he was away slid off his shoulders in soft white sheets.
He looked around.
Behind him the golden monastery glowed, and the slope fell away below the shelf into grey. Snow kept coming, as it always did now, and he stood in it and turned the new page over in his thoughts.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW.
A message to carry, an unread scroll of ice, and a woman who wore Atlas’s ring. He would have to decide when to begin, and how, and how much of it to tell the old man in his other ring.
None of those were small questions.
Then he blinked, because someone was standing behind him!

Verys had not moved! The whole time, the Legacy Keeper had stood a few paces behind him on the shelf, hands clasped, cloak pulled close, as still as a statue left out in the storm. There was snow piled on his shoulders an inch deep, and he had not brushed it off!
Noah looked at him, and remembered, belatedly, that there was a sparring session in a few hours.
A sparring session he had agreed to and then not bothered to learn a single thing about.
Who exactly would he be facing? Beings on the road to Immensity, fine, but how far along that road? Were they down under five hundred in their attributes? Or did having a Root push them higher?
"What can you tell me,"Noah said, "about those in this Legacy who have Roots?"
Verys smiled, and bowed, and the snow fell off his shoulders at last.
"It would be my pleasure, Sir."He straightened. "Would you walk with me?"
He rose off the shelf, lifting into the air as easily as a man stepping off a stair, and Noah rose alongside him.
From above the Glacial Mountain, the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity went on forever!

Noah had seen it once already, arriving at Poona’s side. Now he looked. Mountains rose in every direction as far as sight could go, each one a sealed Elsedimension grown into the shape of a peak, some white with snow like his own, some black and glasy, some green, one burning a slow sullen red from summit to root. Well, snow pervaded all of them regardless.

Between them, far below, the ground was rivers! Broad, winding rivers of purple and gold, braiding and parting and braiding again across the whole floor of the Legacy, shining up through the falling snow.
Existential Conduits climbed out of that shining floor like the trunks of impossible trees, pillars of flowing authority rising past the mountains and away into the heights.

Conduit Lifeforms drifted everywhere between them, small incandescent things in their thousands, riding the currents, perching on the pillars, sipping from the authority that ran through them. A flock of them swept past Noah close enough to touch, bright and chiming, and vanished into the snow!
And above it all hung domains.

Dimensions and Observable Existences floated in the sky of the Legacy by the thousands, each one turning slowly on its own axis, glittering through the snowfall like lanterns hung over a festival that had been going on since before memory. Some were close enough that Noah could make out oceans on them! Others were only sparks.
Verys led him out over the purple and gold rivers, unhurried, as if he had walked this road ten thousand times, which he probably had.
"Sir asked about the Roots," the Keeper said. "To understand them, it helps to understand where most of them come from."

"When Those Who Remain write sentences into lesser things, or lie with Provenance Lifeforms, they produce Descendants. Some of those Descendants are fairly powerful." Verys glanced down at a mountain passing beneath them, black and glassy.

"But when Immense Ones lie with each other, what arises is something far more terrifying and very rare. Among those rarities, some of those children are born with a Root already in them. An Inherent Root of Immensity."
Noah looked at him. "Born with it?"
"Born with it, Sir. Imagine the genetic material of two Immense Ones making up the whole of your weavings."Verys smiled faintly.
"What a child like that can inherit has no ceiling. Some inherit more than others, of course. Two parents of the same greatness do not always make two children of the same greatness."
"And the ones who inherit less?"
"If they are grand enough, and if they are born with an Inherent Root, they stay within their parents’ Legacy, where they can grow in safety. If they are not..."

Verys spread one webbed hand. "They go out into existence. Across Dimensions and Observable Existences. They are encouraged to found Lineages of their own, and breed Descendants, and wait, and see whether something grand might arise from their blood in some later generation."
Noah thought about that. About the Vheldrani, twelve self-made beings in the low two hundreds, sent to pick a dead man’s bones on an Immense One’s errand.
About the Vasiliou, hunted for generations, and all the other Provenance Lineages that had drifted through his road like leaves.
"So that is what a Provenance Lineage is," he said.
"Some of them, Sir. A few Descendants who found each other and built their Provenance up across the ages, and never quite made it into a Root."

The Keeper’s large dark eyes were thoughtful. "Some of them are lucky. Existence has accidents in it, and sometimes an accident happens in the blood, and a genius rises out of a Lineage that had no business producing one. When that happens, and the genius forms a Root, the whole Lineage earns the right to live in a Legacy again."
Noah thought of the people he had carried here.
"You, Sir, have brought in a few beings who do not have Roots,"Verys went on, as if he had heard the thought. "But it is within your allowable limit."
"What is the allowable limit?"
"A few hundred should be fine, Sir. Whatever family and servants you choose to keep."
A few hundred!

"But the ones you will spar with in a few hours,"Verys said, "are mostly Progeny. Children of Immense Ones, born with their Roots. Very few are like you, or like Sir Achilles, who formed a Root themselves."
He slowed, and his voice dropped, as a storyteller’s voice drops before the part of a story that matters. "Among them, there are three you should watch for."
"Who?"
"The first is Sir Dravos. Progeny of THE Ashen Cantor."
A glance at a mountain burning sullen red in the distance. "His Root is Physical. The second is Sir Batiatus. Progeny of THE Hollow Choir, and he should hold a Conceptual Root."
Noah almost smiled!
"And the third?"

Verys did not answer at once! They were passing between two Existential Conduits, the pillars rising on either side of them like the doorposts of some enormous hall, and the Keeper waited until they had come out the other side.

"Ma’am Minerva..."he said. "Her mother is an Immense One with a gaze as green as early spring. Her Root is Conceptual. Everyone in this Legacy expects that when this Age ends, she is one of the few who is meant to be standing as an Immense One in the next."

He paused. "Others at her stage of power will not be at the sparring at all. They have earned the right to stay away. Minerva has earned it too. She is coming anyway as she seems very...enthusiastic for battles."
A gaze as green as early spring!

Noah kept his face exactly as it was. But he remembered, very clearly, a voice with a verdant weight to it, spoken over his frozen body in Moriarty’s hall. A voice that had talked about him, and about what he might be.
"And you know all of this how?" he said.
Verys bowed slightly as they flew, and something that was very nearly mischief crept into his calm face.
"Legacy Keepers like me have our own network, Sir. We love to gossip about the goings-on of the Legacy. It is one of the few pleasures of the position."
He looked up at the falling snow. "And since the snow began to fall, a great many things have begun to happen! You, Sir, are one of the more recent pieces of gossip."
Noah raised his brows!
"You gossiped about me?"

"Of course not, Sir." Verys bowed again, deeper, the very picture of respect. "But Tatiana did. And of course Ma’am Poona is very talkative. The other Immense Ones of her standing tend to stay away from her for exactly that reason among others, so she has a great deal of time to talk to those of us who cannot leave."
He straightened, and his wet-bright eyes were perfectly innocent!
"She...may have mentioned a few things regarding you."

chapters.title: Chapter 5788: Death and Progeny III
paragraphs: Verys was showing him a garden when the cold pulled at him.
It was a strange garden, grown on the shoulder of a green Elsedimension mountain, and every plant in it was a small sealed Dimension!
The Keeper had been explaining, in his mild, pleased voice everything here.
Then the cold reached up out of the deep of existence and took hold of Noah’s Root, and tugged!
He knew that tug by now. He sent a sliver of his existence down after it, and kept the rest walking beside Verys among the sealed afternoons.
The Cold Place was the same, and the Caretaker was already waiting!
She did not greet him. She raised one pale hand, and the frozen air in front of him thickened into a sheet of pale light, flat and bright as ice on a still lake.
"You wished to see,"she said. "Your sight can hold three glimpses. Here they are."
The first glimpse opened!

It was the Vasiliou Elsedimension, or what was left of it. The houses were gone. The white avenues were gone. There was only a churning grey light where a sealed reality had been, and in the middle of it hung the hazy vastness of THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, and below him, small and still, stood the frost-visage of Lucy.
The Collector spoke!

Noah could not hear the words, but he could see what they did. Wherever the Collector’s voice fell, existence rewrote itself. A whole region of the churning grey turned to gold, then to coins, then to an account written in letters of light, and every line of that account said the same thing: mine.

He spoke again, and the air around Lucy was declared his. He spoke again, and her very existence was entered as a debt, owed to him, payable now, and existence agreed to it! That was what an Immense One of his kind did. He did not throw his power at a thing. He said what was true, and existence rearranged itself to make it so.
It was the grandest act of authorship Noah had ever witnessed!
And the frost-visage of Lucy looked at him.

That was all. She stood in the middle of an existence that had just been rewritten into a debt with her name on it, and she looked up at the Collector with her pale ice eyes, and nothing happened to her.

His words landed on her and slid off. Her name sat in the account as owed, and she did not become owed. The Collector had written a perfect sentence, and he had written it on a mountain, and a mountain does not care what is written on it!
Then that glimpse went dark.
A second opened!
Lucy moved!

She did not speak. She did not answer his sentences with sentences of her own. There was no art in what she did at all. She took a single step up into the sky, and the whole Elsedimension sank under the weight of that step, and she drew back one hand and struck the Collector.
That was it. She hit him!
Noah saw the blow land, and saw everything the Collector had written shatter around it like glass under a hammer!

Every rewritten region, every account, every line that said mine burst apart at once, because none of it had anything to hold onto. The Collector’s power was a story told to existence, and Lucy was not a story.

She was simply heavier than the story, and so the story broke. The hazy vastness of the Immense One caved around her fist, and the white film of sky above him cracked from end to end, and he did not fall because there was nowhere left to fall to.
Darkness again.
A third opened!
It was over!

The churning grey had gone still. The white film of sky had faded. And in the middle of the stillness drifted a corpse, vast and ruined and no longer hazy at all, only dead, the body of THE UNPAID COLLECTOR lying open to the cold with nothing left in it to argue for its own existence.
The snow was already pouring in!
Great rivers of white drained into the dead Immense One from every side, the same way they had drained into the Overseeing One above the frozen forest. And out of the corpse, something began to rise!

It came up slow and enormous, heavy beyond measure, a titan of frost with a body like a mountan range and four legs like the pillars of a cold cathedral. Its back was covered in long shaggy fur, white and rimed and hanging in frozen ropes. Two great tusks curved out and up from its head, pale blue ice as long as rivers, and its eyes were blank.
A mammoth, or the shape a mammoth would take if winter itself decided to walk. It lifted its trunk to the dead sky and opened its mouth, and no sound came out, and the snow around it doubled!
The screen went dark and did not open again.
Noah stood in the frozen dark and said nothing at all.
He understood it now, in a way no lecture had ever taught him.Moriarty had told him once that an Empyros rewrites the rules of a fight, and a Fiend is simply stronger than the rules.

He had nodded and thought he understood. He had not. The Collector had rewritten existence itself with a sentence, and Lucy had broken the sentence with her hand. That was the difference! One of them was the grandest writer Noah had ever seen. The other was the page.
And there was something else, something colder.

Two Immense Ones had died in the span of a few days. Two! Beings that had stood at the top of existence since long before Noah was born. And both of them had died, one way or another, because of something he had done.

The Overseeing One had fallen to a Vestige he had helped write back into existence. The Collector had fallen because he had held his wife in the snow and called an Immense One a bum until it came down to kill him.
Around the Caretaker, the snow was growing heavier!
He saw it thicken as she stood there, her pages turning, the flakes coming down denser and denser, as if the winter itself were answering a death.
"A tiny bug starves in a puddle of mud," the Caretaker said.

"Somewhere else, very far away, a giant who ruled a thousand Dimensions has his throat opened and dies. To everything that bowed to the giant, it feels like the end of existence. But existence does not pause for either. The snow goes on falling. No one weeps for the bug. The giant, in the end, receives the same."
The snow thickened.

"Neither of them asked to arrive. They came, they took up a little space for a while, and when their time ran out, existence took that space back. Between the arriving and the leaving, they walked about. They ate, and slept, and fought over patches of ground, and told themselves they mattered. Because they could feel fear, they assumed existence could feel their pain. They shouted their names into the dark, certain that something out there was keeping count."
A pause, very slight.
"Nothing is keeping count."
The flakes fell so thick now that her frost dress was vanishing into them.

"Look back at everything that lived before you. Beyond counting. And for nearly all of it, nothing it did mattered at all. It was noise. It thought the thoughts its elders handed it, lived by rules it did not write, labored until it broke, and went into the cold without moving a single grain of sand. The moment it was gone, it was as if it had never been."
Her flat eyes held him through the snow. "And now this winter has come. It hates nothing, and it does not hear how loudly anyone screams. It walks through the room and clears it."
The underworld had gone very quiet around her. Even the rivers seemed to slow.
"Many will live through it, and many will not. You cannot stop that. The only thing that was ever truly yours is the span between arriving and leaving. That is the one place anything gets to choose."

The Caretaker’s voice dropped lower still. "And nearly everything wastes it. They spend it afraid. Borrowing warmth from someone else. Begging the roof to hold. They live copied lives, die common deaths, and go back into the dark without leaving a mark."
The snow was a wall now! Only her eyes showed through it.

"Being alive is nothing. A stone is alive enough to sit where it was put. So is a corpse. If the time you have is to mean anything, surviving the cold will not be enough. Asking existence for permission to breathe will not be enough. You must stand on your own feet and make something so true, so stubbornly and entirely your own, that when the dark swallows everything, existence is forced to remember you were here."
She let the silence stand for a long moment.
"Arriving is common. Leaving comes for everyone. The span between is an empty page, and nearly everyone who ever held one wrote down someone else’s name, closed their eyes, and was forgotten."

Her gaze did not waver. "So I ask you. What will you etch across existence? What will you dream, you who call yourself THE Human Dreamer, that will be grand enough to one day not be like the Collector who now lies dead? He became an Immense One. It did not save him."
The snow stopped thickening. It simply hung there, heavy, waiting.
"What will you do differently?"
Noah opened his mouth.
Nothing came!

He, who had an answer for Immense Ones and Runestones and prophecies, who had talked his way past titans and dreamed his way through impossibilities, stood in the frozen dark before a caretaker of the cold and found, for the first time in a very long time, that he did not have one.

sentences.text: Verys was showing him a garden when the cold pulled at him.
It was a strange garden, grown on the shoulder of a green Elsedimension mountain, and every plant in it was a small sealed Dimension!
The Keeper had been explaining, in his mild, pleased voice everything here.
Then the cold reached up out of the deep of existence and took hold of Noah’s Root, and tugged!
He knew that tug by now.
He sent a sliver of his existence down after it, and kept the rest walking beside Verys among the sealed afternoons.
The Cold Place was the same, and the Caretaker was already waiting!
She did not greet him.
She raised one pale hand, and the frozen air in front of him thickened into a sheet of pale light, flat and bright as ice on a still lake.
"You wished to see,"she said.
"Your sight can hold three glimpses.
Here they are."
The first glimpse opened!
It was the Vasiliou Elsedimension, or what was left of it.
The houses were gone.
The white avenues were gone.

There was only a churning grey light where a sealed reality had been, and in the middle of it hung the hazy vastness of THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, and below him, small and still, stood the frost-visage of Lucy.
The Collector spoke!
Noah could not hear the words, but he could see what they did.
Wherever the Collector’s voice fell, existence rewrote itself.
A whole region of the churning grey turned to gold, then to coins, then to an account written in letters of light, and every line of that account said the same thing: mine.
He spoke again, and the air around Lucy was declared his.
He spoke again, and her very existence was entered as a debt, owed to him, payable now, and existence agreed to it!
That was what an Immense One of his kind did.
He did not throw his power at a thing.
He said what was true, and existence rearranged itself to make it so.
It was the grandest act of authorship Noah had ever witnessed!
And the frost-visage of Lucy looked at him.
That was all.
She stood in the middle of an existence that had just been rewritten into a debt with her name on it, and she looked up at the Collector with her pale ice eyes, and nothing happened to her.
His words landed on her and slid off.
Her name sat in the account as owed, and she did not become owed.
The Collector had written a perfect sentence, and he had written it on a mountain, and a mountain does not care what is written on it!
Then that glimpse went dark.
A second opened!
Lucy moved!
She did not speak.
She did not answer his sentences with sentences of her own.
There was no art in what she did at all.
She took a single step up into the sky, and the whole Elsedimension sank under the weight of that step, and she drew back one hand and struck the Collector.
That was it.
She hit him!
Noah saw the blow land, and saw everything the Collector had written shatter around it like glass under a hammer!
Every rewritten region, every account, every line that said mine burst apart at once, because none of it had anything to hold onto.
The Collector’s power was a story told to existence, and Lucy was not a story.
She was simply heavier than the story, and so the story broke.
The hazy vastness of the Immense One caved around her fist, and the white film of sky above him cracked from end to end, and he did not fall because there was nowhere left to fall to.
Darkness again.
A third opened!
It was over!
The churning grey had gone still.
The white film of sky had faded.

And in the middle of the stillness drifted a corpse, vast and ruined and no longer hazy at all, only dead, the body of THE UNPAID COLLECTOR lying open to the cold with nothing left in it to argue for its own existence.
The snow was already pouring in!
Great rivers of white drained into the dead Immense One from every side, the same way they had drained into the Overseeing One above the frozen forest.
And out of the corpse, something began to rise!
It came up slow and enormous, heavy beyond measure, a titan of frost with a body like a mountan range and four legs like the pillars of a cold cathedral.
Its back was covered in long shaggy fur, white and rimed and hanging in frozen ropes.
Two great tusks curved out and up from its head, pale blue ice as long as rivers, and its eyes were blank.
A mammoth, or the shape a mammoth would take if winter itself decided to walk.
It lifted its trunk to the dead sky and opened its mouth, and no sound came out, and the snow around it doubled!

chapters.title: Chapter 5789: The Death of Time! I
paragraphs: Noah did not have an answer good enough to give, so he did not give one.
What would he do differently? He meant to climb. To gather power, all of it he could reach, and become an Immense One.

But the Collector had done exactly that, and it had not given him a grand life. It had given him a long one, and then a cold end in a Dimension of snow at the hand of a thing that did not even speak. Bug or one of Those Who Remain, a being lived, and then it died. Becoming Immense only made the second part take longer.
So he looked at the Caretaker a moment longer, standing in snow so thick now it was nearly a wall, and he left.
The hours after that passed slower than any hours had passed for him in a long time.
But they passed.
THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering was never still, and this corner of it least of all!
In this place, Noah floated in a region where time itself had gone murky, as if the weavings here had been left out in the rain for a few billion years and started to rot.

Old currents of it hung in the air like smoke that had forgotten how to rise, grey-violet and heavy, and through them drifted things he could only half-perceive: the outline of an ocean that had dried long ago, the echo of a Dimension that had not been born yet, stretches where a single moment had been worn so thin by repetition that he could see straight through it.
It felt ancient in a way nothing else in the Chrysalis did.
On either side of him floated the two who had been with him longest, and they had come out of their acclimation changed!

Ruination’s crimson eyes no longer simply glowed. Beams of crimson light shot from them in steady lines, reading everything they touched, and she wore a long coat of crimson and gold, cut clean and severe, with the unchangeable script of her new Root showing faintly at her collar and wrists.
THE Infiniverse wore a thick fur coat of many colors, heavy and trailing, and her face held an expression Noah had rarely seen on it before. Imperious. Unbound
The look of a being who had just discovered exactly how much reality she could hold in one hand.
He had brought them here to test those new Roots, and for a second reason as well. He needed a Rare Gu for the Time Inscription. More than that, if he could manage it, he wanted a Rare Time Gu.
He had been ranging across the endless stretches of the Chrysalis for hours with this body, until at last he found this domain, soaked through with the old weavings of time.
"Master, if you can bear with me a little bit, I will explain my vision at this moment in time..." Ruination said.
Her crimson beams swept slowly across the murky currents as she spoke.

"A lifeform looks at the dirt beneath its feet and believes that is all there is to see. Ask it what happened a moment ago, and it must remember. Ask it what happens next, and it must guess. It spends its whole existence peering through a crack in a wall, watching existence slide past one second at a time."
The beams paused. "I...no longer look through the crack."
Noah waited. She was clearly not finished!

"When I open my senses now, distance stops being a road that must be walked. In THE Infiniverse, a million Dimensions from here, a woman drops a clay pot. I do not simply see it fall. I see her fingers letting go. I see the pot hanging in the air. I see the five different ways it may break against the floor, all in the same breath. The past is not a memory. Tomorrow is not a mystery. They are only... different corners of the same table."
She turned her head, and the beams turned with it, into the deeper murk.

"Across this domain, I have already located the information of two Rare Time Gu. Where they are, where they have been, and where probability says they will be one minute from now. I can take you to where they will be, Master, and we can simply wait for them to arrive."
Noah smiled.
She was showing off a little. He did not mind in the least!
"Lead," he said.
They followed her. Each step they took crossed gigaparsecs, the murky currents blurring past, and at the place Ruination chose they stopped, and waited, and the Chrysalis came to them.

It was a place of purple clouds, slow and towering, and between them spun disks of raw time! Great flat wheels of it, violet-edged and whirling, and anything they touched was severed from billions of years in an instant, cut clean out of its own history. One sliced through a drifting rock ahead of them and the rock simply was not there anymore, had never been there, left no trace!

None of the disks came near the three of them. Around Noah and his companions, rivers of dream flowed slow and serene, blue and gold, and the disks of time curved away from them like wind parting around a standing stone.
And far ahead, through the clouds, they saw the Gu!
There were two of them, and they were titanic!

Each one looked something like a butterfly, if a butterfly had been dragged up from the deepest trench of a lightless sea. Their bodies were long and transluscent, lit from within by cold bioluminescent lures that dangled from their heads on thin stalks.

Their mouths were rimmed with glassy needle teeth, and trailing tendrils drifted beneath them for miles. But their wings were glorious. Vast and violet, burning with time, every scale a small flame of shifting hours!
And the two of them were holding a chain!

It ran between them, purple and gold, each end clasped in a set of long pale claws, and along its length flowed a current Noah recognized at once, because he had drunk its like from a river of time only days ago. Provenance. The Provenance of Time itself, coursing back and forth between the two great Gu without pause.
|RARE GU: THE ANCHORED HOUR (bound to the Past).|
|VERITAS: 471. POTENTIA: 468. PONDUS: 476. PROVENANCE: 489.|
|RARE GU: THE UNARRIVED HOUR (bound to the Future).|
|VERITAS: 474. POTENTIA: 470. PONDUS: 472. PROVENANCE: 491.|
|A mated pair, joined by a chain of their own Provenance of Time. One lives entirely in the Past. The other lives entirely in the Future. Neither exists in the present at all.|
|A blow struck at one may be undone by the other before it lands, or will already have been avoided in a moment that has not yet come.|
|Their attributes are not extreme. Their paradox is.|

Noah’s eyes narrowed. High four hundreds. Beneath him, on paper, by a fair margin. And none of that mattered in the least, because how exactly did you hit something that was not here? One of them lived before the blow and the other lived after it, and between them they held the only moment where a blow could land.
The two Gu turned their great heads toward the three intruders.
|THE ANCHORED HOUR and THE UNARRIVED HOUR speak as one.|
|"You are strong. We see it. We have always seen it, and we will see it again."|

|"But strength is a thing of the present, and we do not live there. Many greater than you have come. None of them could pass the paradox of what was and what will be. We have mastered it. Leave, or be left behind."|
Noah’s eyes shone brilliantly!
He was already moving to answer when THE Infiniverse stepped forward.

There was no asking, and no glance back at him. She simply took one step past his shoulder into the purple clouds, and her multicolored coat swung heavy behind her, and the whole domain felt her arrive!

The disks of time turned toward her at once, a dozen of them, a hundred, whirling in to cut her away from her own history. They struck her, and they broke! Instead of cutting, they shattered against her like thrown plates against a cliff, because there was too much of her.

A disk like that could sever a rock from billions of years. It could not sever her, because she was not a thing that had happened. She was simply there, heavier than anything in the domain, too vast to be cut out of anything!

The Gu reacted. THE Unarrived Hour wrenched its burning wings, and in the future THE Infiniverse had not yet reached, it had already moved. THE Anchored Hour pulled on the chain, and the moment she had just stepped through began, quietly, to unhappen behind her.
In answer, THE Infiniverse raised one hand.
Domains grew from it!

Dimensions and Observable Existences budded off her fingers, as they had budded along her branches in his Root Domain, but these did not stay small. They swelled as they fell, heavy, whole, each one crowded with seas and continents and weight, and she let them drop into the domain of purple clouds one after another after another. Ten. A hundred. Thousands! More!

The Gu’s paradox needed a gap. A narrow space between what was and what would be, where the two of them could live apart and pass a blow back and forth between them. THE Infiniverse did not argue with that paradox, or try to reason her way past it, or rewrite its rules.

She filled the gap with existence, pouring new Dimensions into the space between past and future until there was no space left, until the Past and the Future were packed so tight with sheer grown reality that they had nowhere to hide from each other, and nowhere to hide from her!
The chain between the two Gu went taut!
THE Infiniverse walked forward through her own falling domains, and took hold of it.
Noah watched her do it, and he saw a snowbound Elsedimension, and a frost-visage taking a single step, and a hand closing on an Immense One who had written existence into a debt.

The Collector had been a writer, and Lucy had been the page. These Gu had written a paradox, and THE Infiniverse was the page too. She did not out-think them. She simply had more existence than their idea could hold. That was what a Physical Root meant!
That was what it would grow into, one day: a Fiend. A thing that was stronger than the rules!
She pulled!

The Anchored Hour came out of the Past, dragged by its own chain. The Unarrived Hour came out of the Future. Both of them, wrenched screaming into the one moment they had never stood in, the present, and there, at last, they could be touched!

Chains bloomed from THE Infiniverse’s hands, bright and many-colored, the same brilliance as her coat, and wound around both Gu, wings and tendrils and lures, binding the burning violet down. The great creatures thrashed, and the chains did not care!

She turned, and walked back through the purple clouds toward Noah, dragging the two bound titans behind her like a hunter bringing home the season’s catch. The falling domains settled around her into slow orbits, and the disks of time kept their distance now, and the Provenance of Time still ran up and down the golden chain between her prisoners, though neither of them could escape into it anymore.
She stopped before her Master, and let them drop at his feet!
"Master," THE Infiniverse said. Her voice was calm. Her face was imperious and utterly unbothered. "Your Rare Gu."

THE Unarrived Hour wrenched its burning wings, and in the future THE Infiniverse had not yet reached, it had already moved.
THE Anchored Hour pulled on the chain, and the moment she had just stepped through began, quietly, to unhappen behind her.
In answer, THE Infiniverse raised one hand.
Domains grew from it!
Dimensions and Observable Existences budded off her fingers, as they had budded along her branches in his Root Domain, but these did not stay small.
They swelled as they fell, heavy, whole, each one crowded with seas and continents and weight, and she let them drop into the domain of purple clouds one after another after another.
Ten.
A hundred.
Thousands!
More!
The Gu’s paradox needed a gap.
A narrow space between what was and what would be, where the two of them could live apart and pass a blow back and forth between them.
THE Infiniverse did not argue with that paradox, or try to reason her way past it, or rewrite its rules.

She filled the gap with existence, pouring new Dimensions into the space between past and future until there was no space left, until the Past and the Future were packed so tight with sheer grown reality that they had nowhere to hide from each other, and nowhere to hide from her!
The chain between the two Gu went taut!
THE Infiniverse walked forward through her own falling domains, and took hold of it.
Noah watched her do it, and he saw a snowbound Elsedimension, and a frost-visage taking a single step, and a hand closing on an Immense One who had written existence into a debt.
The Collector had been a writer, and Lucy had been the page.
These Gu had written a paradox, and THE Infiniverse was the page too.
She did not out-think them.
She simply had more existence than their idea could hold.
That was what a Physical Root meant!
That was what it would grow into, one day: a Fiend.
A thing that was stronger than the rules!
She pulled!
The Anchored Hour came out of the Past, dragged by its own chain.
The Unarrived Hour came out of the Future.
Both of them, wrenched screaming into the one moment they had never stood in, the present, and there, at last, they could be touched!
Chains bloomed from THE Infiniverse’s hands, bright and many-colored, the same brilliance as her coat, and wound around both Gu, wings and tendrils and lures, binding the burning violet down.
The great creatures thrashed, and the chains did not care!
She turned, and walked back through the purple clouds toward Noah, dragging the two bound titans behind her like a hunter bringing home the season’s catch.

The falling domains settled around her into slow orbits, and the disks of time kept their distance now, and the Provenance of Time still ran up and down the golden chain between her prisoners, though neither of them could escape into it anymore.
She stopped before her Master, and let them drop at his feet!
"Master," THE Infiniverse said.
Her voice was calm.
Her face was imperious and utterly unbothered.
"Your Rare Gu."

chapters.title: Chapter 5790: The Death of Time! II
paragraphs: The two Rare Time Gu lay bound at Noah’s feet in THE Infiniverse’s many-colored chains, their violet wings dimmed, their long lures trembling, and he reached down to take them.
And yet...
He never touched them!
A moment before anything happened, Ruination went rigid!

Her crimson beams had been drifting lazily across the purple clouds, reading the spin of the time-disks and the slow currents between them, and all at once they locked in place. The script at her collar and wrists flared bright. The endless text scrolling through her eyes stopped scrolling, and held on a single thin line that had just appeared at the far edge of everything she could see.
"Master," she said.
Her voice was as level as ever, but it came quickly, and Ruination never spoke quickly.
"There is a branch. Point zero zero zero three percent. It should not be possible for it to..."
It should not be possible, but...it happened anyway.
The Provenance of Time came down on them like a falling sea!

It poured out of the purple sky in heavy, turbulent sheets of violet and gold, and every current of it was thick with more ages than the whole murky domain had held a breath before. The time-disks spinning through the clouds stopped dead mid-turn, frozen in place like coins dropped into ice!

The towering clouds stopped drifting. Even the light changed. It began arriving late, reaching Noah’s eyes a long, strange instant after it should have, so that everything he looked at seemed to be happening a little in the past.
At his feet, very quietly, the two bound Rare Gu began to weep.

Noah moved on instinct. He reached for his Provenance, for his Root, for the rivers of dream that had kept every danger in this domain curving harmlessly around him and his companions like wind around a standing stone.
Nothing came!
That was the first strange thing. His Provenance had not gone anywhere. He could feel all of it, vast and blue and gold, filling him exactly as it always did. It simply would not move.
His Root was there too, turning at the center of him, except that it was not turning. It had been caught mid-beat, like a heart that had been told its next beat was not permitted.

Beside him, THE Infiniverse had frozen with one hand half-raised! The domains she had grown hanging motionless in their orbits around her. Ruination’s beams were still lit and still fixed on that impossible branch, and she could not turn them away from it.
So Noah reached for the one thing on him that had never needed his permission.

THE Enduring Gu Elsedimension Ring sat on his finger, and at its heart was an Existential Narrative Displacement, woven there for exactly this. The moment any authority grander than his own closed around him, it would tear him out of that place and throw him somewhere safer, whether he willed it or not.
And yet...
It did not fire!
He understood why a heartbeat later.
The ring’s displacement worked by carrying him into the next moment, somewhere else. To do anything at all, a being needed a next moment to do it in.
And there was no next moment anymore!

Something had reached across time and taken it away. The clock had not been stopped.The next moment had simply been removed from existence around them, so that every authority and every Root the three of them owned stood pinned inside one single instant, whole and grand and completely useless, with nowhere at all to go.
It was a very simple thing. That was what made it so terrifying.
Far above, something began to show itself!

At first there was only an absence. A place in the purple sky where the light did not arrive at all, a shape made out of lateness. Then the lateness gained edges, and the edges gained weight, and Noah began to see, or almost see, or see in pieces his sight could not quite hold together.

A limb came first, jointed and impossibly long, reaching down through the clouds like the hand of a clock that counted Ages instead of hours. Then another. Then a body, segmented and vast, each segment a great slab of something like amber, deep gold and translucent, and inside each slab, perfectly preserved, lay an entire Age!

He could see them! Oceans and cities and burning stars, and the tiny frozen figures of beings who had lived and died long befor anything he knew had begun, all of it sealed segment upon segment down the length of a body that ran on past the edge of his sight.

Wings spread above it! They were not made of any substance at all. They were made of stopped moments, thousands upon thousands of frozen instants gathered from every corner of existence and laid edge to edge like scales.
Then the head came down through the clouds!

It had no face. Where a face should have been there was only a smooth dark hollow, and around that hollow, set like a crown, were eyes. A great many eyes, and in each one a different Age was still happening. Noah looked into one and saw a Dimension being born. In the one beside it, the same Dimension dying. In the next, a war, and in the one after, the same war won by the other side.
|THE FIRST GU OF TIME.|
The prompt gave him nothing else. Beneath the name lay only a smear of question marks that his sight slid off of, as though the rest of what she was had quietly declined to be read.
"You have come a very long way to take something that was never yours,"THE First Gu of Time said.
Her voice did not come from the hollow where her face should have been. It came from the stopped moments in her wings, all of them at once, cool and clear and perfectly composed.

"I have watched your kind come. Across more Ages than you could count if I gave you every moment I hold to count them in."The crown of eyes turned, unhurried, toward the two bound Rare Gu, and the Ages burning in them softened very slightly. "Tell me. What did these small ones do to you, that you should hunt them?"
The Rare Gu whimpered in their chains.

"I have seen lifeforms like you move through my children as reapers move through a field. You take them. You grind them down. You bind them into rings, render them into engines, and pour their small lives into vessels to keep yourselves warm, and then you call it craft, as though the word makes it clean. What gave you the right?"
Noah could not answer. The instant held his mouth as firmly as it held everything else.

"Consider it turned around,"THE First Gu of Time went on, quietly. "Consider my children moving through your Dimensions and your Observable Existences. Through your proud Lineages. Taking your Descendants from their cradles and your Provenance Lifeforms from their halls, and grinding their bodies into material for our own warmth."
Every eye in her crown held him. "How would it feel, to be the harvest? I have asked this of a great many of your kind. Not one has ever answered me well. Why is there such cruelty in all of you?"
WAA!

And Noah thought...of the Common Dream Gu sealed at the heart of the ring on his finger. It had dreamed only of warmth, and of being left alone. He thought of the Common Gu that had died screaming in his first failed inscription, cracked apart by a Letter too heavy for it to carry, and of how he had come to this domain today to take a Rare Gu and forge it into a tool, and had never once, not for a single breath, cared.
It was kill or be killed right? Natural selection?
He had looked at them as material!
And the Collector, not so very long ago, had looked at the Vasilious in a similar manner.
He did not like how close those two thoughts sat to each other. He did not like it at all.
"You are silent? Nobody truly ever has a devent answer as at least...you are silent."THE First Gu of Time said.
Her crown of eyes turned away from him, slowly, and came to rest on THE Infiniverse and Ruination.
"These two are dear to you," she said. It was not a question. "I have seen every moment you have ever spent looking at them. They are very dear."
Something in Noah’s pinned existence strained against the instant so hard that the frozen moment around him creaked.
But...
It did not break!
"Then they will learn what my children learn,"THE First Gu of Time said."I take no pleasure in it. But you have made it clear that you learn nothing from words. Perhaps you will learn from this."
She never touched them. There was no need!
THE Infiniverse’s domains began to age and die!

The small new Dimensions orbiting her, the ones she had grown only moments ago from her Root of Genesis and been so quietly proud of, went grey. Their seas dried to craked beds. Their continents crumbled. Whole spans of time were forced through each of them at once, and one after another they withered to dust and drifted away from her like ash from a dead fire.

THE Infiniverse could neither move nor cry out, but her starlit eyes were open, and Noah saw in them exactly what she felt: every one of those domains dying as she was made to feel their death amplified by many times!

And Ruination kept recording as her Root was the Root of the Record. Everything she observed, she kept, perfectly and forever, beyond the reach of any hand that might try to edit it. Pinned in place, unable to look away, she could not stop THE First Gu of Time from pouring the grinding deaths into her. The sinilar long, slow experience of a Gu being taken apart for material, again and again and again, and every instant of it written into her unchangeable record.

Noah watched the two of them forced to experience and record boundless deaths in amplified time, pinned and powerless, his Root frozen mid-beat and his Provenance sitting vast and useless inside him, and he knew what defeat was!
He had tasted it before, and it always sucked. But he had never tasted it like this.
Then, very slightly, the instant loosened around his mouth.
The First Gu of Time wanted him to speak!

Noah did not beg as he did not know how, and he would not have done it here even if he had. But he did not lie either. He had been honest with himself when a caretaker of the cold asked him what he would do differently and he found he had no answer. He could at least be honest now.
"I am human," Noah said.
His voice came out low and steady.
"And humans make mistakes. I will take this as one of mine. I came here to take your children the way I have taken others, and I never once asked what that meant to them. That is on me."
He held the crown of burning eyes with his own. "But you and I are not enemies past forgiving. We have a disagreement. So...what price needs to be paid for you to stop here?"
The eyes did not blink. The Ages inside them went on happening.

"I do not have the power right now to steer this where I want it to go. I know that. You have made very certain I know it. But I will have that power, in the future. Above everything else I am, I am determined. So determined that if I had to, I could make it the one absolute aim of my existence to ruin Time itself."
The frozen disks hung in the air around them. The dust of THE Infiniverse’s domains drifted slowly past. Ruination’s eyes kept writing.
"I would rather not," Noah said. "So. What price needs to be paid for us to go our separate ways?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5791: The Death of Time! III
paragraphs: THE First Gu of Time considered his question for a long moment.
Snow fell heavily all around them!

The Ages kept burning in her crown of eyes while she did. A Dimension was born in one and died in the next. A war was won, then lost. Somewhere in the frozen amber of her body, a whole civilization went on standing exactly where it had stood when she sealed it, and never noticed that it had stopped.
"They acted at your behest," she said at last.
Her gaze moved, unhurried, across THE Infiniverse with the dust of her domains still drifting around her, and across Ruination with her eyes still writing.
"They took my children because you wished my children taken. So I will not ask them to pay for it any longer. Let us see instead what you are made of."
Her voice stayed as cool and even as still water. "You may take their pain for them. In exchange for letting them go, and for letting you go, you will experience the Death of Time itself."
Experience the death of time itself?
Noah did not know what that meant. A being that could take the next moment out of existence did not offer a price that could be understood before it was paid.
It was a heavy thing!
He nodded anyway, without a word.

At once, the instant loosened! Not around him, but around the two beside him. He felt the anchoring locks on THE Infiniverse and Ruination come undone, felt their Roots catch their next beat and their authorities start to move again, and he saw THE Infiniverse’s starlit eyes turn to him, and Ruination open her mouth.
He waved his hand before either of them could speak!
They were gone, sent back through the Chrysalis and down into the safety of his Existential Root Domain. Better that way. He did not want to argue with them, and he did not want them to watch.
Then he stood alone in the frozen purple sky, before THE First Gu of Time.

The two Rare Time Gu had slipped free of their many-colored chains the instant THE Infiniverse left. They drifted now near their ancient mother, their violet wings burning bright again, their long lures swaying, and the Past-bound one turned its eyeless head toward him with a slow, satisfied tilt that was nothing but gloating. The Future-bound one looked at him as if it already knew how this ended.
Perhaps it did.
"Hold still," said THE First Gu of Time. "There is nothing you can do to make this easier."
Her wings opened wide!
Every stopped moment laid along them came loose at once, thousands upon thousands of frozen instants, and they turned into rivers!
Boundless rivers of time, violet and gold and roaring, poured off her wings in a flood that filled the whole sky, and every one of them came down on Noah.
Instead of striking him, they entered him!
Through his chest, through his eyes, through the spinning mobius at the center of his crystalline body, the rivers of time surged in, and Noah felt himself come apart into every direction at once!
He felt like he was dreaming, but it was not a dream.
He...was very small!

He was so small that he had no eyes, no mind, nothing at all except a wall of thin skin and a hunger. He drifted in a warm dark sea he could not perceive and divided, and divided again, and ate, and divided, and never once knew he was alive. Then the warm sea grew cold, and he stopped. That was the whole of it. A microbe, born in a drop of water somewhere, and dead when the water dried.
He was an insect.

Six legs, a hard green shell, and one summer spent climbing the same tall stalk of grass, again and again, toward a light at the top he could never quite reach. Eating. Singing with his wings in the evening. On the last warm day of the year a bird took him from the stalk, and he felt its beak close, and that was that.

Then a virus, never knowing what it was. A mouse, afraid for its entire short life, and right to be. A great grey wolf that ran for eleven years across a winter forest and died old and alone in a den it had dug itself.
Time started, and time died!
He was an orc!

His name was Gashr, and he was born on a battlefield in a Dimension that did not remember him, in the mud behind a war camp, to a mother who died that same night. He grew up hard. He grew up fast. He learned to swing an axe before he could read a single runne, and he learned to read runes anyway, secretly, by firelight, from a stolen book he hid under his bedroll for twenty years.

He fought in nine wars and won six. He married a one-armed smith who made him laugh. They had four children, and he buried two of them. He was eighty-one when a young warlord with a borrowed Intent burned his village for the ore beneath it, and he died in the doorway of his own house with the axe still in his hands, and the last thing he thought was that he had never finished the stolen book.
Time moved.

He was now a fae, glass-winged and bright, and lived nine hundred years in a moonlit forest singing songs to the trees. The forest was cleared for a road. She followed it for a while, then stopped following, and faded away into the morning light.

He was a goblin named Nib, who stole shiny things and was proud of every one of them and was, all things considered, very happy. He was hanged for a stolen spoon at the age of forty. It had been a very nice spoon!
He was a Gu!

Small and pale and new, a Common Gu, born out of loose existence in the drifting light of a Chrysalis, a hundred of one thing and nothing of anything else. It did not want much: to drift, to be warm, to be left alone.

For a while, it was. Then a hand closed around it. A great, patient, greedy hand, and he felt himself taken, and bound, and set on a workbench, and slowly, carefully, ground down into material for someone else’s ring. It hurt the entire time. It took a very long time. Nobody asked him anything, and when it was over, there was nothing left of him but a faint glow in a stranger’s craft.
Noah felt that one more than any of the others!
Time moved on.
He was a Provenance Lifeform, self-made, proud, who spent three million years building a Lineage out of nothing and watched another Provenance Lineage collect it in an afternoon.
He was a Descendant, born with a sentence in his blood, who lived four hundred years in a gilded court knowing every day of it exactly when he would die, and died exactly then, cursed.
And at the very last, he was an Immense One!
An Immense One!

No one could have held all of it. He stood at the top of existence for longer than there had been anything to measure it by, and existence agreed with every word he spoke, and he grew bored, and then cold, and then far beyond cold.

He watched Ages rise and fall like breath on a window. Whatever he wanted, he took, because nothing had ever told him no. And then one day something did, something he had never seen coming, and his vastness caved around it, and he learned, for the first and only time, what the smallest bug in the mud had always known.
That everything ends!
Microbe, insect, orc, goblin, Gu, Immense One. Killed or faded or simply finished.
Each life he lived, he lived through to its very last moment, and he felt each last moment arrive. And when the last life ended, he was not released.

He was held there, at the end of all of them at once, and made to feel every death he had just lived, not one after another but together, all of them, the whole weight of time running out for everything at the same instant.
That was the death of time.
It was the worst thing he had ever felt!
Even the cold of the Long Night felt mild!
It went on and on, past anything that had a name, past the frozen underworld, past any lives he lived!
He had no body to scream with and no mind left to break, and he did not break anyway, because some small stubborn thing at the very center of him refused.
It was human, that thing. It was the part of him that had lived every one of those lives and remembered, even in the worst of it, that every one of them had been worth living.
He held on to that.
He held on to it through the end of everything!
