The rivers of time were still pouring into him, but they were no longer flooding him. They were being taken in. Drawn down into his Root, which had begun, very slowly, to beat again, and every beat it took pulled more of the lived and ended time inside it and pressed it close.
His Provenance did not grow. That was the strangest part of all. It did not swell or surge or climb. Instead it compressed!

Every life he had lived pressed down into it like snow packing into ice, layer on layer on layer, countless years of living and ending crushed into something smaller and denser and harder with every beat of his Root, refined past anything a mere number could hold.
His Root drank it and was reinforced, deepened, hardened, until it turned inside him with a weight it had never had, the weight of having been every kind of thing there was.
His body followed!
The crystalline frame thickened, broadened at the shoulders and chest, the long lean lines of him filling out with the dense, heavy muscle of a man who had lived more lives than there were stars.

The youth drained out of his face. Not old, not bent, but older. Fine lines settled at the corners of his eyes. His jaw set harder. He looked like someone who had worked a very long time and endured a great deal and come out the other side stronger for every day of it.
And around him, clouds began to bloom!

The stopped disks of time, frozen mid-turn, trembled in their places. Currents of old violet smoke wavered and blurred at their edges.

Time itself was dreaming!
THE First Gu of Time pulsed!

Her crown of eyes, which had watched countless Ages without once looking away, turned toward the clouds drifting through her wings. The Ages burning in them flickered. For the first time since she had appeared, she did not look like a being who already knew how everything ended.
The two Rare Time Gu had stopped gloating. They shrank back against their mother, lures trembeling.
In the middle of the dreaming sky, Noah opened his eyes.

They were not young eyes anymore. They held an age that had nothing to do with years, the age of a microbe and an orc and a goblin and a Gu and an Immense One, the age of every life he had just lived and every death he had just felt, and they were so ancient that for a moment that one could mistake them for the eyes of an Immense One.
He looked at her for a long while before he spoke.
"Thank you," Noah said.
His voice was quiet, and deeper than it had been.

"Thank you for showing me that." He glanced at the two Rare Gu pressed close against her amber body, and then back up at her crown of burning eyes. "And I apologize for what I did. Wholeheartedly. I will not use Gu as materials for anything I do. Not again."
The dream-clouds drifted around him, and the frozen time went on dreaming.
"My dreams. My time. My humanity," Noah said. "That will be enough."

sentences.text: THE First Gu of Time considered his question for a long moment.
Snow fell heavily all around them!
The Ages kept burning in her crown of eyes while she did.
A Dimension was born in one and died in the next.
A war was won, then lost.
Somewhere in the frozen amber of her body, a whole civilization went on standing exactly where it had stood when she sealed it, and never noticed that it had stopped.
"They acted at your behest," she said at last.
Her gaze moved, unhurried, across THE Infiniverse with the dust of her domains still drifting around her, and across Ruination with her eyes still writing.
"They took my children because you wished my children taken.
So I will not ask them to pay for it any longer.
Let us see instead what you are made of."
Her voice stayed as cool and even as still water.
"You may take their pain for them.
In exchange for letting them go, and for letting you go, you will experience the Death of Time itself."
Experience the death of time itself?
Noah did not know what that meant.
A being that could take the next moment out of existence did not offer a price that could be understood before it was paid.
It was a heavy thing!
He nodded anyway, without a word.
At once, the instant loosened!
Not around him, but around the two beside him.

He felt the anchoring locks on THE Infiniverse and Ruination come undone, felt their Roots catch their next beat and their authorities start to move again, and he saw THE Infiniverse’s starlit eyes turn to him, and Ruination open her mouth.
He waved his hand before either of them could speak!
They were gone, sent back through the Chrysalis and down into the safety of his Existential Root Domain.
Better that way.
He did not want to argue with them, and he did not want them to watch.
Then he stood alone in the frozen purple sky, before THE First Gu of Time.
The two Rare Time Gu had slipped free of their many-colored chains the instant THE Infiniverse left.

They drifted now near their ancient mother, their violet wings burning bright again, their long lures swaying, and the Past-bound one turned its eyeless head toward him with a slow, satisfied tilt that was nothing but gloating.
The Future-bound one looked at him as if it already knew how this ended.
Perhaps it did.
"Hold still," said THE First Gu of Time.
"There is nothing you can do to make this easier."
Her wings opened wide!
Every stopped moment laid along them came loose at once, thousands upon thousands of frozen instants, and they turned into rivers!
Boundless rivers of time, violet and gold and roaring, poured off her wings in a flood that filled the whole sky, and every one of them came down on Noah.
Instead of striking him, they entered him!
Through his chest, through his eyes, through the spinning mobius at the center of his crystalline body, the rivers of time surged in, and Noah felt himself come apart into every direction at once!
He felt like he was dreaming, but it was not a dream.
He...was very small!
He was so small that he had no eyes, no mind, nothing at all except a wall of thin skin and a hunger.
He drifted in a warm dark sea he could not perceive and divided, and divided again, and ate, and divided, and never once knew he was alive.
Then the warm sea grew cold, and he stopped.
That was the whole of it.
A microbe, born in a drop of water somewhere, and dead when the water dried.
He was an insect.
Six legs, a hard green shell, and one summer spent climbing the same tall stalk of grass, again and again, toward a light at the top he could never quite reach.
Eating.
Singing with his wings in the evening.
On the last warm day of the year a bird took him from the stalk, and he felt its beak close, and that was that.
Then a virus, never knowing what it was.
A mouse, afraid for its entire short life, and right to be.
A great grey wolf that ran for eleven years across a winter forest and died old and alone in a den it had dug itself.
Time started, and time died!
He was an orc!
His name was Gashr, and he was born on a battlefield in a Dimension that did not remember him, in the mud behind a war camp, to a mother who died that same night.
He grew up hard.
He grew up fast.
He learned to swing an axe before he could read a single runne, and he learned to read runes anyway, secretly, by firelight, from a stolen book he hid under his bedroll for twenty years.
He fought in nine wars and won six.
He married a one-armed smith who made him laugh.
They had four children, and he buried two of them.

He was eighty-one when a young warlord with a borrowed Intent burned his village for the ore beneath it, and he died in the doorway of his own house with the axe still in his hands, and the last thing he thought was that he had never finished the stolen book.
Time moved.
He was now a fae, glass-winged and bright, and lived nine hundred years in a moonlit forest singing songs to the trees.
The forest was cleared for a road.
She followed it for a while, then stopped following, and faded away into the morning light.
He was a goblin named Nib, who stole shiny things and was proud of every one of them and was, all things considered, very happy.
He was hanged for a stolen spoon at the age of forty.
It had been a very nice spoon!
He was a Gu!
Small and pale and new, a Common Gu, born out of loose existence in the drifting light of a Chrysalis, a hundred of one thing and nothing of anything else.
It did not want much: to drift, to be warm, to be left alone.
For a while, it was.
Then a hand closed around it.
A great, patient, greedy hand, and he felt himself taken, and bound, and set on a workbench, and slowly, carefully, ground down into material for someone else’s ring.
It hurt the entire time.
It took a very long time.
Nobody asked him anything, and when it was over, there was nothing left of him but a faint glow in a stranger’s craft.
Noah felt that one more than any of the others!
Time moved on.
He was a Provenance Lifeform, self-made, proud, who spent three million years building a Lineage out of nothing and watched another Provenance Lineage collect it in an afternoon.
He was a Descendant, born with a sentence in his blood, who lived four hundred years in a gilded court knowing every day of it exactly when he would die, and died exactly then, cursed.
And at the very last, he was an Immense One!
An Immense One!
No one could have held all of it.
He stood at the top of existence for longer than there had been anything to measure it by, and existence agreed with every word he spoke, and he grew bored, and then cold, and then far beyond cold.
He watched Ages rise and fall like breath on a window.

That everything ends!
Microbe, insect, orc, goblin, Gu, Immense One.

chapters.title: Chapter 5792: A Boundless Dream of Time!
paragraphs: For a long while after he spoke, nothing in the purple sky moved except the clouds of dream drifting off Noah’s shoulders.

He let them drift. He was still sorting through what had just been poured into him, the microbe and the orc and the goblin with his very nice spoon, the Gu on the workbench, the Immense One who learned at the very end what every bug in the mud had always known. It was a great deal to carry. He found, a little to his suprise, that he did not want to put any of it down.
THE First Gu of Time watched him with her crown of burning eyes!
"Gu are a passive kind," she said at last. "We do not hunt. We do not hoard. For the most part, we do not even want. And a great many beings have taken that as permission."
The Ages in her eyes turned slowly. "The worst of them, and the one who took more of my children than any other, was an engineer. His name was Atlas."
Noah kept perfectly still!
On his finger, the faint illusory ring that only he could see gave no sign of anything at all.

"He is gone now," THE First Gu of Time went on, "but his way of thinking has outlived him. Others study what he left and try to walk where he walked. They collect my children as ingredients, as though a living thing were a measure of salt."

Her voice stayed soft and even."I will not ask you to make it your life’s work. But if you continue to travel this place, and you see any being grinding down a Gu, I would have you stop them. And save whichever of my children you can."
She let her gaze drift out over the frozen time-disks, the violet smoke, the vast drowning dark of the Chrysalis beyond them.

"I am a Gu myself, you understand. I am passive as well, most of the time. I would have remained so today.But the cold is spreading everywhere now, and a great many of my children will die in it no matter what anyone does. I could not simply watch while two more were taken on top of that."
Noah inclined his head. He had nothing to say to that which would have been worth saying.
"Existence is vast," she said, more quietly. "It does not have to be cruel."
The frozen disks trembled faintly in the dream-clouds around them!

"You should also know that with the coming of the cold, doors that were shut for a very long time are beginning to open again. Those who are already Immense will not find those doors easily. Most of them will never find them at all. Those who grasp Immensity in this cold, on the other hand, may have a chance."

Her many eyes settled on him. "I have a few children in whom I see that chance. There is a brilliance in them. I saw a similar brilliance in you when I passed this way, and in the two you brought with you. That is why I found it such a shame to see what the three of you were doing."
She was quiet for a moment.
"You have a chance. All of you do. But in existence, that is all it will ever be. A chance. Nothing at all is guaranteed."
Then her wings, which had gone still, began to stir again!

The two Rare Time Gu drew in close against her amber body. The stopped moments along her wings rippled like scales settling on a great animal about to rise. And as the vast shape of her began to withdraw into the purple sky, THE First Gu of Time turned her crown of eyes back to him one last time.

"I meant to tell you that you have been touched by time," she said. "But that is not quite right, is it. Your dreams are unusual. They have taken the time into themselves rather than the other way around."

The Ages in her eyes flickered, curious."I doubt you will ever reach where I stand, where time is concerned. But should you grasp something profound, and wish to challenge time itself, you will find me at the very end of it."
BOOM!
The sky shook, once, and THE First Gu of Time was gone!

The two Rare Gu went with her, violet wings shrinking into nothing, and in the space where her vast amber body had hung there was only purple cloud and slow violet smoke. Around Noah, the frozen time-disks lurched, caught their spin again, and went on turning. The light started arriving on time!
The next moment came back into existence as quietly as it had left, and everything that had been pinned in place simply continued, as though it had never been stopped at all.
Noah stood alone in the dreaming sky!
He was quiet for a long time. Then he raised his hand and looked at the faint illusory ring on his finger.

Atlas had not said a word since the purple sky came down. Not one! The old engineer, who had an opinion on everything and could not bear to let a clever thing pass without comment, had been utterly silent while a First Gu named him the worst hunter of her children in all existence.
"Atlas," Noah said calmly. "The Time Inscription you meant to write with your Quill. What was it going to do?"

He asked without accusation. But he asked it knowing now, as he had not known that morning, that even the grandest inscription was not absolute. That behind every clever piece of engineering there might be a great many small lives that had never been asked.
The ring stayed silent a moment longer.

"It...was an inscription for advantage," Atlas said at last. His voicewas quieter than Noah had ever heard it."Time, turned to your favor. As the seconds passed, you would charge it, and when it was charged you would activate it, and your Provenance and your foundations would gain the progression of days. Or weeks, or months, depending on the rarity of the Gu at its heart and the depth of your Provenance. That was the plan, anyway. But now..."
He did not finish.
There was no need. Noah had promised, in this same purple sky, not to hunt Gu or use them as material for anything he did. And an inscription with a Rare Gu at its heart was exactly that.
"Then I will make things simpler for myself,"Noah said.
He lowered his hand.

"Gu are external. At the end of the day, that is all they are, to someone like me. Something outside of me, taken and made use of. Your engineering needed them because it was your engineering, built your way, on your terms. That is not a flaw in it. It is simply what it was."

He looked out across the turning time-disks. "But I can have my own existential engineering, and it can need different things. For me, my dreams are enough. My dreams are sufficient. And right now, my dreams have more perception of time, and more weavings of time, than anything I could have caught and put in a ring."
HUUM!
Noah closed his eyes, and raised his hands!

The dream-clouds around him surged! They rose off his skin thicker and brighter than before, rolling out through the purple sky in great slow banks of blue and gold, and through them, from somewhere deep inside him, rivers of Infinity began to pour. Dialetheic Infinity, the finite and the infinite at once, a truth that was also its own opposite. It had always run through him. But now it was different.
Now every river of it carried time in it, violet threads of lived and ended moments woven all through the blue and gold, running beside every current.
"An impossibility," Noah said quietly, with his eyes still closed, "is only a moment that has not been dreamed yet."
The rivers rolled out around him!

"People think Infinity means more. More and more and more, forever, a line that never stops. It is not that. Infinity is every moment at once. The beginning and the end of a thing, and everything between them, all held in the same hand. I have been every kind of life there is, from the first breath to the last. So I know."He opened his hands wider.
"Nothing is impossible that has a beginning. And everything has a beginning. Even the end of time began somewhere."
In that deep, strange stillness, he lifted one hand and laid it against his own chest.
Time poured out of it!

Boundless and violet and gold, spiling out of the spinning mobius at the center of him and away into the dreaming sky, and as it poured he remembered. Gashr in the doorway with her axe. Nib and his spoon. The small pale Gu on the workbench. The wolf in its den. The Immense One who had never once been told no. Every life he had lived, from its first moment to its last, and every stretch of time that had begun and ended inside each one.
"A dream, from its beginning to its end, is a measure of time,"Noah said."A dream can start. A dream can end. And that alone is enough to mark where time begins, and where it stops."
His hand stayed flat against his chest. "Between my dreams and existence, there is a gap. I can only ever try to close it. I can only ever live my dreams, across time."
His Provenance raged around him!

It came off him in a great storm, as it had in the frozen underworld, but it was not blue and gold alone anymore. Purple ran through it now. Deep violet hues, the color of the Rare Gu’s burning wings and the amber of THE First Gu of Time and every stopped moment in her scales, threaded through every current of his Provenance, and the whole storm of it turned and turned and would not settle.
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer has acquired a Quality of Time.|
|Having lived and ended countless lives in the Death of Time, your Dreams now measure time from within.|
|The first Osmontian Inscription has been forged: THE OSMONTIAN INSCRIPTION OF THE DREAMING HOUR.|
|Ingredients: your Root. Your Provenance. Time. Nothing external.|

|Passive, THE Lived Hour: while you live, your Dreams live longer. Every second that passes in existence, your Provenance and foundations are refined as though far more time had passed within your Dreams. At present, days for each second. As your Provenance deepens, weeks. Then months. No charging is required. It does not stop.|

|Active, THE Dreamt Epoch: by entering a deep Dream, you may compress a far greater span of refinement into a single held moment. The span scales with the depth of the Dream and the density of your Provenance.|
|Passive, THE Hour That Dreams: weavings of time that act upon you are drawn into your Dreams. Near you, time does not simply pass. It dreams, and a dreaming hour moves as you would have it move.|
It was everything Atlas had meant to build!

More, in places! And there was no Gu at the heart of it. There was nothing at the heart of it at all except Noah himself, his Root and his Provenance and the time he had lived through in the dark. It was his, entirely and truly, in a way no ring on his finger had ever been.
The illusory ring was silent for a long moment!

"I promised to teach you a great many things,"Atlas said. There was something in his voice Noah could not quite place. Not bitterness. Something older and more tired than bitterness. "Why do I get the feeling that you are about to tell me you don’t really need my engineering?"
Noah opened his eyes.

"Everyone’s path is different," he said. "You were a grand engineer. You can still build things as you always built them. I am not an engineer. I am a dreamer, who can choose to engineer things when he wishes. And I dream of infinite possibilities, so what I do and what you do are going to part ways sometimes."

He looked at the ring. "You helped me. I can still help you. But I will follow my own path the way I choose to. I will learn every wonder existence has to show me, and then I will take them into myself however I see fit."
He lifted his gaze from the ring, out past the turning time-disks and the violet smoke, into the vast and boundless dark of the Chrysalis.

"Existence breathes. Epochs pass. Civilizations rise and become monuments, and the monuments crumble into memory, and by the time that breath comes again, even the memory is gone. All of them. Boundless civilizations, boundless dreams, every one of them lost somewhere in time."
His Provenance roared around him, blue and gold and purple. "And in all those epochs, in all of that lost time, I...want to reign supreme."
HUUM!
The dream-clouds rolled outward across the whole of the sky!
"I want to experience boundless existence,"Noah said, "and reign supreme!"
BOOM!

"Atlas," Noah said calmly.
"The Time Inscription you meant to write with your Quill.
What was it going to do?"
He asked without accusation.
But he asked it knowing now, as he had not known that morning, that even the grandest inscription was not absolute.
That behind every clever piece of engineering there might be a great many small lives that had never been asked.
The ring stayed silent a moment longer.
"It...was an inscription for advantage," Atlas said at last.
His voicewas quieter than Noah had ever heard it."Time, turned to your favor.
As the seconds passed, you would charge it, and when it was charged you would activate it, and your Provenance and your foundations would gain the progression of days.
Or weeks, or months, depending on the rarity of the Gu at its heart and the depth of your Provenance.
That was the plan, anyway.
But now..."
He did not finish.
There was no need.
Noah had promised, in this same purple sky, not to hunt Gu or use them as material for anything he did.
And an inscription with a Rare Gu at its heart was exactly that.
"Then I will make things simpler for myself,"Noah said.
He lowered his hand.
"Gu are external.
At the end of the day, that is all they are, to someone like me.
Something outside of me, taken and made use of.
Your engineering needed them because it was your engineering, built your way, on your terms.
That is not a flaw in it.
It is simply what it was."
He looked out across the turning time-disks.
"But I can have my own existential engineering, and it can need different things.
For me, my dreams are enough.
My dreams are sufficient.
And right now, my dreams have more perception of time, and more weavings of time, than anything I could have caught and put in a ring."
HUUM!
Noah closed his eyes, and raised his hands!
The dream-clouds around him surged!

They rose off his skin thicker and brighter than before, rolling out through the purple sky in great slow banks of blue and gold, and through them, from somewhere deep inside him, rivers of Infinity began to pour.
Dialetheic Infinity, the finite and the infinite at once, a truth that was also its own opposite.
It had always run through him.
But now it was different.
Now every river of it carried time in it, violet threads of lived and ended moments woven all through the blue and gold, running beside every current.
"An impossibility," Noah said quietly, with his eyes still closed, "is only a moment that has not been dreamed yet."
The rivers rolled out around him!
"People think Infinity means more.
More and more and more, forever, a line that never stops.
It is not that.
Infinity is every moment at once.
The beginning and the end of a thing, and everything between them, all held in the same hand.
I have been every kind of life there is, from the first breath to the last.
So I know."He opened his hands wider.
"Nothing is impossible that has a beginning.
And everything has a beginning.
Even the end of time began somewhere."
In that deep, strange stillness, he lifted one hand and laid it against his own chest.
Time poured out of it!
Boundless and violet and gold, spiling out of the spinning mobius at the center of him and away into the dreaming sky, and as it poured he remembered.
Gashr in the doorway with her axe.
Nib and his spoon.
The small pale Gu on the workbench.
The wolf in its den.
The Immense One who had never once been told no.
Every life he had lived, from its first moment to its last, and every stretch of time that had begun and ended inside each one.
"A dream, from its beginning to its end, is a measure of time,"Noah said."A dream can start.
A dream can end.
And that alone is enough to mark where time begins, and where it stops."
His hand stayed flat against his chest.
"Between my dreams and existence, there is a gap.
I can only ever try to close it.
I can only ever live my dreams, across time."
His Provenance raged around him!
It came off him in a great storm, as it had in the frozen underworld, but it was not blue and gold alone anymore.
Purple ran through it now.

Deep violet hues, the color of the Rare Gu’s burning wings and the amber of THE First Gu of Time and every stopped moment in her scales, threaded through every current of his Provenance, and the whole storm of it turned and turned and would not settle.
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer has acquired a Quality of Time.|
|Having lived and ended countless lives in the Death of Time, your Dreams now measure time from within.|
|The first Osmontian Inscription has been forged: THE OSMONTIAN INSCRIPTION OF THE DREAMING HOUR.|
|Ingredients: your Root.
Your Provenance.
Time.
Nothing external.|
|Passive, THE Lived Hour: while you live, your Dreams live longer.
Every second that passes in existence, your Provenance and foundations are refined as though far more time had passed within your Dreams.
At present, days for each second.
As your Provenance deepens, weeks.
Then months.
No charging is required.
It does not stop.|
|Active, THE Dreamt Epoch: by entering a deep Dream, you may compress a far greater span of refinement into a single held moment.
The span scales with the depth of the Dream and the density of your Provenance.|
|Passive, THE Hour That Dreams: weavings of time that act upon you are drawn into your Dreams.
Near you, time does not simply pass.
It dreams, and a dreaming hour moves as you would have it move.|
It was everything Atlas had meant to build!
More, in places!
And there was no Gu at the heart of it.
There was nothing at the heart of it at all except Noah himself, his Root and his Provenance and the time he had lived through in the dark.
It was his, entirely and truly, in a way no ring on his finger had ever been.
The illusory ring was silent for a long moment!
"I promised to teach you a great many things,"Atlas said.
There was something in his voice Noah could not quite place.
Not bitterness.
Something older and more tired than bitterness.
"Why do I get the feeling that you are about to tell me you don’t really need my engineering?"
Noah opened his eyes.
"Everyone’s path is different," he said.
"You were a grand engineer.
You can still build things as you always built them.
I am not an engineer.
I am a dreamer, who can choose to engineer things when he wishes.
And I dream of infinite possibilities, so what I do and what you do are going to part ways sometimes."
He looked at the ring.
"You helped me.
I can still help you.
But I will follow my own path the way I choose to.
I will learn every wonder existence has to show me, and then I will take them into myself however I see fit."
He lifted his gaze from the ring, out past the turning time-disks and the violet smoke, into the vast and boundless dark of the Chrysalis.
"Existence breathes.
Epochs pass.
Civilizations rise and become monuments, and the monuments crumble into memory, and by the time that breath comes again, even the memory is gone.
All of them.
Boundless civilizations, boundless dreams, every one of them lost somewhere in time."
His Provenance roared around him, blue and gold and purple.
"And in all those epochs, in all of that lost time, I...want to reign supreme."
HUUM!
The dream-clouds rolled outward across the whole of the sky!
"I want to experience boundless existence,"Noah said, "and reign supreme!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5793: There Will Only Be Me!
paragraphs: <THE Sealed One>
The feast had been going on for three days, and THE Sealed One had enjoyed almost none of it.

It was held in the great hall of the Aurum Crest, the highest palace of an Observable Existence that the Superbius Gilded had ruled for eleven thousand years. The hall was gold. Everything in it was gold, the floor and the pillars and the long tables and the vaulted ceiling far overhead, where a painted sun made of real, burning light hung eternally at noon.
The Superbius liked it that way. Pride was the root of their power, and nothing fed pride quite like a room that shone back at you from every surface.

There were hundreds of them at the tables. Tall and beautiful and gilded to the fingertips, their skins shining faintly with the Ego that made them what they were, their voices loud and warm and very pleased with themselfs. They told stories of old conquests and laughed at the stories they had heard a thousand times, and toasted each other’s victories, and argued, fiercely and happily, about whose great-great-grandfather had been the grander tyrant, and then they toasted that too.
And every few minutes, one of them would rise, and lift a golden cup, and turn toward the head of the table.
"To our great honor!"
"To THE Sealed One!"
The whole hall would roar it back, cups raised, faces bright, and THE Sealed One would incline his head and lift his own cup, and smile.
He was very good at smiling!

He sat at the head of the long table in a high-backed chair of gold that the Superbius had made for him specially, tall and pale and composed, his long hair pale gold shading into white, his long dark coat immaculate against all that shining metal.

On either side of him lounged a Luxuria. One was dark-haired and laughing, draped half across the arm of his chair, feeding him grapes she had dipped in honey. The other sat curled at his feet with her head resting against his knee, humming some old song of her people, content in the simple, uncomplicated way of a being whose whole existence was built around wanting and being wanted.
They were happy. All of them!
He watched them being happy, and he tried.
He had always tried. Across more Ages than he could count, THE Sealed One had sought out connection as other beings sought out food.
Thats why he mixed in with useless Gilded Ones like he was today. He had mixed with Descendants and Provenance Lifeforms at certain points. Just to...feel.

He had sat at feasts like this one in a thousand Observable Existences. He had lived for centuries among the Gilded in particular, because the Gilded felt so loudly. The Superbius and their bottomless pride. The Luxuria and their hungers. The Ira and their glorious, burning rage. They lived so openly and simply inside their own emotions, and he had always thought that if he stood close enough to feelings that strong, some of it might catch in him, as a spark catches in dry grass.
It never had.

He had tried Descendants. Walked among the sons and daughters of Those Who Remain, with their borrowed grandeur and their sentences in their blood. He had tried Provenance Lifeforms, proud self-made things who should, of anyone, have understood what it was to stand alone at the top of something. And every time, in every hall, at every table, it was the same.
He felt like an outsider!
No guest still learning the customs, either. An outsider as a man is an outsider at an anthill.

He could sit among them, and talk with them, and let them feed him grapes and toast his name, fuck them and make love to them, and underneath all of it he could feel, as clearly as he felt his own heartbeat, that he was above them.
All of them. Every being in every hall he had ever sat in. And a being who stands above everything cannot touch anything. He can only look down.
The Luxuria at his side pressed another honeyed grape to his lips, laughing.
The hall roared his name again.
THE Sealed One set down his cup.
"This... isn’t it,"he said quietly.
The dark-haired Luxuria paused, a grape halfway to his mouth. "My lord?"
"This isn’t it." He looked out across the golden hall, at the hundreds of shining, laughing faces."I don’t feel a thing."
HUUM!
He snapped his fingers!
The sound was very small. It was the only sound in the hall for a moment, because every voice in it had stopped at once. Then every Gilded Lifeform in the Aurum Crest burst!

Hundreds of them, all at the same instant. The Superbius at the long tables, mid-toast, cups still raised. The Luxuria at his side with the grape in her fingers, and the one at his feet with her song half-sung.

Every one of them came apart into a puddle of crimson gold blood that splashed across the golden floor and the golden tables and the golden walls, until the whole shining hall was painted red and gold and dripping!
There was no scream. There had been no time for one!
THE Sealed One sat very still in his gold chair in the middle of it as for ever a brief moment...he almost feltsomething. Almost!
Then he opened his mouth!

The blood came to him. It rose off the floor and the tables and the walls in long slow ribbons, crimson gold and shining with the last of all that pride and hunger, and flowed across the air and into his mouth, and he drank it. All of it!

Every drop of Ego and every scrap of feeling that had lived in hundreds of Gilded Lifeforms a moment ago, and he took it into himself without hurry, like a man finishing a cup of water he is not particularly thirsty for.
When it was done, the hall was only gold again, and very empty, and quiet.

His expression had not changed at all through any of it. There was no pleasure on his face. No triumph. Only a tired, faraway apathy, and under the apathy, if anyone had been left alive to see it, something very much like sadness.
He sighed.
"You’ve been watching from up there this whole time," THE Sealed One said to the painted sun. "What is it?"
The painted sun opened!

It split down the middle like an eyelid, and behind it there was no sun at all, only an eye. Vast and dark and old, burning with a sleepless, patient attention that did not blink, and never had, and never would!
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND regards you from above.|
|"You are truly a hateful thing."|
|"And yet all of them believe you hold the best chance of opening the door. So they support you."|
THE Sealed One laughed softly, and leaned back in his golden chair.

"But you were always the one who found me,"he said. "Ages ago, when I was only bright and very young and very stupid about it. You came down to look, and you never quite left." He spread his pale hands. "So. Any news?"
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND answers coldly.|
|"You will be given what you want."|
|"You missed the one called the Assimilation Factor. That was careless of you."|
|"But every other identified Anomaly, every Undefined Lifeform we have found, will be given to you to devour. Your list is long."|
And in the empty golden air of the hall, names began to rise!
They wrote themselves in lines of pale fire, one after another, drifting up toward the vaulted ceiling like sparks from a bonfire that would not stop burning.
THE REMNANT SEER.
THE LAST OF HOUSE VESPER.
THE ORCHARD THAT WALKS.
THE INFINITY EATER.
THE CONTINUUM PARADOX.
THE WRITER OF MYTHOS.
ANAXIMANDER.
THE CREATURE...

On and on they climbed, dozens of them, a long burning column of every strange and singular existence that had drawn the notice of Those Who Remain in this cold Age. And at the very top of the list, larger than the rest, brighter than the rest, burning above them all:
NOAH OSMONT.
THE Sealed One rose from his chair and walked out into the empty hall! He lay down in the middle of it, on his back, among the bones.

There were a great many bones. The Gilded had left them behind when their blood came to him, white and scattered across the golden floor, and he lay in them as another being might lie in a field of grass, and looked up at the burning names.
"Do you know," he said, "how unlikely it is that any of them will ever become anything?"
His voice drifted up toward the painted eye, calm and conversational and completely without mercy.

"I have watched anomalies for a very long time. Existence throws them up by the thousand, these strange little one-of-a-kind things, and everyone gets very excited, and then they die. They die in wars. They die in winters. They die of their own cleverness. The chance that any single one of them becomes something that matters is so small it barely deserves the word."

He lifted one pale hand toward the column of fire and let his fingers trail across the names. "So why leave it to chance? Why let them squander it? I can take every one of them into myself. Their lives. Their existences. Everything strange and singular about them, all of it put to use as fuel for something far greater than any of them would ever have become on their own."
He smiled up at the name at the very top.
"They should be grateful, really. It is the only way most of them will ever mean anything at all."
The names burned on above him. THE Sealed One lay in the bones and the gold and looked at them for a long, long time.

"They keep saying three," he said softly. "THE Augury of the Long Night. Three at the turning. It is the one scrap of it any of them could scry through the fog, and they will not stop repeating it. I am tired of the number."
His gold eyes narrowed.
"There will not be three. There will only be one. There will only...be me."
BOOM!

The empty hall shook! The golden pillars trembled on their bases, and the bones across the floor rattled and jumped, and the burning names above flared so bright that for a moment the whole Aurum Crest was lit with pale fire from end to end!
Above him, the vast dark eye of THE SLEEPLESS FIEND watched without blinking.
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND recites words he has only recently come to hold.|
|"And at the turning, count three.|
|One shall look upon all that is, and grieve.|
|One shall take up every weight, and not set it down.|
|One shall no longer remain, and yet remain.|
|By their three hands the cloth is torn, or the cloth is woven anew,|
|and no living soul may say which"|
THE Sealed One went very still among the bones!
Three is a number, and one is a number. For all their scrying, the Immense Ones had only ever held a scrap of THE Augury of the Long Night, a count of three glimpsed through the winter’s fog.
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND observes.|
|"You say there will only be one. The Augury does not disagree with you. It simply declines to promise."|
The eye pulsed, once, slow.
|"Come to the Legacy. A great variety of Gu have been captured for your consumption."|
|"They are all feeding you. Fattening you up. Pouring everything they have into the hope that you are the one who opens the door."|
|"If you do not deliver what they want, boy, oh boy."|
THE Sealed One laughed!

He rose from the floor among the bones, slowly, unhurried, and the last scattered droplets of crimson gold blood on the golden floor lifted and flowed into him as he stood. He straightened his dark coat, and looked up at the eye of THE SLEEPLESS FIEND, and at the burning list of everything he meant to eat, and at the one name that shone above all the others.
"Epochs have passed," THE Sealed One said.
"The same things will rise, and the same things will fall, and the same small bright things will think they are special right up until someone takes them."
His gold eyes shone in the empty hall.
"In every epoch that has passed, and in every epoch still to come, only one will remain supreme. And it...will be me."

chapters.title: Chapter 5794: Myths and Legends!
paragraphs: <THE Writer of Mythos>
The page was white before her, and then it was not as words appeared.
I will die.

She tore it away. Beneath it lay another page, just as white, and she set her pen to it with great care, meaning to write something else entirely. A river, perhaps. A mountain. A girl walking home in the rain. Anything at all.
And yet...
I will die.
She tore that one away too!

The floor around her desk was deep in pages. Hundreds of them, thousands, drifting in soft white banks against the legs of her chair, and every one of them said the same three words in the same neat hand. Her hand. She had not meant to write a single one of them!

She sat at the heart of an Existential Immense Domain, and it was not hers. It was far too grand to be hers. It was a library that had no walls, only shelves, shelves that climbed up past the reach of any sight and went on climbing, carved from a dark and polished wood that had never grown on any tree.

Every shelf was packed with books, and every book was a life, and every life was written in ink. Rivers of that ink ran slow and black through the air between the shelves, curling and settling, never spilling a drop. The whole place smelled of old paper and of rain on stone. There was no ceiling. Far above, where a ceiling should have been, there was only a vast pale sky of blank parchment, and across it, even here, fell the snow.
This was the personal domain of an Immense One. THE MATRIARCH OF INK!
Her mother.
The Writer of Mythos dipped her pen again. The ink came up black and shining. She held it over a fresh page for a long time, and she thought, very hard, of a river in a green valley in spring.
And yet..
I will die.
She set the pen down. Her hand was shaking!

"Since the snow began to fall," she said quietly, to the shelves, to the ink, to the endless pale sky, "this has been the only Mythos of my existence. The only one. Before, I could write anything. A war and its ending. A kingdom and its fall. My own next breath, if I wished, and my Narrative would agree to it. Now my Narrative has only one thing left to say to me, and it will not stop saying it."
She looked down at the banks of white pages drifting around her ankles.
"It tells me I will die. Not in some far Age, not someday. Soon. And no matter what I write, however I try to write around it, this one line is always what comes out of the pen."
Her voice caught, just slightly. "And it tells me who. It will be existence itself that kills me. Not an enemy, not a curse. Existence."
She laughed, and there was no humor in it. "Isn’t that cruel, Mother? That the Mythos I am most certain of is the one I most want to be wrong?"
The ink in the air went very still!
Then the whole domain seemed to lean toward her, as a room leans toward the one who owns it, and the pale sky above rippled like a page being turned.
|THE MATRIARCH OF INK speaks.|
|"Nothing will collapse you. Nothing will take you from me."|
|"If existence itself comes calling, my ink will write it a different ending. I have written endings for things far older than existence’s patience."|
The rivers of ink curled close around the desk, slow and protective.
|"And you are THE Writer of Mythos, are you not? Then write a different ending. Write a Mythos in which, whatever comes, you do not die."|
|"Your next Mythos is your Root of Immensity. Finish it. Once you have, I will take you to THE Legacy of THE Fraternity. I have a few friends there, at least."|
The Writer of Mythos wiped her eyes with the back of her ink-stained hand.
"Why not THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity?"she asked. "The few weavings of Mythos I have ever caught about Legacies all say it is one of the grandest there is. Lucy founded it. THE Acharya."

|"THE Acharya is not the only grand Lifeform ever to rise in existence and found a Legacy,"|said THE MATRIARCH OF INK.|"She was one of the most powerful, certainly. But the grandest Legacy is not always the most fitting one. There are things in THE Legacy of THE Fraternity you can obtain that will suit you far better than anything in hers."|
The ink settled.
|"But put all of that aside for now. Write your Mythos. Write your Root. I will share my Immensity with you freely."|

|"You were born with a Root of Immensity already in you, and you refused it, because you wanted to earn one of your own. You have earned it. You have labored long enough. Now you need only claim what was always yours."|
|"It is time for you to ascend."|
The Writer of Mythos was quiet for a moment.

Then she smiled. It was a glorious smile, bright and sure and a little fierce, the smile of a girl who has been told by the only voice in existence she has never once doubted that she is allowed to win.
She nodded!

There was no fresh page this time. Instead she pinned up her long dark hair with the pen, then drew it free again, turned it in her fingers, and set its nib against her own wrist, against her own skin, against her own existence!
And she began to write!

The ink flowed out of the pen and into her, bright and black and glittering, and the rivers of her mother’s ink rose up all around her in answer, pouring down through the endless shelves toward the little desk at the heart of the Immense Domain. The pale sky rippled from end to end, and the white pages on the floor lifted in a slow spiral around her chair.
Her pen moved, and a Mythos of her own Root began to take shape across her skin.
But somewhere at the very back of her mind, where the pen could not reach, a single line was still waiting. It had not gone anywhere. It simply sat there, patient and certain, in her own neat hand.
I will die.
<THE Creature>
There was nothing where their Observable Existence used to be.

It was not even emptiness, since emptiness was at least a kind of shape. This was undefinition, a vast murky foam of obsidian that went on in every direction, bubbling slowly, with no floor and no sky and no edge, as though existence had been scraped out of this place and nobody had ever bothered to fill it back in.

Once, there had been a home here. A small Observable Existence, the one where he had first opened his eyes, and Osmont was also born here, and Anaximander, and a great many others, all of them sprung from the same unremarkable corner of everything. THE Sealed One had taken it. Now there was only the foam!
THE Creature sat in the middle of it.

The snow fell here too. It fell everywhere now. But here it did something it did nowhere else. It did not settle on him or slide off him. It flowed into him, drifted in through his vast dark shoulders and out through his back, and around him in slow eddies, moving through his body exactly as it moved through the foam, as if there were no difference between the two. As if he were not sitting in this empty place at all, but were simply part of it.
As if he were one with existence!

He was titanic now, even for him as an invisible statue seemed to be fully layered unto him. His figure rose out of the obsidian foam like a mountain range with a man’s shape, wreathed in flames, white and obsidian, burning together and never mixng, the white in the black and the black in the white. And beneath the flames, simmering close against his skin, lay a Provenance that had no color at all. Neither clear nor blank, it was simply the color of existence before anyone had decided what color existence should be.
He raised one enormous hand and looked at it.
"What was established in the future," THE Creature said, "is bleeding into the present."
His voice was flat, unhurried, heavy as always.

"My Provenance of existence in the future is my Provenance of existence now. I brought it here."He turned the hand over, slowly. "But to do so, I crossed many bounds. Did things existence does not do. That...bore a cost."
He lowered his hand to his chest.

There was a crack there! It ran from his collarbone down toward his heart, jagged and faintly glowing, and through it, if anyone had been close enough to look, they would have seen something forming inside him. A Root. A Root of Immensity, and not of any one thing in particular, but of existence itself!

It was beautiful and it was vast and it was fractured, split through along a line that did not close, and every so often it flickered, unsteady, and when it did, the flames around THE Creature flared too high, and something moved across his flat, heavy face that was very nearly anger, or very nearly grief, before it settled again.
He sat with that for a while, in the foam and the snow.
Then, for the sake of stability, he opened his mouth.
"Anaximander," THE Creature said. "Come."
One second later, his oldest friend was standing beside him in the undefinition, with his hands in his sleeves.

He looked exactly as he always had. White scholar’s robes, a little rumpled. Tousled hair. No authority on him at all, none whatsoever, and still the obsidian foam drew back from his feet as though it had remembered a rule it had forgotten. Only his eyes had changed.
They were older than they had been, far older, the eyes of a man who had spent a great deal of time in places where time behaved strangely and come back carrying some of it.
Anaximander smiled at THE Creature.
He did not say anything. He simply stepped closer and laid one hand on the titan’s vast shoulder.
The flames eased! The crack across THE Creature’s chest steadied its flickering glow, and the thing that had been moving across his face grew still.
"Big guy," Anaximander said gently. "Why does it seem that you did something so hasty?"
THE Creature was quiet a moment.
"Existence moves whether the rest of us move or not," he said. "It moved faster than I expected. So I had to catch up."
The white and obsidian flames turned slowly around him. "A Great Ruler cannot hang back while everything moves past him. I did what had to be done. Like existence, I bear what I must."
He looked down at the scholar beside him. "As do you, my friend."
Anaximander said nothing to that. He only kept his hand where it was.
THE Creature regarded him for a long moment, through the drifting snow.
"Existence now, or existence years from now,"he said. "It is still existence. Let me help an old friend. Let me bring your weavings from the future into the present."
Anaximander shook his head, still smiling a little.
"I don’t need anything right now," he said. "I’m good with where I’m at."
THE Creature looked at him.

He looked at his oldest friend in the whole of existence, the one who had come every time he was called, the one who had put a hand on his shoulder in a place where nothing else remained, and something in the vast, flat, heavy face shifted in a way it almost never did.
"I do not wish to be alone, Anaximander,"THE Creature said.
The snow drifted through him.
"Existence is boundlessly lonely. Far too many things exist in it, and still one can feel desolate among all of them."The flames burned low and steady.
"There is much to be done. It would be grand if we could move as we used to. Together."
Anaximander was quiet for a while.
Then he smiled, lightly and he sighed.
"Okay," he said. "I was thinking of relaxing for a bit, but..."
He tipped his head back and looked up at the snow falling out of the endless obsidian dark. "Those with power and the means to use it have a responsibility not to only relax. Alright. Alright."
HUUM!
With that, existence began to swirl!

The obsidian foam churned. The undefinition around them heaved and rolled, and out of the dark overhead, boundless storms of snow came cascading down, thicker than they had fallen anywhere, pouring over the two figures in the place where their home had been.
Anaximander raised a hand to shield his eyes.
THE Creature did not!

The snow poured down on him, and for the first time since he had sat in this place, it did not flow through him. It settled! It gathered on his vast shoulders, heavier and heavier, the weight of a whole Age’s winter piling up on him in the dark.
Anaximander glanced at it, and reached up as if to brush it off.
"Leave it," THE Creature said.
He rose to his feet, slow and titanic, with the whole weight of the falling winter on his shoulders.
And he did not set it down.

chapters.title: Chapter 5795: Sparks and Fear!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
THE First Gu of Time was gone.
The purple sky of the Chrysalis had gone back to being only a sky.

The time-disks spun on through the clouds as though nothing had hapened. The violet smoke drifted. Far off, something enormous and slow turned over in the murk and went back to sleep. And Noah stayed exactly where he was, floating in the middle of it all, because he had just been given a new piece of himself and he wanted to understand it before he took it anywhere else.
THE Osmontian Inscription of THE Dreaming Hour.

He had forged it out of nothing but his own Root, his own Provenance, and the time he had lived through. No Gu at its heart. No borrowed material. It was his in a way nothing he had ever carried had been his, and yet he needed to fully understand what it actually did. The prompts had told him, of course. But prompts were only words. He wanted to feel it.
So he started with THE Lived Hour!
He closed his eyes and turned his attention inward, and waited for a single second to pass.
It passed!

And inside him, far more than a second went by. He felt it happen. His Provenance turned over and settled, turned over and settled, again and again, as though it had been left to work at itself through a long quiet day with nothing to disturb it. His foundations did the same. An entire day’s worth of refinement, worked through in the space of one breath, and then the next second came, and it happened again.
That was all it did. It simply kept happening, every second, without being asked!
Noah opened his eyes and looked at his hands.

He had half expected his attributes to start climbing. That was what progress had always looked like, for most of his rise. More. Bigger numbers, bigger reserves, a bigger shadow thrown across existence. But that was not what THE Lived Hour was doing to him at all.
It was pressing him down!

Every second, every hidden day of refinement packed inside that second, pressed his Provenance a little closer together. Tighter. Denser. The same amount of him, fitted into a smaller and smaller space, as a blacksmith hammers the same iron over and over until the metal that comes out the other side weighs the same and is nothing like what went in.
He looked deeper, down past his foundations, past the Root, down to the very smallest pieces of what he was made of.
His quarks!

Not long ago, in a very different stage of his existence, he had remade every quark of his body one by one into something that carried his own aims. They were still there, all of them, countless as sand. But now, looking at them, he found each one packed. Crammed full!

Dense with his Provenance, blue and gold, pressed into every one of them past anything he would have believed a single quark could hold. And threaded all through that Provenance, cold and clean, was something else.
The Long Night!

The cold was in him. It had been in him since the frozen underworld. But he had always felt it as something he carried. Something he survived. Now, looking down at his own quarks, he saw that the cold had been compressed in alongside his Provenance, layer on layer, until the two had become one substance. Warm and cold. Dream and winter. Neither fighting the other.
As he watched, snow began to surge around him!

The Long Night’s snow reached deeper into this murky corner of the Chrysalis, and it came drifting down through the purple clouds toward him, and sank in! Rivers of it, drawn out of the sky, flowing into his crystalline body and down into the packed quarks, and every flake that sank in was pressed down with everything else, and every flake left him cleaner.

As the snow poured in and the Lived Hour pressed and pressed, he felt more and mofe sublime. One by one, any rough specks were ground out and pushed away, until his whole existence, from the surface of his crystalline skin down to the smallest packed quark, was unblemished!
Then he looked at his Root.

THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin turned at the center of him as it always did, the endless mobius spinning in his chest. But it turned heavier now. Slower, with more behind it. And when he looked at it closely, with everything he had, he could see its two natures more clearly than he had ever seen them.
He had known now that his Root was Dual. Conceptual and Physical at once.

On one side of it, the Conceptual side, he could feel the Dreamer. The part of him that dreamed a thing and watched existence adjust to agree. That was the Collector’s kind of power, the Empyros kind, the power of a being who could write something true and make existence live inside the sentence.
One day, if he lived long enough, that part of his Root would make him an Empyros Immense Lifeform, able to rewrite whatever he looked at.

And on the other side, the Physical side, he could feel the weight of his Dreams and infinity and everything else. The packed quarks. The cold compressed into his body until his body had become harder than any material in existence. That was Lucy’s kind of power. THE Infiniverse’s kind. The Fiend kind, a being simply heavier than the rules!
One day, that part of his Root would make him a Fiend Immense Lifeform, so dense and so real that no sentence anyone wrote could hold him.
Both at once!

He had watched the Collector write a perfect sentence on a mountain and break against it. He had watched THE Infiniverse fill a paradox with so much existence it had nowhere left to hide. One of them had been the writer. The other had been the page.
He was going to be both!

Noah smiled quietly, alone in the purple sky. What a ridiculous thing to be. A writer who was also the page, a dreamer who was also the weight. Was there anything in existence that could argue with that?
He did not know.
Then he looked up, and stopped smiling!

He had been floating in this same place for a long while now, testing and feeling and turning his power over, without moving at all. No attack, no dream sent outward, no reaching for anything around him. Only himself, sitting still, letting the Lived Hour work.
And everything around him had begun to dream!

The time-disks nearest him had slowed. Their violet edges had gone soft and blurred, like a thing half remembered. The purple clouds had drifted into strange shapes, towers and faces and wide calm seas that had never been clouds before, shapes that came from nowhere any cloud could have learned them. The violet smoke of old time curled into slow spirals, turning over and over like a sleeper shifting in a warm bed. Even the Dimensions far off in the murk twinkled in a new rhythm, slow and even, like breath.
And drifting close by, not ten paces from him, was a Gu!

A small one. Common, pale and new, the sort he would once have reached out and taken without a second thought. It floated in the purple air with its thin wings drawn in, perfectly still, and it was not afraid of him. It was asleep! Curled up in the dream that was spreading out of him through this whole region of the Chrysalis, and whatever it was dreaming about, it looked content.

THE First Gu of Time was gone.
The purple sky of the Chrysalis had gone back to being only a sky.
The time-disks spun on through the clouds as though nothing had hapened.
The violet smoke drifted.
Far off, something enormous and slow turned over in the murk and went back to sleep.
And Noah stayed exactly where he was, floating in the middle of it all, because he had just been given a new piece of himself and he wanted to understand it before he took it anywhere else.
THE Osmontian Inscription of THE Dreaming Hour.
He had forged it out of nothing but his own Root, his own Provenance, and the time he had lived through.
No Gu at its heart.
No borrowed material.
It was his in a way nothing he had ever carried had been his, and yet he needed to fully understand what it actually did.
The prompts had told him, of course.

He closed his eyes and turned his attention inward, and waited for a single second to pass.
It passed!

He felt it happen.
His Provenance turned over and settled, turned over and settled, again and again, as though it had been left to work at itself through a long quiet day with nothing to disturb it.
His foundations did the same.
An entire day’s worth of refinement, worked through in the space of one breath, and then the next second came, and it happened again.
That was all it did.
It simply kept happening, every second, without being asked!
Noah opened his eyes and looked at his hands.
He had half expected his attributes to start climbing.
That was what progress had always looked like, for most of his rise.
More.
Bigger numbers, bigger reserves, a bigger shadow thrown across existence.
But that was not what THE Lived Hour was doing to him at all.
It was pressing him down!
Every second, every hidden day of refinement packed inside that second, pressed his Provenance a little closer together.
Tighter.
Denser.

The same amount of him, fitted into a smaller and smaller space, as a blacksmith hammers the same iron over and over until the metal that comes out the other side weighs the same and is nothing like what went in.
He looked deeper, down past his foundations, past the Root, down to the very smallest pieces of what he was made of.
His quarks!
Not long ago, in a very different stage of his existence, he had remade every quark of his body one by one into something that carried his own aims.
They were still there, all of them, countless as sand.
But now, looking at them, he found each one packed.
Crammed full!
Dense with his Provenance, blue and gold, pressed into every one of them past anything he would have believed a single quark could hold.
And threaded all through that Provenance, cold and clean, was something else.
The Long Night!
The cold was in him.
It had been in him since the frozen underworld.
But he had always felt it as something he carried.
Something he survived.
Now, looking down at his own quarks, he saw that the cold had been compressed in alongside his Provenance, layer on layer, until the two had become one substance.
Warm and cold.
Dream and winter.
Neither fighting the other.
As he watched, snow began to surge around him!
The Long Night’s snow reached deeper into this murky corner of the Chrysalis, and it came drifting down through the purple clouds toward him, and sank in!

Rivers of it, drawn out of the sky, flowing into his crystalline body and down into the packed quarks, and every flake that sank in was pressed down with everything else, and every flake left him cleaner.
As the snow poured in and the Lived Hour pressed and pressed, he felt more and mofe sublime.
One by one, any rough specks were ground out and pushed away, until his whole existence, from the surface of his crystalline skin down to the smallest packed quark, was unblemished!
Then he looked at his Root.
THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin turned at the center of him as it always did, the endless mobius spinning in his chest.
But it turned heavier now.
Slower, with more behind it.
And when he looked at it closely, with everything he had, he could see its two natures more clearly than he had ever seen them.
He had known now that his Root was Dual.
Conceptual and Physical at once.
On one side of it, the Conceptual side, he could feel the Dreamer.
The part of him that dreamed a thing and watched existence adjust to agree.
That was the Collector’s kind of power, the Empyros kind, the power of a being who could write something true and make existence live inside the sentence.
One day, if he lived long enough, that part of his Root would make him an Empyros Immense Lifeform, able to rewrite whatever he looked at.
And on the other side, the Physical side, he could feel the weight of his Dreams and infinity and everything else.
The packed quarks.
The cold compressed into his body until his body had become harder than any material in existence.
That was Lucy’s kind of power.
THE Infiniverse’s kind.
The Fiend kind, a being simply heavier than the rules!
One day, that part of his Root would make him a Fiend Immense Lifeform, so dense and so real that no sentence anyone wrote could hold him.
Both at once!
He had watched the Collector write a perfect sentence on a mountain and break against it.
He had watched THE Infiniverse fill a paradox with so much existence it had nowhere left to hide.
One of them had been the writer.
The other had been the page.
He was going to be both!
Noah smiled quietly, alone in the purple sky.
What a ridiculous thing to be.
A writer who was also the page, a dreamer who was also the weight.
Was there anything in existence that could argue with that?
He did not know.
Then he looked up, and stopped smiling!
He had been floating in this same place for a long while now, testing and feeling and turning his power over, without moving at all.
No attack, no dream sent outward, no reaching for anything around him.
Only himself, sitting still, letting the Lived Hour work.
And everything around him had begun to dream!
The time-disks nearest him had slowed.
Their violet edges had gone soft and blurred, like a thing half remembered.
The purple clouds had drifted into strange shapes, towers and faces and wide calm seas that had never been clouds before, shapes that came from nowhere any cloud could have learned them.
The violet smoke of old time curled into slow spirals, turning over and over like a sleeper shifting in a warm bed.
Even the Dimensions far off in the murk twinkled in a new rhythm, slow and even, like breath.

A small one.
