chapters.title: Chapter 5796: The Convocation of Roots! I
paragraphs: In THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity.
The Existential Conduit beneath Noah’s feet was warm, and it was moving rapidly.

It did not look like a road. It looked like what it was, a vast pillar of flowing authority bent over on its side, pale gold and faintly humming, a river of existence’s own veins laid out through the snowy air of the Legacy.

But it was as firm underfoot as any paved street, and it carried whoever stood on it along its length like a current carrying a leaf, smooth and quiet and sure. Those who knew the Legacy called them the Keepers’ Roads.
Every mountain was joined to every other by them, a web of glowing pathways running through the falling snow between the peaks, and all of them, today, seemed to be running in the same direction.
Verys stood a pace ahead of him on the Conduit, hands clasped behind his back, cloak pulled close against the cold.
Noah looked around.

He was not the only one being carried. Far off across the snowy gulfs, on other Conduits, other small figures stood in pairs. A Legacy Keeper at the front of each, dressed in black and fur the same as Verys, and behind each Keeper, a being.

Some of them were small at this distance. Some of them were not small at all. A great winged shape rode one Conduit in the far east, its wings drawn tight against the snow. A figure made of what looked like slow-burning coal stood on another. Every one of them was fairly powerful, and every one of them was heading the same way.
Ahead of them all rose a mountain!

It was larger than any Elsedimension Mountain Noah had seen in the Legacy, by a long way. It dwarfed the peaks around it as a grown man dwarfs children, broad at its base and climbing, climbing, into the grey of the snowing sky until its summit was lost in cloud.
Snow blanketed it from root to peak, the same as everything else. But even beneath the snow, it seemed to glow faintly, as though something inside it had never quite finished being bright.
"The Elsedimension Mountain everyone is gathering on," Verys said without turning, "is called THE Firmament Mountain."
"Mmm," Noah nodddd.
"It is the oldest mountain in the Legacy, Sir. The first one THE Acharya ever raised." The Keeper’s voice took on the careful tone of a man reciting something he had been taught young.

"Legend says that on this mountain, THE Acharya of Immensity was ambushed by ten other Immense Ones at once. And legend says that she pressed down a single finger, only one, and crushed the whole of their collective Immensity beneath it, and painted the mountain in their blood."
HUUM!
Noah looked at the distant snowy peak.
"Legend says,"Verys went on, mildly. "But who knows what really happened, Sir."
Ten Immense Ones. One finger!
Noah had watched a single frost-visage of Lucy break THE UNPAID COLLECTOR with one blow. He was not inclined to call the legend an exaggeration.

The Conduit carried them on through the snow, and as the Firmament drew nearer, Noah began to count. A few more pairs converging from the north. A cluster from the west, three Keepers leading three beings in a line.

Others from below, rising up out of the purple-gold rivers on Conduits that climbed like stairways. Ten. Twenty. Thirty. Dozens of them, all beings with Roots of Immensity, all converging on the one great mountain from every direction at once!
He kept himself very reserved.

That had been decided before they left the Glacial Mountain. His Provenance he drew in tight, close against his crystalline skin, and held it there. His Infinity he pulled down into the packed depths of himself where nothing outside could feel it. And he stilled his dreams, so that the snow around him fell only as snow and the Conduit beneath him stayed only a Conduit, and nothing near him, not one flake, began to dream.
He wanted to look first. To see how deep this Legacy really ran before anyone looked back at him.
THE Firmament Mountain did had a plain flat surface for a peak.

The Conduits carried everyone up its sides in long glowing spirals, past slopes of blue-white snow and old carved stone half buried beneath it, past great weathered statues of figures Noah did not recognise, standing with their hands raised as though they were holding up the sky.
And at the very top, the mountain simply stopped climbing and opened out, flat and broad and perfectly level, a vast white plain as wide as a small country, open to the snowing sky on every side.
Verys called itTHE Plain of Accord.
Everyone who arrived stepped off their Conduits onto the edge of it, and Noah stepped off with them, and looked around.
He did it carefully, the thinnest touch of his Dreamer’s sight, reading only what was offered on the surface. It was enough.

A woman made of what looked like deep water stood a little way off, her whole body clear and blue and faintly rippling, small fish of light swimming slowly through her chest. She read at around six hundred in most attributes.
A tall thin man beside her wore a robe that was not cloth but written text, lines of shifting script running down from his shoulders to his feet, and he read nearer seven hundred.

Further along, a being with the head of a stag and a crown of antlers hung with small bells stood very still, and every bell rang softly whenever he breathed, and Noah read him at nearly eight hundred in attributes!
Five hundred. Six hundred. Seven. The very strongest near eight hundred!

And almost every one of them had their own Provenance! Most of them were self-made, or Progeny with Provenance of their own grown on top of what they had inherited. Ethereal things. Otherworldly things, every one of them looking as though they had stepped out of some older and stranger Chapter of existence to stand here in the snow.
And yet...

Noah looked at the stag-headed one again, the one at nearly eight hundred Provenance Essence, and waited to feel it. The pressure. The weight a being that far above him on paper should have pushed against his existence just by standing nearby.
It did not come!

His existence felt nothing. No oppression at all. The stag-headed being stood there shining with eight hundred Provenance Essence, and Noah, at a number lower than that, simply looked at him and felt entirely at ease.

Was that the compression? Was his foundation really so dense now, every point of him packed so tight by the Lived Hour and the death of time, that a being with more on paper simply could not press on him? He did not know. Nothing could be assumed yet!
Everyone flowed toward the center of the plain, and Noah flowed with them.
Above the center, the thrones hunng.

They floated in the snowing sky in a great ring, dozens of them, high above the plain, each one carved from something different. There was one of black glass, and one that was a single colossal bone, and one made of living wood still in leaf, and one that seemed to be a hollowed star. Every one of them was empty.
Except one!

Poona sat on hers grandly, a throne of pale gold like the curve of a great eye, her legs crossed, her chin on her hand. Her eyes were bright. And when Noah looked up, those bright eyes found him at once and lit up, and she waved at him, openly and cheerfully, from her throne above the gathering of Roots.
Noah waved back.
Several of the beings around him looked from Poona to Noah with open curiosity. He paid them no mind.

Verys led him on across the snow, to where a ring of golden clouds hung a little above the plain, drifting slow and soft and bright. There were dozens of them, arranged in a wide circle beneath the thrones, and each one had a name written across its side in flowing golden script. Verys stopped before one.
It said Osmont!
"If Sir will take your position," the Keeper said, "things will begin soon."
He bowed.
"I wish you luck, Sir."
Noah rose and sat on the golden cloud. It was softer than it looked and warmer than the snow, and it held him easily. He looked to either side.

Dozens of other golden clouds stretched away around the ring, each with its own name, most still empty. And nearest to him, close enough to speak without raising his voice, was one that read Adrastia.
It was empty!

Noah looked at the name for a moment. He wondered how far that monster of assimilation had come in a single day, with his brand-new Root and his river of time and the woman who lifted him by the scruff of his neck.
He waited.
And while he waited, something locked onto him!
It came from far across the plain, a stifling pressure that closed around his existence and held, heavy, focused, aimed entirely at him.

For one moment he thought an Immense One had turned its eyes his way. But it was not that. It was not quite that heavy. Close, very close, closer than anything he had felt from a being that was not Immense. But not quite.
Noah turned his head to the right.

A figure had just arrived at the edge of the plain, stepping off the last Conduit, and her eyes were already on him. Piercing eyes, green and burning, and around her, existence itself seemed to be suffocating, the ground shimmering at her feet as though it were not sure it wanted to stay solid under her.

She wore a long green robe, heavy and fine, trailing through the snow behind her. On her head sat a crown of verdant leaves and thorns, and it hung there lazily, tipped a little to one side, as if she had put it on in a hurry and never bothered to straighten it.
Noah’s sight opened her.
|MINERVA.|
|VERITAS: 999. PROVENANCE: 999. POTENTIA: 999. PONDUS: 999.|
|ROOT OF IMMENSITY: ???|
The snow falling all around the plain whipped suddenly heavier!
Noah raised his brows.
Nine hundred and ninety-nine in everything. And a Root he could not read at all. He had not done anything yet. So why did it feel as though he had already been marked as a target?
Minerva looked at him a moment longer, her green eyes steady and unreadable.
Then she turned away, as though he were no longer interesting, and walked to her own golden cloud on the far side of the ring, and sat.
The golden clouds filled!

One after another, Legacy Keepers led their charges across the snow and bowed them onto their places, and the ring of clouds under the empty thrones began to fill with terrifying figures. The water-woman. The man robed in text. The stag with the ringing bells. A towering figure in forge-dark armor who sat heavily on a cloud marked Dravos.
A pale smiling youth with a restless mouth on one marked Batiatus, already talking to his neighbor. Dozens more, each stranger than the last, each with a Keeper standing a pace behind their cloud.
And as they filled, Noah sensed that Minerva was not alone at her height.
There were others. A few of them, scattered around the ring. One sat so still in a cloak of grey mist that the mist did not move even in the wind.
Another hummed a low tune that made the snow around her fall in slow spirals. They were close to Minerva’s level, some of them. Perhaps one or two were at it.
Existence was vast, truly. Every single being on this plain carried a Root of Immensity, and every one of them had a Keeper of their own, and there were still more of them arriving!
Many of them talked freely, clearly old acquaintances, laughing and arguing across the gaps between their clouds. Others, like Noah, sat silently and watched.
Then, on the cloud beside him, someone sat down.

Noah turned his head. Achilles Adrastia had arrived, his young king’s face calm, his ancient eyes solemn and new at the same time. He sat on the cloud marked Adrastia and looked over at Noah, and nodded once, gravely.

Behind his cloud, two women stood side by side. Tatiana, red-haired and gorgeous in her Keeper’s black, smiling very grandly at nothing in particular. And Rose, standing exactly one pace closer to Achilles than Tatiana was, with her arms crossed and her face perfectly pleasant.
Achilles looked away from Noah and around at the whole gathering, at the thrones and the clouds and the terrifying figures and the Keepers, and his eyes widened slightly.
There was a great deal to see. The entire plain seemed packed with power, with existences, with Roots.
The last golden cloud filled at this time.
And the sky cried out!

It happened seconds later. Above the ring of thrones, the grey snowing sky split open, not in one place but in many, one after another all around the great circle, and through every opening an aura bloomed!
Auras of Immense Ones!
They came down onto the floating thrones one by one, and their very existence announced each of them as they came!
|THE DIMENSIONAL DEVOURER, POONA, already seated, raises a hand in greeting to the others.|
|THE ASHEN CANTOR descends upon the throne of black glass. Embers drift from its shoulders and sing as they fall.|
|THE HOLLOW CHOIR takes the throne of bone.|
|THE DISSECTING SCHOLAR settles onto a throne of polished instruments, adjusts his spectacles, and looks over the Roots below with open academic delight.|
|THE VERDANT REGARD takes the living throne in leaf. A green gaze, soft as early spring, settles upon one golden cloud below and stays there.|
|THE SALT-CROWNED MATRON takes the hollowed star. The snow around her throne turns to brine and falls as rain.|
|THE LANTERN OF THE LAST SHORE descends. Its light is warm. Its throne is empty of anything but that light.|
|THE KEEPER OF THE UNBROKEN VOW arrives, and says nothing, and has never needed to.|
And more still, throne after throne filling, until dozens of the floating seats were occupied!
Noah’s eyes shone brilliantly!
Some of the Immense Ones he could see clearly, vast and terrible and perfectly visible on their thrones. A titan of ember and ash!
A great soft shape of green light. Moriarty with his tentacles and his spectacles, beaming!

But others were only haze. Their Dimensionality was simply too deep, and they let it express itself freely, so that when Noah looked at their thrones he saw only a blur of light and weight and presence, a shape his sight could not hold together no matter how hard it tried.
Power!

This was power! His whole existence buzzed with it. A few dozen Immense Ones, gathered in one ring above one mountain, each one of them a blinding sun. Was this all of them? Or was this only a glimpse of how deep the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity truly ran?
Below the thrones, all around the ring, the beings on the golden clouds began to rise.

They did it together, without anyone telling them to. The stag stood with his bells ringing softly. The water-woman rose. Minerva stood, unhurried, crown still tilted. Even Achilles rose from his cloud, straight-backed, eyes lifted to the ring of suns above.
Noah was the last!
He stood, slowly, and looked up at the thrones. Every one of them seemed to blaze like a sun in the snowing sky.
Standing was no issue. He could respect their power! They had come very, very far to sit where they sat, further than he had come yet.
But he looked up at those floating thrones, at the beings on them shining through the snow, and he could not help wondering.
How long would he stand down here on a cloud, instead of sitting up there on a throne?
Only time would tell!

sentences.text: In THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity.
The Existential Conduit beneath Noah’s feet was warm, and it was moving rapidly.
It did not look like a road.
It looked like what it was, a vast pillar of flowing authority bent over on its side, pale gold and faintly humming, a river of existence’s own veins laid out through the snowy air of the Legacy.
But it was as firm underfoot as any paved street, and it carried whoever stood on it along its length like a current carrying a leaf, smooth and quiet and sure.
Those who knew the Legacy called them the Keepers’ Roads.
Every mountain was joined to every other by them, a web of glowing pathways running through the falling snow between the peaks, and all of them, today, seemed to be running in the same direction.
Verys stood a pace ahead of him on the Conduit, hands clasped behind his back, cloak pulled close against the cold.
Noah looked around.
He was not the only one being carried.
Far off across the snowy gulfs, on other Conduits, other small figures stood in pairs.
A Legacy Keeper at the front of each, dressed in black and fur the same as Verys, and behind each Keeper, a being.
Some of them were small at this distance.
Some of them were not small at all.
A great winged shape rode one Conduit in the far east, its wings drawn tight against the snow.
A figure made of what looked like slow-burning coal stood on another.
Every one of them was fairly powerful, and every one of them was heading the same way.
Ahead of them all rose a mountain!
It was larger than any Elsedimension Mountain Noah had seen in the Legacy, by a long way.
It dwarfed the peaks around it as a grown man dwarfs children, broad at its base and climbing, climbing, into the grey of the snowing sky until its summit was lost in cloud.
Snow blanketed it from root to peak, the same as everything else.
But even beneath the snow, it seemed to glow faintly, as though something inside it had never quite finished being bright.
"The Elsedimension Mountain everyone is gathering on," Verys said without turning, "is called THE Firmament Mountain."
"Mmm," Noah nodddd.
"It is the oldest mountain in the Legacy, Sir.
The first one THE Acharya ever raised." The Keeper’s voice took on the careful tone of a man reciting something he had been taught young.
"Legend says that on this mountain, THE Acharya of Immensity was ambushed by ten other Immense Ones at once.
And legend says that she pressed down a single finger, only one, and crushed the whole of their collective Immensity beneath it, and painted the mountain in their blood."
HUUM!
Noah looked at the distant snowy peak.
"Legend says,"Verys went on, mildly.
"But who knows what really happened, Sir."
Ten Immense Ones.
One finger!
Noah had watched a single frost-visage of Lucy break THE UNPAID COLLECTOR with one blow.
He was not inclined to call the legend an exaggeration.
The Conduit carried them on through the snow, and as the Firmament drew nearer, Noah began to count.
A few more pairs converging from the north.
A cluster from the west, three Keepers leading three beings in a line.
Others from below, rising up out of the purple-gold rivers on Conduits that climbed like stairways.
Ten.
Twenty.
Thirty.
Dozens of them, all beings with Roots of Immensity, all converging on the one great mountain from every direction at once!
He kept himself very reserved.
That had been decided before they left the Glacial Mountain.
His Provenance he drew in tight, close against his crystalline skin, and held it there.
His Infinity he pulled down into the packed depths of himself where nothing outside could feel it.
And he stilled his dreams, so that the snow around him fell only as snow and the Conduit beneath him stayed only a Conduit, and nothing near him, not one flake, began to dream.
He wanted to look first.
To see how deep this Legacy really ran before anyone looked back at him.
THE Firmament Mountain did had a plain flat surface for a peak.

The Conduits carried everyone up its sides in long glowing spirals, past slopes of blue-white snow and old carved stone half buried beneath it, past great weathered statues of figures Noah did not recognise, standing with their hands raised as though they were holding up the sky.
And at the very top, the mountain simply stopped climbing and opened out, flat and broad and perfectly level, a vast white plain as wide as a small country, open to the snowing sky on every side.
Verys called itTHE Plain of Accord.
Everyone who arrived stepped off their Conduits onto the edge of it, and Noah stepped off with them, and looked around.
He did it carefully, the thinnest touch of his Dreamer’s sight, reading only what was offered on the surface.
It was enough.
A woman made of what looked like deep water stood a little way off, her whole body clear and blue and faintly rippling, small fish of light swimming slowly through her chest.
She read at around six hundred in most attributes.
A tall thin man beside her wore a robe that was not cloth but written text, lines of shifting script running down from his shoulders to his feet, and he read nearer seven hundred.

Further along, a being with the head of a stag and a crown of antlers hung with small bells stood very still, and every bell rang softly whenever he breathed, and Noah read him at nearly eight hundred in attributes!
Five hundred.
Six hundred.
Seven.
The very strongest near eight hundred!
And almost every one of them had their own Provenance!
Most of them were self-made, or Progeny with Provenance of their own grown on top of what they had inherited.
Ethereal things.
Otherworldly things, every one of them looking as though they had stepped out of some older and stranger Chapter of existence to stand here in the snow.
And yet...
Noah looked at the stag-headed one again, the one at nearly eight hundred Provenance Essence, and waited to feel it.
The pressure.
The weight a being that far above him on paper should have pushed against his existence just by standing nearby.
It did not come!
His existence felt nothing.
No oppression at all.
The stag-headed being stood there shining with eight hundred Provenance Essence, and Noah, at a number lower than that, simply looked at him and felt entirely at ease.
Was that the compression?
Was his foundation really so dense now, every point of him packed so tight by the Lived Hour and the death of time, that a being with more on paper simply could not press on him?
He did not know.
Nothing could be assumed yet!
Everyone flowed toward the center of the plain, and Noah flowed with them.
Above the center, the thrones hunng.
They floated in the snowing sky in a great ring, dozens of them, high above the plain, each one carved from something different.
There was one of black glass, and one that was a single colossal bone, and one made of living wood still in leaf, and one that seemed to be a hollowed star.
Every one of them was empty.
Except one!
Poona sat on hers grandly, a throne of pale gold like the curve of a great eye, her legs crossed, her chin on her hand.
Her eyes were bright.
And when Noah looked up, those bright eyes found him at once and lit up, and she waved at him, openly and cheerfully, from her throne above the gathering of Roots.
Noah waved back.
Several of the beings around him looked from Poona to Noah with open curiosity.
He paid them no mind.
Verys led him on across the snow, to where a ring of golden clouds hung a little above the plain, drifting slow and soft and bright.
There were dozens of them, arranged in a wide circle beneath the thrones, and each one had a name written across its side in flowing golden script.
Verys stopped before one.
It said Osmont!
"If Sir will take your position," the Keeper said, "things will begin soon."
He bowed.
"I wish you luck, Sir."
Noah rose and sat on the golden cloud.
It was softer than it looked and warmer than the snow, and it held him easily.
He looked to either side.
Dozens of other golden clouds stretched away around the ring, each with its own name, most still empty.
And nearest to him, close enough to speak without raising his voice, was one that read Adrastia.
It was empty!
Noah looked at the name for a moment.
He wondered how far that monster of assimilation had come in a single day, with his brand-new Root and his river of time and the woman who lifted him by the scruff of his neck.
He waited.
And while he waited, something locked onto him!
It came from far across the plain, a stifling pressure that closed around his existence and held, heavy, focused, aimed entirely at him.
For one moment he thought an Immense One had turned its eyes his way.
But it was not that.
It was not quite that heavy.
Close, very close, closer than anything he had felt from a being that was not Immense.
But not quite.
Noah turned his head to the right.
A figure had just arrived at the edge of the plain, stepping off the last Conduit, and her eyes were already on him.
Piercing eyes, green and burning, and around her, existence itself seemed to be suffocating, the ground shimmering at her feet as though it were not sure it wanted to stay solid under her.
She wore a long green robe, heavy and fine, trailing through the snow behind her.
On her head sat a crown of verdant leaves and thorns, and it hung there lazily, tipped a little to one side, as if she had put it on in a hurry and never bothered to straighten it.
Noah’s sight opened her.
|MINERVA.|
|VERITAS: 999.
PROVENANCE: 999.
POTENTIA: 999.
PONDUS: 999.|
|ROOT OF IMMENSITY: ???|
The snow falling all around the plain whipped suddenly heavier!
Noah raised his brows.
Nine hundred and ninety-nine in everything.
And a Root he could not read at all.
He had not done anything yet.
So why did it feel as though he had already been marked as a target?
Minerva looked at him a moment longer, her green eyes steady and unreadable.
Then she turned away, as though he were no longer interesting, and walked to her own golden cloud on the far side of the ring, and sat.
The golden clouds filled!
One after another, Legacy Keepers led their charges across the snow and bowed them onto their places, and the ring of clouds under the empty thrones began to fill with terrifying figures.
The water-woman.
The man robed in text.
The stag with the ringing bells.
A towering figure in forge-dark armor who sat heavily on a cloud marked Dravos.
A pale smiling youth with a restless mouth on one marked Batiatus, already talking to his neighbor.
Dozens more, each stranger than the last, each with a Keeper standing a pace behind their cloud.
And as they filled, Noah sensed that Minerva was not alone at her height.
There were others.
A few of them, scattered around the ring.
One sat so still in a cloak of grey mist that the mist did not move even in the wind.
Another hummed a low tune that made the snow around her fall in slow spirals.
They were close to Minerva’s level, some of them.
Perhaps one or two were at it.
Existence was vast, truly.
Every single being on this plain carried a Root of Immensity, and every one of them had a Keeper of their own, and there were still more of them arriving!
Many of them talked freely, clearly old acquaintances, laughing and arguing across the gaps between their clouds.
Others, like Noah, sat silently and watched.
Then, on the cloud beside him, someone sat down.
Noah turned his head.
Achilles Adrastia had arrived, his young king’s face calm, his ancient eyes solemn and new at the same time.
He sat on the cloud marked Adrastia and looked over at Noah, and nodded once, gravely.
Behind his cloud, two women stood side by side.
Tatiana, red-haired and gorgeous in her Keeper’s black, smiling very grandly at nothing in particular.
And Rose, standing exactly one pace closer to Achilles than Tatiana was, with her arms crossed and her face perfectly pleasant.
Achilles looked away from Noah and around at the whole gathering, at the thrones and the clouds and the terrifying figures and the Keepers, and his eyes widened slightly.
There was a great deal to see.
The entire plain seemed packed with power, with existences, with Roots.
The last golden cloud filled at this time.
And the sky cried out!
It happened seconds later.
Above the ring of thrones, the grey snowing sky split open, not in one place but in many, one after another all around the great circle, and through every opening an aura bloomed!
Auras of Immense Ones!
They came down onto the floating thrones one by one, and their very existence announced each of them as they came!
|THE DIMENSIONAL DEVOURER, POONA, already seated, raises a hand in greeting to the others.|
|THE ASHEN CANTOR descends upon the throne of black glass.
Embers drift from its shoulders and sing as they fall.|
|THE HOLLOW CHOIR takes the throne of bone.|
|THE DISSECTING SCHOLAR settles onto a throne of polished instruments, adjusts his spectacles, and looks over the Roots below with open academic delight.|
|THE VERDANT REGARD takes the living throne in leaf.
A green gaze, soft as early spring, settles upon one golden cloud below and stays there.|
|THE SALT-CROWNED MATRON takes the hollowed star.
The snow around her throne turns to brine and falls as rain.|
|THE LANTERN OF THE LAST SHORE descends.
Its light is warm.
Its throne is empty of anything but that light.|
|THE KEEPER OF THE UNBROKEN VOW arrives, and says nothing, and has never needed to.|
And more still, throne after throne filling, until dozens of the floating seats were occupied!
Noah’s eyes shone brilliantly!
Some of the Immense Ones he could see clearly, vast and terrible and perfectly visible on their thrones.
A titan of ember and ash!
A great soft shape of green light.
Moriarty with his tentacles and his spectacles, beaming!
But others were only haze.

Their Dimensionality was simply too deep, and they let it express itself freely, so that when Noah looked at their thrones he saw only a blur of light and weight and presence, a shape his sight could not hold together no matter how hard it tried.
Power!
This was power!
His whole existence buzzed with it.
A few dozen Immense Ones, gathered in one ring above one mountain, each one of them a blinding sun.
Was this all of them?
Or was this only a glimpse of how deep the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity truly ran?
Below the thrones, all around the ring, the beings on the golden clouds began to rise.
They did it together, without anyone telling them to.
The stag stood with his bells ringing softly.
The water-woman rose.
Minerva stood, unhurried, crown still tilted.
Even Achilles rose from his cloud, straight-backed, eyes lifted to the ring of suns above.
Noah was the last!
He stood, slowly, and looked up at the thrones.
Every one of them seemed to blaze like a sun in the snowing sky.
Standing was no issue.
He could respect their power!
They had come very, very far to sit where they sat, further than he had come yet.
But he looked up at those floating thrones, at the beings on them shining through the snow, and he could not help wondering.
How long would he stand down here on a cloud, instead of sitting up there on a throne?
Only time would tell!

chapters.title: Chapter 5797: The Convocation of Roots! II
paragraphs: They all stood grandly and the thrones settled, and for a long moment nothing on THE Firmament Mountain moved but the snow.

It fell over the Plain of Accord, over the ring of golden clouds and the strange figures standing on them, over the Keepers waiting a pace behind each cloud. It drifted up toward the floating thrones of black glass and colossal bone and living leaf, and on the Immense Ones seated there it simply vanished, like flakes landing on hot stone.
Then Sir Moriarty rose!

He rose from his throne of polished instruments without any ceremony at all, eight tentacles uncurling, small neat spectacles glinting, and yet the whole plain turned toward him at once, every Root Bearer and every Keeper, as though he had rung a bell.

"Welcome," Moriarty said. It carried to every corner of the plain without seeming to try. "Welcome to THE Convocation of Roots. ARoot that never meets another Root grows crooked, and one that never tests itself grows soft. So we gather you here, on the oldest mountain in the Legacy, and let you find out what you are. The rules are few."

A tentacle lifted. "First, no one dies. A bout ends when one of you yields, is carried from the Plain, or a Keeper steps between you. Do not argue with your Keepers when they do. Several are considerably older than they look."
Behind Noah’s cloud, Verys did not blink!

"Second, there is no order of bouts. There is only the Challenge. Step into the center and name who you wish to face. The one named may refuse, once, in the whole of the Convocation. A refusal is remembered. The Legacy has a very long memory."
One refusal. Spend it, and everyone watching would know exactly who had made you flinch! Noah thought of this and set it aside. He did not intend to flinch from anyone here.

"Third, and the one most of you came for. Favors. Any Immense One seated here may grant a Favor to whoever impresses them. A sliver of their Immensity. A lesson. A Relic from their keeping. A door opened that you could not open yourself."His spectacles glinted.
Above him, the thrones stirred!
|THE ASHEN CANTOR shifts on its throne of black glass. Embers fall from its shoulders. It appears bored.|
|THE HOLLOW CHOIR murmurs in a thousand low voices. It is taking bets. It will not say on what.|
|THE SALT-CROWNED MATRON has already chosen three favorites and intends to be proven right.|
|THE DIMENSIONAL DEVOURER, POONA, is very excited, and would like everyone to know it.|
Noah almost laughed. He sat very still on his golden cloud instead, and turned the rules over one by one.

A tournament, then, where the audience were the titans of the Legacy and the prize was their attention. Winning was worth pride and standing. But a Favor was worth more than every win on this plain put together.
Okay!
He kept his Provenance drawn tight and his dreams still. First he wanted to see how the others fought. Information first.
"Then let us begin," Moriarty said. "Who steps first onto the Plain?"
The cloud marked Dravos sagged as the figure on it stood.

He was huge! Dark armor covered him from throat to heel, scorched and dented and glowing dull red along evry seam, as though the fire inside had never gone out. He stepped down onto the plain, and the ground beneath the snow dented into a shallow crater under a single step.
A Physical Root, Progeny of THE Ashen Cantor, built to be heavier than anything in his way!
On the throne of black glass, the embers stopped falling for a moment.
Dravos walked toward the center, each step a slow crater, and the whole ring of clouds watched him go. He clearly meant to go first, and felt no need to wait for anyone’s opinion on it.
Yet at this time...
"Wait, wait, wait!"
Every head on the plain turned!

Someone was running up the last Conduit, actually running, feet flying along the glowing path with no Keeper in front of her! She came over the edge in a spray of snow, skidded to a stop with a hand on her knee, and grinned around at everyone.
She wore a silk dress of deep blue embroidered all over with gold, high collar closed at the throat, slits cut high up both sides so nothing would ever get in the way of her moving.
Her black hair was wound into two tight spiraled buns tied with white ribbons, half loose from the run.
And her legs!
They were the first thing anyone noticed and the last thing anyone would forget.

Thick, powerful thighs heavy with muscle, the thighs of someone who had spent her whole existence kicking things that did not want to be kicked, and calves drawn tight as strung bows beneath them, bare but for white wrap-bands at the ankles and soft cloth shoes!
Every shift of her weight moved them with a coiled, springing ease that promised a great deal of violence.
She was thick!
Her face was round and cheerful, eyes crinkling at the corners with a smile Noah suspected never left.
She bowed to the thrones, too fast and almost slipped on the snow.
Noah’s sight opened her.
|SHEN HUALING(LING).|
|VERITAS: 1. PROVENANCE: 1. POTENTIA: 1. PONDUS: 1.|
|ROOT OF IMMENSITY: ???|
Noah’s smile faded.
One in everything!
And every hair on Noah’s body lifted at once!

It was not pressure. Minerva pressed on him like a weight from afar. This girl pressed on nothing at all, and standing near that absence felt like standing beside a mountain that had decided to look like a pebble.
His packed, compressed existence, unbothered by beings at eight hundred, went quietly still.
Across the ring, Minerva had gone very still too.
The girl brushed snow off her knee and waved at everyone.
"Sorry for being late! But I was promised to go first!"
Moriarty was quiet a moment. "Promised by whom, young lady?"
She tipped her head back and smiled, not at Moriarty but at one of the hazy thrones, where an Immense One sat so deep in its own Dimensionality that no one could see it at all.
"Oh," she said cheerfully. "You know."
The hazy throne did not answer!
In the center of the plain, Dravos turned his helmeted head slowly toward her, and the red at his seams brightened.
"The Plain,"he said, like a furnace door grinding open,"is mine first."
She looked him over, the armor, the craters, the glow, and her whole face lit up!
"Big fucker, you need an opponent anyways. Loosen the fuck up! Come on!"

She hopped down off the Conduit and walked out onto the Plain of Accord, soft shoes leaving small neat prints beside his craters. She stopped a few paces in front of him and bounced on her toes, once, twice, rolling her shoulders, the great muscles of her thighs flexing and settling.
"Ready? I am Ling, big fucker, and I...love to fight!"
Dravos did not answer her as he was actually a but angry!
He planted his feet, and his Provenance came out of him!

It poured off his body in a red-black flood that did not stay a flood for long. Hardening, it set in plates and ridges and interlocking scales, layer on layer, like molten iron setting on an anvil, until he stood inside a second suit of armor built over the first, taller than before, broader, every seam of it running with a dull forge-glow.
His Provenance had a name, and it announced itself in the heat rolling off him: THE Provenance of THE Unquenched Forge. Whatever touched it would be hammered. Whatever struck it would be struck back.
He took one step toward her, and the Plain of Accord shook!

The crater under his foot was deeper this time. On the golden clouds ringing the plain, Root Bearers who had been lounging a moment ago sat up straight, and more than one of them gripped the edge of their cloud as it rocked!
This was a Progeny of THE Ashen Cantor, a Fiend-path Root, and he was genuinely grand.
"Yield," Dravos said. "I do not hold back well as it would be a shame for there to be an accidental death. You feel...ridiculously weak. Do you even have any Provenance?"
Ling bounced on her toes, ribbons swaying, and looked him up and down with open admiration as if she had never seen someone so fucking stupid.
"I came here to test myself against the truly grand,"Dravos went on, his voice grinding out of the helm. "Not to break a girl who ran up the stairs late. Step off the Plain."
"Aw,"Ling said. "That’s sweet!"
And she stepped in.
WUU!
She did not use a single authority. Noah watched for one, a weaving, a flicker of Provenance, anything at all, and there was nothing. She simply took one step forward, turned her hips, and kicked.
Her shin met his breastplate.
BOOM!

It rang like a bell the size of a Dimension being struck! The sound rolled out across the whole Plain of Accord and up into the thrones and away over the snowing mountains of the Legacy, and in the middle of it, THE Provenance of THE Unquenched Forge caved in around the shape of a single girl’s leg!
Dravos went backward!
He slid, feet still planted, carving a trench through the snow and the stone of the oldest mountain in the Legacy, a hundred paces of it, before he stopped.
The plain went dead silent!
Then Ling was on him again!

It was not a fight. It was a performance, and she was having the time of her life! She kicked from the knee and from the hip, snapping strikes that cracked the forged plates wherever they landed. Her open hands swung out like hammers and the armor buckled under her palms. Then up his chest she ran, launched off his shoulders, came down heel-first on his helm, and landed laughing.

Then she threw a flurry of kicks so fast they stopped looking like kicks at all, only a blur of thick powerful legs and flying white ribbons, and every strike sprayed blood and red-hot flakes of shattered Provenance across the snow!
She laughed the whole time. Bright, delighted, cheeks flushed, and getting less sane by the second.
Dravos roared, and his Root answered.

Noah felt it happen! Across the ring, the forge-glow of THE Ashen Cantor’s throne flared in answer to its son. The Physical Root inside the armor bore down on itself, and Dravos grew heavier. Denser. The plain groaned beneath him as his weight doubled, doubled again, until he was a being simply stronger than the rules of the fight, the Fiend-path made flesh, too heavy for any blow to move!
And yet..
Oh, and yet!
Ling kicked him, and he moved!
It did not matter. None of it mattered! However heavy he made himself, she was heavier still, a girl with 1 in every measure, and his weight meant nothing at all to hers.
Noah let his Provenance unfurl, just a little. Just enough to look properly.
And he saw it!

Her existence had abandoned everything else. There was nothing in her but one thing. No layers, no borrowed weavings, no Causes or Intents or grown foundations stacked on top of a Root, as everyone else carried theirs. Her Root did not sit inside her. It was her, from her skin to her core, all of her. The Root and the girl existed as one.
She was a Root of Immensity!
Above the plain, the thrones broke their composure.
|THE ASHEN CANTOR rises half out of its throne of black glass. Its embers have stopped singing.|
|THE HOLLOW CHOIR falls silent, all thousand voices at once.|
|THE SALT-CROWNED MATRON leans forward. "...What is that child? Whose child is it? Is she one of the new entrants?"|
|THE DISSECTING SCHOLAR is writing very quickly. His spectacles nearly slipped.|
|A hazy throne ripples. It appears pleased.|
Ling ducked a haymaker that would have flattened a mountain range and came up grinning, blood on her smile.
"More!" she shouted. "More, more, give me more! Are those big muscles for show? Is all that Provenance for show?! Lots are watching- dodge this at least!"
HUUM!
She swept his legs out from under him. His guard dropped. She stamped once, hard.
The Plain of Accord cratered!
The ground caved inward around her foot in a bowl wider than a city, and Dravos went down into the bottom of it in a crash of shattered armor, and the whole mountain shuddered from peak to root!
On its throne, THE Keeper of the Unbroken Vow pulsed once.
It was over!

A Keeper was already at the bottom of the crater, an old grey-bearded figure in black and fur who had not been there a heartbeat before, standing over Dravos with both hands raised and his face perfectly calm. Dravos lay in the ruin of his own forge-armor, alive, barely, plates scattered across the snow in smoking pieces. His Root flickered weakly inside him like a banked coal that someone had stepped on.
Ling stood at the rim of the crater, breathing hard, ribbons hanging loose, blood speckled across the gold embroidery of her dress, and beamed.
Noah sat back on his cloud, and let his Provenance settle tight against his skin again.

A Physical Root, crushed. Not by a greater Physical Root, not by an Empyros rewriting the fight, but by something that had thrown away everything that was not its Root, until there was nothing left of her to be anything else. Dravos had carried his Root. She simply was hers. And a being that is entirely one thing cannot be split, or weighed against itself, or found wanting in any part, because there are no parts!
So that was what the 1s meant. Not weakness. There was only one of her, and it was all Root!
How did a being even get like that? And what had she given up to do it?
He did not know. He wanted to!
|THE ASHEN CANTOR speaks, and its voice is a forge.|
|"The child lost. I grant him a Favor regardless. Let him remember why he needed it."|
Down in the crater, Dravos went very still. Somewhere under the ruin of his helm, Noah suspected, a young giant was trying very hard not to weep.
Because that was a fucking humiliation.
A Favor to its own defeated son. A mercy, and a humiliation, and the whole Legacy had just watched it land.
|A hazy throne speaks. No one can see what speaks.|
|"A Favor to the girl."|
Ling looked up at the haze and bowed, too fast again, bouncing on the snow. Then she turned and walked back along the ring of golden clouds, humming.
She passed right in front of Noah’s cloud, and looked up at him.
She winked.
"Big boy," she said cheerfully,"I want to see how you would do between my thighs! I’ve heard a little about you! I’ll let others take the ring for now but afterwards...you and I need to have a go..."
She skipped off before he could answer and sat down on the very edge of the Plain, with no cloud of her own at all, swinging her legs over the drop and humming to herself.
Noah watched her go, and for once he genuinely did not know what to say!

There is only the Challenge.
Step into the center and name who you wish to face.
The one named may refuse, once, in the whole of the Convocation.
A refusal is remembered.
The Legacy has a very long memory."
One refusal.
Spend it, and everyone watching would know exactly who had made you flinch!
Noah thought of this and set it aside.
He did not intend to flinch from anyone here.
"Third, and the one most of you came for.
Favors.
Any Immense One seated here may grant a Favor to whoever impresses them.
A sliver of their Immensity.
A lesson.
A Relic from their keeping.
A door opened that you could not open yourself."His spectacles glinted.
Above him, the thrones stirred!
|THE ASHEN CANTOR shifts on its throne of black glass.
Embers fall from its shoulders.
It appears bored.|
|THE HOLLOW CHOIR murmurs in a thousand low voices.
It is taking bets.
It will not say on what.|
|THE SALT-CROWNED MATRON has already chosen three favorites and intends to be proven right.|
|THE DIMENSIONAL DEVOURER, POONA, is very excited, and would like everyone to know it.|
Noah almost laughed.
He sat very still on his golden cloud instead, and turned the rules over one by one.
A tournament, then, where the audience were the titans of the Legacy and the prize was their attention.
Winning was worth pride and standing.
But a Favor was worth more than every win on this plain put together.
Okay!
He kept his Provenance drawn tight and his dreams still.
First he wanted to see how the others fought.
Information first.
"Then let us begin," Moriarty said.
"Who steps first onto the Plain?"
The cloud marked Dravos sagged as the figure on it stood.
He was huge!
Dark armor covered him from throat to heel, scorched and dented and glowing dull red along evry seam, as though the fire inside had never gone out.
He stepped down onto the plain, and the ground beneath the snow dented into a shallow crater under a single step.
A Physical Root, Progeny of THE Ashen Cantor, built to be heavier than anything in his way!
On the throne of black glass, the embers stopped falling for a moment.
Dravos walked toward the center, each step a slow crater, and the whole ring of clouds watched him go.
He clearly meant to go first, and felt no need to wait for anyone’s opinion on it.
Yet at this time...
"Wait, wait, wait!"
Every head on the plain turned!
Someone was running up the last Conduit, actually running, feet flying along the glowing path with no Keeper in front of her!
She came over the edge in a spray of snow, skidded to a stop with a hand on her knee, and grinned around at everyone.
She wore a silk dress of deep blue embroidered all over with gold, high collar closed at the throat, slits cut high up both sides so nothing would ever get in the way of her moving.
Her black hair was wound into two tight spiraled buns tied with white ribbons, half loose from the run.
And her legs!
They were the first thing anyone noticed and the last thing anyone would forget.

Thick, powerful thighs heavy with muscle, the thighs of someone who had spent her whole existence kicking things that did not want to be kicked, and calves drawn tight as strung bows beneath them, bare but for white wrap-bands at the ankles and soft cloth shoes!
Every shift of her weight moved them with a coiled, springing ease that promised a great deal of violence.
She was thick!
Her face was round and cheerful, eyes crinkling at the corners with a smile Noah suspected never left.
She bowed to the thrones, too fast and almost slipped on the snow.
Noah’s sight opened her.
|SHEN HUALING(LING).|
|VERITAS: 1.
PROVENANCE: 1.
POTENTIA: 1.
PONDUS: 1.|
|ROOT OF IMMENSITY: ???|
Noah’s smile faded.
One in everything!
And every hair on Noah’s body lifted at once!
It was not pressure.
Minerva pressed on him like a weight from afar.
This girl pressed on nothing at all, and standing near that absence felt like standing beside a mountain that had decided to look like a pebble.
His packed, compressed existence, unbothered by beings at eight hundred, went quietly still.
Across the ring, Minerva had gone very still too.
The girl brushed snow off her knee and waved at everyone.
"Sorry for being late!
But I was promised to go first!"
Moriarty was quiet a moment.
"Promised by whom, young lady?"
She tipped her head back and smiled, not at Moriarty but at one of the hazy thrones, where an Immense One sat so deep in its own Dimensionality that no one could see it at all.
"Oh," she said cheerfully.
"You know."
The hazy throne did not answer!
In the center of the plain, Dravos turned his helmeted head slowly toward her, and the red at his seams brightened.
"The Plain,"he said, like a furnace door grinding open,"is mine first."
She looked him over, the armor, the craters, the glow, and her whole face lit up!
"Big fucker, you need an opponent anyways.
Loosen the fuck up!
Come on!"
She hopped down off the Conduit and walked out onto the Plain of Accord, soft shoes leaving small neat prints beside his craters.
She stopped a few paces in front of him and bounced on her toes, once, twice, rolling her shoulders, the great muscles of her thighs flexing and settling.
"Ready?
I am Ling, big fucker, and I...love to fight!"
Dravos did not answer her as he was actually a but angry!
He planted his feet, and his Provenance came out of him!
It poured off his body in a red-black flood that did not stay a flood for long.

Hardening, it set in plates and ridges and interlocking scales, layer on layer, like molten iron setting on an anvil, until he stood inside a second suit of armor built over the first, taller than before, broader, every seam of it running with a dull forge-glow.
His Provenance had a name, and it announced itself in the heat rolling off him: THE Provenance of THE Unquenched Forge.
Whatever touched it would be hammered.
Whatever struck it would be struck back.
He took one step toward her, and the Plain of Accord shook!
The crater under his foot was deeper this time.
On the golden clouds ringing the plain, Root Bearers who had been lounging a moment ago sat up straight, and more than one of them gripped the edge of their cloud as it rocked!
This was a Progeny of THE Ashen Cantor, a Fiend-path Root, and he was genuinely grand.
"Yield," Dravos said.
"I do not hold back well as it would be a shame for there to be an accidental death.
You feel...ridiculously weak.
Do you even have any Provenance?"
Ling bounced on her toes, ribbons swaying, and looked him up and down with open admiration as if she had never seen someone so fucking stupid.
"I came here to test myself against the truly grand,"Dravos went on, his voice grinding out of the helm.
"Not to break a girl who ran up the stairs late.
Step off the Plain."
"Aw,"Ling said.
"That’s sweet!"
And she stepped in.
WUU!
She did not use a single authority.
Noah watched for one, a weaving, a flicker of Provenance, anything at all, and there was nothing.
She simply took one step forward, turned her hips, and kicked.
Her shin met his breastplate.
BOOM!
It rang like a bell the size of a Dimension being struck!

The sound rolled out across the whole Plain of Accord and up into the thrones and away over the snowing mountains of the Legacy, and in the middle of it, THE Provenance of THE Unquenched Forge caved in around the shape of a single girl’s leg!
Dravos went backward!
He slid, feet still planted, carving a trench through the snow and the stone of the oldest mountain in the Legacy, a hundred paces of it, before he stopped.
The plain went dead silent!
Then Ling was on him again!
It was not a fight.
It was a performance, and she was having the time of her life!
She kicked from the knee and from the hip, snapping strikes that cracked the forged plates wherever they landed.
Her open hands swung out like hammers and the armor buckled under her palms.
Then up his chest she ran, launched off his shoulders, came down heel-first on his helm, and landed laughing.

Then she threw a flurry of kicks so fast they stopped looking like kicks at all, only a blur of thick powerful legs and flying white ribbons, and every strike sprayed blood and red-hot flakes of shattered Provenance across the snow!
She laughed the whole time.
Bright, delighted, cheeks flushed, and getting less sane by the second.
Dravos roared, and his Root answered.
Noah felt it happen!
Across the ring, the forge-glow of THE Ashen Cantor’s throne flared in answer to its son.
The Physical Root inside the armor bore down on itself, and Dravos grew heavier.
Denser.
The plain groaned beneath him as his weight doubled, doubled again, until he was a being simply stronger than the rules of the fight, the Fiend-path made flesh, too heavy for any blow to move!
And yet..
Oh, and yet!
Ling kicked him, and he moved!
It did not matter.
None of it mattered!
However heavy he made himself, she was heavier still, a girl with 1 in every measure, and his weight meant nothing at all to hers.
Noah let his Provenance unfurl, just a little.
Just enough to look properly.
And he saw it!
Her existence had abandoned everything else.
There was nothing in her but one thing.
No layers, no borrowed weavings, no Causes or Intents or grown foundations stacked on top of a Root, as everyone else carried theirs.
Her Root did not sit inside her.
It was her, from her skin to her core, all of her.
The Root and the girl existed as one.
She was a Root of Immensity!
Above the plain, the thrones broke their composure.
|THE ASHEN CANTOR rises half out of its throne of black glass.
Its embers have stopped singing.|
|THE HOLLOW CHOIR falls silent, all thousand voices at once.|
|THE SALT-CROWNED MATRON leans forward.
"...What is that child?
Whose child is it?
Is she one of the new entrants?"|
|THE DISSECTING SCHOLAR is writing very quickly.
His spectacles nearly slipped.|
|A hazy throne ripples.
It appears pleased.|
Ling ducked a haymaker that would have flattened a mountain range and came up grinning, blood on her smile.
"More!" she shouted.
"More, more, give me more!
Are those big muscles for show?
Is all that Provenance for show?!
Lots are watching- dodge this at least!"
HUUM!
She swept his legs out from under him.
His guard dropped.
She stamped once, hard.
The Plain of Accord cratered!
The ground caved inward around her foot in a bowl wider than a city, and Dravos went down into the bottom of it in a crash of shattered armor, and the whole mountain shuddered from peak to root!
On its throne, THE Keeper of the Unbroken Vow pulsed once.
It was over!

A Keeper was already at the bottom of the crater, an old grey-bearded figure in black and fur who had not been there a heartbeat before, standing over Dravos with both hands raised and his face perfectly calm.
Dravos lay in the ruin of his own forge-armor, alive, barely, plates scattered across the snow in smoking pieces.
His Root flickered weakly inside him like a banked coal that someone had stepped on.
Ling stood at the rim of the crater, breathing hard, ribbons hanging loose, blood speckled across the gold embroidery of her dress, and beamed.
Noah sat back on his cloud, and let his Provenance settle tight against his skin again.
A Physical Root, crushed.
Not by a greater Physical Root, not by an Empyros rewriting the fight, but by something that had thrown away everything that was not its Root, until there was nothing left of her to be anything else.
Dravos had carried his Root.
She simply was hers.
And a being that is entirely one thing cannot be split, or weighed against itself, or found wanting in any part, because there are no parts!
So that was what the 1s meant.
Not weakness.
There was only one of her, and it was all Root!
How did a being even get like that?
And what had she given up to do it?
He did not know.
He wanted to!
|THE ASHEN CANTOR speaks, and its voice is a forge.|
|"The child lost.
I grant him a Favor regardless.
Let him remember why he needed it."|
Down in the crater, Dravos went very still.
Somewhere under the ruin of his helm, Noah suspected, a young giant was trying very hard not to weep.
Because that was a fucking humiliation.
A Favor to its own defeated son.
A mercy, and a humiliation, and the whole Legacy had just watched it land.
|A hazy throne speaks.
No one can see what speaks.|
|"A Favor to the girl."|
Ling looked up at the haze and bowed, too fast again, bouncing on the snow.
Then she turned and walked back along the ring of golden clouds, humming.
She passed right in front of Noah’s cloud, and looked up at him.
She winked.
"Big boy," she said cheerfully,"I want to see how you would do between my thighs!
I’ve heard a little about you!
I’ll let others take the ring for now but afterwards...you and I need to have a go..."
She skipped off before he could answer and sat down on the very edge of the Plain, with no cloud of her own at all, swinging her legs over the drop and humming to herself.
Noah watched her go, and for once he genuinely did not know what to say!

chapters.title: Chapter 5798: The Convocation of Roots! III
paragraphs: After Ling, the Convocation found its rhythm, and the bouts came fast.
The water-woman stepped onto the Plain against a Progeny wreathed in white fire, and for a moment the fire seemed to have the better of it, roaring over her in sheets.

Then she simply went deeper. Her Dimensionality sank beneath the fire’s, a whole ocean opening under the Plain where no ocean should fit, and a tide rose out of it lit from within by swimming fish of light. It closed over the flames from below, where they could not reach, and drowned them!
Batiatus went next, and talked the entire time.

"Your left foot is slipping," he said, and it slipped. "You are tired," he said, and his opponent staggered. "That blow will miss," and it missed, by an inch, every sentence true for three breaths within a few paces of him, his Dimensionality pressing each word into the ground around him like a stamp.
He was gloriously, unbearably annoying. He was also winning, right up until he challenged the stag-headed one!
The stag lowered its antlers, and every small bell hung on them rang once.

The sound did not travel outward. It sank inward, down into the Dimensionality of the space around it, and where it reached, speech stopped existing. Batiatus opened his mouth, and nothing true came out.
Nothing at all came out! He mimed a very rude sentence in silence, and the stag struck him off the Plain.

Then the figure in the grey cloak of mist stood, and its opponent attacked, and every blow passed straight through where it seemed to be. It sat at a depth of existence its opponent could not reach, so every strike landed on a shadow a layer above it. It did not move once. The opponent exhausted itself on nothing and yielded!
And Favors fell from the thrones like coins tossed onto a stage. A glint of light from the Salt-Crowned Matron. A murmur from the Hollow Choir. A slip of green from the throne in leaf.
Noah watched all of it, and learned.

Not by copying. He had no interest in carrying someone else’s water or wearing someone else’s silence. But every bout was a different answer to the same question: what is existence, and how does one stand in it? What were their dreams?

The water-woman believed depth was power. Batiatus believed words were. The mist believed it was enough simply to be where no one else could reach. Each of them was a way of looking, and each one struck a small spark somewhere in his own Dream. He let the sparks land, and kept them.
Then Achilles stood.
The king stepped off his cloud onto the snow!
Achilles walked to the center and looked across the plain.
"You," he said to the stag.

It was a strange choice. Noah read Achilles’s panel as he walked and found his attributes barely reaching four hundred. The stag stood near eight. Half the Plain seemed to think the same thing at once as they could also measure relative Dimensionality, and a murmur ran around the golden clouds!
The stag’s bells rang as it stepped onto the arena as if it had been offended!

The silence came down on Achilles like a falling wall, and the stag came with it, antlers lowered, and he took the first blow full on. He flew. He hit the snow and rolled and came up bleeding, and the stag was already on him agian.

The first exchanges were ugly. The stag was twice his weight in every measure, and every time its antlers came down, the silence came with them, pressing into the Dimensionality around Achilles until even his breath seemed to stop existing. He was losing, badly.
But he was very, very hard to catch.

Noah saw it before anyone else. Achilles was not dodging through space. He was dodging through time, stepping a fraction of a moment out of where the antlers came down, sliding half a heartbeat sideways so a blow meant for him landed on the place he had been.
He was slippery as an eel in a river of hours. And while he slipped, he was reaching.
The bell-silence closed on him again.
And this time he did not dodge it. He let it in.
"Assimilate," he said, and nothing came out of his mouth, because the silence took the word. It did not matter. The silence went into him anyway, and became him, as everything he touched became him!
The next time the stag’s bells rang, Achilles rang with them, and the silence broke against a king who was now made partly of silence himself!
A gasp went up from the whole plain!
On his throne of instruments, Moriarty set down his quill and leaned forward.
Then the time came out even more!

Achilles’s body flickered. Young. Old, suddenly, lined and white-haired and thin. Young again. His fist met the stag’s shoulder before his arm had moved, and his foot was already planted where the stag was going to step. All of him shone faintly purple with the signature of the rivers of time Noah had watched him swallow, and for a long moment, the smaller king held the larger stag to a standstill!
And then the cold came!

Frost spread from his feet. It ran out across the plain in fine white lines, spidering over the snow, and the falling snow above him bent in its fall, all of it curving toward him as though he were drawing it in. His breath went pale in the air. It was not a man’s breath. It was a winter’s breath, long and slow and old.
Noah went utterly still!
He knew that cold. He had knelt in it in a frozen underworld, and drunk rivers of it. It was packed into his quarks, compressed alongside his Provenance, and he would know it anywhere in existence.
Had this monster... begun assimilating THE Long Night itself?

The stag slowed. Its bells rang, muffled. Its hooves dragged in the frost. The cold was on it now, in it, pulling every movement down toward stillness, and Achilles slipped around it through the edges of time, striking, striking!
HUUUM!
But not wounding.

Achilles could slow the stag and evade it forever, stepping between moments and dragging winter behind him. He simply did not have the power to break it. Every blow he landed skated off a being twice his weight and left nothing but frost.
A Keeper stepped between them as nobody wanted to watch an endlessly boring fight, so it was called!
A draw.

The stag stood utterly furious at having a draw by something so weak, rimed to the tips of its antlers. Achilles stood across from it, breathing slow, and around him the snow was still falling. It neither melted on him nor froze him. It simply settled into him and was gone, as it settled into Noah.
Above the plain, several thrones stirred, and not warmly.
|THE SALT-CROWNED MATRON watches in silence. The rain around her throne has turned to sleet.|
|A hazy throne dims.|
|THE ASHEN CANTOR’s embers fall very slowly.|
None of them said a word. They did not need to. The Plain of Accord felt the chill all the same!
Achilles walked back to his cloud and sat. He looked across at Noah with solemn eyes, frost still clinging to his lashes, and gave a slight nod.
What was this monster thinking? And...had he been brought into the folds of The Caretaker as well?
Noah tapped his knee thoughtfully!
Behind him, Rose finally moved. She reached out and brushed the frost off his shoulder.
It did not come off.
And at this moment, across the ring, Minerva rose!
She leaped!

She came down in the middle of it, and as she landed, seeds spilled from the hem of her green robe. Small, green, glowing, dozens of them scattering across the snow, and wherever one fell, a Dimension bloomed. Tiny ones, pocket realities opening like flowers, each one green and full of leaves and gone again in a breath.
She lifted a hand and pointed.
"Osmont."
The plain went silent. Every Provenance Lifeform and every Progeny on the golden clouds turned to look at him at once!

Above, THE Verdant Regard’s green gaze sharpened until it was almost painful to be under. Poona leaned forward on her throne, eyes shining. Moriarty set down his quill again, laced his tentacles in his lap, and arranged his face into something very carefully neutral.
Was it finally his time to make a move?
Noah stretched and stepped down off his cloud, and walked out onto the snow to face her as he wasn’t fearful even though she was grand!
Her voice came into his mind.

"There’s been a lot of talk, in case you didn’t know. Some of the Immense Ones think you’re one of them. The three. There’s a prophecy of the Long Night, and I don’t even know if you know it, but Mother and some of the others have been whispering it since the hour you were brought here."
Her green eyes held his.
"I don’t believe it. I reject it. Why should existence listen to a rhyme? Why should everything that is be bound to three supposed beings?"

"...I’m sorry. For the animosity it seems I have. It isn’t you, really. I just want to prove them wrong. Existence is too grand to be steered by three beings. It has to be. Or what are the rest of us for? Just background? Just nothing?"
Her crooked crown caught the snowlight.

"The moment anything is born, it has a role to play. Some love to think the man in the gilded chair matters more than the farmer pulling weeds in the dirt. They convince themselves existence is a grand play, where a few loud names run the stage while everyone else is scenery filling up the dark. It doesn’t work like that. Not one role is grander than the next. No one is a background character, made just to watch someone else live. The king, the beggar, and the stray dog. Every single life carries its own weight."
Noah almost smiled.

Him? One of the three, in some random prophecy? He could say with a fair amount of certainty that that was not the case. For a long while now, he had been reining in the weavings of THE PROTAGONIST, precisely so that they would not drag him into the center of anything grand and ridiculous without his say!
He could be mistaken for some grand figure, certainly. But he was not going to fit neatly into any role that others had designed for him in advance!

"I don’t know whether I’m one of three," he answered, calm, in his mind to hers. "Idon’t much care. I don’t live by prophecy either. I live by my Dream. We agree on more than you think so...let’s find out who’s right anyway."
They had just been eye fucking each other intently this whole time as from above, a booming command came!
"Begin," said Moriarty.
Minerva looked at him.

That was all she did at first, and it was enough. Where her gaze landed, existence was judged, and what was judged began to grow. The snow at Noah’s feet sprouted. Green shoots burst up through it, budded, bloomed into pale flowers, rotted, and returned as fresh shoots, all in the span of a single glance!

Roots of green authority tore up out of the Plain and out of the empty air itself, thick as tree trunks, wrapping around him, growing into whatever they held and through it, meaning to take root in him and grow him into something else.
They found nothing to grow into.

Noah stood still and let them try. The roots wrapped his crystalline body and pressed, searching for a seam, a borrowed thread, anything at all that was not his own, and his compressed existence gave them nothing. There was no soil in him that was not already him. The roots slid, and scraped, and could not sprout.
But the pressure behind them was immense. Nine hundred and ninety-nine in everything, all of it bearing down at once, and for the first time since the frozen underworld, his crystalline skin buzzed!
A thin line of light opened along his forarm, and another across his ribs!
Minerva’s voice rang out loud this time, for the whole plain to hear.
"You’re holding back? Everyone here is watching you! Why won’t you confirm or deny what they think? Let’s make everything clear right here! Let them all know there are no chosen ones!"
Noah looked at the green roots wrapped around his arms, at the flowers blooming and dying at his feet, and then up at her.
"I’m... learning at this moment," he said. "Your weavings. Your Provenance. Your Dreams. I am trying to understand, before anything else."
Minerva’s eyes flared, green, then white with anger.
"Then understand this!"
The whole Plain of Accord erupted into a forest of Dimensions!
