Achilles could slow the stag and evade it forever, stepping between moments and dragging winter behind him.
He simply did not have the power to break it.
Every blow he landed skated off a being twice his weight and left nothing but frost.
A Keeper stepped between them as nobody wanted to watch an endlessly boring fight, so it was called!
A draw.
The stag stood utterly furious at having a draw by something so weak, rimed to the tips of its antlers.
Achilles stood across from it, breathing slow, and around him the snow was still falling.
It neither melted on him nor froze him.
It simply settled into him and was gone, as it settled into Noah.
Above the plain, several thrones stirred, and not warmly.
|THE SALT-CROWNED MATRON watches in silence.
The rain around her throne has turned to sleet.|
|A hazy throne dims.|
|THE ASHEN CANTOR’s embers fall very slowly.|
None of them said a word.
They did not need to.
The Plain of Accord felt the chill all the same!
Achilles walked back to his cloud and sat.
He looked across at Noah with solemn eyes, frost still clinging to his lashes, and gave a slight nod.
What was this monster thinking?
And...had he been brought into the folds of The Caretaker as well?
Noah tapped his knee thoughtfully!
Behind him, Rose finally moved.
She reached out and brushed the frost off his shoulder.
It did not come off.
And at this moment, across the ring, Minerva rose!
She leaped!
She came down in the middle of it, and as she landed, seeds spilled from the hem of her green robe.
Small, green, glowing, dozens of them scattering across the snow, and wherever one fell, a Dimension bloomed.
Tiny ones, pocket realities opening like flowers, each one green and full of leaves and gone again in a breath.
She lifted a hand and pointed.
"Osmont."
The plain went silent.
Every Provenance Lifeform and every Progeny on the golden clouds turned to look at him at once!
Above, THE Verdant Regard’s green gaze sharpened until it was almost painful to be under.
Poona leaned forward on her throne, eyes shining.
Moriarty set down his quill again, laced his tentacles in his lap, and arranged his face into something very carefully neutral.
Was it finally his time to make a move?
Noah stretched and stepped down off his cloud, and walked out onto the snow to face her as he wasn’t fearful even though she was grand!
Her voice came into his mind.
"There’s been a lot of talk, in case you didn’t know.
Some of the Immense Ones think you’re one of them.
The three.
There’s a prophecy of the Long Night, and I don’t even know if you know it, but Mother and some of the others have been whispering it since the hour you were brought here."
Her green eyes held his.
"I don’t believe it.
I reject it.
Why should existence listen to a rhyme?
Why should everything that is be bound to three supposed beings?"
"...I’m sorry.
For the animosity it seems I have.
It isn’t you, really.
I just want to prove them wrong.
Existence is too grand to be steered by three beings.
It has to be.
Or what are the rest of us for?
Just background?
Just nothing?"
Her crooked crown caught the snowlight.
"The moment anything is born, it has a role to play.
Some love to think the man in the gilded chair matters more than the farmer pulling weeds in the dirt.
They convince themselves existence is a grand play, where a few loud names run the stage while everyone else is scenery filling up the dark.
It doesn’t work like that.
Not one role is grander than the next.
No one is a background character, made just to watch someone else live.
The king, the beggar, and the stray dog.
Every single life carries its own weight."
Noah almost smiled.
Him?
One of the three, in some random prophecy?
He could say with a fair amount of certainty that that was not the case.
For a long while now, he had been reining in the weavings of THE PROTAGONIST, precisely so that they would not drag him into the center of anything grand and ridiculous without his say!
He could be mistaken for some grand figure, certainly.
But he was not going to fit neatly into any role that others had designed for him in advance!
"I don’t know whether I’m one of three," he answered, calm, in his mind to hers.
"Idon’t much care.
I don’t live by prophecy either.
I live by my Dream.
We agree on more than you think so...let’s find out who’s right anyway."
They had just been eye fucking each other intently this whole time as from above, a booming command came!
"Begin," said Moriarty.
Minerva looked at him.
That was all she did at first, and it was enough.
Where her gaze landed, existence was judged, and what was judged began to grow.
The snow at Noah’s feet sprouted.
Green shoots burst up through it, budded, bloomed into pale flowers, rotted, and returned as fresh shoots, all in the span of a single glance!

Roots of green authority tore up out of the Plain and out of the empty air itself, thick as tree trunks, wrapping around him, growing into whatever they held and through it, meaning to take root in him and grow him into something else.
They found nothing to grow into.
Noah stood still and let them try.
The roots wrapped his crystalline body and pressed, searching for a seam, a borrowed thread, anything at all that was not his own, and his compressed existence gave them nothing.
There was no soil in him that was not already him.
The roots slid, and scraped, and could not sprout.
But the pressure behind them was immense.
Nine hundred and ninety-nine in everything, all of it bearing down at once, and for the first time since the frozen underworld, his crystalline skin buzzed!
A thin line of light opened along his forarm, and another across his ribs!
Minerva’s voice rang out loud this time, for the whole plain to hear.
"You’re holding back?
Everyone here is watching you!
Why won’t you confirm or deny what they think?
Let’s make everything clear right here!
Let them all know there are no chosen ones!"
Noah looked at the green roots wrapped around his arms, at the flowers blooming and dying at his feet, and then up at her.
"I’m... learning at this moment," he said.
"Your weavings.
Your Provenance.
Your Dreams.
I am trying to understand, before anything else."
Minerva’s eyes flared, green, then white with anger.
"Then understand this!"
The whole Plain of Accord erupted into a forest of Dimensions!

chapters.title: Chapter 5799: No Immensity! I
paragraphs: The Plain of Accord was gone!

In its place, in a single heartbeat, stood a forest older than any forest had a right to be. Trees the size of mountains tore up out of the snow, trunks thick as rivers, canopies lost somewhere up among the floating thrones, and they did not stand still.

They grew, and died, and grew again. Every leaf that budded on them held the weight of a Dimension blooming into being, and every leaf that fell was that Dimension collapsing, thousands upon thousands of them erupting and dying and erupting again in every branch, so that the whole forest roared with the sound of realities being judged!
On the edge of the Plain, Ling clapped, eyes shining.
On the golden clouds, Progeny and Provenance Lifeforms leaned forward as one, and no one said a word.
And in the middle of it all, Noah stood and took the forest on his body.
It came down on him from every side. Roots thicker than towers wrapped his legs and crushed. Branches swung like the arms of titens. Leaves fell on him like a rain of breaking Dimensions!

His body glistened through it. His crystalline skin had taken on the sheen of ancient jade, dense and deep and faintly luminous, and beneath it infinite dreams and Provenance moved in slow blue-gold currents. It held. Even so, Minerva’s Provenance was so heavy that fine cracks kept spreading across it, one after another, light leaking out of each thin line!
But he held on.
Against a being at nine hundred and ninety-nine in everything, crashing down on him with the weight of an entire Dimensional forest, he held on!
Every second had been a day of compression for him, and every one of those days was packed into him now, and it was grand. His foundation did not so much as tremble.
Oh!
But what more could he do?!
He let the lid come off.

Not all at once. One layer at a time, carefully, as a man opens a door into a room he has never entered. Stellar golden clouds billowed out of him first, soft and bright, rolling out through the roots and the trunks into the forest around him.
The dreams went first.

Wherever the golden clouds drifted, the forest slowed. Its frantic growing and dying turned lazy and strange. Trees that had been erupting toward the sky began instead to bloom into shapes no tree could ever have learned, towers and faces and curling stairways of bark that led nowhere.
Leaves drifted down slowly, turning over and over as they fell. Time itself, near him, began to dream, and Minerva’s growth-speed stumbled in it!

Noah then let the Physical side of his Root press outward, all the dense weight of those packed quarks, the cold of the Long Night crushed down into every one of them. His body simply became heavier than her forest could move. The great roots around his legs wrapped tighter, and heaved, and lifted nothing. He was not holding them back. They simply could not find the strength to move him!
Then the Conceptual side.
He looked at the forest around him and dreamed, plainly and completely, that it was a forest in a dream.
And existence half-agreed!

Around him, the trunks went hazy at their edges. The roaring of breaking Dimensions softened into something far away and muffled, the sound of a storm heard from inside a warm house. Half the forest was still real. Half of it was a dream Noah was having about a forest, and that half began, very gently, to sleep.
This was it. This was what he had seen from the inside, in the purple sky of the Chrysalis!

Minerva wrote growth onto existence. That was her Root, an Empyros’s power, judging and growing and rewriting whatever her eyes fell on. And Noah was heavier than the writing, the Fiend’s answer, a thing so dense that no sentence could lift it. But he also wrote back, dreaming his own sentence over hers.
He was both. The writer and the page!
Her judgment landed on him, and he stood.
His dream landed on her forest, and it slept!
He took a step forward.
Then another!

He walked through her forest toward her, step by step, across the dreaming Plain, and everything she threw at him either broke on his weight or fell asleep in his dream. Across from him, Minerva’s eyes flickered coldly in his sight.
Above the Plain, the thrones broke.
|THE DIMENSIONAL DEVOURER, POONA, is standing on her throne and cheering.|
|THE DISSECTING SCHOLAR’s spectacles have fogged. His quill is racing.|
|THE ASHEN CANTOR’s embers have stopped.|
|THE VERDANT REGARD’s gaze has gone cold and fierce. It is fixed on her daughter.|
|A voice from a hazy throne: "...His power is lower. So why is she not dominating?"|
|Another answers: "One of them walks the path of a Fiend, but still..."|
Minerva felt it.

Noah watched her realize it. She had come onto this plain to dominate, to show the whole Legacy that no chosen one existed, that existence was not bound to three beings whispered about in the snow. And she was not dominating!
In front of every throne and every cloud, she was being pushed back across the Plain of Accord by the very being she had meant to disprove.
Her pride was cracking, and her argument with it.
She stopped. She drew one long, calm breath, and lifted her head toward the sky. Toward the ring of floating thrones, and every Immense One seated on them.
Then she looked back down at Noah, and spoke to him alone.

"To live true to yourself," Minerva said into his mind, "means you keep walking even when the ground gives out beneath your feet. It means you believe in what you are doing even when the whole of existence looks at you, spits in the dirt, and calls you a fool. Even when existence itself stops believing in you."
Her green eyes held his, steady.

"But where is the line? How far can someone push before stubbornness just becomes madness? How true can anyone actually live? When the sky says no, and the cold says no, and every turning of the road says no, and no, and no again, how much can you believe before your own ribs crack under the weight?"
She did not look away.

"I don’t know where that edge is. Maybe you only find out when you fall off it. But I know what sits inside my own chest. I believe in my own skin. I believe in what I can build with my own hands. And right now, I don’t believe in this existence. I don’t believe its rules, and I don’t believe its winter."
The dreaming forest drifted around them, slow.
"So if existence wants to tell me no, let it. I will pit my belief against existence itself. And we will see which one breaks first."
Minerva stopped attacking.

Her forest died all at once. Every mountain-trunk, every root, every leaf of breaking Dimension, gone in an instant, crumbling into green dust that the snow buried in moments. The Plain of Accord lay bare and white again, and silent.
In the silence, she whispered aloud.
"Then I’ll become Immense right here, and prove it with that."
What?
Motherfucker, what?!
HUUM!
She called everything.

Every sliver of Immensity she had ever been given, she drew into herself at once. Everything she had inherited from her mother. Everything she had grown on her own. Every Favor ever granted to her by any throne. It all came pouring in from wherever it had been kept, green-gold light streaming across the snow toward her, and her Root blazed!
The Plain of Accord shook to its foundations!
On the golden clouds, Progeny and Provenance Lifeforms cried out and gripped the edges as they rocked. Above them, the thrones leaned in, all of them at once.
|THE VERDANT REGARD half rises from her throne of living leaf.|
|"Minerva. Stop."|
"Not here, child!"Moriarty’s voice cracked across the plain, sharp for the first time since Noah had known him. "Not in this cold!"
Noah went still.

THE First Gu of Time had said it, in the purple sky of the Chrysalis. Those who grasp Immensity in this cold may have a chance. Only a chance, and nothing guaranteed. And Minerva was actually trying it, here and now, in front of everyone?!
At this time.
The snow answered her.

It thickened. It spiraled. Out of the grey sky above the thrones, it began to pour toward her from every direction at once, a vast white vortex drawing down onto a single figure in a green robe at the center of the Plain. The Long Night had turned its attention onto a Root trying to become Immense beneath it.
And for one heartbeat, she almost did it!

A crown of green-gold light rose over her hed, far grander than the crooked one of leaves she wore. Her figure grew, climbing upward, vast and radiant, until she stood taller than the floating clouds. Behind her, a shape formed in the air, tall and narrow and edged in light!

And on her chest, the Root of Immensity that had always been hidden from Noah’s sight blazed into view, and it was changing. Its fibers were thickening, branching, reaching upward into a trunk. It was becoming a tree!
An Immensity was blooming, right there on the Plain of Accord!
Awe lit every face on every cloud. Even the thrones went still.
But...
The light of an opening door shut.
Her eyes filled with belief and immensity became ashen!
No door opened and let her through. It simply closed, soundlessly, in her face.
Her Root cracked.
Then it severed!
BOOM!

The sound of it carried across the whole Legacy, from the Firmament Mountain to the farthest peak, the sound of a great tree breaking in half. Green light poured out of her like blood, spilling down her robe and into the snow, and Minerva screamed!
"OOOOOH!"
Her eyes rolled back, showing white.
Then they turned pale!
And she spoke, but it was not her voice.
It was layered. Ancient. Calm, and terrible, a great many voices speaking together through a single throat, and every word fell on the silent Plain like a stone.
|No door shall open, because no new Immensity shall rise to open it. In the endless winter, no new Immensity shall arise!|
Absolute silence.
Every Immense One on every throne went still. Several of the hazy thrones flickered violently, their shapes jolting in and out of sight!
On his throne of instruments, Moriarty’s quill snapped in his grip. Poona was not smiling anymore.
And at the edge of the Plain, Ling had stopped swinging her legs.
Noah stared at the girl in the center of the Plain with the winter in her eyes.

No door shall open? THE First Gu of Time had said the opposite, not long ago. Doors are opening, she had said. The Caretaker had said a door shut long ago was beginning to be unshut. Even the Augury, the one prophecy everyone seemed to be whispering, ended by promising that the True would walk out the far side of the Night.
And this voice said no. No door. No new Immensity. Not ever.
So who was speaking?
He did not know!
The pale light drained out of Minerva’s eyes.
She collapsed into the snow.
Above, THE Verdant Regard rose from her throne.

For the first time, an Immense One left its seat. A vast green presence sank down out of the sky, soft as spring, shrinking as it came, until it was only a figure made of gentle green light kneeling in the snow at the center of the Plain. She gathered her daughter’s limp body against her and held her.
She looked down at Minerva with grief. Pure and plain! And under the grief, something unfathomable rose!
Then she lifted her head, and looked at Noah.
Her gaze was cold.
She said nothing. Not one word. And then she was gone, and her daughter with her.
The center of the Plain of Accord lay empty.
In the snow where Minerva had fallen, an illusory Root lay smoking, green and severed, broken clean in two. As Noah watched, frost began to creep across it from the broken end.
Slowly, it was freezing.

chapters.title: Chapter 5800: No Immensity! II
paragraphs: The severed Root lay in the snow where Minerva had fallen, green and broken and faintly smoking, and the frost crept across it from the broken end.

No Progeny stirred on the golden clouds. No Keeper stepped forward. Above, on their ring of floating thrones, the Immense Ones sat as still as the statues on the mountain’s flanks, and not one of them spoke.
Only the snow moved!
And then, very slowly, it began to change!

It thickened first. The steady fall that had covered the Legacy since THE Long Night began grew heavier, and heavier still, flakes crowding the air until the far thrones blurred and the edge of the Plain vanished into white. Thicker than anyone on the mountain had ever seen it. Thicker than anyone in the Legacy had ever seen it!
Then the wind came!

It came out of nowhere. There had been no wind on THE Firmament Mountain in all the time Noah had stood there, only the quiet fall, and now there was a wind that howled! It tore across the Plain in a single screaming gust and the snowfall became a blizzard, whipping sideways, stinging, roaring over the golden clouds and the thrones and away across the Legacy.

Noah felt it spread. Across every Elsedimension Mountain in every direction, the black glass peaks and the green ones and the one that burned sullen red, the blizzard came howling down. It tore acros the purple-gold rivers on the Legacy’s floor and whipped them into white-capped waves. It shook the thousands of domains hanging in the sky like lanterns in a storm!

All around the Plain, the Keepers moved at once. Authority rose off them, and Dimensionality with it, spreading out in shields over the clouds of the beings they served. Verys stood behind Noah with one webbed hand raised, and the blizzard broke through.
Conduit Lifeforms scattered from the pillars in bright, frightened flocks, chiming in alarm, and vanished into the white! The golden clouds rocked on the wind.
And then existence began to speak!

There was no voice. There was no cognizance with a name above it, no speaker at all. The knowledge simply arrived, in Noah and in every being on the Plain at the same instant, as cold arrives in the bones on a winter night. Nobody told it to you. You simply knew it, all at once, and could not stop knowing it.
|THE FIRST FROST HAS FALLEN.|
|No new Immensity shall arise.|
|Any Root that attempts to complete itself shall undergo IMMENSE SEVERING.|
|THE COUNTING HAS BEGUN. Existence now counts every Root. Each Root makes the cold heavier upon every other Root, and upon all others besides.|
Every being on the Plain went still inside the howling storm!

On the golden clouds, Progeny and Provenance Lifeforms went pale. The water-woman’s glowing fish went dark all at once. The stag’s bells stopped ringing. Batiatus, who had not stopped talking since he arrived, sat with his mouth open and nothing coming out of it!

Dravos, still being tended at the edge of the Plain, lifted his broken helm toward the sky. More than one of them pressed a hand flat against their chest, over the place where their Root sat, as if they could hold it still.

Above, the thrones perceived it too! Noah felt them take it in, all of them, the vast presences flickering behind the storm. On the throne of black glass, the embers went out entirely. The hollowed star dimmed. Even the hazes, which no one could see, seemed to draw in on themselves, as though something very large had just felt a draft of coldness.
Noah looked at his hands as he...only he did not feel the cold as terrifying as all others did.
But a weight arrived even for him.

It settled onto his Root without any fuss at all. It was there, a pressure that had not existed a heartbeat ago, sitting on the turning mobius at the center of him like snow gathring on a roof. And as he felt it land, he understood with a cold, clean certainty that it would only ever get heavier.
Noah’s expression grew heavy.

Beside him, on the next cloud, Achilles had gritted his teeth. The frost on his lashes thickened as the blizzard poured past him, and inside him Noah could feel the new Root, barely a day old, flicker under the added weight.
Noah sat very still on his cloud, and thought.

Only days ago, he had sat down with THE Writer of Mythos and begun writing a Narrative together. A small thing, it had seemed. One thread pulled, and then another, until Vakochev had been called forth, and an Immense One had died, and waves of cold had poured out of the corpse, and a Hollow Night Lifeform wearing Lucy’s face had risen out of it.
It had only gotten colder since!

And now this. He had come to a Convocation of Roots meaning only to watch and learn. A Progeny of an Immense One had singled him out, fought him, tried to become Immense to prove him wrong, and failed. And because she failed, here was a harder winter than any before it!
No new Immensity, ever. And a cold that grew heavier with every single Root that dared to exist.
All these fucking things kept happening!
He knew he had not caused them. Not really. The Writer had written; Vakochev had come; Minerva had chosen her own gamble. But every time he moved, the winter seemed to grow teeth.

Did he simply need to not fucking do anything? Sit in his Existential Root Domain and never come out? Because it felt, sitting here in the howling snow, that the more he moved, the more everything around him deteriorated!
And then there was the other thing!
It came to him slowly, as he turned the information over, and he did not like it at all.

The Counting did not only press on Roots. Upon every other Root, and upon all others besides, existence had said. All others. Even the Immense Ones would be heavily affected, then. Even the thrones above him would feel the cold grow heavier with every Root that existed.
Which meant that anyone who wanted the cold to ease on themselves now had a very simple way to do it.
Fewer Roots!

If you were an Immense One, and the winter sat heavier on you for every young Root counted beneath you, then every Root that stopped existing would make your own winter a little lighter. Just a little. Just enough to be worth thinking about.
Noah’s expression grew heavier still!
He lifted his head and looked up through the blizzard at the ring of floating thrones.

The snow was so thick now that he could barely see them. Only shapes. The black glass. The bone. The living leaf, empty now. The hollowed star. The hazes. Great vague presences sitting in the storm above the Plain, looking down at the golden clouds where every being with a Root of Immensity sat pale and still.
And it felt, suddenly, as though he were looking up at countless pairs of eyes.
Chilly eyes. Calm eyes. Eyes that had just been handed a very simple sum, and were looking down at him, and at Achilles, and at every other Root on the mountain, and quietly beginning to count!

chapters.title: Chapter 5801: Difficult! I
paragraphs: For a long time, the only sound on THE Firmament Mountain was the blizzard.
Then Sir Moriarty rose from his throne of instruments!
There was no slow, pleased rising this time. He simply stood and when he spoke his voice cut through the howling wind as cleanly as a blade through cloth.
"The Convocation is ended."
The Plain went still inside the storm!
"Every one of you will return to their mountain with their Keeper. Now." His spectacles were white with frost. "There will be no Favors granted. There will be no closing rite. Go."
There was no warmth in it at all. None of the dry amusement, none of the scholar’s delight, nothing but precision, each word set down exactly where it was needed and not one word more.
Nobody argued!

Noah looked out across the Plain, at the blizzard tearing sideways over the golden clouds, white and endless and roaring. He could feel it stretching away past the edge of the mountain, past the Legacy, past anything he could perceive.
It was not only here. He was nearly certain of it. Across every Dimension and every Observable Existence, the same storm was likely raging right now.
Above, one after another, the thrones began to empty!

The pressure of the Immense Ones’ gazes lifted from the Plain like a hand taken off a chest. First the black glass. Then the hollowed star, the bone, the living throne in leaf that had already stood empty. The hazes thinned and vanished. Moriarty was gone. Poona lingered a moment longer than the rest, her bright eyes sweeping once across the golden clouds below, and then she was gone too.
The ring of thrones hung empty in the storm, filling slowly with snow!
On the Plain, the Progeny and Provenance Lifeforms began to disperse.
They did it quietly. The water-woman stepped off her cloud with her fish still dark inside her and let her Keeper lead her away. The stag followed his, antlers bowed, bells silent.

Batiatus went without a word. Keepers led their charges to the edge of the mountain one pair after another, onto the glowing Conduits, and away into the white, until the golden clouds stood mostly empty and the Plain of Accord was only snow.
Noah stayed where he was!
He stood at the edge of his cloud and looked at the place where Minerva had fallen. The snow had nearly buried it already.
"Wow," said a voice beside him. "What a crazy thing your actions had a hand in propagating."
Ling was standing in the snow beside his cloud!
He had not seen her come, and he had not felt her come, which was a great deal more unsettling! One moment the snow beside him was empty, and the next she was simply there, looking up at him.

Her round face was somber for once, the smile gone quiet. But her eyes were bright. They were full of something that was not sorrow at all, a sharp, curious light, like someone who knows a great deal more.
Noah did not turn to look at her.
"I did not have a hand in propagating anything,"he said.
Ling held out her hand, palm up. Snow gathered on it at once, piling up fast, a small white heap in the middle of her palm.

She was dressed for a summer afternoon, not a blizzard at the end of existence. The same blue silk dress embroidered with gold, cut high at both sides, her thick powerful thighs and strong calves bare to the storm but for the white wrap-bands at her ankles.
No coat, no cloak, no fur. The wind tore at her ribons and whipped her spiraled buns and she did not so much as shiver. She stood in the howling white looking perfectly, entirely at ease.
She smiled!
And her voice arrived in his mind, for him alone.
"Every time you take a step, authority shifts beneath you. Every time you open your mouth, the air changes. You make a choice, and existence answers. Cause and effect. It’s that simple."
She tipped her palm, and the little heap of snow slid off it.

"Some people love to cry about bad luck. They point at their ruined existence and call it an accident. A twist of fate. A coincidence. But nothing in this life is coincidental. Whether you want to admit it or hide behind it, causality is inescapable. Every choice you ever made has an effect."
Her eyes went to the buried green glow in the snow.

"Minerva did what she did of her own will. But you were among the things that came together to make it happen as it happened. Is it bad luck that she had to be the first one to try to become Immense, only to fail? That the new conditions of existence were revealed through her, and the cold got colder?"
She hummed. "Hmm. We just said luck is something people cry about. There’s no fate. There’s no luck. There’s only us. What we are, and what we choose to do, Big Boy."
The snow poured down around them.
"And I’ve made a choice. It’ll have its own causality, same as everything. I’m inviting you to my mountain."
An invitation to her mountain? Now? In the middle of all this?
Noah turned his head, finally, and looked at her!
"Whatever for?"he sent back, for her alone.
Ling blinked at him. Then she smiled brilliantly.
"Why," she said, "to put your head between my thighs and see if I can crack it."
Noah said nothing!
Ling laughed!

"Kidding." She tilted her head, and for a moment the brightness in her eyes went very focused. "I’ve made a choice, and so has the Immense One behind me. Someone a great deal more powerful than Sir Moriarty, and a great deal more mysterious, wants to have a talk with you."
She held out her hand, palm up again, empty this time. "Walk with me?"
Noah looked around!
The Plain of Accord was nearly empty now, a white field under a white sky, the blizzard howling across it and the empty thrones hanging overhead full of snow.

A few golden clouds still held figures. On the nearest one, Achilles had drawn Rose close against his side, one arm around her, frost thick on both of them, his solemn eyes on the storm. Rose’s face was pressed into his shoulder. Neither of them was looking at anything but each other.
Noah looked back at the girl who was a Root, entirely, from her skin to her core.
A mysterious Immense One. More powerful than Moriarty.
He needed time to think anyway. Maybe an Immense One would be illuminating.
He nodded!
Ling grinned. She flicked one foot against the snow, a light, careless little motion, and her hand snaked out and closed around his. Her grip was warm.
She flicked her foot again.
And the two of them were gone!
In the place where they had stood, the snow crashed down harder than before, filling in their footprnts in an instant, as though the blizzard had been waiting for them to leave.
Ling’s mountain was unlike any other in the Legacy.

It rose alone out of the blizzard, wrapped from root to hidden peak in a trembling golden-violet haze. That haze was the light of an Immensity, burning steadily and deliberately all the way around, and where the storm struck it, the snow simply stopped. The blizzard screamed and whipped against it and could not get through. Like a massive coat of Immensity wrapped around an entire mountain!
Ling let go of his hand and went ahead up the slope.

Inside the haze there was no snow, and yet the mountain was cold! Its slopes were dull grey-black stone, the air still and heavy. Gnarled trees with bark like old iron lined the way, their branches bent back on themselves, and every one of them was shivering in the windless air, as if they remembered the cold even with it kept out.
Ahead, a cave swelled out of the mountainside like a great stone throat, twisted trees crowding its mouth and pale smoke drifting out of it.
Ling went in without slowing. Noah followed, and at the stone lip, his sight bloomed.
|You are entering the periphery of an Existential Immense Domain.|
|The Immense One who controls it holds absolute authority within it.|
|Although, to be clear, it would hardly matter whether they wished you harm here or anywhere else.|
Noah stopped!

A little way into the misty tunnel, Ling turned her head, the smoke curling around her face. For a moment she did not look like a cheerful girl who had run late up a Conduit. She looked like something that lived in a place like this.
"I don’t bite," she said. "Neither will the owner of this place. Come on."
Noah did not do afraid. And even if he had, curiosity had always won that argument in him. He stepped in!
The tunnel was long and close and warm, its walls damp under his fingertips, so thick with mist he could barely see her blue silk ahead of him. The smell of incense grew stronger with every step.
Then it opened into a cavern!
Its ceiling was lost in the dark and mist filled all of it, grey banks rolling slow across the floor. It felt enormous, and occupied, like a room where someone sits very still in a corner.
Ling stopped at the edge of the mist and stretched, arms high, then bending one leg and the other, her powerful thighs flexing and loosening under the silk.
For a moment she simply stood there with her eyes closed, the mist curling around her ankles, as if listening for something only she could hear. She breathed out.
And then...she danced!

It began slow: one step, her arms sweeping a wide, flowing arc, drawing a circle on the air. Her body turned with it and the arc continued unbroken, circles within circles, every motion flowing into the next with no seam between them. Her face had gone calm and far away. She was a priestess at a rite, and the rite was her.
Then her feet struck the stone!
DUM!

Heel, then ball, a hard stamp that rolled through the cavern like a drum. Another. A rhythm rising, older than words. Her palms struck her own thighs and chest in time, call and answer, skin answering stone. Her hips moved loose and grounded, her body sinking low toward the earth and rising again, arms flung wide.
With every turn, the mist drew back from her in rings!

And as it cleared, flames appeared! Purple torches set in the cavern walls kindled one after another as the mist fell away from them, two, then six, then a great ring of dozens burning deep, steady violet, throwing long trembling shadows across the stone and across the dancing girl at the center of it all.

The rhythm quickened. Her turns tightened, and the violet light caught on her and trailed behind her hands like ribbons of flame. Twelve turnings, Noah counted, each one different, and on the twelfth she spun so fast the purple light wrapped her entirely!
|You are witnessing a NARRATIVE INSCRIPTION RITUAL DANCE: THE Kindled Circle.|
|It is not performed. It is written, with the body, onto the domain.|
|Each turning draws the dancer closer to their own Root of Immensity, attuning existence and Root to one another.|
|Performed to its Truest Essence, the distance between the two closes entirely. The dancer and their Root become one.|
Noah went very still!

Become one with their Root? He looked at the girl spinning in the violet light, at the panel of 1s he had read on the Plain, at the being whose Root did not sit inside her but was her, from her skin to her core.
So that was how! Somewhere, at some point, she had danced this until there was nothing left between her and her Root at all, and whatever she had been before that, she had stopped being it.
The last haze thinned at the far end of the cavern, where the ring of torches met, and lifted. Behind it lay an old, faded prayer mat.
And on it sat an Immense One!
Noah could not quite see it. Its Dimensionality ran so deep that his sight kept sliding off its edges. But he saw enough to know he would never forget it.

It sat, vast as a mountain range drawn down into the shape of a giant. Enormous prayer beads, each the size of a boulder, dark and polished by some unimaginable span of handling, hung around its hands and thick forearms on a cord older than many. Its eyes were open, pale and pupil-less, and slow tears ran from them down a broad, solemn face, hissing faintly where they met the violet fire at its jaw.

And yet the mouth beneath was set in a wide, fierce line, almost a smile, burning with terrible cheerful certainty. Its hair rose from its brow like a mane of fire, and the fire was purple, wreathing its shoulders and beads and knees in slow, deep violet.
It wept, and it smiled, and it burned!
Unmoving and silent, it sat on its prayer mat, and its weight filled the whole mountain!
Ling’s dance wound down to stillness directly in front of Noah. She rose tall, lifted her arms once toward the ceiling, and let out one long breath, the purple light sliding off her like water.
Then she sat cross-legged on a second mat laid before the prayer mat, patted the empty space beside her, and looked back over her shoulder.
"Come."
Noah stood a moment longer, looking at the weeping, smiling, burning thing!

This was what an Immense One felt like. Poona waving from a golden throne, Moriarty adjusting his spectacles over a corpse, those had been Immense Ones choosing to look like something he could stand beside.
This one chose nothing. It simply was, and the air pressed on him so heavily that he had to decide, deliberately, to keep breathing it.
Why would a being like this call him here?
The answer was not his yet. He wanted it!
So he crossed the cavern floor between the purple torches, sat down on the mat beside Ling, and looked up at the Immense One.

A mysterious Immense One.
More powerful than Moriarty.
He needed time to think anyway.
Maybe an Immense One would be illuminating.
He nodded!
Ling grinned.
She flicked one foot against the snow, a light, careless little motion, and her hand snaked out and closed around his.
Her grip was warm.
She flicked her foot again.
And the two of them were gone!
In the place where they had stood, the snow crashed down harder than before, filling in their footprnts in an instant, as though the blizzard had been waiting for them to leave.
Ling’s mountain was unlike any other in the Legacy.
It rose alone out of the blizzard, wrapped from root to hidden peak in a trembling golden-violet haze.
That haze was the light of an Immensity, burning steadily and deliberately all the way around, and where the storm struck it, the snow simply stopped.
The blizzard screamed and whipped against it and could not get through.
Like a massive coat of Immensity wrapped around an entire mountain!
Ling let go of his hand and went ahead up the slope.
Inside the haze there was no snow, and yet the mountain was cold!
Its slopes were dull grey-black stone, the air still and heavy.

Gnarled trees with bark like old iron lined the way, their branches bent back on themselves, and every one of them was shivering in the windless air, as if they remembered the cold even with it kept out.
Ahead, a cave swelled out of the mountainside like a great stone throat, twisted trees crowding its mouth and pale smoke drifting out of it.
Ling went in without slowing.
Noah followed, and at the stone lip, his sight bloomed.
|You are entering the periphery of an Existential Immense Domain.|
|The Immense One who controls it holds absolute authority within it.|
|Although, to be clear, it would hardly matter whether they wished you harm here or anywhere else.|
Noah stopped!
A little way into the misty tunnel, Ling turned her head, the smoke curling around her face.
For a moment she did not look like a cheerful girl who had run late up a Conduit.
She looked like something that lived in a place like this.
"I don’t bite," she said.
"Neither will the owner of this place.
Come on."
Noah did not do afraid.
And even if he had, curiosity had always won that argument in him.
He stepped in!
The tunnel was long and close and warm, its walls damp under his fingertips, so thick with mist he could barely see her blue silk ahead of him.
The smell of incense grew stronger with every step.
Then it opened into a cavern!
Its ceiling was lost in the dark and mist filled all of it, grey banks rolling slow across the floor.
It felt enormous, and occupied, like a room where someone sits very still in a corner.
Ling stopped at the edge of the mist and stretched, arms high, then bending one leg and the other, her powerful thighs flexing and loosening under the silk.
For a moment she simply stood there with her eyes closed, the mist curling around her ankles, as if listening for something only she could hear.
She breathed out.
And then...she danced!
It began slow: one step, her arms sweeping a wide, flowing arc, drawing a circle on the air.
Her body turned with it and the arc continued unbroken, circles within circles, every motion flowing into the next with no seam between them.
Her face had gone calm and far away.
She was a priestess at a rite, and the rite was her.
Then her feet struck the stone!
DUM!
Heel, then ball, a hard stamp that rolled through the cavern like a drum.
Another.
A rhythm rising, older than words.
Her palms struck her own thighs and chest in time, call and answer, skin answering stone.
Her hips moved loose and grounded, her body sinking low toward the earth and rising again, arms flung wide.
With every turn, the mist drew back from her in rings!
And as it cleared, flames appeared!

Purple torches set in the cavern walls kindled one after another as the mist fell away from them, two, then six, then a great ring of dozens burning deep, steady violet, throwing long trembling shadows across the stone and across the dancing girl at the center of it all.
The rhythm quickened.
Her turns tightened, and the violet light caught on her and trailed behind her hands like ribbons of flame.
Twelve turnings, Noah counted, each one different, and on the twelfth she spun so fast the purple light wrapped her entirely!
|You are witnessing a NARRATIVE INSCRIPTION RITUAL DANCE: THE Kindled Circle.|
|It is not performed.
It is written, with the body, onto the domain.|
|Each turning draws the dancer closer to their own Root of Immensity, attuning existence and Root to one another.|
|Performed to its Truest Essence, the distance between the two closes entirely.
The dancer and their Root become one.|
Noah went very still!
Become one with their Root?
He looked at the girl spinning in the violet light, at the panel of 1s he had read on the Plain, at the being whose Root did not sit inside her but was her, from her skin to her core.
So that was how!
Somewhere, at some point, she had danced this until there was nothing left between her and her Root at all, and whatever she had been before that, she had stopped being it.
The last haze thinned at the far end of the cavern, where the ring of torches met, and lifted.
Behind it lay an old, faded prayer mat.
And on it sat an Immense One!
Noah could not quite see it.
Its Dimensionality ran so deep that his sight kept sliding off its edges.
But he saw enough to know he would never forget it.
It sat, vast as a mountain range drawn down into the shape of a giant.
Enormous prayer beads, each the size of a boulder, dark and polished by some unimaginable span of handling, hung around its hands and thick forearms on a cord older than many.
Its eyes were open, pale and pupil-less, and slow tears ran from them down a broad, solemn face, hissing faintly where they met the violet fire at its jaw.
And yet the mouth beneath was set in a wide, fierce line, almost a smile, burning with terrible cheerful certainty.
Its hair rose from its brow like a mane of fire, and the fire was purple, wreathing its shoulders and beads and knees in slow, deep violet.
It wept, and it smiled, and it burned!
Unmoving and silent, it sat on its prayer mat, and its weight filled the whole mountain!
Ling’s dance wound down to stillness directly in front of Noah.
She rose tall, lifted her arms once toward the ceiling, and let out one long breath, the purple light sliding off her like water.
Then she sat cross-legged on a second mat laid before the prayer mat, patted the empty space beside her, and looked back over her shoulder.
"Come."
Noah stood a moment longer, looking at the weeping, smiling, burning thing!
This was what an Immense One felt like.
Poona waving from a golden throne, Moriarty adjusting his spectacles over a corpse, those had been Immense Ones choosing to look like something he could stand beside.
This one chose nothing.
It simply was, and the air pressed on him so heavily that he had to decide, deliberately, to keep breathing it.
Why would a being like this call him here?
The answer was not his yet.
He wanted it!
So he crossed the cavern floor between the purple torches, sat down on the mat beside Ling, and looked up at the Immense One.

chapters.title: Chapter 5802: Difficult! II
paragraphs: Noah watched the Immense One on the prayer mat, and in the next moment, it spoke!
|THE THINKER AT THE END OF EXISTENCE welcomes you.|

The voice rose out of the stone and the purple torches and the thin mist lingering in the corners, deep enough to rumble in Noah’s ribs like a great drum struck softly. There was no cruelty in it. There was courtesy, and patience, and underneath both a distance so vast that every word seemed to fall from very far above.
The beads around its forearms shifted, click by heavy click, though its hands never moved.
|"Existence will only grow harder from here. The winter will be colder, and a great many will die in it. That is simply what existence is now, as we walk into an age that very few are ready for."|
|"In time, even the Immense will be fighting over warmth."|
The beads clicked again.
|"But set all of that aside. Tell me something. In all of existence, at this very hour, who would you say carries the hardest adversity?"|
Noah listened with everything he had!

Every word from this being was heavy. Heavy, like a word carried for a very long time before it was finally set down. And the manner of it was old, older than any voice he had heard, measured and unhurried.
But the question itself was simple.
"Those who have formed their Roots," Noah said calmly.
The tears kept running from those pale, pupil-less eyes, hissing where they met the violet fire at its jaw.

|"You cannot advance. And now you may be hunted besides, your Roots cut away so the cold sits a little lighter on everyone else. And yet it was in this very cold that the newly risen Immense were meant to open the door. They were to be the Key to THE Great Becoming. And now not one of them can become Immense at all."|
A long, rumbling sigh moved through the cavern.
|"A conundrum, isn’t it?"|
The purple flames around its shoulders rose, slow, and settled.

|"The air is growing thinner. With the coming of THE Long Night, existence will grow colder and colder from here. The frost is not going to thaw, and it is not going to take pity on anyone. Those who became Immense before this fell upon us do not hold the key. Even I do not hold it, as I..."|
It stopped.
Then, slowly, the Immense One turned on its prayer mat!
The beads dragged across the stone. The great kneeling shape shifted, vast as a mountain range turning in its sleep, until THE THINKER AT THE END OF EXISTENCE had its back to them. And Noah saw.
A gash ran down it!

It began at the crown of its head and ran the whole length of its back, a single enormous wound, deep and ragged and wide enough to lose a Dimension in. The edges were torn. Its purple fire could not close over it; the flames reached for the edges and sputtered and fell back. And the wound was full of frost!

Thick white rime packed into it and spiling over its lips, cold so dense it steamed against the heat of the flames, and through the frost, faintly, a light was leaking. Immensity. The Thinker’s own Immensity, seeping out of it in thin pale threads, drifting up into the cavern air and fading.
Gory, and heavy, and wrong. It looked like something that should have killed whatever carried it a long time ago!
Beside Noah, Ling was on her feet.

She had risen so suddenly that her mat skidded on the stone, and her face had gone the color of old ash. The cheer was gone from it entirely. Her eyes were wide and fixed on the wound, and her hands had come up in front of her as though she could reach across the cavern and hold it shut.
"Father..." Her voice cracked. "What is this?! When did this happen?! What the fucking fuck?!"
Father.
Slowly, the Thinker turned back around to face them. The fierce almost-smile had not changed. The tears had not stopped.
It looked at Ling. Then at Noah.
|"I am dying."|
BOOM!
An Immense One was dying!
Noah sat very still on his mat. An Immense One, one of the beings at the top of all existence, was dying in front of him, and its wound was made of cold.

His eyes flickered. He thought of a frost-visage wearing Lucy’s face, rising out of the snow of the Vasiliou Elsedimension to strike down THE UNPAID COLLECTOR, and of how he had held his wife in the snow and called that Immense One a bum until it came down to die.
He thought of the Overseeing One above the frozen forest. And now here was a third, kneeling on a prayer mat with the winter packed into its back.
Beside him, Ling sat down.

She did not so much sit as collapse, all at once, as though whatever had been holding her up had simply let go. She sat on her mat with her powerful legs tucked beneath her and her hands limp in her lap, and her eyes were ashen and empty, staring at nothing. It was as though the bright cheerful soul Noah had watched laugh through a bloody bout had simply gone out of her.
The Thinker looked at Noah.
|"The winter is brutal on us all. I tried to find answers by going into the winter itself. And this was the result."|
The faint threads of Immensity kept rising from behind it, fading into the dark.
|"My Immensity was too bright. It drew in things that were brighter still, and far more terrible."|
Noah raised his head.
"Where exactly did you go?"
He had to ask. He had an inkling, and he did not like it.
The fierce line of the Thinker’s mouth widened, very slightly, into something that was almost a smile.
|"I went where you have gone. That is why I brought you here."|

|"Any Immense One who goes there meets a certain death. A few of us, the more reckless ones, studied the cold as soon as it came. We took it into our own bodies. We learned where it leads. And yet when we went into that place, the answer that came back at us was so very heavy."|
The pale eyes held him.
|"Why do you suppose that is?"|
The Cold Place!
Noah’s eyes were bright. He did not answer.

There was no need. He knew the frozen seas and the seated dead and the rivers of cold that poured out of the dark and away across existence. He had knelt in them, and drunk them, and walked back out again, every time.
|"Wherever the opposition is greatest,"|the Thinker went on, mild as ever, |"that is where the answers are. The answers to this winter lie past that place. Past that doorway of endless cold."|
"A doorway?" Noah said. "The Cold Place is a doorway?"
|"Is that what you call it?"| A small, dry sound, very nearly a laugh. |"Its true name is THE Undersnow. And the first place you arrive when you go down is only its doorway."|
The beads clicked, slowly.

|"The Long Night was meant to be hard. It was never meant to be obscene, or impossible. When I began to die, even my Teacher was surprised, and she reached out to me. The Long Night has been tainted, she said. The adversity of it, the turning of the great cycles of existence, has been interfered with. And not even an Immense One should have the power to do such a thing."|
The flames sank low around its shoulders.

|"As things stand, it will only grow colder. Even the common masses, even the lifeforms that hold no authority at all and were never meant to freeze in this Night, even they will become blocks of ice. And the conditions laid upon the Immense are heavy. They were made so that we cannot even come close to the answer."|
The pale, weeping gaze settled on Noah and stayed there.
|"But others can come close. Others can enter THE Undersnow and come back alive."|
|"Others like you."|
BOOM!
Noah’s gaze flickered, and his eyes grew heavy!
The Thinker watched him a moment longer. Then, slowly, tenderly, it rose.

It leaned forward from its prayer mat, vast and burning, the frost-packed wound shifting on its back, and reached out its enormous hands, the great beads swinging and clicking from its forearms, and gathered Ling up off her mat as gently as someone lifting a sleeping child, and drew her into its lap, and held her there.
Ling did not resist. She curled against it, small against the great burning chest, her ashen eyes wet.
The Thinker stroked her hed. Its enormous hand moved over her spiraled buns and her loose white ribbons, slow and careful, the purple fire parting around her so it would not touch her.
|"I have lived a very long time. I do not care much about dying."|
Its hand kept moving over her hair.
|"But I want my Progeny to live fruitful lives. I do not want them to freeze into nothing."|
It looked up at Noah over the top of Ling’s head.

|"There is a prophecy going around. It speaks of THE Long Night, and of three key figures who might be its answer. Moriarty and a few others believe you may be one of them, since yours was the first Root formed after the Night began."|
|"I think it is a smoke screen. A trick. There are no chosen ones in existence. Much less some tidy, neat set of instructions for surviving the Long Night."|
The beads clicked.

|"I think a bill that went unpaid for a very long time has finally come due. Things were done in the past. My Teacher, THE ACHARYA OF IMMENSITY, did things in the past. Good things. Bad things. The First Sundering was one of them, and a great deal of what came after is connected to it."|

|"There are no chosen ones who will come to save everyone. But there is cause and effect. Every deed calls back its answer, measure for measure. And sometimes the answer that comes back is far larger than the deed, and far more terrible. That is THE Long Night."|
Its hand paused on Ling’s hair.

|"But its coming also leaves ways for existence to adapt. Something, for example, that can take the cold of that Night into itself and not come apart. Something that can enter its gateway and walk into whatever secrets lie beneath it. Or, for example, a whole lifeform whose entire existence is a Root."|
It looked down at the girl in its lap, and back up.
|"Existence finds a way. So no. You are not chosen. You were favored by probability, lucky enough to have access, and strong enough to survive it. That is all. It is also a great deal."|
The pale eyes did not leave him.
|"Tell me. Do you have family? Attachments?"|
The question boomed out through the cavern.
Noah raised his head, somber, and looked at this vast dying being with its daughter in its lap. The Thinker did not wait for his answer.
|"THE Long Night will strip a great many families of every scrap of warmth and love they have. We need to find out what happened. And we need to change the course of things."|
The flames rose, slow and steady.

|"I am sure I am not the only one. You may not be the only one either. A great many lives across existence will move, each trying to find their own answer. Legacies will believe they have found the chosen beings who will save them, and perhaps they have. Who knows? But none of us can sit back and wait, and hope that someone else finds the answer first."|
It looked down at its wound, then back at Noah.
|"So I am here, though I am dying. I have thought through a great many probabilities, and I am THE THINKER AT THE END OF EXISTENCE. My distinction has made me grand even in the face of all this."|
The beads went still.
|"Dreamer. It is going to be brutal. But may I back you, as you seek answers in the places the Immense cannot reach?"|
The fierce almost-smile widened.
|"I am dying. But I can die for a long time. After all, I am THE THINKER AT THE END OF EXISTENCE."|
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5803: THE Undersnow I
paragraphs: A dying Immense One wanted to back him.

Noah sat on the mat with that thought. He was being offered protection to go and uncover mysteries he could not even begin to fathom yet. The cold that had grown teeth. The door that had shut in Minerva’s face. A Night that was never supposed to be obscene, tainted by something no Immense One should have had the power to touch.
And he had his own questions too.

Every second that passed, his attributes grew heavier. THE Osmontian Inscription of THE Dreaming Hour pressed and pressed at him, one passing second worth an entire day, compressing his Provenance down tighter and tighter, and he was climbing. He could feel it. He was walking toward Immensity one packed second at a time!
And existence had just made it perfectly clear that nothing was allowed to become Immense.
He wanted to understand that. He wanted to understand it very badly!

But more than that, under all of it, he thought of his mother, his son, his daughter. Of his women, and every life sleeping in THE Infiniverse, dreaming their long dreams on a golden shore. He did not want those dreams frozen solid. If things were only going to grow colder, and harder, as time passed, then he needed to know why. And if it could be put right, he needed to put it right.

It would have been easy to call this a natural cycle of existence. But THE THINKER had said the Night was tainted. He had said it was a bill, coming due for something the Immense had done a very long time ago.
What had they even done?
There were so many things he wanted to know. But first things first.
"You said you want to back me," Noah said. "How?"
The beads clicked. The tears kept falling. In THE Thinker’s lap, Ling lay curled and silent, her ashen eyes open.
|"The existence that is now taking shape will give very different priorities to different lives,"|THE Thinker said.

|"The lives of those who might change things will matter more than ever. And the ones the Immense believe to be among the three will be the most critical of all. To be watched. To be guarded. They are the only answer many of the Immense believe in. The only way through the cold that still opens the door, so that they need no longer be merely Those Who Remain."|
A long, rumbling breath echoed.

|"I do not believe in chosen ones, as I have told you. But you are still a figure who will need protecting while you do what you must. Because I do not believe it, but others do. Moriarty believes it. And it is very hard to say what believers will do, given enough time and enough cold."|
The purple flames settled lower.
|"There is more. A friend of mine, in another Legacy, has told me that they hold someone they have affirmed as one of the three. They have held that belief for a very long time. THE Sealed One."|
Noah’s eyes narrowed.
|"And among the things he has discovered is your name. It has gotten out, you see. The first Root to form after THE Long Night began."|

The Thinker’s voice stayed mild. |"Though he is no longer sealed, so I suppose he is simply Riven now. THE Riven. He is being groomed as one who can reach the answer and find the key. And among the many things he has said he wants is you."|
The beads clicked, once, very slowly.

|"So I expect Immense Ones will move at his word to obtain what he wants. Out of their own belief. Because they want him to be the key. Because they want the door opened, so that they are no longer only Those Who Remain."|
|"Existence has become so brutal and so ridiculous that it is reaching a point where lesser beings merely wave their hands and give commands, and the Immense move to fulfill them."|
The pale, weeping eyes held him.
|"Until I die, I can be your backer. That much I can promise."|
Noah thought about that for a long moment.
The fucking Sealed One. Riven!
He had dragged himself into a position like that, the favored candidate of an entire Legacy of Immense Ones, with Immense Ones ready to move at his word? And he was still gunning for him?
Of course he was!
Noah’s eyes flashed with decisiveness. He nodded.
"Very well. I will go and confirm things regarding the Cold Place....THE Undersnow, for now."
THE Thinker’s weeping eyes shone!

For the first time, they did not look distant at all. They blazed, bright and resplendent, as though something very old had just been given a reason to keep going a little longer. The great hands moved in its lap. Tenderly, it lifted its daughter, and turned her round to face Noah.
|"Take her as well. Remember, it will be brutal, and hard, and you cannot do this alone. Little Ling is one of my greatest accomplishments. She will not slow you down."|
Ling’s eyes had changed.
The ash was gone from them. In its place was fire, bright and furious. She wiped her tears away with the back of her wrist, hard, and turned her head to look up at her father.
"Something in there did this to you. Yes?"
The Thinker did not answer.
"Then I’ll just have to fuck it up myself," Ling said. She turned back to Noah, and her face was fierce and burning and very young. "Hey, Big Boy. Let’s go."
Her eyes burned with a furious light!

Noah lifted his hand. Rivers of his Provenance slid out of him, blue and gold, and wound around her wrist, binding her existence to his for the crossing. Then, still sitting on the mat, he closed his eyes and turned his thoughts downward. To the Cold Place. To THE Undersnow.
His Root pulsed. It held the weavings of THE Long Night inside it, packed into every quark he owned, and those weavings answered.
He felt himself begin to sink.
Down, out of the purple-lit cavern and the kneeling burning giant, down through the stone and the snow and the dark, his existence sliding toward that unfathomable place!
He opened his eyes in the Cold Place.
The frozen seas stretched away to every horizon, blue and white and shining, as they always had. Drifting crystals hung in the air, and the rivers of cold still rolled out of the dark.
But the Hollow Night Lifeforms were gone!

Every one of them. The countless seated dead, the ranks upon ranks of blank-eyed things in their turning pillars of cold, the beasts and giants and lions with wrong heads, all of them gone. The rivers ran over nothing, and the great frozen expanse lay empty as far as he could see.
And the place where the Caretaker had always stood, her pages turning around her in the air, was empty too.
Noah stood very still.
Beside him, the air shivered, and Ling appeared.

She landed in a crouch on the frozen sea, then sprang up and turned in a full circle, looking everywhere at once. Her face was ferocious. It was also, somehow, still a little cute, round-cheeked and fierce, a small furious thing glaring at an entire frozen underworld as if it had personally insulted her family, which, as far as she was concerned, it had.
She finished her circle and looked at him, and her voice was earnest.
"You didn’t have to agree to anything. So thank you in advance. For moving on this, and looking into it." She planted her hands on her hips.

"My father can say he’s dying all he likes. But his Immensity is exactly that... immense. He’s THE Thinker at the End of Existence. Just think how well that name fits these times." Her eyes sharpened."If you make any headway into all this, I’ll reward you too."
Her words were sharp and her eyes were sharper.
Noah listened while he looked around. The empty seas, the empty place where the Caretaker should have been, the rivers of cold pouring on over nothing.
His gaze grew firm. He rose, and looked out across the endless frozen seas.
"Let’s go."
He dove!
Straight down, into the sea of cold, and it closed over his head like a lid. Ling hit the water a heartbeat behind him, and followed.

The sea was colder than anything he had ever touched. Colder than the rivers he had drunk in the frozen underworld, colder than the Collector’s gaze, a cold so deep it seemed to have a weight of its own, pressing in from every side. It was white-blue and faintly luminous, and the deeper they went the darker and denser it grew, until it was less like water and more like diving through the frozen heart of a glacier.
Noah’s body drank it.

The cold poured into him through his skin and ran straight down into his Root, and his Root took it and refined it, pressing it down into the packed quarks alongside his Provenance and the Long Night already waiting there. Every stroke deeper, he grew a little denser. A little colder. A little more himself.

Beside him, Ling swam down through the freezing dark as though it were a warm pond in summer. The cold did not touch her at all. It slid off her bare arms and her powerful legs and her fluttering white ribbons and found nothing to take hold of. She was a Root, all the way through, with a unique quality!
Down. Further down. The light above them dimmed to nothing. The pressure mounted. Down past anything Noah had ever reached in the Cold Place, past anything he had even known was there!
And after a long while...
POP!

They passed through something. A barrier, thin and taut as the skin on a drum, and it burst around them. The sea’s pressure vanished all at once, and instead of sinking further they were rising, carried upward, breaking out through the surface of a white-blue sea into open air.
Noah surfaced, and looked around, and went still.
It was terrible, and it was wondrous!

Radiant frozen landmasses floated all around them, vast islands of blue-white ice glowing faintly from within, drifting slowly through a dim, endless sky. Trees grew on them, towering trees taller than mountains, their trunks and branches filled with cold, rimed so thick they glittered like frozen lightning. And everywhere, hanging in the air between the floating islands in their thousands, were Dimensions and Observable Existences.
Broken ones.

Every single one of them was shattered. Ripped in half, some of them, cleanly, as though something enormous had taken each one in its hands and torn it apart. Others were cracked through like dropped plates, their broken halves drifting slowly apart with seas and continents and dead frozen cities spilling out of the tears. Thousands upon thousands of them, a whole sky full of torn realities, hanging frozen in the dark.
Ruination’s prompts came fast. She was reading every thread of information she could reach, as quickly as she could reach it, and her words came clipped and urgent.
|Master. You have arrived at THE BASAL FLOOR of THE Undersnow.|
|Multiple dangerous lifeforms sensed nearby. Designation: EMPOWERED HOLLOW NIGHT LIFEFORMS.|
|Each one appears to hold a LESSER KRYOS EXISTENTIAL CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN within its existence.|
Noah let out a long, heavy breath.

There truly was more to the Cold Place than he had ever known. A whole existence under the ice, and he had been standing on its doorstep all along. Would the answers be here, somewhere, among the broken realities and the frozen islands? Would anything here be willing to give them up?
Before he could even settle his thoughts...
KAAA!
A cry split the frozen sky!
Something came down out of the dark and landed on the edge of a floating island directly above them, and the whole island dipped under its weight.
It was a crow.

It was the size of a mountain range, and it was wrong in evry way a crow could be wrong. Its feathers were long jagged shards of black ice, layered and overlapping and chiming faintly against each other whenever it moved, and through the gaps between them Noah could see its ribs, white and bare, glazed in frost.

Its beak was a great curving tower of dark rime, cracked along its length, long enough to impale a Dimension, and its talons hooked over the edge of the island like iron grapnels, and where they gripped, the ice spread in white veins.

It had many eyes. They ran in rows down both sides of its head, a dozen or more, each one a pale cold blue and each one fixed on him. And on its head sat a crown. A tall, jagged crown of frozen spikes, branching like the antlers of some dead king, glittering with a light that was colder than light had any right to be.
Tattered banners of snow trailed from its wings. A halo of drifting frost circled it slowly, like a ring of dust around a dying star.
It looked down at Noah with every one of its eyes, and the weight of it came down on him!
It was suffocating. Not Immense. Not quite. But heavy, crushing, a presure that pressed on his Root and on the Counting’s weight already sitting there, and made both of them heavier.
|You are not allowed here.|
|Return.|
Noah’s gaze grew heavy.
"What if I do not wish to return?"he said. "What if I want answers?"
The crow looked down at him, cold and unblinking, and slowly spread its great wings. Rivers of snow streamed from them in the dark.
|There are no answers.|
|There is only THE Long Night.|
Noah breathed out.
He rolled his shoulders. He stretched, loosening his arms, his back, his neck. And golden clouds began to spill from him, soft and bright, drifting out across the white-blue sea.

Beside him, Ling had gone utterly still, and then not still at all. Her thighs were trembling with readiness. Her whole body hummed with it, every muscle drawn tight, her powerful legs vibrating faintly beneath her, as though her entire existence had become a single coiled weapon waiting for someone to let it loose!
Noah looked up at the crow again.
"In this epoch, I intend to be supreme," he said. "And it seems I will have to become more dominating than I have ever been. Existence wants to be brutal? Okay!"
His eyes shone. "Then I will be more brutal. I will be unfair."
"I can be very unfair!"
HUUM!
An infinite pillar of dreams erupted out of him!

It tore up from the white-blue sea in a column of golden light that did not end, stretching up past the floating islands and the broken Dimensions and away into the dark. And out of it, wreathed in it, a fiendish creature made of dreams, Noah shot upward toward the frozen crown!
