chapters.title: Chapter 5804: The Undersnow II
paragraphs: When Noah thought back across his whole existence, there had been times he could only be called a bully.

He had been terrifying with his power. Overpowered, grand, tyrannical, a being who walked into a war and ended it with a single drop of his blood or mana while armies wept at the edge of his shadow. He did not regret it. It had been who he was, and what the moment needed.

But the higher he climbed, the more complicated existence became. The beings grew stranger. The rules grew deeper. And it grew harder and harder to simply overpower anything, even with everything that made him unique.
Harder. Not impossible.

And through all of it, in every one of those moments when he had stood over something that should have crushed him, there had been one answer to his terrible immensity. One thing underneath all the others.
His Infinity.
So.
He looked at the crow ahead, and his sight opened it!
|EMPOWERED HOLLOW NIGHT LIFEFORM.|
|VERITAS: 999 (+100). PROVENANCE: 999 (+100). POTENTIA: 999 (+100). PONDUS: 999 (+100).|
Nine hundred and ninety-nine, and a hundred more on top of each line!

Noah’s eyes narrowed as he flew. The base alone matched Minerva, the very ceiling she had hit and broken herself against. And then a hundred more in everything, sitting on top of it like a borrowed coat. Where did that come from? The Basal Floor? The cold itself, feeding the things that lived in it? Or something the crow carried inside it, a stolen heart of true Immensity pushing it past a limit it could not reach alone?
He did not know. It did not matter yet. What mattered was that it was stronger than him on paper, in every line!
And yet his numbers were packed and its numbers were hollow. He had learned that much in the snow. Digits were only what existence could be bothered to count. They were never the whole of a thing.
He raised his hand.
"I AM."
HUUM!
He was.
But he was what?

With those two words he pulled every ounce of his Provenance and every scrap of his power together into a single point, and it came out of him as an aurora of dreams. Blue and gold, incandescent, drawn out long and thin and sharp into the shape of a blade, and it shot across the frozen sky toward the crow with a sound like the largest bell in existence being struck once and cut off!
It hit the crow full on!
The crow lowered its head and met it with its beak.
BOOM!

The blade of dreams struck the cracked tower of rime and broke apart against it, scattering into drifting golden sparks. At most, the crow’s head rocked back a fraction, and a thin line of frost cracked along the edge of its beak. That was all.
Little damage. Almost none!
But...
"THE MORTAL COIL."
HUUM!

Golden clouds descended. They came down out of the frozen dark all around the crow, settling over the snow and the floating islands and the torn Dimensions, soft and bright and silent, and wherever they touched, borrowed things began, quietly, to be disallowed. The crow’s hundred extra points flickered. The cold in its feathers wavered.
Every eye it had narrowed! A low sound rattled in its throat, the first sound it had made since it told him there were no answers. It had felt the Coil land, and it did not like it.
"I AM!"
HUUM!

A second aurora of dreams tore out of him, brighter, sharper, a blade of blue-gold light shearing through the air. It hit the crow across the breast, and this time something gave. Black-ice feathers sheared away in a spray, a handful of them, spinning off into the dark as glittering shards!
Out of nowhere, Ling appeared beside the crow’s head.

She had not flown there. She was simply there, one leg already rising, and it came down in a single swing. Her thigh pulsed with a physicality so terrifying that the air around it bent. It hit the crow in the side of the skul, and the whole mountain-range bulk of it was knocked sideways off its island, sent hurtling through the frozen sky straight at Noah!
KAAAA!
The crow screamed as it tumbled, and the storm of its cold howled after it, black feathers and blue-white frost streaming off it like smoke off a comet.
He bellowed it again.
"I AM!"

Another blade tore out of him, and another, every repetition of the words a new eruption of dreams, each one carving across the tumbling crow. His own body began to glisten. Light ran along his crystalline skin in bright veins, blue and gold, and he rushed forward to meet the crow in the air.
His hand met its beak as...
The impact broke him in half!

Half his body simply went, shattered from the shoulder down to the hip in an explosion of crystal and light, and before he could even feel it, the crow’s wing swept around. The rime-banners along its edge had gone sharp as a blade of frost, and they took his other half clean off.
He Root and Existence pulsed as it was overwhelmed and decimated as effectively...
He died!

Ling stopped in the air, one leg still half-raised. Her fierce face went blank with shock, and for one heartbeat she simply hung there in the frozen dark, staring at the empty place where he had been.
A moment later, golden clouds began to gather.
They drew together out of the frozen dark where he had been, bright and slow, and in the heart of them, something took shape again. Then the clouds opened, and Noah came out of them.
|Your existence has ended.|
|Your Dream has not.|
|Your Dream is Infinite. Even death will not stop it.|
He came out cold. He came out dominant!

There was no armament on him. No garment of Provenance, no crystal plate, nothing at all. Only his skin, smooth and shining and unbroken, and the dense packed muscle of a body that had been pressed and refined by the Lived Hour a second at a time into something harder than anything the Basal Floor had ever seen.

He hung in the frozen air entirely naked, a long and heavy thing between his legs, swinging freely as he turned, utterly unconcerned with it. Golden-blue light rolled off his shoulders. His eyes were very calm.
He looked at the crow, and the crow, for the first time, looked back at him warily!
"I am Human," Noah said.
The clouds around him began to churn.
"I am THE Protagonist."
The churning gathered, tightened, took shape.
"I am Quintessential."
All around him, the clouds of dream broke apart into Dimensions!

Small ones at first, each one no larger than a fisst, unstable and flickering, blue-gold bubbles of existence that trembled and pulsed as though they could barely hold themselves together. Thousands of them, blooming out of the clouds in every direction. Then tens of thousands. Then hundreds of thousands, still more of them coming, filling the frozen sky around him until he hung in the heart of a vast, trembling clusters of his own unstable dreams!
One after another, they began to surge toward the crow.
"My dream is fucking infinite," Noah said. "What about yours?!"
BOOM!
He surged forward to meet it!

And as he went, his Dream began, subtly, to change. Infinity threaded into it, more and more, until the two could not be told apart. His Root began to spin inside him, faster and faster, turning like an engine that had just been given all the fuel it had ever wanted. And both of his Inscriptions burned!

sentences.text: When Noah thought back across his whole existence, there had been times he could only be called a bully.
He had been terrifying with his power.
Overpowered, grand, tyrannical, a being who walked into a war and ended it with a single drop of his blood or mana while armies wept at the edge of his shadow.
He did not regret it.
It had been who he was, and what the moment needed.
But the higher he climbed, the more complicated existence became.
The beings grew stranger.
The rules grew deeper.
And it grew harder and harder to simply overpower anything, even with everything that made him unique.
Harder.
Not impossible.
And through all of it, in every one of those moments when he had stood over something that should have crushed him, there had been one answer to his terrible immensity.
One thing underneath all the others.
His Infinity.
So.
He looked at the crow ahead, and his sight opened it!
|EMPOWERED HOLLOW NIGHT LIFEFORM.|
PROVENANCE: 999 (+100).
POTENTIA: 999 (+100).
Nine hundred and ninety-nine, and a hundred more on top of each line!
Noah’s eyes narrowed as he flew.
The base alone matched Minerva, the very ceiling she had hit and broken herself against.
And then a hundred more in everything, sitting on top of it like a borrowed coat.
Where did that come from?
The Basal Floor?
The cold itself, feeding the things that lived in it?
Or something the crow carried inside it, a stolen heart of true Immensity pushing it past a limit it could not reach alone?
He did not know.
It did not matter yet.
What mattered was that it was stronger than him on paper, in every line!
And yet his numbers were packed and its numbers were hollow.
He had learned that much in the snow.
Digits were only what existence could be bothered to count.
They were never the whole of a thing.
He raised his hand.
"I AM."
HUUM!
He was.
But he was what?
With those two words he pulled every ounce of his Provenance and every scrap of his power together into a single point, and it came out of him as an aurora of dreams.

Blue and gold, incandescent, drawn out long and thin and sharp into the shape of a blade, and it shot across the frozen sky toward the crow with a sound like the largest bell in existence being struck once and cut off!
It hit the crow full on!
The crow lowered its head and met it with its beak.
BOOM!
The blade of dreams struck the cracked tower of rime and broke apart against it, scattering into drifting golden sparks.

Little damage.
Almost none!
But...

HUUM!
Golden clouds descended.

The crow’s hundred extra points flickered.
The cold in its feathers wavered.

chapters.title: Chapter 5805: I Dream Your End!
paragraphs: Noah felt like an engine!

THE Osmontian Inscription of THE Dreaming Hour churned inside him, pressing a day into every second. His Root spun at the center of his chest, faster and faster, the mobius turning like a wheel that had finally been given a road. And through all of it, through every packed quark and every current of Provenance, the idea of Infinity was spreading. Seeping in. Soaking into his Dream until he could no longer tell where one ended and the other began.
He raised his hands.
The crow roared!

It was a maddened sound, stripped of any grace it had carried before, and with it came a wave. A glacial wave of cold rolled out of its body in every direction, white and total, and everything it touched froze. Drifting islands, torn Dimensions, the white-blue sea below and the frozen air above, gigaparsecs of it in every direction, all of it locked solid in a single instant, as though this region had become a gem with the three of them sealed inside it!
Ling froze mid-leap.
Noah froze mid-reach.
For one breath, nothing moved at all.

Then, around Ling, the ice began to melt. It ran off her in streams and sheeted away from her skin, because there was nothing in her for it to hold. And around Noah, the ice began to dream. It softened. It blurred at its edges into drifting golden haze, slow and drowsy, until he was simply moving through it as though it had never frozen at all.
He lowered his hands, and spoke.
"My Tongue is young," Noah said. "Undeveloped. I dream of it growing, and it will. I have Letters. I have Words. All of them built on my own Root and my own foundations."
His eyes held the crow.
"So I will make a sentence. One built for nothing but destruction."
He breathed in.
"I DREAM OF YOUR END."
HUUM!
|THE OSMONTIAN TONGUE: A SENTENCE has been composed.|
|I DREAM OF YOUR END.|
|Your Root, your foundations, and your Provenance are gathered to a single purpose: to dream, simply and purely, the end of what you behold.|
|While you hold the target in your gaze, its existence is dreamed toward its conclusion. What is dreamed away does not vanish. It returns to the dreamer.|
|The more certain the Dream, the faster the ending.|
The edges of the crow began to glow!

A thin line of gold ran along the rims of its great wings, along the tips of its talons, along the cracked edge of its beak. It shone for a moment, soft and warm and wrong against all that black ice. Then the glowing edges began to flake away. Tiny golden flakes, drifting loose from the crow like ash from a burning page, and they did not fall. They flowed. Across the frozen sky in slow shining streams, all of them drifting toward Noah, sinking into his skin, and he felt each one arrive as a small warm weight in his chest!
The crow screamed and lookd at its own wing.
Then its crown rang.

It was a terrible sound as around the crown, shapes began to form. Rendered shapes, many-faced and vast, turning slowly in the frozen air. A colossal orange one, facet upon facet, so intricate Noah’s eyes pulsed trying to follow it. And inside that, a violet one, and inside that, another orange. Shrink. Push. Shrink again. The three of them spun together around the crown and then drove at Noah as one, a single rendered weapon built to crush everything it touched down into a point smaller than a quark and then scatter the point across existence!
Noah looked at it coming.
He composed another sentence.
"I DREAM OF HEALING INFINITELY."
HUUM!
|A second SENTENCE has been composed.|
|I DREAM OF HEALING INFINITELY.|
|While it holds, whatever of you is broken is dreamed whole again before your existence can come apart.|
|It does not prevent the blow. It refuses the wound.|
The rendered weapon hit him.
BOOM!

It crushed his left arm down to nothing, pushed his ribs out through his back, and condensed half his skull into a point and flung the point away. And golden clouds bloomed on every wound in the same instant, and his arm was there again, and his ribs, and his skull, whole, whole, whole, each broken part dreamed back into place before the rest of him could even notice it was gone!
He walked through the rendered weapon as it tore him apart and remade him, over and over, and came out the other side untouched.
Then he landed on the crow’s back!
He stood there among the black-ice feathers and the frosted ribs, naked and gleaming, heavy with muscle, and raised both hands over his head, and brought them down like hammers!
WAA!
The crow cried out!

Its back buckled under the blow. Golden light ran out from the point of impact in cracks, and more of it flaked away, and the flakes streamed up into him. He brought his hands down again. And again. Every strike, more of the crow came loose into dreams and drifted home to him.
"When a dream is small, it dies with the morning," Noah said, and his voice rolled out across the whole frozen region.
He struck.
"But when a dream has enough weight, when it has enough teeth, it stops being a dream. It becomes existence."
He struck again.
"My dream is not an invitation. It is an unyielding decree, moving with absolute certainty. Struggling against it is an ant cursing an avalanche. It changes nothing at all."
His hands came down, and the crow’s spine groaned.
"Sit down. Stop thrashing against it. Do not fucking resist! The dream will happen, and your permission was never asked!"
ROOOAR!
The crow reared under him, screaming, thrashing, the whole mountain-range bulk of it bucking in the frozen air.
And Ling moved.

She hung in the air beside its head, and her thighs flexed. They swelled, visibly, the great muscles expanding as though something inside her had just been given room to breathe, and she began to spin. A hazy light wrapped around her, golden-violet, the same light that had burned around her father’s mountain, and her eyes changed. The pupils went out of them. They were pale and blank and white, exactly like her father’s, and she turned in the air in a slow, flowing circle, and then another.

The Kindled Circle. A piece of it. Three turnings, four, drawing her closer and closer to the Root that was her whole existence, until Noah could not tell, watching, where the girl ended and the Root began.
On the last turning, she kicked the crow’s beak.
BOOM!
It shattered in half!

The whole great cracked tower split down its length with a sound like a glacier breaking off a mountain, and the two halves tumbled away into the dark, and from the ruin of the crow’s face, gold poured out. Flakes and flakes of it, a river of them, streaming across the sky and into Noah!
Noah roared!

He threw his hands up, and the blue-gold clouds all around him gathered into them, and took shape. Spears. Long and bright and made of his own Provenance, humming with his Dream. He drove the first one down into the crow’s back. Then the second. Then a third.

The crow flipped. It rolled over in the air, trying to throw him, and its feathers came off it in a freezing storm, and they cut him open. Across the chest, the thighs, the throat. Heavy wounds, deep and cold, the kind that should have ended him. Every one of them was dreamed shut before his existence could so much as start to break apart.
He kept throwing spears.

Four. Ten. Twenty. He drove them in faster than the crow could thrash, one after another after another, until its whole back was a forest of blue-gold shafts, skewered from the base of its broken crown down to its tail.
And from behind, Ling kicked it.

She came up under its tail and drove her foot straight into its ass, with every ounce of her Root behind it, and the sound the crow made then was not a scream. It was a sound no creature should ever have to make!
The kick drove the whole beast upward onto the spears. Every one of them sank in to the haft. And the crow split.
Down the middle, spine to breast, the two halves of it tearing away from each other in the frozen dark!
Noah’s sentence grew grander.

Now he could see it. Truly see it, the end of this thing, as clearly as he could see his own hands, and the more certain he was of it, the faster the Dream moved. The crow’s halves glared at him with every eye they had left, furious, hating. Golden clouds closed around them. And all at once, the whole of its body turned to dream!
BOOM!
The explosion was frozen. It burst outward in a sphere of white and gold and blue, ice and dream together, and for one moment the whole region was lit by it, and then it was gone.
Noah steadied himself in the air where the crow had been.
He looked grand. Naked and gleaming, packed with muscle, gold still drifting into him from the dust of the thing he had just ended.
|Your Infinity has permeated your weavings.|
|THE PROTAGONIST and THE Tide That Owes Nothing have become interlinked, for results most geared to you.|
|Loot shall once more flow from your enemies.|
|For granting death to an extremely powerful enemy, you have obtained: LESSER KRYOS EXISTENTIAL CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN x5, and one GLACIAL RECORD OF A CRUEL CROW.|
Five slivers of pale blue crystal drifted out of the settling dust, each one a snowflake grown down into itself, pulsing cold and slow. They circled him, bright against the frozen dark.
And behind them came something else. A shard of ice, thin and clear, with light moving inside it. It floated up to him on its own, touched his brow, and sank in!
He saw the Basal Floor through the crow’s eyes.

Scattered scenes, dozens of them, flickering past. Frozen islands. Torn Dimensions. Other Empowered Hollow Night Lifeforms, huge and cold, prowling the dark. And then one scene held, and would not let him go.
THE Caretaker, bound in chains!

Her pages were gone. Her frost dress was torn. Great chains of pale light were wound around her arms and her waist, and she was being led. Before her walked a figure, long and slender and humanoid, far taller than she was, and it had no face at all. Only smooth, pale blankness where a face should have been. It led her across the Basal Floor, toward a massive crack in the ice, a vast blue rift splitting the frozen dark from top to bottom.
In the memory, the faceless thing stopped.
It turned around.
It had no eyes, and it looked at him anyway. Noah felt its invisible gaze land on him, through the crow’s dead memory, across however much distance lay between them.
And...
BOOM!
His upper body exploded!

It was erased, shoulders and chest and head wiped out of existence as cleanly as a word scraped off a page. And in the same instant, the golden clouds came roaring in, and his sentence held, and he was dreamed back together, whole, gasping.
The memory was gone. Ripped out of him!
But he hung there in the frozen air, grand and heavy-eyed and whole, having just defeated something far grander than himself.
Ling floated over. She was bleedng from a dozen cuts, her ribbons long gone, her pupils back again and bright with something that looked very much like approval. She looked him up and down.
Mostly down.
She whistled.
"Be decent and cover up when you fight, Big Boy," she said, still looking at his lower half. "You don’t want to be distracting."
Noah glanced down. A pair of blue-gold trousers wove themselves out of his Provenance and settled over his hips.

Then he turned his calm gaze back to the Lesser Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins, and waved his hand. Three more slid out of his keeping, the ones the Caretaker had given him, and joined the five in the air. Eight of them now, circling him in the dark.
They began to spin around each other, faster and faster.
And four of them began to fuse into one!

A shard of ice, thin and clear, with light moving inside it.
It floated up to him on its own, touched his brow, and sank in!
He saw the Basal Floor through the crow’s eyes.
Scattered scenes, dozens of them, flickering past.
Frozen islands.
Torn Dimensions.
Other Empowered Hollow Night Lifeforms, huge and cold, prowling the dark.
And then one scene held, and would not let him go.
THE Caretaker, bound in chains!
Her pages were gone.
Her frost dress was torn.
Great chains of pale light were wound around her arms and her waist, and she was being led.
Before her walked a figure, long and slender and humanoid, far taller than she was, and it had no face at all.
Only smooth, pale blankness where a face should have been.
It led her across the Basal Floor, toward a massive crack in the ice, a vast blue rift splitting the frozen dark from top to bottom.
In the memory, the faceless thing stopped.
It turned around.
It had no eyes, and it looked at him anyway.
Noah felt its invisible gaze land on him, through the crow’s dead memory, across however much distance lay between them.
And...
BOOM!
His upper body exploded!
It was erased, shoulders and chest and head wiped out of existence as cleanly as a word scraped off a page.
And in the same instant, the golden clouds came roaring in, and his sentence held, and he was dreamed back together, whole, gasping.
The memory was gone.
Ripped out of him!
But he hung there in the frozen air, grand and heavy-eyed and whole, having just defeated something far grander than himself.
Ling floated over.
She was bleedng from a dozen cuts, her ribbons long gone, her pupils back again and bright with something that looked very much like approval.
She looked him up and down.
Mostly down.
She whistled.
"Be decent and cover up when you fight, Big Boy," she said, still looking at his lower half.
"You don’t want to be distracting."
Noah glanced down.
A pair of blue-gold trousers wove themselves out of his Provenance and settled over his hips.
Then he turned his calm gaze back to the Lesser Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins, and waved his hand.
Three more slid out of his keeping, the ones the Caretaker had given him, and joined the five in the air.
Eight of them now, circling him in the dark.
They began to spin around each other, faster and faster.
And four of them began to fuse into one!

chapters.title: Chapter 5806: Purely Educational!
paragraphs: The eight Lesser Kryos spun faster around each other, trailing pale blue light behind them like comets chasing their own tials!

Noah watched them close. Each one was a quarter of a true Immensity’s remains, a snowflake grown inward on itself, cold and dense and pulsing with the settled weight of something that had once stood at the very top of existence. And as they spun, they began to press together. Two merged first, and then two more, and the pale blue light between them flared, and flared again.
When the light settled, only two crystals hung in the air before him where four had been.
They were larger. Brighter. Denser, each one humming with a low, steady thrum that Noah could feel in his Root, and they were no longer Lesser!
|KRYOS EXISTENTIAL CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN x2.|
|Each holds the settled weight of an Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin formed within an Immense One. Far grander than the Lesser variety.|
Two genuine Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins born crom 8 Lesser Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins! At this time...
A blur of blue silk swung past his face.

Ling had flipped upside down in the frozen air, legs tucked, ribbonless hair hanging loose, and she drifted to a stop directly in front of the two Kryos with her face an arm’s length from them. Her eyes were bright with open interest, studying the crystals as a jeweler studies a stone she has not seen before.
Then those same interested eyes lifted from the Kryos and settled on Noah!

He gazed back at her. She hung there upside down, round-faced and blood-speckled and curious, and he thought about a great many things in a very short time. About the Basal Floor stretching away beneath them, cold and vast and full of things that wanted to kill them. About the fact that she was THE Thinker’s daughter, and a Root made flesh, and the only being in this place who could match him blow for blow.
About how she fought, and how she laughed, and the fierce burning look in her eyes when she had kicked the crow’s beak in half.
And about the fact that he was, at the end of all of it, still human. But he had to draw his boundaries.
"Are you interested in me?"Noah said.
Ling blinked!
"I am deciding to change a certain aspect of myself,"he went on,"I do not wish to disappoint you with any misunderstandings."
Ling righted herself in the air, slowly, until she was facing him properly. Her smile was wide and warm and a little sharp at its edges.

"I do find you interesting," she said. "But it is more curiosity than anything. There were a few lifeforms in the Legacy who caught my eye. But I didn’t even deem them worthy enough to have anything with."

She shrugged, and the shrug carried her whole body. "It’s a matter of pride. I believed myself so much grander that I couldn’t possibly allow someone weaker than me to experience the wonder of my thighs."
Noah almost laughed. Almost!
"I have been loose with my love and my affection," he said. "Multiple women. And I have not done right by them. So I came to a conclusion that I cannot do that again."

He looked at her directly. "But I am still human, and humans are lustful beings. I can offer you a purely...educational relationship. We learn about each other’s weavings of existence. No emotions. No attachments. We will be working together for a while in this place, and it would do me well to understand the extent of your power. You can try to understand mine."
Ling’s mouth fell open into a wide O!
Then she laughed, the sound ringing out across the frozen dark of the Basal Floor.

"What an arrogant fucking guy you are!" She wiped a tear of laughter from the corner of her eye. "Do we even have time for such things? I can sense a distant aura out there, at least one just as powerful as that crow, if not more."
"One can always dream more time," Noah said. "Come. Let us see how strong your thighs are."His eyes held hers. "And remember. No emotions, and no attachments."
Ling tilted her head!

She looked at him for a long moment, and her smile changed. It lost none of its warmth, but something in it sharpened into a blade, the smile of a being who had just been offered a game she was very confident she could win.
"No emotions," she said. "No attachments."
Her eyes glittered.
"Okay!"
Golden clouds bloomed around them!

Thick and warm, they poured out of Noah’s Provenance in soft, bright banks, rolling out through the frozen air and closing over both of them, and their figures vanished into the gold. Whatever sounds followed were between them, and the Basal Floor, cold and indifferent, did not care to listen!
The Basal Floor drifted on around the clouds, vast and cold and full of things that prowled in the dark.
And on the frozen island where a terrifying Hollow Night Lifeform had just been killed, atop the ruins of its shattered crown, Noah Osmont sought to understand a very unique lifeform!
<THE Infiniverse>
The golden shore of THE Infiniverse was quieter than ever.

Snow fell on it now! The farmland beyond the shore stretched away in long green rows, heavy with the crops his people had tended days ago, and the snow came down on all of it in soft white sheets, settling on the golden sand. It was not a blizzard here. Not yet as THE Infiniverse afforded a layer of protection.
The Counting of The Long Night pressed on everything, even inside his own Infiniverse!

Noah stood at the edge of the shore with a Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin turning slowly in his hand, pale blue and cold and humming, and he looked across the farmland at the figure sitting in the snow.
Thalia was meditating!

She sat cross-legged in the middle of a plowed field, her dark red hair loose around her shoulders, her hands resting on her knees. The snow gathered on her. It settled on her hair and on her lashes and on the tops of her bare feet, and she did not brush it off. Her eyes were closed. Her breathing was slow and even. Around her, the crops closest to her body had bent toward her, very slightly, as if she were a sun and they knew it.
Noah watched her for a while before he moved.

He had been thinking, amidst this apocalypse of snow, about the women who had helped him. There had been several. There had been more than several, and he had been loose with his affection, and he had not done right by most of them.
He had told Ling that on the Basal Floor. He had made a decision about it. No more carelessness. No more taking someone’s warmth and leaving them to wonder what it had meant.
If he was going to change that, he ought to start with the most recent one.

Thalia had come to him out of a white pool, bleeding, carrying warnings from a future. She had taught him the Sovereign Genesis. She had wept one tear when he remade his quarks, and called herself his destiny and his Provenance, and he had not yet given her much in return, except the decimation of her Lineage that was a causality from a decision they both made.
So he walked across the snow to her field, and knelt in front of her, and waited until she opened her eyes.
"You are back," Thalia said.
"I am back."
She looked at the Kryos in his hand! The pale blue light of it played across her face. She did not ask what it was.
"I brought you something," Noah said. "Two things, actually. One to show you, and one to give you."
He raised his free hand, and the air between them filled with a dream.

He showed her the Vasiliou Elsedimension. The white avenues, the frost-visage of Lucy, the Collector’s hazy vastness rewriting existence into a debt. He showed her the blow, the single strike that shattered everything the Collector had written, and the corpse, vast and ruined, and the mammoth of frost rising out of it.
He showed her the death of the being that had once promised to rip her in half.

Thalia watched it all with her hands still on her knees and her breathing still even. When the dream faded, she was quiet for a long moment. Then the corners of her mouth moved, just slightly, and her eyes were bright.
"He is gone," she said.
"Mmm."
"Good."She breathed out, and some tension Noah had never noticed in her, went out of her all at once. "Good."
The snow fell on them both.
"The second thing," Noah said.
He held out the Kryos.
"I want to help you form a Root."he said.
Thalia looked at the crystal, and then at him.
She held his gaze for a long time. Then she reached out, and her fingers closed around the Kryos, and the pale blue light ran up her arm and into her chest!
Her body shuddered. Her eyes widened. The Provenance within her brightened!
Noah had done this multiple times before as it was second nature now as he guided the formation of another Gonadotropin.

The Provenance within her was not swelling; the essense was focusing, each one narrowing down to a point so fine it could slip between the threads of a living thing’s existence and alter what it found there. Rewrite how a body was built. Reshape the code that made a being what it was, at the deepest level, where existence wrote its instructions.
A Root bloomed in her chest as it devoured the Kryos ECG!
It was small, and bright! And it turned with a quiet, surgical certainty that reminded Noah of her hands when she had traced a line on his chest.
|A ROOT OF IMMENSITY has been formed.|
|Bearer: THALIA VASILIOU.|
|THE GENOMIC CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN.|
|CONCEPTUAL ROOT OF IMMENSITY.|
|Nature: EXISTENTIAL GENOME ALTERATION. The bearer perceives and rewrites the foundational code of any existence she touches, including her own.|
|At its peak, nothing in existence is built in a way she cannot take apart and rebuild.|
Thalia breathed in sharply, and the farmland around them bloomed!

The crops nearest her shot up a foot in an instant, their leaves spreading wide, their colors deepening from green to a rich, vivid emerald. The plowed earth beneeth the snow stirred and settled into neater rows, as though it had just been told a better way to be soil. Even the snowflakes falling on her seemed to land more carefully, each one finding its place.

She opened her eyes, and they were different. Still grand, still warm. But behind the warmth, something moved with the calm, focused precision of a surgeon who has just been given a blade sharp enough to cut anything in existence.
Noah looked at her, and felt his own Root hum in answer, and smiled!
Then the snow grew heavier!

It came down harder across the whole of THE Infiniverse, on the golden shore and the farmland and the sleeping dreamers inside them. The Counting had noticed! One more Root in existence, one more weight on every other Root, and the cold answered it at once.
Noah lifted his face to the falling snow and let it land on him!
He was doing many things at this moment as his existence was also present...elsewhere.
In a small, utterly unknown world.
The desert was gone.

Noah stood in the sky above the small world where an old woman had once recited THE Augury of the Long Night to him by firelight, and the desert he remembered was buried. The dunes were white, and the black tents were white.
The blizzard howled across it!

It had been snowfall when he first placed his protection here. Gentle, strange, a thing the desert people had never seen and did not have a word for. Now it was a storm, and the storm was not gentle, and the people beneath it were hurting! He could feel them! Small, warm, fragile lives huddled around their fires, burning everything they had, and the cold eating through their walls anyway.
And this was not only here!

This was happening across trillions of worlds at once. Across uncounted realms, Observable Existences, and drifting Dimensions, in places Noah had never been and never would be, the same blizzard was falling on the same fragile lives. The ambient temperature of reality itself was dropping toward nothing, and there was no one standing over most of those lives as he was standing over these.
Two figures appeared beside him in the sky!

THE Infiniverse materialized on his left, her multicolored fur coat heavy with snow, her starlit eyes grave. Ruination appeared on his right, crimson beams sweeping the horizon, her coat of crimson and gold sharp against the white. Both of them looked down at the buried desert and said nothing, because there was nothing to say that the blizzard was not already saying.
Noah looked at them, and then out across the storm, and spoke.

"The frost is settling across countless regions at once. We did not author this winter, even if our hands are tangled somewhere in the thread. And we are not saviors walking the dark to be worshiped."
The snow whipped past all three of them!

"The billions of lives shivering on those far Dimensions do not know my face, and I will never learn their names. Pulling them into our shelter buys us no strategic advantage. It leaves no debt to collect, offers no return on the investment, and does nothing to halt the turning of the Night. It is completely, utterly unnecessary."
He paused. The blizzard filled the silence.
"It is merely my human sentimentality. A quiet, irrational refusal to let the frost take them all just because the sky decided to go cold."
He turned to them.

"So do not hesitate. Pull upon my Infinity. Open the borders of THE Infiniverse and swallow every Dimension and Observable Existence you can reach. Bring them into our warmth. We cannot carry the whole of existence, but where our reach extends, let us save as many as we can."
Ruination’s crimson beams were already moving!
Her Root of the Record had grown grander than ever. She could find Dimensions now as a hawk finds mice in a field, rapidly, precisely, and without mercy toward the distance between them.
And THE Infiniverse was already opening!

Her Root of Genesis answered the command at once. The borders of her existence widened, and widened again, and kept widening, a living thing stretching herself to take in countless things into the warmth of her body because her Master had told her to, and because it was unnecessary, and because he was human.
Toward his words, they had only a single answer.
|Yes, Master.|

Below them, the buried desert began, very slowly, to rise. The whole world and small Observable Existence peeled away from its place in the freezing dark and drifted upward, into the open borders of THE Infiniverse, into the warmth, and the people inside their tents did not know what had saved them.
They only knew the wind had stopped being a blizzard as only light sprinkling of snow cascaded down!

chapters.title: Chapter 5807: Existence Is So Beautiful!
paragraphs: <THE Sealed One>
THE Keepers of Existence was a Legacy that looked, from a distance, like something that should not exist during a winter.

Boundless seas of crimson gold rolled away in every direction beneath a sky that had no end, shining and warm, and rivers of the same color ran through them and above them in slow winding currents that crossed and parted and crossed again. Floating islands drifted across those seas, serene and green, some the size of small Dimensions, some no larger than a garden, and every one of them was blanketed in snow.

The blizzard reached even here. It howled across the crimson gold, and where the flakes touched the seas they hissed into threads of steam, and where they touched the islands they piled and stayed, white on green, cold settling over warmth.

It was a Legacy shared by dozens of Immense Ones, THE SLEEPLESS FIEND among them, each one a pillar holding the same roof. Those who served in it spoke its name as one speaks the name of a law, because that was what it was. THE Keepers of Existence. The ones who had kept things exactly as they were for longer than anything could remember!
At the heart of those seas, on a great dais of black iron rising from the crimson gold, THE Sealed One stood and looked at what had been brought to him.

A dozen Rare Gu hung in chains along the dais’s rim, strung up in black iron, each one a different strange and shining thing. A moth whose wings were written light, and a serpent with scales of closed eyes. Something like a jellyfish made of old brass bells. All of them silent, because the chains had been designed to keep them silent as they were filled with Immensity.
Beyond the Gu, a dozen Provenance Lifeforms knelt in a row with their heads bowed. Every one of them carried a Root of Immensity.
And at the very front, in the lightest chains of all, two figures.

THE Champion Alcaeus knelt with his broad back straight, bronze-skinned and scarred from his shouldrs to his heels, his long matted hair frozen with blood. He had been a champion. Now he did not look at THE Sealed One at all, only at the snow.
Beside him crouched THE Infinity Eater.
Behind THE Sealed One, the air split like an eyelid!

A vast dark eye looked out of it, sleepless, patient, burning with an attention that had never once blinked. Its face was barely perceptible behind the haze, but the mouth was visible, and it was smiling.
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND regards you.|
|"They say if you die, the door is forever lost. Existence will become harder and more brutal to live in, but many core members of this Legacy believe you are one of the core keys."|
|"Others, even here, believe differently."|
|"So you will be protected. Five Immense Ones on your security detail at all times. And they continue to fatten you up, like a pig."|
The smile widened behind the haze.
|"Now we are even giving you our own Descendants."|
THE SLEEPLESS FIEND looked at THE Infinity Eater as he said this!
And the betrayal on THE Infinity Eater’s face was heavy.

It turned its great head, slowly, from the Fiend to THE Sealed One and back again, and its burning eyes held the Immense One, and there was not a single glimmer of respect in those vast dark pupils. Not a shred of decorum. Only the flat, enormous disbelief of a hound that has just been handed to the butcher by the man who raised it.

"I live in Infinity," THE Infinity Eater said, and its voice was the torrent of every voice it had ever swallowed. "My existence is grand. I was meant to form a glorious Immensity of Infinity. How could I be sitting before another like a meal right now? How could I be discarded so simply?"
THE Sealed One smiled!

He rose from where he sat and walked toward THE Infinity Eater, unhurried, his long dark coat trailing across the black iron. He stopped in front of it, close enough to touch, and looked up at its churning Infinity and its betrayed, burning eyes.

"You depended on the power of another to get what you had,"THE Sealed One said, softly. "That is why you were discarded in the end. A rented coat always gets taken back when the cold comes. You built an entire life out of borrowed wood, and now you look surprised that the landlord kicked the door in to reclaim his timber."
His gold eyes held THE Infinity Eater.

"In a way, I am just like you right now. I lean on the power of Immense Ones to find my footing. I sit in their snow, I take their craft, and I learn their ways. But the difference between us is simple. I know what the bill looks like. I know they want something from me, and I want something from them. Two strangers striking a trade across an open fire before the wood burns out. And I will not need their fire for very long."
The Infinity Eater strained against its chains!

"You never understood the exchange," THE Sealed One went on, still soft. "You thought a master’s favor was love. You thought being a useful hound meant they would let you sleep by the hearth forever. But a hound that goes lame gets left behind in the brush."
He tilted his head. "Maybe if you had anything left to offer, they would not have thrown you into the ditch."
His mouth opened.
It kept opening!

His jaw came loose from his face and went on widening, the pale skin of his cheeks stretching thin as paper, lips peeling back and back until his mouth was no longer a mouth at all but a vast black opening, wider than he was tall, wider than THE Infinity Eater itself. Inside it there was no throat. Only dark, and a pale gold glint far, far down, like something very old at the bottom of a well.
"In existence," THE Sealed One whispered from inside that impossible mouth, "most things are discarded."
OOOOH!
THE Infinity Eater screamed!

It threw itself backward. The chains held. It clawed at the dais, infinity snapping, every swallowed voice howling out of it at once. THE Sealed One leaned forward, and swallowed it whole. The chains snapped like thread. The scream went down into the dark and stopped, and the jaws slid back into place, and he was a lean pale man in a long dark coat again, standing alone.
His whole body shone!
Pale gold light spread outward from his chest, bright, brighter, the Infinity of a thousand devoured beings churning through him, and his Root sat a little lighter.
Then he turned, shining, to the Champion and the Gu and the dozen Provenance Lifeforms shackled and bound before him with their flickering Roots.
He licked his lips!

Then he raised his arms, palms up, and let the snow fall on them. It settled on his open hands and on his shining coat and on his pale gold hair, and he smiled, brilliantly, the smile of a man standing in a garden he intended to eat.
"Existence... is so beautiful, isn’t it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5808: Emotion!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
Noah’s existence was stretched across many places at once, and one of them was a dream.
It was Emotive’s dream!

He had visited a great many dreams since he built the Dream Engine. Adelaide’s snowbound capital. The Emperor Penguin’s army of robots wearing his face. Each one had been a window into what a person wanted most, rendered in whatever shape their heart could hold.
Emotive’s was different.

He arrived floating in a vast, shining expanse that took him a moment to recognize. It was THE Earliest Folds. Or rather, it was Emotive’s memory of them, reimagined and polished and made grander than they had ever truly been, the old strange spaces of his long-lost Observable Existences rebuilt in a dreamer’s hands.
Massive structures of THE Loom rose everywere through it, the great woven works that Emotive and THE Living Paradox had once built together.
They climbed and arched and spiraled away in every direction, towers of woven light, bridges of thread thick as continents.
And everywhere, in every direction, stood statues of Noah!
Hundreds of them. Thousands. Some small enough to hold in two hands, some so vast their heads were lost among the woven towers. Noah seated on a throne. Laughing, head thrown back.

Arms spread wide, painting a Dimension in his blood. Standing over a fallen titan. Every one of them was stellar, grand, carved with such devotion that each seemed to have captured the very best thing about him in a single moment and held it there forever.
He floated before one of them, and stopped.

It was made of pure Luxuria Ego Authority. The whole enormous figure shone with a deep red light, warm and heavy and intoxicating, the raw substance of desire shaped into a man. It was him with crimson hair and golden eyes, wearing a fitted red suit, standing with one hand in his pocket and the faintest knowing smile on his face.
And sitting on its shoulder was Emotive!

She wore a loose red dress that hung loose and careless off her fair figure, her white skin shining brilliantly in the red light of the statue beneath her. Her hair burned. Not with one color, but with many, all of them shifting at once, crimson and violet and electric blue and a green like poison and a gold like sunrise, every shade of every feeling a being could have, tangled together and flickering madly. And her eyes, when they found him, blazed with that same bottomless mania.
She was beautiful. She had always been beautiful!
Then those eyes found him.
And she smashed forward off the statue’s shoulder, crossed the space between them in an instant, and wrapped her whole body around his feet!
She clung there, arms locked around his ankels, cheek pressed to the top of his foot, and let out a long, deep sigh of absolute contentment!
Noah sighed too. He reached down and patted her burning hair.
"You can just hug my body, you know," he said. "Why wrap yourself around my feet?"
She did not let go.

Sometimes her love and her fascination with him felt too extreme. Sometimes it unsettled even him. But this was who she was. This was the woman who had torn her own Heart out and given it to him, to save him from becoming an apathetic, mindless version of himself. He could put up with a great deal of strangeness from someone who had done that.

"I like what I like!"Emotive said into his foot. Then she lifted her face, and her manic eyes blazed up at him. "And I can feel so many emotions coming off your existence right now. So many! How can I be of service to you, my Everything?"
Noah looked into those eyes of boundless mania, and produced a Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin.
It hung in his palm, pale blue and humming.

He reached down with his other hand and took Emotive by the neck, not gently, and lifted her up off his feet until she hung before him, her toes dangling, her burning hair spilling around her face. Her eyes went wide and bright with delight.

He was not being cruel. He knew her. She liked to be handled a little roughly, liked to feel his grip and his certainty, and in her own mad way this was how she knew she was loved. He was only speaking her language.
Then he drove the Kryos into her chest!
She gasped, and her eyes never left his face, absolute mania and absolute trust burning in them together.
Noah went to work. He reached into her existence through the Kryos and began to build a Root, and the moment he looked closely at what was in there, he was alarmed.
He had known her emotions were strong. But..

She had elevated the Seven Deadly Sins and their Virtues to heights he had never imagined. Luxuria and Castitas, Ira and Patientia, Superbius and Humilitas, every one of them and their Egos refined and deepened and stacked atop each other in her existence until they formed a structure so dense and so volatile it hummed like a storm about to break. She had been busy, in her long dream. Terrifyingly busy.

He did not change any of it. He only used what she had already built, guiding the Kryos along the paths she had carved herself, letting her Egos and her emotions shape the Root as it formed. It was hers. He was just helping it find its footing.
Minutes passed.
HUUM!
Emotive floated free of his hand.

She hung in the dreaming air before him, arms loose at her sides, her many-colored hair streaming upward as though caught in a wind that blew from her own chest. Her whole body glowed. Waves of emotion rolled off her, one after another, joy and fury and longing and grief and a madness underneath all of it, each wave carrying the weight of an Ego so heavy it bent the woven light of THE Loom’s towers around her.
|A ROOT OF IMMENSITY has been formed.|
|Bearer: EMOTIVE.|
|THE PASSIONAL CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN.|
|THE ROOT OF EMOTION.|
|PHYSICAL ROOT OF IMMENSITY.|
|Nature: Emotion made flesh. Every feeling the bearer holds is carried in her body as mass, force, and weight. The more she feels, the heavier and stronger she becomes.|
Physical?
Noah stared at the prompt!

How could a Root of Emotion be Physical and not Conceptual? Emotion was the most abstract thing he could think of. It had no shape, no weight, nothing to put your hand on. Unless it did. Unless a racing heart and shaking hands and a throat gone tight with grief were not the side effects of feeling at all, but the feeling itself. Unless every emotion she had ever had lived in her body first, and she had simply never let it be anywhere else.
His eyes shone!
Before him, Emotive dropped from the air and knelt. Terrifying waves of power and Ego vibrated off her, rippling out through the whole dream, and she bowed her burning head to him.
Anyone watching would have thought he had just wasted two Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins. One on Thalia. One here. Two of the rarest treasures of the Long Night, given away, gone.
But they would have been wrong.

His Foundation, THE Tide That Owes Nothing, sat at the very forefront of his existence now, and it was no longer simply collecting the boons of his actions and filtering them. His Provenance of THE Human Dreamer had wrapped itself around the Tide, tightly, and together they were doing something new.
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has answered your giving.|
|Given: two Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins. Aided: the formation of two Roots of Immensity.|
|Returned, as dreamed: QUINTESSENTIAL EXISTENTIAL CHORIONIC GONADOTROPIN x10.|
|Your Root buzzes with excitement at the thought of consuming them.|
Ten!

Noah felt his Root hum in his chest, eager, hungry, spinning faster at the mere thought of them. Ten Quintessential ECGs, returned for two Kryos given freely. That was the Tide. That was what happened when he gave with open hands and a clear heart.

He could be magnanimous. He could give things away, and get back even grander returns. His women and his family could be spoiled, and things could be made right for all the women he had not exactly ignored, but had never quite given their proper due.
A great many things could be made right. And in doing so, he would keep living his Dream grandly, and keep making tremendous gains, and there was no contradiction in that at all.
He was still thinking it when two small arms came around him from behind.
Emotive had risen from her kneel and come up at his back, and now she wrapped herself around him, her cheek pressed between his shoulder blades, her small hands locking tight across his chest.
"I want to end my dream soon," she said softly. "So I can be by your side again."
Her grip tightened.
"I’m connected to your emotions more than anyone. So I’m the most in tune with what you feel, and what you want. And you, my Everything, are voracious."

Her voice dropped."I can feel the cold you’re fighting against, and taking in. I can feel your fear. Your doubts. I can feel you wondering if you have what it takes against this Long Night, for something that seems so complex, with so many moving pieces."
Noah’s eyes pulsed as her small hands wrapped tighter around his chest!

"But I can feel your Tyranny too," Emotive went on. "Boundless. And your Quintessence, roaring inside you, screaming that even in all this, you will reign supreme. I can feel you more than anyone else can, whether you meant it to be that way or not."
She pressed closer.

"Emotion is one of the strongest things in all of existence. Every lifeform does everything it does because of how it feels. Immense Ones move by emotions, an ant moves by emotion. Your grand dreams, you enact them because of how you feel. You feel grand!"
Her voice trembled with something between devotion and madness. "And I want to make sure existence has no choice but to bend to your will."
Her burning hair spilled over his shoulder.
"This dream you put me in let me hone my emotions and my Egos. I won’t leave it just yet. But even without leaving it, I can still feel you, and I can do many things...even If I am not awake."
She paused as her voice turned low and very hungry. "I’m also unfathomably thirsty. And true to my emotions. I want to spend the next few years in this dream doing some unspeakable things to you."
She pressed her lips to his ear.
"Are you ready, my Master?"
Noah’s eyes pulsed with voraciousness.
So did hers.

And the grand dream went on around them, the statues of him watching from every direction, the woven structures of THE Loom arching overhead, as time in the dream stretched out long and slow and theirs!

And in doing so, he would keep living his Dream grandly, and keep making tremendous gains, and there was no contradiction in that at all.
He was still thinking it when two small arms came around him from behind.
Emotive had risen from her kneel and come up at his back, and now she wrapped herself around him, her cheek pressed between his shoulder blades, her small hands locking tight across his chest.
"I want to end my dream soon," she said softly.
"So I can be by your side again."
Her grip tightened.
"I’m connected to your emotions more than anyone.
So I’m the most in tune with what you feel, and what you want.
And you, my Everything, are voracious."
Her voice dropped."I can feel the cold you’re fighting against, and taking in.
I can feel your fear.
Your doubts.
I can feel you wondering if you have what it takes against this Long Night, for something that seems so complex, with so many moving pieces."
Noah’s eyes pulsed as her small hands wrapped tighter around his chest!
"But I can feel your Tyranny too," Emotive went on.
"Boundless.
And your Quintessence, roaring inside you, screaming that even in all this, you will reign supreme.
I can feel you more than anyone else can, whether you meant it to be that way or not."
She pressed closer.
"Emotion is one of the strongest things in all of existence.
Every lifeform does everything it does because of how it feels.
Immense Ones move by emotions, an ant moves by emotion.
Your grand dreams, you enact them because of how you feel.
You feel grand!"
Her voice trembled with something between devotion and madness.
"And I want to make sure existence has no choice but to bend to your will."
Her burning hair spilled over his shoulder.
"This dream you put me in let me hone my emotions and my Egos.
I won’t leave it just yet.
But even without leaving it, I can still feel you, and I can do many things...even If I am not awake."
She paused as her voice turned low and very hungry.
"I’m also unfathomably thirsty.
And true to my emotions.
I want to spend the next few years in this dream doing some unspeakable things to you."
She pressed her lips to his ear.
"Are you ready, my Master?"
Noah’s eyes pulsed with voraciousness.
So did hers.

And the grand dream went on around them, the statues of him watching from every direction, the woven structures of THE Loom arching overhead, as time in the dream stretched out long and slow and theirs!

chapters.title: Chapter 5809: Compression!
paragraphs: The snow still fell on the Basal Floor, even inside a golden dream.
Noah had raised the domain around the place where the crow had died, a sphere of soft blue-gold haze floating in the frozen dark, and inside it the air was warm and still.

The shattered Dimensions hung beyond its edge in their thousands. And the snow came down through the dream anyway, slow and fat, settling on the golden haze and melting there into small bright drops that never quite reached the ground.
Ling sat cross-legged on a drift of dream-cloud with her chin in her hands.

Cheeks pressed into her palms, elbows on her knees, she was watching him, her face flushed. The ribbons were gone, her hair loose and tangled, and she had the dazed, bright-eyed look of someone who had just learned something she had not expected to learn.
Their educational entanglement had ended a little while ago!
Now Noah was dancing!

He moved in the center of the golden domain, barefoot on the air, stripped to the waist, and he was performing THE Kindled Circle. The dance her father had passed down to her. She had shown it to him, turning by turning, somewhere in the middle of everything else, and he had learned it as he learned everything that mattered: completely.

His arms swept out in a wide, unbroken arc. His body turned with it. Circles within circles, every motion flowing into the next with no seam between them, and then his feet struck the air, heel and ball, a hard stamp that rolled through the domain like a drum!
He waved a hand in the middle of a turning.
A Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin appeared in his palm!

It was not pale blue like the Kryos. It was blue and gold, the exact colors of his own Provenance, dense and humming and shaped like nothing he had words for, a small star pressed down into itself a thousand times over. The Tide had returned it to him, and it knew him.
He swallowed it without breaking the dance.
It went down into him like a sun, and his Root drank it and spun!
Ling’s hands slid down to cover her mouth!

The second turning. His palms struck his own chest and thighs, call and answer, and a second Quintessential ECG appeared, and he swallowed that too. The third turning, and a third. With each one his body answered. The muscle across his shoulders and back thickened, dense and heavy. Tendrils of blue-gold light spread acros his bare chest and down his arms, branching and glowing just beneath the skin like rivers seen from very high, and every tendril pulsed in time with the stamping of his feet!
Four! Five!

He grew. Not taller, exactly, though he was taller. Denser. More there. His crystalline skin took on the dark sheen of polished diamond-jade, and the tendrils of light burning beneath it made him look like something cut from a mountain and set alight from within. His hair rose off his shoulders and hung in the air as though it had forgotten how to fall.

Around his head, the light gathered into a shape, a broad and jagged crown of blue-gold radiance that swept back from his brow like the horns of some ancient war-lord, and the mobius at the center of his chest spun so fast it blurred into a solid disc of light!
Six! Seven!

The Kindled Circle was drawing him closer to his Root with every turning. He could feel it happening. The distance between Noah and THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin, which had never been large, was growing smaller and smaller, the Root and the man leaning into each other as two halves of a thing lean together before they close.
Eight!
His stamping shook the whole dream. Snow fell faster outside the golden haze.
Nine!
On the twelfth turning, he spun so fast that the blue-gold light wrapped him entirely, and he stopped.

He stood in the center of the dream, bare-chested and burning, the crown of light blazing around his head, every tendril beneath his skin lit at once. He was breathing slow and deep. His eyes were very calm.
One Quintessential ECG remained, drifting at his side. Nine were inside him now.
And his existence began to change!
|THE Kindled Circle has been performed. Your Root and your existence have drawn nearer to one another than ever before.|
|Nine Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins have been consumed.|
|Your existence has been compressed and refined beyond its prior limit. What was many is becoming one.|
He felt it before the prompts finished.

Everything he was, every ability and Foundation and Inscription, every trick and art and scrap of power he had gathered across an entire existence, all of it was sliding together. Pressing close. Finding the places where one thing and another thing were really the same thing wearing two names, and closing the gap.
The Dual Root at the center of him was doing it, and he was so close to his Root now that he could feel it choosing.
|Consolidation has begun.|
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer has absorbed THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign.|
|They were never two. The Sovereign’s authority to perceive and rewrite the foundational design of any existence now flows through your Dreams. What you dream of a being, you may also build into it.|
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer retains its Quality of Time.|
|THE Nine Foundations have become THE One Foundation.|

|THE Unkneeling Crown, THE Tide That Owes Nothing, THE Mirror That Keeps, THE Hunger That Refines, THE Unmoved Verdict, THE Pure Trajectory, THE All-Drawing Stillness, THE Remembered Truth, and THE Sovereign Existence have collapsed into a single bedrock beneath your existence.|

|THE One Foundation: Ineffable. It cannot be made to kneel, moved, compelled, deceived, or diverted. Everything drawn to you is refined without waste. Everything observed is kept. Everything given returns grander. Existence near you must conform to what you are.No weight laid upon you is ever wasted. Pressure, suppression, command, and cold do not lift from you, but where they press, they are kept and built upon, each burden hardening into more of the floor you stand on. Even THE Counting, bearing down upon your Root, now leaves behind a sliver of foundation for every moment you bear it.|
Noah breathed out!
The prompts kept coming!
|Core Capability I: THE Dream Without a Far Wall.|
|Consolidated from: THE Infinite Dream; the Sentence I Dream of Healing Infinitely; Perpetual Baryogenesis; Bedrock; the Sediment-Shed.|

|Your Dream has no end, and neither do you. Death within your Dream is not death. Whatever is broken is dreamed whole before your existence can come apart. What is borrowed cannot settle on you. You do not recover; you refuse the wound.Every death you return from, you dream once more, slowly, from within. You learn the blow that killed you, and how it found you, and it can never kill you the same way twice|
|Core Capability II: THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour.|
|Consolidated from: THE Osmontian Inscription of THE Dreaming Hour (THE Lived Hour, THE Dreamt Epoch, THE Hour That Dreams); Foundational Acceleration; the Quality of Time.|

|Every second you exist, your existence is refined as though far more time had passed in your Dreams. You may enter a deep Dream and compress an Epoch of refinement into a held moment. Time that acts upon you is drawn into your Dreams, and a dreaming hour moves as you would have it move.|
|Core Capability III: THE Waking Decree.|
|Consolidated from: THE Waking Dream; the Dream Engine; Dream-steering; the passive dreaming of existence near you; the Sentence I Dream of Your End; THE Dream State of Sonder.|

|You may dream around any existence without putting it to sleep, so that it fights as one dreaming. You may enter, steer, and build within the Dreams of others. Existence near you dreams whether you will it or not. What you behold with certainty, you may dream to its end, and what is dreamed away returns to you. You see every being as the center of its own story, and are not moved by it.|
|Core Capability IV: THE Living Grammar.|

|Consolidated from: THE Osmontian Tongue (the Letters I Am, Osmont, Quintessential, Human, and Protagonist; the Words THE Mortal Coil and THE Unbound Lineage; the Sentences I Dream of Your End and I Dream of Healing Infinitely).|

|Your Tongue is no longer a list. It is a grammar. Letters may be spoken alone, joined into Words, or composed into Sentences in the moment of need, each one drawing on your whole existence. THE Mortal Coil disallows borrowed authority wherever it is spoken. THE Unbound Lineage frees a line of descent from any hand behind it.A Sentence you compose may be spoken onto another. For as long as you will it, they carry that Sentence as though it were their own, drawing on your Tongue to heal, to end, or to endure|
|Core Capability V: THE Rendered Design.|
|Consolidated from: the Rendering’s Ruling; the Sovereign’s foundational design (absorbed), the inverted-Elsedimension technique; Infinite Sanguine Cause Mortar.|

|You may render shapes that pull, push, grow, and shrink existence, partition a Root or a being along its natural seams, seal what must be quarantined inside itself, and mortar what you build with your own blood and Causes. What you design, holds.|
|Core Capability VI: THE Tide-Crowned Protagonist.|
|Consolidated from: THE Tide That Owes Nothing; the Letter Protagonist; THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle (hidden); THE Mirror That Keeps; THE Hunger That Refines.|

|The story you walk through bends its spoils toward you. Every enemy you grant death to becomes a Chapter concluded, and what it carried flows to you. Every gift you give freely returns as what can be dreamed. Any capability you witness, you may study and keep. Everything you consume is integrated without waste.You perceive, faintly, the shape of the next great adversity turning toward you, and the spoils it carries, before either arrives. It comes to you as a title without a page. This is known as THE Unwritten Page.|
|Core Capability VII: THE Unkneeling Chill.|
|Consolidated from: THE Unkneeling Crown, THE Unmoved Verdict ...THE Precept of Solipsism; THE Chill of Negative Immensity.|

|You cannot be made to kneel. Bindings and commands find no hold on you. Your committed will cannot be diverted. You see beings truly beneath every mask. What cannot perceive you cannot touch you. And a chill of Negative Immensity runs through every weaving you make, so that your authority passes through any other.The cold of THE Long Night lives in your quarks, and it no longer only obeys the winter. Frost within your reach may be turned, and set upon whatever is borrowed in another, freezing it from within while leaving what is truly theirs untouched|
|Core Capability VIII: THE Sanguine Covenant.|
|Consolidated from: the Sanguine Arts; the Blood Marks...|

|Your blood is your authority. What you mark with it becomes bound to you, its fate held apart from every framework but yours. Your Provenance may divide into its Open Hand and its Closed Crown, and either may act in your stead.Those you have marked with your blood carry a sliver of your Dream within them. Should one of them die, your Dream may catch them once at the edge of their ending, and carry them home to you.|
|Substrate: Dialetheic Infinity.|
|Beneath every capability lies a truth that is also its own opposite. You are finite, and you are infinite. Every capability above draws from it without limit.|
The prompts stopped.
Noah stood in the silence after them and felt what he had become.

For so long, he had been a collection of things, a Foundation here and an Inscription there, an art bolted onto a Word bolted onto a Provenance, each one grand and each one separate. Now he reached for any one of them and found all of them answering at once, because they were no longer separate. They were one body of power, moving as one.
And the Root at the center of him was so close he could almost touch it.
His Dreamer’s sight opened, and showed him.
|Noah Osmont. THE True Human Emperor. THE Human Dreamer.|
|VERITAS: 918. PROVENANCE: 950. POTENTIA: Infinite. PONDUS: 903. OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 941.|
|Density: Consolidated. The numbers count only what existence is willing to count.|
|Root: THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin. Dual Conceptual and Physical Existential Root of Immensity. Attunement: near-union. Future path: Empyros and Fiend, at once.|
|Provenance: THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer (Sovereign-absorbed, Quality of Time).|
|Foundation: THE One Foundation. Ineffable.|

|Core Capabilities: I. THE Dream Without a Far Wall. II. THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour. III. THE Waking Decree. IV. THE Living Grammar. V. THE Rendered Design. VI. THE Tide-Crowned Protagonist. VII. THE Unkneeling Chill. VIII. THE Sanguine Covenant.|
|Substrate: Dialetheic Infinity.|
|Held: one Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin.|
Nine hundred and fifty!

Not quite at Minerva’s ceiling, the very number she had broken herself against trying to become something the winter would not allow. Not quite at the crow’s base, either. But these were not the same kind of number. Every point of his had been pressed and packed and refined until it held far more than any of theirs, and he knew it now as surely as he knew his own name.
Outside the golden domain, the snow fell faster!
And the figure of Ling rose up as she clapped her hands!
