chapters.title: Chapter 5810: Brutality! I
paragraphs: He wanted to test a few things of his newly elevated power, so he tested them.

He started with the frost. Snow was still drifting down through the edge of the golden dome, and he reached for one flake and asked the cold inside it to turn. It did. The flake stopped in the air, spun once, and drifted back up along its own path, against the fall of every other flake around it. He tried a second, and a third. They all answered.
Next, THE Unwritten Page.

He reached for it as he would reach for a thought at the edge of sleep, and something came. A title, faint and unfinished, hanging in his mind with nothing written under it. He could not read all of it. Enough of it was legible to know it pointed downward, deeper into the Basal Floor, toward the direction the Glacial Record had shown him. More information wss slowly coming from this as it seemed to be running in thr background for now.
Last, the Lent Clause.
He told Ling what he wanted to try something.
"Big Boy, you have already tried many things today. What more are you planning on doing?"
He spoke I Dream of Healing Infinitely onto her.
WUU!
It settled into her like a coat laid over her shoulders. She looked at her hands, then bit the pad of her own thumb until it bled. The cut closed before the first drop could fall.
"Oh,"she said. Her eyes had gone very bright, and she kept looking at her thumb as though it had told her a secret.
Results, then. The frost turned. The Page gave him a direction and was still working right now to give him results. And the Clause held on someone else.
He focused on something else.
The memory of the Caretaker being led away in chains was not the only thing the crow had carried.

Ruination spent a long while going through the rest of it! The devoured weavings of the crow had settled into Noah when its body turned to dream, and she read them as she read everything now, thread by thread, perfectly, keeping all of it.

Most of what she found was hunger. Ages of it, flat and endless, the long patrol of a thing that circled the same frozen islands and ate whatever came through the barrier. A good part of the rest was cold, simply cold, the texture of the Long Night soaking through a mind until there was nothing else in it.

But under the hunger and the cold, there were shapes. Routes. Places the crow had been told never to go. Places it had been told to guard. And other things, much larger than it, that it had been afraid of its whole existence!
Ruination passed it to him piece by piece, and Noah listened with his eyes closed.
It was not enough! It was a map drawn by something that had only ever walked one corridor.
So he reached for THE Unwritten Page to finish its work!
He pressed on it, and fed it everything Ruination had pulled from the crow, every route and every forbidden place, and let the Page make the shape of what lay ahead.
The title sharpened. And under it, for the first time, a page began to write itself!
|THE Unwritten Page turns.|
|THE Undersnow is not a single place. It is a descent.|

|THE Basal Floor is its uppermost layer. Here prowl the Guards: Empowered Hollow Night Lifeforms, each one bound to a stretch of frozen dark, each one carrying a Lesser Kryos within it. They do not live here. They keep watch here.|
|Beneath THE Basal Floor lies the second layer.|
|THE Evergrave of THE Unthawed Ages.|
The name settled into him grandly.
|THE Evergrave is not a floor. It is an expanse. It holds skies, seas, frozen Dimensionalities, and lands that stretch farther than any Guard has ever wandered.|
|Its inhabitants are not Hollow as they are Night Lifeforms in truth: whole, aware, and old beyond counting. They remember, and speak, and keep customs no living thing has kept for a very long time.|
|They were not born there.|

|Every one of them unjustly died. Across the ages, and across the cycles of existence that came before this one, reaching back to before THE First Sundering. And when they died, the Night did not let them go. It kept them and has maintained their existences ever since.|
|Many of them are First Lifeforms.|
|Within THE Evergrave, lifeforms approaching Immensity, and lifeforms seated at it, are abundant.|
|Extreme caution is recommended.|
Noah opened his eyes!

First Lifeforms. Provenance Lifeforms from the very beginning! Dead, all of them. Dead for longer than the Legacies had existed. And kept. Held in the cold by the Night, their existences maintained, age after age after age, and The Long Night that was abundant here...now permeated across existence.
Why?!

Why would a winter keep its dead? For what? And who had the Caretaker been, to walk among them and come above the Undersnow to give him missions, and who was the faceless thing that had chained her and led her down toward them?
He did not have the answer. He had a direction, and a name, and a warning, and a great deal more to think about than he had had an hour ago.
And he had one more thing!

Because the Page had not stopped at the Evergrave. At the very bottom of it, there was another line, shorter than the rest, and it was not about the layers below. It was about right now. About the golden bubble of dream he had raised over the place where the crow had died, and what was waiting on the other side of its walls.
He read it twice!
Then he let out a slow breath and looked at Ling.
She was still sitting on her drift of dream-cloud, watching him, but the dazed look had gone out of her face. She had seen his eyes open.
"Hey," Noah said. "We’re going to be pressed a bit, and made to suffer. But even you shouldn’t die with my Osmontian Tongue on you. Hang in there, okay?"
He said it simply. Then he picked the tenth Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin out of the air beside him and threw it to her.
She caught it!
Her eyes went wide!

It was the last one. She held it in her palm and stared at him as if he had tossed her his own heart. Then her existence drew it in. Greedily, all at once, the blue-gold star sinking into her palm and vanishing, and her whole body lit up from the inside. The Root that was her entire existence drank it and blazed, and she shone, her skin glowing gold-violet, her loose hair lifting, the air around her humming with a power that had not been there a heartbeat ago!
He had meant it as preparation.
Then he waved his hand.
The clouds of dream fell!

The golden haze that had held them came down all at once, sinking away into nothing, and the frozen dark of the Basal Floor rushed back in around them. Cold, first. Then the torn Dimensions drifting in their thousands, and the snow, no longer melting, falling straight onto their faces.
And the things that had been waiting in ambush that he had forseen!
There were nine of them!

They had gathered around the dream while it stood, silent, patient, ringed in a wide circle across the floating islands and the empty dark, and every one of them was as large as the crow had been. Some were larger. All of them were Empowered Hollow Night Lifeforms, and every one of them was looking at him.
A wolf with three heads, each one a different age of the same animal, pup and prime and grey-muzzled elder, frost dripping from all three jaws.
A whale that swam through the empty air, vast and slow, its ribs showing white through its frozen hide, whole drowned Dimensions trapped in the ice of its belly.
A spider with legs of clear glass, each leg taller than a mountain, and in the web it had strung between two torn Dimensions hung frozen bodies, hundreds of them, turning slowly in the cold.
A headless titan in armor of black ice, sitting astride a horse made entirely of snow.
An elk whose antlers were a chandelier of frozen light, every branch hung with small pale flames that did not melt anything.
A scorpion of blue ice as long as a mountian range, its tail curled high, its stinger dripping something colder than frost.
An owl with a hundred faces where its one face should have been, all of them human, all of them with their eyes closed.
A hydra of icicles, nine necks swaying, every head blind.
And at the center of the ring, rising up out of the dark before them, the ninth.
A Naga!

Its lower body was a serpent’s coil so long its tail vanishd somewhere among the distant islands, scaled in white and pale blue, and its upper body was a creature with the shape of a woman and none of the warmth of one. It had six arms, long and thin and jointed wrong, each hand holding a blade of rime. Its hood flared wide behind its head, and the inside of that hood was lined with frozen eyes. Its face was beautiful and fiendish and utterly cold, and it smiled at him with far too many teeth.
Noah’s panel-sight flickered across all nine, and every reading came back at the crow’s level or higher!
Okay! They saved him the time to go looking!
The Naga lowered its head toward him!
|You do not belong here.|
|But you do not listen, so...|
|Let this place where you have killed also be your grave.|
<THE Verdant Regard>
It was always spring in the Existential Immense Domain of THE Verdant Regard.

It had been spring there since before some Legacies were founded. Endless meadows rolled away under a pale green sky, thick with flowers that bloomed and fell and bloomed again without ever wilting. Rivers of clear sap ran between them. Trees older than most Dimensions leaned ovver those rivers, their leaves whispering softly, and everything in the whole vast domain grew toward its center, toward her, as flowers turn toward the sun.
The snow had found its way in anyway!
It fell on the meadows in thin grey flakes, and wherever it landed, the flowers did not wilt. They simply stopped. Frozen mid-bloom, petals half open, waiting for a warmth that did not come.
At the center of it all, THE Verdant Regard sat on a bed of moss with her daughter in her arms.

Minerva had not woken! Her body lay limp against her mother’s chest, pale and still, the crooked crown of leaves long gone from her head. Beside them, on the moss, lay the illusory green Root that had been severed on the Plain of Accord. It was frozen now, all the way through! The frost had crept up from its broken end until there was no green left in it at all.
THE Verdant Regard looked at it, and did not move.
Something buzzed at this time.
A faint vibration at the edge of her domain, polite, asking for entry. She knew the shape of it before she even turned her attention toward it, and had known that shape for a very long time.
She let it in.
The air of the domain split open like an eyelid, and he stepped through!

THE SLEEPLESS FIEND did not come as an eye this time. He came as a figure, tall and dark and hazy at the edges, his face barely perceptible, and his presence pressed down on the spring meadows until the frozen flowers bowed. He walked toward her through the snow without hurry.

"THE Keepers of Existence have confirmed it again,"he said. His voice was low and warm and very reasonable. "And again. Riven is one of the keys. Perhaps the major key. Even with the winter growing colder, everything remains on track for him."
He stopped a few paces from her.

"We know none of those already Immense will find the door to THE Great Becoming. It has to be an Immensity that rises after the Long Night. And this newest change, Roots no longer able to mature into Immensity at all, only confirms that we are heading in the right direction. I came to ask you to place your cards on the right lifeform. With Riven, things are confirmed. We can all support him. And we can all gain our access."
The snow fell between them.

"The first Root formed after the Long Night, Osmont, may be a key as well. Even if he is not, he is an anomaly enough that Riven feels he needs to devour what Osmont holds, to ensure his own success." His voice softened.
"So I came to ask. Let us work together, as we used to. Allow us to take Osmont. I am sure there are others, even in THE Legacy of THE Acharya, who have their doubts. Let us get past this together."
He came around behind her!

He stood at her back, and his hand came up, slow and tender, and his fingers traced the side of her neck. Lightly. Almost lovingly. Then his hand slid down her arm, and found hers, and his fingers wove through her own.
She was looking at her daughter’s face.
"I am sorry for our daughter," THE SLEEPLESS FIEND said quietly.
Our daughter!
"Through her, I sensed he was involved as well. Yes?"
His thumb moved slowly across the back of her hand. "Existence wraps tightly around anomalies. Even if he is not a key, he is certainly an important weaving. Can I count on you again?"
THE Verdant Regard said nothing!
"If you say yes, I will contact the others and make things ready. Moriarty and a few more will stay loyal to Lucy’s teachings. They will not move."
His fingers tightened, very slightly, around hers."So it may be a small war, to get Osmont. Or it may be a simple extraction, if we plan well enough."
THE Verdant Regard looked down at the frozen Root on the moss.
She looked at it for a long time. Her eyes were heavy, full of grief so old and so deep! The snow settled on the frozen Root, and on her daughter’s still face, and on her own green hair.
Then her eyes sharpened!

She raised her head. Not toward the Fiend. Past him, past the edge of her domain, past the Legacy’s thousand mountains and the blizzard howling between them, toward a place most beings could not have seen at all. A lone dark mountain, wrapped in a trembling coat of hazy Immensity, burning steady against the storm!
Her gaze held there, sharp as a blade.
And her fingers closed tighter around the hand of THE SLEEPLESS FIEND.

chapters.title: Chapter 5811: Brutality! II
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
The Naga’s words had barely finished falling when all nine Guards moved at once!

They came from every direction, above and below and to every side, the ring they had formed around the dream closing like a fist. The whale dove. The wolf’s three heads howled in three different ages of the same voice, and the spider’s glass legs stabbed down through the dark.
Across the ring, the owl’s hundred faces turned toward them in perfect unison, and every one of those closed human eyes began, very slowly, to open.
Noah had perhaps half an instant to think.

Nine of them. Each one at the crow’s level or higher, and the crow alone had killed him once. Ling at his side, shining with the Quintessential ECG he had just thrown her. The Lent Clause already sitting in her like a coat. His eight Core Capabilities, untested in a real fight, all of them still more promise than proof.
As brutal and painful as this would be...it was a great test of what he had become as he welcomed it with unbound tyranny, his body erupting with golden clouds of infinite dreams!
"You first,"he said, looking at the Hydra.
Ling was already moving.

The hydra reached them first because it had nine heads and did not need to see where it was going. Its necks of icicle lashed out in a blind fan, and Ling went straight through the middle of them. Her leg came around in a blur of blue silk and shattered one head, then another, then a third, the ice bursting into glittering fragments as her thighs were packed with enough density to crush trillions of Dimensions!
The heads grew back before the fragments had finished falling.
That was a problem. Noah watched the regrowth once, saw where the cold of THE Long Night flowed up from the hydra’s chest to rebuild each head, and knew where to put his hand.
He had wanted to test the frost on something living. Here it was. He could also control THE Long Night!
He flew in under the fan of necks, his Provenance pressuring the creature as if he weighed infinite density, and he laid his palm flat against the hydra’s breast, and tugged on the cold inside it.

It was the easiest thing he had ever done. The Long Night’s cold lived in his quarks, and the cold inside the hydra was the same cold, borrowed, poured into it by the winter to keep it moving. He simply told that cold to face the other way.
HUUUM!
More than a hundred Provenance Essence burned in his body, but...
The cold did what he commanded it to do!
It turned inward, and froze the hydra from its heart outward, nine necks locking rigid one after another, until the whole creature hung in the air as a single sculpture of blue ice.
Ling kicked it as grandly...
It exploded into powder!
BOOM!
Result: With enough Provenance burned, the frost worked on even a Hollow Night Lifeform. It did not touch what was truly the creature’s own, and there had not been much of that in a Guard.

His new Foundation and Tide worked without him doing a thing as he stood above the corpse of another lifeform, his mouth open as blue gold lava like mist leaked from him, his eyes shooting beams of light as he looked fiendish!
|A Guard has been granted death.|
|The Chapter it carried has concluded.|
|Spoils: Lesser Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin x10. Memories of a Guard.|
Ten!
Ten small snowflake crystals spun out of the drifting powder and into his hand, and behind them came the memories, a thin cold thread of them, sinking into his mind.
He did not have time for much thinking or memories as...
The wolf’s three heads came down on him from above!
The pup’s jaws closed on his left arm, the prime’s on his right shoulder, the grey elder’s on his throat. And he felt it all as their Provenance burned!

They were not biting through his body. They were biting through his time. The pup’s bite made his arm young, soft, unfinished. The elder’s made his throat old, thin, failing. Between them, the prime held him and tore.
It hurt. It hurt in a direction he had not known pain could come from!
But he had met THE First Gu of Time and had felt the death of time itself!
So fuck this motherfucker!
Noah reached for THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour, and drew the wolf’s time into his Dreams.
HUUM!

A dreaming hour moved as he wished it to move. The pup’s jaws went slack, then soft, then aged in a heartbeat into the jaws of something ancient. The elder’s jaws went the other way, back and back, until they belonged to a newborn that could not close them at all.
Suddenly all three heads were the same age: old, older, oldest, the whole creature pouring through its own lifetime in the space of a breath.
He dreamed that an infinite time ravaged across its existence!
It died of old age with its teeth still in him.
He pulled its jaws off his throat and let the corpse fall!
|A Guard has been granted death. Spoils: Lesser Kryos x10. Memories of a Guard.|
Twenty. He had twenty now Lesser Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins now!
He took eight of them, pressed them together in his palms, and felt them fuse. Four into one. Four into one. Two genuine Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins lay in his hands, cold and humming.
He did not keep them.

He sent them down through his own existence and into THE Infiniverse, into the Dream Engine, into the dreams of the people sleeping on the golden shore. One to his mother. One to Seo-yeon. He felt them land, felt each one settle into a dreaming existence like a stone dropped into a well, and felt the Tide notice at once.
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has answered your giving.|
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin x5.|
Five blue-gold stars bloomed at his side.
He ate them one after another, without stopping, while the spider’s glass legs came stabbing down around him, and each one went into him like a sun and packed itself down into his Root!
The attacks did not stop even as he sought to advance!
That was how it went, after that. He stopped counting the minutes.

The scorpion caught him from behind and put its stinger through his chest. Whatever dripped from it was colder than frost, colder than the current Long Night, a cold that did not freeze but ended. He died...well, not really.

The golden clouds caught him and spat him back out, and in the instant of coming back he dreamed that death through once, slowly, from the inside. He learned the cause of the dreamed death. He learned the angle and the timing and the exact shape of the Dimensionality that had killed him.
The scorpion stung him again with its concentrated cold and Provenance, but this time...

It went nowhere. The stinger slid off him as though it had struck a wall, and the scorpion recoiled, confused, and Noah reached out and broke its tail off at the base with one hand, his Dream of it ending covering its body as a cloudy light covered it, and it began to flake off!
"OOOOOH!"
Not even screaming did a damn fucking thing.

Ling finished it. She came down on its back with both heels and drove it into a floating island so hard the island split in half, and she kept kicking until the scorpion stopped moving and the island stopped being an island. Its stinger stabbed Ling many times, but she was healed instantly for anything that passed through!
|Spoils: Lesser Kryos x10. Memories of a Guard.|
He fused eight. Two Kryos, down into the dreams of Henry and Adelaide.
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin x5.|
He ate them all.
What he was doing now almost became second nature as he killed, he gave away, and he got back even more in return!
But the brutal battle was still ongoing.
The owl opened its eyes.

All hundred faces at once, every eye in every one of them snapping open and fixing on the two of them, and the weight of that gaze came down like a mountain! It was a perception so total that it did not just see them. It held them. Ling froze mid-kick, locked in place, her mouth opening in a silent scream as a hundred human gazes crushed down on her Root.
Noah was not held.

He looked at the owl, and the owl could not quite find him. Its hundred faces kept sliding off him, searching, blinking, their eyes watering with the strain. What could not perceive him could not touch him, and even with a hundred faces, this thing could not see him properly.
He walked up the length of its gaze, into the space between its hundred faces, and dreamed its end.
He looked magisterially grand as tendeils of blue gold leaked out of him as he stared tyrannically into a monstrous beast, his Provenance beginning to flood into it.

He looked at it with total certainty, and the owl began to dream away. Its faces went first. One by one, their eyes closed again, and they flaked off into golden dust and drifted into him. Then its feathers. Then its body. Ling dropped free and caught herself in the air, gasping, as the last of the owl’s hundred faces went soft and gold and gone.
|Spoils: Lesser Kryos x10. Memories of a Guard.|
The loot was fused and sent to Barbatos. And another to Adelaide, because he could!
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin x5.|
He ate them.

He was getting stronger. He could feel it now, not in steps but in a steady rising pressure, as a flood rises behind a wall. Every Kryos he gave away came back to him as something grander, and everything that came back to him he swallowed, and his Root drank and drank and would not stop.
The remaining Guards had noticed as the pressure he radiated has nearly fucking doubled as it was insane.
He finally felt like he was returning to his old self!

The Empowered Hollow Night Lifeforms pulled back. The spider, the elk, the whale, the headless titan, and the Naga, all five of them drawing out of reach and circling, wary now. Four of their number were dead. They had come to bury him, and he was burying them instead!
Ling came up beside him, bleeding from both arms and the side of her head, her gold-violet light flickering where the owl’s gaze had crushed it.

Noah asked her mentally, in a few words, whether she could keep going. She told him, in fewer, exactly where he could put that question. She was smiling when she said it as her fair complexion looked extremely murderous!
He put a hand on her shoulder and turned the Lent Clause up even more.
"Then let’s finish it," he said.

The spider had spent the pause building. Its web stretched between three torn Dimensions now, thick with frozen bodies, every strand of it humming with a cold that caught and held. It flung the whole web at them at once.
Noah rendered.

A shape bloomed in the air before him, and another inside it, and another, a nested design of partition. He did not burn the web or break it. He found its seams, the natural lines where it had been woven together, and cut along all of them at once. The web fell apart into a thousand clean pieces, and the frozen bodies tumbled loose and drifted away into the dark, and the spider was left standing on its glass legs with nothing between it and him.
His golden clouds how now become a sea as they crashed down into it!

The elk lowered its chandelier antlers and every small pale flame on them flared white, and the light that came off them was a light that erased. Where it touched, things stopped having been. Noah felt it take a piece of his shoulder and leave nothing behind, not even a wound.
He spoke.
"I Dream of Your End."

And while the elk’s erasing light was still pouring across him, he composed another Sentence in the moment and spoke it onto Ling. She carried it at once, the Clause settling onto her, and she flew straight through the elk’s white light untouched and kicked its antlers off its head.
BOOM!
His Provenance and her ridiculous existence imposed itself on thr creature simultaneously as it could do nothing else!
The elk dreamed away into gold.
|Spoils: Lesser Kryos x10, and again x10. Memories of two Guards.|
Four more Kryos, fused and given. His mother again. Seo-yeon again. Henry. Emotive, still dreaming in her Earliest Folds.
Well, there were Kazuhiko and Erikson and others, but their time would come.
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin x10.|
He ate them all!
WUU!
Simultaneously...the whale came down on them like a falling Dimension.

It was the largest of the nine, the size of a contnent, and it simply swam down onto them through the dark, meaning to crush them flat against a floating island under the whole weight of its frozen body and the drowned Dimensions inside it.
Noah did not move out of its way.

He let it land on him. All of it, the whole impossible mass pressing down, and THE One Foundation took the weight and kept it. Did not lift it. Did not resist it. Simply kept it, and built on it, and every immensity of that pressure hardened into more of the floor beneath him. He stood under the whale and felt himself grow heavier with every heartbeat it spent trying to crush him!
Then he pushed up as he looked like a fiendish dreamer bearing the weight of all of existence!
The whale rose. It was lifted, slowly, bodily, by a man standing under it, and Ling came in from the side and drove her knee into its eye as she struck like a sharp blade, piercing into it!

Noah’s Provenance added on as he dreamed it dead, and between the two of them, they broke it open along its spine. The drowned Dimensions in its belly spilled out into the dark, frozen, silent, and the whale went still.
The headless titan charged before the whale had finished falling.
It came on its horse of snow with a sword of black ice as long as a river, and its first swing caught Ling across the waist and threw her half a Gigaparsec!
Noah’s eyes flashed coldly.
He let his Provenance divide.

The Closed Crown rose out of him, arms crossed, dark gold at the edges, a smaller shape of himself burning with every scrap of his tyranny, and he did not hold it back. He stepped aside and let it act in his stead. Seas of infinite Dreams raged out and converged on it!
It met the titan’s next swing with its bare forearm and shattered the sword with boundless dreams, then took the titan’s horse by the neck and snapped it.
Last, it took the titan by the stump where its head should have been, and pulled, and the titan came apart in its hands like a doll made of frozen straw.
Across the dark, Ling got up. She wiped the blood off her mouth and looked at the Closed Crown, and then at Noah, and did not say anything at all.
|Spoils: Lesser Kryos x10, and again x10. Memories of two Guards.|
More loot was fused as this time, Kazuhiko and THE Emperor Penguin got something!
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin x10.|
He ate them.
And then there was only the Naga.
Noah stretched and cracked his neck as he breathed out lava like blue gold flames while staring ahead.

It had not fought. It had watched, coiled at the edge of the dark, six arms still and its hood of frozen eyes open wide, while every other Guard died in front of it. Now it rose up before him, its tail vanishing into the distant islands, its six blades of rime lifting together.
Its beautiful face was no longer smiling.
Noah looked at it, and he affirmed it was the strongest of the nine by a wide margin. He could feel that, and he could also feel, underneath all its composure, that it was afraid!
So he began to dance.

THE Kindled Circle, the dance Ling had taught him in the golden dream, the dance her father had passed down to her. His arms swept out in a wide, unbroken arc, and his body turned with it, and his feet struck the empty air, heel and ball, a stamp that rolled out across the whole Basal Floor like a drum!
The Naga struck at him with all six blades at once.

He turned through them. Every blade that came at him found only the arc of his turning, the flowing, seamless motion carrying him through the gaps between the strikes, and as he turned he struck back, each stamp of his feet a blow, each sweep of his arms a cut. A blade came off in his hand. Then an arm. Then another!
His Provenance of THE Human Dreamer became sharp and deadly!
Ling came in from above, and together they took the Naga apart.

He drew closer to his Root with every turning. He could feel it happening, faster now, faster than it had in the golden dream. The Root and the man, leaning into each other, the gap between them closing.
On the ninth turning, he tore the Naga’s head open, and every frozen eye inside it brust!
On the tenth, he took its last two arms.
On the eleventh, he reached into its chest, where its cold heart pulsed around its Kryos, and closed his hand.
The Naga looked at him with its beautiful, fiendish, terrified face.
On the twelfth turning, he ripped its heart out, and it died!
|The last Guard has been granted death.|
|Spoils: Lesser Kryos x10. Memories of the Naga.|
And his existence caught fire!
|THE Kindled Circle has been performed to its Truest Essence.|
|The distance between you and your Root has closed entirely.|
|Your existence and your Root have become one.|
It was like nothing he had ever felt. The Root at the center of him had always been his, spinning, turning, a heart of Immensity he carried. Now there was no center to carry it in.
The Root was everywhere. It was in his skin and his blood and his packed quarks, in his Provenance and his dreams and the cold of the Long Night inside him. He...did not have a Root anymore.
He was one.

His entire existence buzzed with utterly overwhelming power, a pressure so vast and so total that the snow stopped in the air around him, and the torn Dimensions drifting in the dark trembled, and across the whole Basal Floor, everything that could still feel anything felt him.
He hung in the frozen dark among the corpses of nine Guards, with Ling beside him bleeding and staring, and sensed what he had become.
And he knew, with perfect clarity, that he could not take it any further.

He could feel the door. Exactly where it should be, at the very top of everything he now was, the place where a Root became Immense. And it was shut. Simply not there to be opened, because existence had decided there would be no more Immensity, and existence had meant it!
He could not make his Root Immense. Not now. Perhaps not ever.
Noah looked up into the falling snow as it fell more and more heavily.
"Do I...have to be Immense?"
His voice carried across the whole dark expanse.
"Is Immensity the only path? If existence itself makes becoming Immense impossible, does one... simply give up?"
The snow held still around him, as if it were listening.
"I have advanced so much since merely shooting fireballs,"Noah said. "Can I...not do something unfathomably Quintessential here?"

They came from every direction, above and below and to every side, the ring they had formed around the dream closing like a fist.
The whale dove.
The wolf’s three heads howled in three different ages of the same voice, and the spider’s glass legs stabbed down through the dark.
Across the ring, the owl’s hundred faces turned toward them in perfect unison, and every one of those closed human eyes began, very slowly, to open.
Noah had perhaps half an instant to think.
Nine of them.
Each one at the crow’s level or higher, and the crow alone had killed him once.
Ling at his side, shining with the Quintessential ECG he had just thrown her.
The Lent Clause already sitting in her like a coat.
His eight Core Capabilities, untested in a real fight, all of them still more promise than proof.
As brutal and painful as this would be...it was a great test of what he had become as he welcomed it with unbound tyranny, his body erupting with golden clouds of infinite dreams!
"You first,"he said, looking at the Hydra.
Ling was already moving.
The hydra reached them first because it had nine heads and did not need to see where it was going.
Its necks of icicle lashed out in a blind fan, and Ling went straight through the middle of them.

Her leg came around in a blur of blue silk and shattered one head, then another, then a third, the ice bursting into glittering fragments as her thighs were packed with enough density to crush trillions of Dimensions!
The heads grew back before the fragments had finished falling.
That was a problem.
Noah watched the regrowth once, saw where the cold of THE Long Night flowed up from the hydra’s chest to rebuild each head, and knew where to put his hand.
He had wanted to test the frost on something living.
Here it was.
He could also control THE Long Night!
He flew in under the fan of necks, his Provenance pressuring the creature as if he weighed infinite density, and he laid his palm flat against the hydra’s breast, and tugged on the cold inside it.
It was the easiest thing he had ever done.
The Long Night’s cold lived in his quarks, and the cold inside the hydra was the same cold, borrowed, poured into it by the winter to keep it moving.
He simply told that cold to face the other way.
HUUUM!
More than a hundred Provenance Essence burned in his body, but...
The cold did what he commanded it to do!
It turned inward, and froze the hydra from its heart outward, nine necks locking rigid one after another, until the whole creature hung in the air as a single sculpture of blue ice.
Ling kicked it as grandly...
It exploded into powder!
BOOM!
Result: With enough Provenance burned, the frost worked on even a Hollow Night Lifeform.
It did not touch what was truly the creature’s own, and there had not been much of that in a Guard.

His new Foundation and Tide worked without him doing a thing as he stood above the corpse of another lifeform, his mouth open as blue gold lava like mist leaked from him, his eyes shooting beams of light as he looked fiendish!
|A Guard has been granted death.|
|The Chapter it carried has concluded.|
|Spoils: Lesser Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin x10.
Memories of a Guard.|
Ten!
Ten small snowflake crystals spun out of the drifting powder and into his hand, and behind them came the memories, a thin cold thread of them, sinking into his mind.

The wolf’s three heads came down on him from above!
The pup’s jaws closed on his left arm, the prime’s on his right shoulder, the grey elder’s on his throat.
And he felt it all as their Provenance burned!
They were not biting through his body.
They were biting through his time.
The pup’s bite made his arm young, soft, unfinished.
The elder’s made his throat old, thin, failing.
Between them, the prime held him and tore.
It hurt.
It hurt in a direction he had not known pain could come from!
But he had met THE First Gu of Time and had felt the death of time itself!
So fuck this motherfucker!
Noah reached for THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour, and drew the wolf’s time into his Dreams.
HUUM!
A dreaming hour moved as he wished it to move.
The pup’s jaws went slack, then soft, then aged in a heartbeat into the jaws of something ancient.
The elder’s jaws went the other way, back and back, until they belonged to a newborn that could not close them at all.
Suddenly all three heads were the same age: old, older, oldest, the whole creature pouring through its own lifetime in the space of a breath.
He dreamed that an infinite time ravaged across its existence!
It died of old age with its teeth still in him.
He pulled its jaws off his throat and let the corpse fall!

chapters.title: Chapter 5812: Epiphany!
paragraphs: Noah looked at himself with every single sight. He turned his whole perception inward and looked at what he had become, standing in the frozen dark of the Basal Floor among the corpses of nine Guards, his existence and his Root one thing now, buzzing with a power so total that the snow still hung motionless in the air around him.
And at the very top of it, where the door should have been, there was nothing!
He looked at that nothing for a long time.

If a being could not become Immense, then that was the end of the road. Wasn’t it? That was what everyone believed. Every Provenance Lifeform, every Progeny on evry golden cloud, every Immense One on every throne. Immensity was the formula. It was the shape existence had given to growth itself, the one direction every climbing thing had always climbed. And existence had just closed it.
So that was it, then. The ceiling. The end!
But...
Was it?!
He turned the thought over again, slowly, and looked at it from the other side.

Existence had shut the door. But existence did not do things for no reason. Even the Long Night, tainted as it was, even the cold that culled and the cold that closed, even the Counting pressing on every Root in existence, all of it came from somewhere and pointed somewhere. So what was a closed door pointing at?
Everyone assumed it meant no!
What if it did not?!
"What if it is not a negative thing?" Noah said quietly, to the frozen dark. "What if it is existence saying... do not follow?"
His existence buzzed!

It shook through him from his skin to his core, a single deep resonant note, as if every packed quark in his body had just heard something it agreed with. The snow around him trembled in the air. Somewhere far off, a torn Dimension drifted, and the light inside it flickered!
|A reading of existence has been made.|
|The door to Immensity is closed to all who would pass through it.|
|A closed door does not only say no. It also says: not this way.|
|Existence has not forbidden growth. It has forbidden following.|
Not this way!
Noah breathed in, slow and deep, and let his Dream open.

He dreamed an infinite dream! It was not a dream of one thing. It was a dream of everything that could be, every possible path his existence could take from this exact moment, all of them at once, spread out before him in the span of a single instant.

He saw himself Immense, and saw that version of himself crushed against the closed door, severed like Minerva, weeping in the snow. He saw himself refusing to climb and freezing slowly in the Long Night with his family around him.

He saw himself as a tyrant eating whole Legacies. He saw himself as nothing. He saw himself as everything. Billions of futures and more, branching and branching, each one real for the space of the instant, each one his.
And somewhere in all of them, under all of them, a pattern!
He came out of the instant, and it had not even been an instant!
"I see it now," Noah said.
His voice had gone very calm. Very far away.
"All of it. Every path I could take, at once. They are all happening. They have all already happened. It is strange, how simple it looks from here."

He looked at his own hands. "Every one of those paths that climbs toward Immensity ends at the same shut door. Every single one. It does not matter how strong I become, or how clever. The door is the same. It was built to stop things exactly like me."
The snow drifted around him.
"But the other paths do not climb. They change."

He was quiet for a moment."I watched the ones that change. Under pressure, they become something else. They always have. A creature is cornered by the cold, and its children grow fur. A creature is starved, and its children learn to eat stone. Humans were soft things once, in places that wanted them dead, and they did not become Immense. They became...human. Over and over, under every weight that was ever laid on them, they became something that had not existed before."
He lifted his head.

"Existence does not want another Immense One. It has enough of those. It has shut the old road, and every being on it will keep pushing on the door and wondering why it will not open." A pause."I do not have to push. I only have to...evolve."
|Your Infinite Dream has gazed upon boundless possibility.|
|A path has been found where no path was written.|
|Path established: THE Osmontian Culmination.|
|Your existence may evolve.|
|Not into Immensity. Into something that has never existed.|

|Everything you have ever dreamed, every memory, every emotion, every life you lived in the death of time, every battle, every gift, every loss, every experience your existence has held across its entire span, will be gathered and culminated.|
|From all of it, a new lifeform will be made. It will be the product of everything you have lived, and it will belong to no path but your own.|
|Requirement: your present existence must first be filled to its Absolute. Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins are the current best means.|
|Present saturation: 44 integrated. Estimated saturation of your present existence: 11%.|
|The road is arduous. The resources required are unfathomable.|
|Your Dream holds that it is possible.|
Eleven percent!

Forty-four Quintessential ECGs, and he was barely a tenth of the way there. Hundreds more. Perhaps far more than hundreds, if the Absolute of his existence kept growing as he grew. Every one of them earned by giving, every gift paid for by killing things like the nine Guards dead around him, and all of it under a winter that grew heavier with every Root that dared to exist.
It would be the hardest road he had ever walked!
And it was his!

Not written by Those Who Remain. Not handed down by a Legacy. Not the door every Immense One in existence had passed through and every Root in existence was now pounding on in vain. A road nobody had ever walked, because nobody had ever looked at a shut door and understood that it was pointing somewhere else.

Noah looked up into the falling snow. It had begun to move again around him, drifting down across the dead Guards and the torn Dimensions and the frozen islands of the Basal Floor, and Ling hung beside him in the dark, silent, watching his face.
He smiled!
"Fuck Immensity," Noah said. "Fuck the written path."
His existence buzzed, and the snow scattered around him!
"Fuck existence."
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5813: Arrogance!
paragraphs: His mind still buzzed with his proclamations!
Thirty-four Lesser Kryos still turned in the air around Noah, pale blue and cold, the last spoils of the nine Guards.
He did not intend to keep any of them!

He pressed them together four at a time. Each set flared, fused, and settled into a single genuine Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin, dense and huming, until eight whole Kryos hung before him and two Lesser ones remained, too few to make another.
Four went to Achilles. The king had swallowed the Long Night’s cold to make his day-old Root stronger, and Noah could afford to give to help him.
Noah sent the Kryos through his Legacy body, across existence, to the mountain where Achilles stood with Rose amidst the snow.
The other four went home, into THE Infiniverse and the Dream Engine, to three people. Two to Eon. One to Ul’moreth. One to Naldine, along with the last two Lesser Kryos.
He felt each one land!
And THE Tide answered!
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has answered your giving.|
|Given: eight Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins and two Lesser Kryos, to four lives you hold dear.|
|Returned, as dreamed: Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin x22.|
Twenty-two blue-gold stars bloomed around him in the frozen dark!
He took them all, one after another, and felt each one spread through the whole of him at once. His existence climbed with every one!
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins integrated: 66.|
|THE Osmontian Culmination. Present saturation: 16%.|
|Estimated Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins still required: 334. The estimate will rise as your existence rises.|
Sixteen percent! A long road lay ahead.
Then he looked at himself.
|Noah Osmont. THE True Human Emperor. THE Human Dreamer.|
|VERITAS: 999/1. PROVENANCE: 999/1. POTENTIA: Infinite. PONDUS: 999/1. OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 999/1.|
He frowned!

The numbers would not hold still. VERITAS read nine hundred and ninety-nine, then one, then nine hundred and ninety-nine again. PROVENANCE slid from one to nine hundred and fifty to seven hundred and back. Every line on the panel shifted between one and nine hundred and ninety-nine, never landing for longer than a breath.
He understood it quickly. His Root and his existence were one now, so there was no separate thing inside him for existence to measure. It was the same reason Ling’s panel read one in every line.
So he tested it!
He chose five hundred for VERITAS. It settled there and stayed. Nine hundred and ninety-nine, and it went there. One, and it sat quietly at one.
He stopped.

The panel was his to set anywhere in that range, and others read whatever he chose. Under it, the real thing kept climbing. The door to Immensity was shut, but his foundation could still be refined and his Provenance still elevated, and the ceiling existence had built hung over a road he no longer walked.
He left the panel at one. It seemed polite.
Then he closed his eyes and went looking through the memories of the dead!

Nine Guards,. Alone, each was a narrow corridor, one route through the frozen dark walked for longer than anything should have to walk it. He laid them over one another, route on route, island on rift on torn Dimension, and they began to fit.
|The memories of nine Guards have been combined. THE Basal Floor has been mapped.|
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer now extends across the whole of it. Every Empowered Hollow Night Lifeform upon this Floor dreams a little, and where it dreams, you may perceive it.|
And Ruination went further!
|Master. The map is fixed, but they are not.|
|I have run their positions through my Root and recorded every probability of their movement. You now have them in real time, and where they will be for some while after.|
Noah’s eyes opened, and they shone brilliantly!

He saw the whole Basal Floor at once, through his Dreams, with Ruination’s predictions laid over it like a lattice of light. Floating islands of ice by the thousands. Torn Dimensions hanging between them, and towering cold-filled trees. And moving among it all, small bright points where the Guards were dreaming.
Fifty-five of them!
He reached for each one and felt its weight. Every one was at the Naga’s level, some grander, a few a great deal grander. Fifty-five more of what had taken everything he and Ling had to kill nine.
Then he turned his perception north, and went very still.
A rift split the frozen dark there, blue and vast. The way down. He could feel it pulling at the cold in his quarks!
And coiled around its mouth, like a guard dog around a dor, was something that did not fit on the map at all.

It was colossal! The floating islands near it drifted in its shadow. He could not make out its shape. It had too many limbs, or none, or limbs made of the same frozen dark as the space around it, and a halo of stilled snow hung motionless over where its head should be.
Its aura was wrong!

It was Immense, and it was not. The weight he had felt on the Plain of Accord when the thrones filled was there, and then gone, and then there again, as though this thing had climbed toward the door of Immensity, stopped exactly halfway, and stood on that threshold for longer than anything should stand anywhere.
It was not asleep!
He refocused. He turned from the rift in the north to the fifty-five bright points scattered across the dark, and began, very calmly, to plan which one to kill first.
But...
Then he stopped planning!
"Why one at a time?" he said.
Ling looked at him. He was not speaking to her.
"I see all of them. Where they are now, where they will be, every path each of them will walk for some while yet. I see them as a sky sees the ground."
His voice was very calm.
"Fifty-five points. And I was about to choose among them as though I were one of them. As though I had to go to each in turn and stand before it and trade blows until one of us fell."
He looked out across the frozen dark.
"That is the common sense of this place. The Guard patrols its corridor, and the one who comes to kill it walks the corridor too. I do not need to walk their corridors."
He raised his hand, and began to build!
Not a weapon anyone else had made. He had none, and wanted none. Instead he reached into what he now was, Core Capabilities moving as one body, and chose the pieces.

First, the shape. THE Rendered Design drew it in the dark: a great curved frame rendered out of nested pull and push, its limbs sweeping outward and back, partitioned along the seams where a bow must bend and mortared at the grip with his own blood and Teloi so that it would hold under any strain. What he designed, held.
Then the draw. THE One Foundation settled into the limbs as weight.

Then the string. THE Living Grammar spun it from a single Sentence, spoken quietly into the air and drawn taut: I Dream of Your End. Whatever the string sent forward would go already carying that decree.
Then the arrow, and that was the part that made the frozen dark itself go quiet!

He reached into THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour. Every second he existed, he was refined as though far more time had passed inside his Dreams. He had never once turned that the other way. Now he did. He opened a deep Dream and let an Epoch pour into it, and then another, and another, time without end, and he did not refine anything with it. He dreamed it decaying.

Trillions of years of wearing down, of erosion, of stone to sand and sand to dust and dust to nothing, of every bond in a thing slowly letting go of every other. And then he dreamed that decay across trillions more years, and pressed all of it, every aeon of it, down into a single point, and drew that point out along the string into the shape of an arrow.

Last, the edge. THE Unkneeling Chill ran through the arrowhead, the Negative Immensity in his weavings that let his authority pass through any other, and the Kneeling Frost with it, the Long Night’s own cold, turned to hunt whatever was borrowed in a thing.
He closed his hand around the grip!
|THE Rendered Design, THE One Foundation, THE Living Grammar, THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour, and THE Unkneeling Chill have been combined.|
|Its string is the Sentence I Dream of Your End. Everything it looses carries that decree.|

|Its arrows are Epochs of decay. Each one holds trillions of years of time’s erosion on all authority, dreamed across trillions more, compressed to a single point. What an arrow strikes, it ages through all of them at once.|
|Its edge carries the Chill of Negative Immensity and THE Kneeling Frost. Its arrows pass through authority, and turn the borrowed cold within their targets against them.|
|THE Tide-Crowned Protagonist binds the whole: what the bow grants death to, its spoils flow to you.|
|Substrate: Dialetheic Infinity. Your Dream has no far wall. Its arrows have no end.|
He looked at what he had made!

The bow was blue and gold and taller than a mountain, its limbs curving back at their tips like the horns of the crown of light above his brow. The same tendrils that burned beneath his skin ran through its frame, pulsing in time with his existence. It did not look forged. It looked dreamed, because it was, and it looked alive, because it was part of him.
He set his feet on the empty air.

Bare to the waist, skin dark diamond-jade, tendrils branching over his chest and arms, hair hanging weightless around that jagged crown, the bow in his hand, he looked like a fiend out of a dream. A dream archer, drawing on the dark itself!

And both his paths moved through him when he drew. The Fiend was the weight in the limbs and the density of the body holding them. The Empyros was the decree in the string and the Epochs dreamed into the arrow. An arrow from this bow would land as a mountain, and as a sentence, and as the end of more time than anything it struck had ever lived.
He drew the string back!

The arrow formed as he drew, and kept growing. Past the length of the bow. Past the size of a floating island. By the time the string reached his ear, it stretched across gigaparsecs, a spear of compressed aeons so heavy that the torn Dimensions near it began to drift toward it!

Space around him twisted. The frozen dark bent inward toward the arrowhead in long curving lines, and the Dimensionality of the whole region strained at its seams, groaning, as the thing he held pressed on everything around it just by existing.
The snow nearest the arrow aged as it fell, going grey, then brittle, then to powder before it reached the edge of his light.
Ling had backed away several islands’ worth of distance without seeming to decide to as her thighs vibrated!
Noah looked down the arrow at all fifty-five bright points at once.
He let go!

The arrow left the string and split. One became many in a single instant, fifty-five arrows of blue-gold time tearing away in fifty-five directions, each one gigaparsecs long, each one following a line of Ruination’s lattice to exactly where its target would be when it arrived.
An instant passed. And...
HUUM!
The first one hit!

It struck a three-legged titan of hail in the far east, and the titan aged. All of it, all at once. Its ice clouded, then cracked, then crumbled, trillions of years of forced Dimensional erosion arriving in the space of a single heartbeat. Its legs went to gravel beneath it. The island it stood on wore down to sand and drifted apart, and three torn Dimensions nearby went grey and brittle and collapsed like old paper in a fire. When the light faded, half the titan was gone, simply worn away to nothing, and the half that remained was flaking into gold, dreaming toward its end!
Then the rest hit!

Across the whole Basal Floor, fifty-four more flashes bloomed, each one a sphere of blue-gold light where a Guard had been struck by more time than its whole existence had ever held. The sound came late and all at once, one vast rolling roar that shook the islands in their drift.
Most of them survived the first volley. They were each at the Naga’s level or grander. One arrow wore away limbs, heads, whole portions of their existences, but it was not enough.
Noah drew again!

"I...can do this infinitely," he said. "My Dream has no far wall. It does not tire. It does not need to rest between one arrow and the next. So why should I not? Why walk up to each of them and trade blows, when I can stand here and draw?"
Another arrow formed, blazing, gigaparsecs long.
"I do not need to follow the common sense of anything else. I can do what I see fit!"
BOOM!
The third volley landed, and the first of them died.

The titan of hail went first, its dreaming half worn away to the last grain. Then a thing like a frozen jellyfish the size of a sea, far to the south, aged into a cloud of white dust. Then a pair of frost wyrms coiled around a floating island, both of them eroding to bone and then to nothing in the same flash. One after another, across the whole Floor, bright points on Ruination’s lattice went out and did not come back.
And the spoils came.
|A Guard has been granted death. Spoils: Lesser Kryos x10. Memories of a Guard.|
Then again, and again, faster than the prompts could keep up with, until Ruination simply began to tally.
|Guards granted death: 11. Lesser Kryos received: 110.|

Noah fused as they came, without stopping his drawing arm. Four Lesser Kryos pressed together at his hip into a genuine Kryos, then the next four, the fusing happening in the back of his existence while the front of it went on loosing arrows.
Every Kryos he made, he sent away, down into THE Infiniverse, into the dreams of his people, wherever someone he held dear was sleeping.

The Tide answered each gift, and he ate every Quintessential ECG the moment it arrived. Each one spread through the whole of him, and every arrow after it came off the string a little larger and a little more certain!
|Guards granted death: 24. Lesser Kryos received: 240. Kryos fused and given: 60.|
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing notes that gifts given to enemies now considered weaker than you carry less weight than gifts given with thought. Its returns have diminished accordingly.|
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins integrated this battle: 41.|
Diminished due to weakness? Okay!

The Guards that could still fight were fighting back now. Storms of frost came howling at him from a dozen directions. A spear of black ice the length of a Dimension. A wave of cold that froze the air solid for a thousand miles. They broke against his outline, or dreamed away into haze before they arrived, or landed on him and were kept by THE One Foundation, and every ton of that pressure went straight into the limbs of the bow and came back out behind the next arrow.
Nothing they threw slowed his drawing arm.
|Guards granted death: 38. Lesser Kryos received: 380. Kryos fused and given: 95.|
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins integrated this battle: 64. Total integrated: 130.|
|THE Osmontian Culmination. Present saturation: 29%.|
Thirty-eight!

Seventeen bright points remained on the lattice, all of them worn and cracked and aged, several of them fleeing across the Floor as fast as their crumbling bodies could carry them. Following them would be easy. So would drawing until there were none.
He kept drawing!
But he was not looking at them.
His eyes had left the Guards some time ago. Every arrow found its target through Ruination’s lattice and his own Dreams, and he let them. His gaze was fixed somewhere else entirely.
North.
Where the blue rift split the dark, and the colossal thing lay coiled around its mouth.

It had not moved. Not once, through three volleys and thirty-eight deaths. It lay where it had always lain, the halo of stilled snow hanging over its head, its shape still too vast and too strange to resolve. Every arrow he loosed had aged the dark around it, and the dark around it had not aged at all.
It was buzzing!

He could feel it from here, a low vibration running through the frozen dark and into his quarks. Its half-present aura of Immensity was flickering fastr now, there and gone and there, as though something inside it were waking, or deciding.
Fifty-five Guards, and none of them had ever truly been his enemy. They were spoils. They were steps.
This was the only real enemy on the Basal Floor.
And even from here, with his existence packed and climbing and a bow in his hands that could empty a whole Floor of monsters, it was utterly suffocating!
