So he tested it!
He chose five hundred for VERITAS.
It settled there and stayed.
Nine hundred and ninety-nine, and it went there.
One, and it sat quietly at one.
He stopped.
The panel was his to set anywhere in that range, and others read whatever he chose.
Under it, the real thing kept climbing.
The door to Immensity was shut, but his foundation could still be refined and his Provenance still elevated, and the ceiling existence had built hung over a road he no longer walked.
He left the panel at one.
It seemed polite.
Then he closed his eyes and went looking through the memories of the dead!
Nine Guards,.
Alone, each was a narrow corridor, one route through the frozen dark walked for longer than anything should have to walk it.
He laid them over one another, route on route, island on rift on torn Dimension, and they began to fit.
|The memories of nine Guards have been combined.
THE Basal Floor has been mapped.|
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer now extends across the whole of it.
Every Empowered Hollow Night Lifeform upon this Floor dreams a little, and where it dreams, you may perceive it.|
And Ruination went further!
|Master.
The map is fixed, but they are not.|
|I have run their positions through my Root and recorded every probability of their movement.
You now have them in real time, and where they will be for some while after.|
Noah’s eyes opened, and they shone brilliantly!
He saw the whole Basal Floor at once, through his Dreams, with Ruination’s predictions laid over it like a lattice of light.
Floating islands of ice by the thousands.
Torn Dimensions hanging between them, and towering cold-filled trees.
And moving among it all, small bright points where the Guards were dreaming.
Fifty-five of them!
He reached for each one and felt its weight.
Every one was at the Naga’s level, some grander, a few a great deal grander.
Fifty-five more of what had taken everything he and Ling had to kill nine.
Then he turned his perception north, and went very still.
A rift split the frozen dark there, blue and vast.
The way down.
He could feel it pulling at the cold in his quarks!
And coiled around its mouth, like a guard dog around a dor, was something that did not fit on the map at all.
It was colossal!
The floating islands near it drifted in its shadow.
He could not make out its shape.
It had too many limbs, or none, or limbs made of the same frozen dark as the space around it, and a halo of stilled snow hung motionless over where its head should be.
Its aura was wrong!
It was Immense, and it was not.

The weight he had felt on the Plain of Accord when the thrones filled was there, and then gone, and then there again, as though this thing had climbed toward the door of Immensity, stopped exactly halfway, and stood on that threshold for longer than anything should stand anywhere.
It was not asleep!
He refocused.
He turned from the rift in the north to the fifty-five bright points scattered across the dark, and began, very calmly, to plan which one to kill first.
But...
Then he stopped planning!
"Why one at a time?" he said.
Ling looked at him.
He was not speaking to her.
"I see all of them.
Where they are now, where they will be, every path each of them will walk for some while yet.
I see them as a sky sees the ground."
His voice was very calm.
"Fifty-five points.
And I was about to choose among them as though I were one of them.
As though I had to go to each in turn and stand before it and trade blows until one of us fell."
He looked out across the frozen dark.
"That is the common sense of this place.
The Guard patrols its corridor, and the one who comes to kill it walks the corridor too.
I do not need to walk their corridors."
He raised his hand, and began to build!
Not a weapon anyone else had made.
He had none, and wanted none.
Instead he reached into what he now was, Core Capabilities moving as one body, and chose the pieces.
First, the shape.

THE Rendered Design drew it in the dark: a great curved frame rendered out of nested pull and push, its limbs sweeping outward and back, partitioned along the seams where a bow must bend and mortared at the grip with his own blood and Teloi so that it would hold under any strain.
What he designed, held.
Then the draw.
THE One Foundation settled into the limbs as weight.
Then the string.
THE Living Grammar spun it from a single Sentence, spoken quietly into the air and drawn taut: I Dream of Your End.
Whatever the string sent forward would go already carying that decree.
Then the arrow, and that was the part that made the frozen dark itself go quiet!
He reached into THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour.
Every second he existed, he was refined as though far more time had passed inside his Dreams.
He had never once turned that the other way.
Now he did.
He opened a deep Dream and let an Epoch pour into it, and then another, and another, time without end, and he did not refine anything with it.
He dreamed it decaying.
Trillions of years of wearing down, of erosion, of stone to sand and sand to dust and dust to nothing, of every bond in a thing slowly letting go of every other.
And then he dreamed that decay across trillions more years, and pressed all of it, every aeon of it, down into a single point, and drew that point out along the string into the shape of an arrow.
Last, the edge.

THE Unkneeling Chill ran through the arrowhead, the Negative Immensity in his weavings that let his authority pass through any other, and the Kneeling Frost with it, the Long Night’s own cold, turned to hunt whatever was borrowed in a thing.
He closed his hand around the grip!
|THE Rendered Design, THE One Foundation, THE Living Grammar, THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour, and THE Unkneeling Chill have been combined.|
|Its string is the Sentence I Dream of Your End.
Everything it looses carries that decree.|
|Its arrows are Epochs of decay.
Each one holds trillions of years of time’s erosion on all authority, dreamed across trillions more, compressed to a single point.
What an arrow strikes, it ages through all of them at once.|
|Its edge carries the Chill of Negative Immensity and THE Kneeling Frost.
Its arrows pass through authority, and turn the borrowed cold within their targets against them.|
|THE Tide-Crowned Protagonist binds the whole: what the bow grants death to, its spoils flow to you.|
|Substrate: Dialetheic Infinity.
Your Dream has no far wall.
Its arrows have no end.|
He looked at what he had made!
The bow was blue and gold and taller than a mountain, its limbs curving back at their tips like the horns of the crown of light above his brow.
The same tendrils that burned beneath his skin ran through its frame, pulsing in time with his existence.
It did not look forged.
It looked dreamed, because it was, and it looked alive, because it was part of him.
He set his feet on the empty air.
Bare to the waist, skin dark diamond-jade, tendrils branching over his chest and arms, hair hanging weightless around that jagged crown, the bow in his hand, he looked like a fiend out of a dream.
A dream archer, drawing on the dark itself!
And both his paths moved through him when he drew.
The Fiend was the weight in the limbs and the density of the body holding them.
The Empyros was the decree in the string and the Epochs dreamed into the arrow.
An arrow from this bow would land as a mountain, and as a sentence, and as the end of more time than anything it struck had ever lived.
He drew the string back!
The arrow formed as he drew, and kept growing.
Past the length of the bow.
Past the size of a floating island.
By the time the string reached his ear, it stretched across gigaparsecs, a spear of compressed aeons so heavy that the torn Dimensions near it began to drift toward it!
Space around him twisted.

The frozen dark bent inward toward the arrowhead in long curving lines, and the Dimensionality of the whole region strained at its seams, groaning, as the thing he held pressed on everything around it just by existing.
The snow nearest the arrow aged as it fell, going grey, then brittle, then to powder before it reached the edge of his light.
Ling had backed away several islands’ worth of distance without seeming to decide to as her thighs vibrated!
Noah looked down the arrow at all fifty-five bright points at once.
He let go!
The arrow left the string and split.

One became many in a single instant, fifty-five arrows of blue-gold time tearing away in fifty-five directions, each one gigaparsecs long, each one following a line of Ruination’s lattice to exactly where its target would be when it arrived.
An instant passed.
And...
HUUM!
The first one hit!
It struck a three-legged titan of hail in the far east, and the titan aged.
All of it, all at once.
Its ice clouded, then cracked, then crumbled, trillions of years of forced Dimensional erosion arriving in the space of a single heartbeat.
Its legs went to gravel beneath it.
The island it stood on wore down to sand and drifted apart, and three torn Dimensions nearby went grey and brittle and collapsed like old paper in a fire.
When the light faded, half the titan was gone, simply worn away to nothing, and the half that remained was flaking into gold, dreaming toward its end!
Then the rest hit!
Across the whole Basal Floor, fifty-four more flashes bloomed, each one a sphere of blue-gold light where a Guard had been struck by more time than its whole existence had ever held.
The sound came late and all at once, one vast rolling roar that shook the islands in their drift.
Most of them survived the first volley.
They were each at the Naga’s level or grander.
One arrow wore away limbs, heads, whole portions of their existences, but it was not enough.
Noah drew again!
"I...can do this infinitely," he said.
"My Dream has no far wall.
It does not tire.
It does not need to rest between one arrow and the next.
So why should I not?
Why walk up to each of them and trade blows, when I can stand here and draw?"
Another arrow formed, blazing, gigaparsecs long.
"I do not need to follow the common sense of anything else.
I can do what I see fit!"
BOOM!
The third volley landed, and the first of them died.
The titan of hail went first, its dreaming half worn away to the last grain.
Then a thing like a frozen jellyfish the size of a sea, far to the south, aged into a cloud of white dust.
Then a pair of frost wyrms coiled around a floating island, both of them eroding to bone and then to nothing in the same flash.
One after another, across the whole Floor, bright points on Ruination’s lattice went out and did not come back.
And the spoils came.
|A Guard has been granted death.
Spoils: Lesser Kryos x10.
Memories of a Guard.|
Then again, and again, faster than the prompts could keep up with, until Ruination simply began to tally.
|Guards granted death: 11.
Lesser Kryos received: 110.|
Noah fused as they came, without stopping his drawing arm.
Four Lesser Kryos pressed together at his hip into a genuine Kryos, then the next four, the fusing happening in the back of his existence while the front of it went on loosing arrows.
Every Kryos he made, he sent away, down into THE Infiniverse, into the dreams of his people, wherever someone he held dear was sleeping.
The Tide answered each gift, and he ate every Quintessential ECG the moment it arrived.
Each one spread through the whole of him, and every arrow after it came off the string a little larger and a little more certain!
|Guards granted death: 24.
Lesser Kryos received: 240.
Kryos fused and given: 60.|
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing notes that gifts given to enemies now considered weaker than you carry less weight than gifts given with thought.
Its returns have diminished accordingly.|
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins integrated this battle: 41.|
Diminished due to weakness?
Okay!
The Guards that could still fight were fighting back now.
Storms of frost came howling at him from a dozen directions.
A spear of black ice the length of a Dimension.
A wave of cold that froze the air solid for a thousand miles.

They broke against his outline, or dreamed away into haze before they arrived, or landed on him and were kept by THE One Foundation, and every ton of that pressure went straight into the limbs of the bow and came back out behind the next arrow.
Nothing they threw slowed his drawing arm.
|Guards granted death: 38.
Lesser Kryos received: 380.
Kryos fused and given: 95.|
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins integrated this battle: 64.
Total integrated: 130.|
|THE Osmontian Culmination.
Present saturation: 29%.|
Thirty-eight!
Seventeen bright points remained on the lattice, all of them worn and cracked and aged, several of them fleeing across the Floor as fast as their crumbling bodies could carry them.
Following them would be easy.
So would drawing until there were none.
He kept drawing!
But he was not looking at them.
His eyes had left the Guards some time ago.
Every arrow found its target through Ruination’s lattice and his own Dreams, and he let them.
His gaze was fixed somewhere else entirely.
North.
Where the blue rift split the dark, and the colossal thing lay coiled around its mouth.
It had not moved.
Not once, through three volleys and thirty-eight deaths.
It lay where it had always lain, the halo of stilled snow hanging over its head, its shape still too vast and too strange to resolve.
Every arrow he loosed had aged the dark around it, and the dark around it had not aged at all.
It was buzzing!
He could feel it from here, a low vibration running through the frozen dark and into his quarks.
Its half-present aura of Immensity was flickering fastr now, there and gone and there, as though something inside it were waking, or deciding.
Fifty-five Guards, and none of them had ever truly been his enemy.
They were spoils.
They were steps.
This was the only real enemy on the Basal Floor.
And even from here, with his existence packed and climbing and a bow in his hands that could empty a whole Floor of monsters, it was utterly suffocating!

chapters.title: Chapter 5814: Poisonous!
paragraphs: <Sir Moriarty>
Moriarty’s Elsedimension Mountain looked like a study that had kept growing for an Age and never once been tidied, and it could always look different.
Currently...

Shelves climbed its hollow heart in spirals, bowed under books and bones and jars of things that still twitched. Instruments of brass and glass hung from chanes overhead, some of them measuring, some of them only remembering how. Down the center of the great chamber ran a long stone table where specimens lay in careful rows, labeled in his small precise hand, and at the far end of it, under a sheet, lay the half-dissected remains of an Immense One he had been studying for a while.
The snow had reached even here. It drifted down from somewhere high in the dark and settled on the shelves, and Moriarty had given up brushing it off his books.
Poona sat cross-legged on his table, between a jar of preserved eyes and a tray of his pastries, eating the pastries!
"You could at least pretend to have come about the Council," Moriarty said, without looking up from his notes.
"I did come about the Council."She licked sugar off a finger."I just also came about the pastries."

He adjusted his spectacles. There was a great deal to think about before the Legacy gathered. The Convocation had ended in a severing and a voice. The Counting pressed on every Root under Lucy’s roof. And three of the thrones had stopped speaking to him in the corridors.
At this time...
The air in the chamber changed!
It grew warm, and green, and smelled suddenly of spring. Moriarty lifted his head. Poona stopped chewing.
THE Verdant Regard stepped into the study!

No door opened for her. She simply arrived, a tall figure of soft green light with a gaze like new leaves, and the snow nearest her turned to petals and fell. Her head inclined to Moriarty with perfect courtesy, and to Poona with slightly less.
Then she raised her Immensity!

It rose out of her in a slow green tide and poured up the hollow of the mountain, and closed over the whole of it like a dome. Moriarty felt it seal. Every thread of perception that ran in or out of his Elsedimension was quietly shut. Nobody outside could see in now, or hear, or sense so much as a breath. He had never once, in all the ages he had known her, seen her ask for that kind of privacy!
Poona set down her pastry!
"Is this Osmont truly one of the three?"THE Verdant Regard said.
Her voice was gentle, and tired, and very reasonable.
"Will we risk our Immensity and rally around him? Because I have watched him, and it does not seem he will do anything different from any of the others. He does not show any brilliance."
Moriarty frowned!
He took off his spectacles and set them on the table beside his notes. Poona went very still.
"What exactly is your point?" he said. "We are to gather as a Legacy in a little while to decide a direction on all of this. So why say it now, here, under a dome where no one else can hear?"
THE Verdant Regard did not answer at once.
She walked slowly along the length of his table, past the specimens and the jars, trailing one green finger along the stone. Where she touched, small shoots came up through the snow.

"I have begun to think differently," she said. "About a great many things. About the three, and the door, and who should and could be the one to open it. About this Legacy, and what Lucy built it for, and whether what she built it for still matters when the snow is this deep."
She stopped at the end of the table, by the sheeted corpse.
"I think our weavings may no longer be aligned, Moriarty."
"That is a strange thing to come and tell me."
"It is."She turned to face him, and her gaze was sad and green and very old."I did it only as an assurance, you understand. I never wanted to use it. I hoped I never would."
She tilted her head.
"But do you remember all that tea we drank together, over the years?"
Moriarty remembered!

He remembered it all at once, as a scholar remembers the one line in a text he read a thousand times without seeing. Ages of afternons. Her domain, spring and warm, and a cup in his hand that always tasted faintly of green. He had liked it. He had asked her once what was in it, and she had smiled and told him it was only leaves.
She waved her hand!
Green light came out of him!

It leaked from his skin, from the corners of his eyes, from under the seams of his tentacles, a poisonous glowing green that had been growing inside him quietly for longer than he could count. Rather than burning, it bloomed, spreading through his existence along every path the tea had ever taken, and wherever it bloomed, his Immensity went soft and slow and far away.
Moriarty stumbled!

He caught himself against his own table, knocking a jar of eyes to the floor, and the glass shattered, and he stared at his tentacles where green light was pouring out.For once in his long existence, he had nothing at all to say.
Poona’s face changed!

The cheer went out of it entirely. There was no shout and no laugh. Poona slid off the table, and as her feet touched the floor, her shape let go of itself. Her body went soft, translucent, and swelled outward into a vast gleaming mass of living slime, shimmering with every color at once, filling half the study and rising toward the dome of green light, and inside it, turning slowly, her one enormous bright eye fixed on THE Verdant Regard without a trace of warmth.
Then the whole mountain buzzed!

It shook from its roots to its peak, every shelf rattling, every instrument swinging on its chain. The green dome overhead flickered, not breaking, but opening, deliberately, in one place, to let something in.
The air above the long stone table split open like an eyelid!

A vast dark eye looked out of it. Sleepless. Patient. Burning with an attention that had never once blinked. It looked at Moriarty, stumbling and bleeding green light against his own table, and at Poona, vast and gleaming and silent. Last of all, it looked at THE Verdant Regard, standing at the end of the table beside the corpse, and something in it seemed almost fond.
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND regards you.|
|"It is a time for revolution, old friend Moriarty."|

Outside the dome, far below on the snow-covered floor of the Legacy, the purple-gold rivers had begun to run faster. Conduits hummed in a pitch no Keeper had ever heard. On a dozen mountains at once, figures that did not belong to THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity were stepping out of the blizzard, and the snow around them was falling crimson gold.
The incursion had begun!
<THE Creature>
Anaximander sat on nothing.

There was no floor in the undefinition where their home had once been, only the slow obsidian foam and the snow drifting through it, but Anaximander had found a place to sit anyway. He had a book open on his knee. Where the book had come from, THE Creature did not know.
THE Creature watched him.

He had been watching him for some time. Since Anaximander had agreed to take his weavings from the future, since those weavings had come pouring back into the scholar all at once, the friend beside him had changed. His eyes were older. His hands turned the pages more slowly. And there was something in him now that THE Creature could sense clearly, sitting at the very center of his existence.
A Root!

That was what it looked like, to THE Creature’s senses. The shape of it was plain. A Root of Immensity, whole and bright, rooted in the middle of the man as surely as the fractured one was rooted in THE Creature’s own chest.

And yet Anaximander carried no authority at all, not a single thread of it, the same as always. There was no power coming off him, no weight, no pressure. A Root should hum. It should press outward on the existence around it. This one did nothing.
THE Creature looked closer, and understood.

It was no Root that Anaximander had grown. It was a hollow, exactly the shape of a Root, and existence itself had leaned in and filled it. The foam around the scholar curved toward that hollow. The snow drifting past him bent its fall very slightly inward. Existence had looked at the man, and at the space in him where a Root would go, and simply agreed that one was there.
"You’re staring." Anaximander said, without looking up from his book.
"I am," THE Creature said.
"Between the two of us, I am certainly not the bigger monster though?"
THE Creature said nothing. He went on looking at the hollow full of agreement in his friend’s chest, and felt, faintly, something he did not often feel.
Marvel!
Then, in the next moment, he frowned as existence distorted!

Rather than tearing, it bent all at once, the obsidian foam around them warping inward toward a single point in the undefinition, as though something very heavy had just set its foot down on a sheet of cloth. The snow stopped falling. It hung in the air, every flake of it, and trembled.
Anaximander closed his book.
A figure stepped out of the bend!

He was tall and pale, his long hair pale gold shading into white, his eyes gold and bright and very calm. He wore a long dark coat that did not move in any wind. And he was shining, faintly, from the inside, pale gold light seeping out through his skin as though he had eaten something enormous not long ago and was still digesting it.
THE Creature knew him as those eyes were unforgettable!
Everyone from their home knew him. He was the reason there was no home. He had taken their Observable Existence and left nothing behind but this foam.
"Hello again," said THE Sealed One.
His voice was warm, and courteous, and interested, the voice of a scholar greeting another scholar at a lecture.
"It has been quite some time. And yet, not."He tilted his head, taking in the foam, the hanging snow, the two of them."I am sorry to say that I come this time bearing death."
THE Creature and Anaximander moved closer together!

Neither of them decided to. They simply did. Anaximander rose off his seat of nothing and drifted to THE Creature’s side, and THE Creature’s white and obsidian flames rose around both of them, and their faces were grave.
THE Sealed One walked forward, unhurried, and the pressure of him arrived!

It came down on the undefinition like a sky falling. It was not Immensity. THE Creature could feel that it was not; there was no door behind it, no completion, no finished shape. But it was close. It was so close that the difference barely mattered, a weight that pressed on the foam and the snow and on THE Creature’s fractured Root until the crack across his chest began, very faintly, to glow.
"People fear death," THE Sealed One said, "because they think it means being erased. They think the lantern goes out and the room stays cold and empty forever. But that is not what dying is."
He stopped a little way off, and his gold eyes rested on THE Creature.
"Death is just an open hand tipping over a bowl, so something better can drink."
The snow trembled in the air between them.

"Sometimes, death is actually a kindness. When an old tree rots in the brush, it does not curse the dirt. It feeds the ground, so a taller trunk can climb toward the sun. Nothing ever truly vanishes in existence. The weight stays. The heat and the stubborn marrow you carried simply get poured into someone else’s blood."His voice softened.
"In a strange way, you do not really stop walking. You just live on through me."
THE Creature did not answer.
"And look," THE Sealed One went on, almost apologetic. "I do not want to be unfair. You can see the shapes standing behind my shoulder. I am not alone. I have never been alone."
Behind him, the undefinition shifted!

Shapes rose out of the foam at his back, vast and hazy, their Dimensionality flowing so deep that THE Creature could not see them clearly at all. Only the auras came through, pressing out from behind THE Sealed One like five suns rising behind a single hill. Five of them. Each one heavy with the unmistakable, finished weight of true Immensity!
Five Immense Ones, standing in the foam where a home had been.

"But I never liked ganging up on a man,"THE Sealed One said. "It leaves a bitter taste in my mouth, like chewing on burnt gristle. So those behind me will not move. They will not lift a finger. They will not take a single step toward you."
He smiled.
"They are just here to watch the wood get split. It is only you and me."
Five Immense Ones watching. A being very nearly Immense himself walking forward. And THE Creature with a fractured Root and a friend who carried no authority at all.
It was catastrophic!
THE Sealed One’s gold eyes drifted down to THE Creature’s chest, to the crack glowing faintly there, and to what lay inside it.
"You really should be more careful," he said, "and not hang about outside existence with a Root that bright."
His eyes lit with open, delighted curiosity. "A Root of Existence? Man. That is an anomaly worth exploring."
THE Creature looked at him.

He looked at the pale shining figure, and at the five suns rising behind it, and at the foam that had once been everything he came from. He felt the weight of all of it pressing down on him, on his fractured Root, on his friend at his side.
And he began to buzz!

It started low, deep in his vast body, a vibration running up out of the undefinition and into him. His white and obsidian flames rose higher. The colorless Provenance around him began to simmer and churn. The crack across his chest blazed, the fractured Root inside it flickering and flaring, and THE Creature stood up straighter under the weight of five Immense Ones and a devourer, and did not bend!
"Existence," THE Creature said, "is fearless."
The foam around him shook.
"Existence perseveres."
His flames roared up into the dark, and the hanging snow scattered.
"I simply have to... persevere."
THE Sealed One watched THE Creature blaze, and his smile softened into something that looked almost like respect.
"You are a grand being," he said. "I mean that. There are very few things in existence that would stand straighter under this."

He glanced back at the five suns rising behind him, then returned his gold eyes to THE Creature. "But I am afraid it is the end of the line this time. Even Osmont will be, or should already be, very preoccupied right now."
THE Creature’s flames did not waver. But something behind his eyes went very still at that name!
"In existence, there are some who believe themselves invincible no matter what," THE Sealed One went on. "Let us put that to the test for you today."
He rolled his shoulders, loosely, like a man about to lift something heavy. "Will you somehow survive standing before me?"
He took one step forward!
"You never know," said a voice. "Crazy myths and legends get written all the time."
It was a lazy voice. Unhurried, faintly amused, as if its owner had been leaning against a wall somewhere listening to all of this for a while and had finally gotten bored enough to join in.
THE Sealed One stopped. And his smile, instead of fading, widened!
He turned.

Something was descending through the undefinition above them. Ink came first, rivers of it, black and glittering, pouring down out of the dark and curling through the obsidian foam without spilling a drop. Then pages, thousnds of them, drifting down around the ink like white leaves. And in the middle of it all, sitting on the air with one leg crossed over the other, came a woman!

She was tall and slender, with long dark hair pinned up carelessly by a single pen driven through the knot. Her robes were the pale white of good paper and hung loose around her, and every inch of her exposed skin, her hands, her wrists, her throat, the side of her face, was covered in writing.

Fine, dense lines of script in her own neat hand, running and shifting slowly across her body as though they were still being written. Her eyes were dark, and when they moved, faint lines of text moved in them too.

Behind her, so faint it could barely be seen, something vast and patient stood among shelves that climbed out of sight. Only its brilliance showed. An immense, quiet glow of ink and parchment, watching over her shoulder, as a library watches over whoever sits reading in it.
THE MATRIARCH OF INK.
THE Writer of Mythos had arrived, and her name, THE Creature felt, written on the air behind her in letters of ink, was Calliope!
She came to a stop above THE Creature and Anaximander, a little to one side, and looked THE Sealed One up and down with open, unimpressed interest.
"I’m taking a little detour," Calliope said."It might be disastrous."
She shrugged. "But I just can’t watch a myth come to an end, you know? It would be such a shame."
Her dark eyes narrowed, and the script on her skin quickened. "And you seem to be a black hole where myths go to die."
THE Sealed One laughed!
It was a bright, genuine, delighted laugh, and it rang out through the whole undefinition, and the five Immense suns behind him did not so much as flicker.

"Quite the opposite, actually," he said, still smiling. "I will make all your myths live on across history. Your capabilities will be remembered. Every one of them, kept safe inside me for as long as I exist."
He spread his pale hands, almost welcoming. "Now. Let us see who lives, and who dies."
HUUM!
Crimson brilliance erupted from him!

It tore out of his chest and his eyes and his outstretched hands, a light that was Infinity and was also somthing older, bound together and fused, pouring out of a source so far down inside him and so vast that THE Creature could not see the bottom of it.
It roared outward in every direction, through the foam and the snow and the pages drifting around Calliope, and wherever it touched, the color went out of everything else.

The obsidian foam turned red, and the falling snow with it. Rivers of ink, the white of Calliope’s robes, the white and obsidian of THE Creature’s own flames, all of it, painted crimson in an instant.
All of existence, as far as THE Creature could see, was red!

sentences.text: <Sir Moriarty>
Moriarty’s Elsedimension Mountain looked like a study that had kept growing for an Age and never once been tidied, and it could always look different.
Currently...
Shelves climbed its hollow heart in spirals, bowed under books and bones and jars of things that still twitched.
Instruments of brass and glass hung from chanes overhead, some of them measuring, some of them only remembering how.

Down the center of the great chamber ran a long stone table where specimens lay in careful rows, labeled in his small precise hand, and at the far end of it, under a sheet, lay the half-dissected remains of an Immense One he had been studying for a while.
The snow had reached even here.
It drifted down from somewhere high in the dark and settled on the shelves, and Moriarty had given up brushing it off his books.
Poona sat cross-legged on his table, between a jar of preserved eyes and a tray of his pastries, eating the pastries!
"You could at least pretend to have come about the Council," Moriarty said, without looking up from his notes.
"I did come about the Council."She licked sugar off a finger."I just also came about the pastries."
He adjusted his spectacles.
There was a great deal to think about before the Legacy gathered.
The Convocation had ended in a severing and a voice.
The Counting pressed on every Root under Lucy’s roof.
And three of the thrones had stopped speaking to him in the corridors.
At this time...
The air in the chamber changed!
It grew warm, and green, and smelled suddenly of spring.
Moriarty lifted his head.
Poona stopped chewing.
THE Verdant Regard stepped into the study!
No door opened for her.
She simply arrived, a tall figure of soft green light with a gaze like new leaves, and the snow nearest her turned to petals and fell.
Her head inclined to Moriarty with perfect courtesy, and to Poona with slightly less.
Then she raised her Immensity!
It rose out of her in a slow green tide and poured up the hollow of the mountain, and closed over the whole of it like a dome.
Moriarty felt it seal.
Every thread of perception that ran in or out of his Elsedimension was quietly shut.
Nobody outside could see in now, or hear, or sense so much as a breath.
He had never once, in all the ages he had known her, seen her ask for that kind of privacy!
Poona set down her pastry!
"Is this Osmont truly one of the three?"THE Verdant Regard said.
Her voice was gentle, and tired, and very reasonable.
"Will we risk our Immensity and rally around him?
Because I have watched him, and it does not seem he will do anything different from any of the others.
He does not show any brilliance."
Moriarty frowned!
He took off his spectacles and set them on the table beside his notes.
Poona went very still.
"What exactly is your point?" he said.
"We are to gather as a Legacy in a little while to decide a direction on all of this.
So why say it now, here, under a dome where no one else can hear?"
THE Verdant Regard did not answer at once.
She walked slowly along the length of his table, past the specimens and the jars, trailing one green finger along the stone.
Where she touched, small shoots came up through the snow.
"I have begun to think differently," she said.
"About a great many things.
About the three, and the door, and who should and could be the one to open it.
About this Legacy, and what Lucy built it for, and whether what she built it for still matters when the snow is this deep."
She stopped at the end of the table, by the sheeted corpse.
"I think our weavings may no longer be aligned, Moriarty."
"That is a strange thing to come and tell me."
"It is."She turned to face him, and her gaze was sad and green and very old."I did it only as an assurance, you understand.
I never wanted to use it.
I hoped I never would."
She tilted her head.
"But do you remember all that tea we drank together, over the years?"
Moriarty remembered!
He remembered it all at once, as a scholar remembers the one line in a text he read a thousand times without seeing.
Ages of afternons.
Her domain, spring and warm, and a cup in his hand that always tasted faintly of green.
He had liked it.
He had asked her once what was in it, and she had smiled and told him it was only leaves.
She waved her hand!
Green light came out of him!
It leaked from his skin, from the corners of his eyes, from under the seams of his tentacles, a poisonous glowing green that had been growing inside him quietly for longer than he could count.
Rather than burning, it bloomed, spreading through his existence along every path the tea had ever taken, and wherever it bloomed, his Immensity went soft and slow and far away.
Moriarty stumbled!

He caught himself against his own table, knocking a jar of eyes to the floor, and the glass shattered, and he stared at his tentacles where green light was pouring out.For once in his long existence, he had nothing at all to say.
Poona’s face changed!
The cheer went out of it entirely.
There was no shout and no laugh.
Poona slid off the table, and as her feet touched the floor, her shape let go of itself.

Her body went soft, translucent, and swelled outward into a vast gleaming mass of living slime, shimmering with every color at once, filling half the study and rising toward the dome of green light, and inside it, turning slowly, her one enormous bright eye fixed on THE Verdant Regard without a trace of warmth.
Then the whole mountain buzzed!
It shook from its roots to its peak, every shelf rattling, every instrument swinging on its chain.
The green dome overhead flickered, not breaking, but opening, deliberately, in one place, to let something in.
The air above the long stone table split open like an eyelid!
A vast dark eye looked out of it.
Sleepless.
Patient.
Burning with an attention that had never once blinked.
It looked at Moriarty, stumbling and bleeding green light against his own table, and at Poona, vast and gleaming and silent.
Last of all, it looked at THE Verdant Regard, standing at the end of the table beside the corpse, and something in it seemed almost fond.
|THE SLEEPLESS FIEND regards you.|
|"It is a time for revolution, old friend Moriarty."|
Outside the dome, far below on the snow-covered floor of the Legacy, the purple-gold rivers had begun to run faster.
Conduits hummed in a pitch no Keeper had ever heard.
On a dozen mountains at once, figures that did not belong to THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity were stepping out of the blizzard, and the snow around them was falling crimson gold.
The incursion had begun!
<THE Creature>
Anaximander sat on nothing.
There was no floor in the undefinition where their home had once been, only the slow obsidian foam and the snow drifting through it, but Anaximander had found a place to sit anyway.
He had a book open on his knee.
Where the book had come from, THE Creature did not know.
THE Creature watched him.
He had been watching him for some time.
Since Anaximander had agreed to take his weavings from the future, since those weavings had come pouring back into the scholar all at once, the friend beside him had changed.
His eyes were older.
His hands turned the pages more slowly.
And there was something in him now that THE Creature could sense clearly, sitting at the very center of his existence.
A Root!
That was what it looked like, to THE Creature’s senses.
The shape of it was plain.
A Root of Immensity, whole and bright, rooted in the middle of the man as surely as the fractured one was rooted in THE Creature’s own chest.
And yet Anaximander carried no authority at all, not a single thread of it, the same as always.
There was no power coming off him, no weight, no pressure.
A Root should hum.
It should press outward on the existence around it.
This one did nothing.
THE Creature looked closer, and understood.
It was no Root that Anaximander had grown.
It was a hollow, exactly the shape of a Root, and existence itself had leaned in and filled it.
The foam around the scholar curved toward that hollow.
The snow drifting past him bent its fall very slightly inward.
Existence had looked at the man, and at the space in him where a Root would go, and simply agreed that one was there.
"You’re staring." Anaximander said, without looking up from his book.
"I am," THE Creature said.
"Between the two of us, I am certainly not the bigger monster though?"
THE Creature said nothing.
He went on looking at the hollow full of agreement in his friend’s chest, and felt, faintly, something he did not often feel.
Marvel!
Then, in the next moment, he frowned as existence distorted!

Rather than tearing, it bent all at once, the obsidian foam around them warping inward toward a single point in the undefinition, as though something very heavy had just set its foot down on a sheet of cloth.
The snow stopped falling.
It hung in the air, every flake of it, and trembled.
Anaximander closed his book.
A figure stepped out of the bend!
He was tall and pale, his long hair pale gold shading into white, his eyes gold and bright and very calm.
He wore a long dark coat that did not move in any wind.
And he was shining, faintly, from the inside, pale gold light seeping out through his skin as though he had eaten something enormous not long ago and was still digesting it.
THE Creature knew him as those eyes were unforgettable!
Everyone from their home knew him.
He was the reason there was no home.
He had taken their Observable Existence and left nothing behind but this foam.
"Hello again," said THE Sealed One.
His voice was warm, and courteous, and interested, the voice of a scholar greeting another scholar at a lecture.
"It has been quite some time.
And yet, not."He tilted his head, taking in the foam, the hanging snow, the two of them."I am sorry to say that I come this time bearing death."
THE Creature and Anaximander moved closer together!
Neither of them decided to.
They simply did.
Anaximander rose off his seat of nothing and drifted to THE Creature’s side, and THE Creature’s white and obsidian flames rose around both of them, and their faces were grave.
THE Sealed One walked forward, unhurried, and the pressure of him arrived!
It came down on the undefinition like a sky falling.
It was not Immensity.
THE Creature could feel that it was not; there was no door behind it, no completion, no finished shape.
But it was close.
It was so close that the difference barely mattered, a weight that pressed on the foam and the snow and on THE Creature’s fractured Root until the crack across his chest began, very faintly, to glow.
"People fear death," THE Sealed One said, "because they think it means being erased.
They think the lantern goes out and the room stays cold and empty forever.
But that is not what dying is."
He stopped a little way off, and his gold eyes rested on THE Creature.
"Death is just an open hand tipping over a bowl, so something better can drink."
The snow trembled in the air between them.
"Sometimes, death is actually a kindness.
When an old tree rots in the brush, it does not curse the dirt.
It feeds the ground, so a taller trunk can climb toward the sun.
Nothing ever truly vanishes in existence.
The weight stays.
The heat and the stubborn marrow you carried simply get poured into someone else’s blood."His voice softened.
"In a strange way, you do not really stop walking.
You just live on through me."
THE Creature did not answer.
"And look," THE Sealed One went on, almost apologetic.
"I do not want to be unfair.
You can see the shapes standing behind my shoulder.
I am not alone.
I have never been alone."
Behind him, the undefinition shifted!
Shapes rose out of the foam at his back, vast and hazy, their Dimensionality flowing so deep that THE Creature could not see them clearly at all.
Only the auras came through, pressing out from behind THE Sealed One like five suns rising behind a single hill.
Five of them.
Each one heavy with the unmistakable, finished weight of true Immensity!
Five Immense Ones, standing in the foam where a home had been.
"But I never liked ganging up on a man,"THE Sealed One said.
"It leaves a bitter taste in my mouth, like chewing on burnt gristle.
So those behind me will not move.
They will not lift a finger.
They will not take a single step toward you."
He smiled.
"They are just here to watch the wood get split.
It is only you and me."
Five Immense Ones watching.
A being very nearly Immense himself walking forward.
And THE Creature with a fractured Root and a friend who carried no authority at all.
It was catastrophic!
THE Sealed One’s gold eyes drifted down to THE Creature’s chest, to the crack glowing faintly there, and to what lay inside it.
"You really should be more careful," he said, "and not hang about outside existence with a Root that bright."
His eyes lit with open, delighted curiosity.
"A Root of Existence?
Man.
That is an anomaly worth exploring."
THE Creature looked at him.
He looked at the pale shining figure, and at the five suns rising behind it, and at the foam that had once been everything he came from.
He felt the weight of all of it pressing down on him, on his fractured Root, on his friend at his side.
And he began to buzz!
It started low, deep in his vast body, a vibration running up out of the undefinition and into him.
His white and obsidian flames rose higher.
The colorless Provenance around him began to simmer and churn.
The crack across his chest blazed, the fractured Root inside it flickering and flaring, and THE Creature stood up straighter under the weight of five Immense Ones and a devourer, and did not bend!
"Existence," THE Creature said, "is fearless."
The foam around him shook.
"Existence perseveres."
His flames roared up into the dark, and the hanging snow scattered.
"I simply have to... persevere."
THE Sealed One watched THE Creature blaze, and his smile softened into something that looked almost like respect.
"You are a grand being," he said.
"I mean that.
There are very few things in existence that would stand straighter under this."
He glanced back at the five suns rising behind him, then returned his gold eyes to THE Creature.
"But I am afraid it is the end of the line this time.
Even Osmont will be, or should already be, very preoccupied right now."
THE Creature’s flames did not waver.
But something behind his eyes went very still at that name!
"In existence, there are some who believe themselves invincible no matter what," THE Sealed One went on.
"Let us put that to the test for you today."
He rolled his shoulders, loosely, like a man about to lift something heavy.
"Will you somehow survive standing before me?"
He took one step forward!
"You never know," said a voice.
"Crazy myths and legends get written all the time."
It was a lazy voice.
Unhurried, faintly amused, as if its owner had been leaning against a wall somewhere listening to all of this for a while and had finally gotten bored enough to join in.
THE Sealed One stopped.
And his smile, instead of fading, widened!
He turned.
Something was descending through the undefinition above them.
Ink came first, rivers of it, black and glittering, pouring down out of the dark and curling through the obsidian foam without spilling a drop.
Then pages, thousnds of them, drifting down around the ink like white leaves.
And in the middle of it all, sitting on the air with one leg crossed over the other, came a woman!
She was tall and slender, with long dark hair pinned up carelessly by a single pen driven through the knot.
Her robes were the pale white of good paper and hung loose around her, and every inch of her exposed skin, her hands, her wrists, her throat, the side of her face, was covered in writing.
Fine, dense lines of script in her own neat hand, running and shifting slowly across her body as though they were still being written.
Her eyes were dark, and when they moved, faint lines of text moved in them too.
Behind her, so faint it could barely be seen, something vast and patient stood among shelves that climbed out of sight.
Only its brilliance showed.
An immense, quiet glow of ink and parchment, watching over her shoulder, as a library watches over whoever sits reading in it.
THE MATRIARCH OF INK.
THE Writer of Mythos had arrived, and her name, THE Creature felt, written on the air behind her in letters of ink, was Calliope!
She came to a stop above THE Creature and Anaximander, a little to one side, and looked THE Sealed One up and down with open, unimpressed interest.
"I’m taking a little detour," Calliope said."It might be disastrous."
She shrugged.
"But I just can’t watch a myth come to an end, you know?
It would be such a shame."
Her dark eyes narrowed, and the script on her skin quickened.
"And you seem to be a black hole where myths go to die."
THE Sealed One laughed!
It was a bright, genuine, delighted laugh, and it rang out through the whole undefinition, and the five Immense suns behind him did not so much as flicker.
"Quite the opposite, actually," he said, still smiling.
"I will make all your myths live on across history.
Your capabilities will be remembered.
Every one of them, kept safe inside me for as long as I exist."
He spread his pale hands, almost welcoming.
"Now.
Let us see who lives, and who dies."
HUUM!
Crimson brilliance erupted from him!

It tore out of his chest and his eyes and his outstretched hands, a light that was Infinity and was also somthing older, bound together and fused, pouring out of a source so far down inside him and so vast that THE Creature could not see the bottom of it.
It roared outward in every direction, through the foam and the snow and the pages drifting around Calliope, and wherever it touched, the color went out of everything else.
The obsidian foam turned red, and the falling snow with it.
Rivers of ink, the white of Calliope’s robes, the white and obsidian of THE Creature’s own flames, all of it, painted crimson in an instant.
All of existence, as far as THE Creature could see, was red!

chapters.title: Chapter 5815: A Big, Fat, Panda! I
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
The last seventeen Guards did not get far at all.

Noah ran them down across the Basal Floor one volley at a time, and one by one the bright points on Ruination’s lattice went out, until the lattice held nothing at all but the thing in the north. Their Lesser Kryos came to him in handfuls. He fused them as they came, four into one, and sent every Kryos away to his people until none were left to send.
Then he ate what the Tide gave back!
|All fifty-five Guards of THE Basal Floor have been granted death.|
|Lesser Kryos received: 550. Kryos Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins fused and given: 137. The two Lesser Kryos remaining have been given as well.|
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has answered, though gifts weigh less due to power discrepancy.|
|Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins received and integrated since the first volley: 90. Total integrated: 156.|
|THE Osmontian Culmination. Present saturation: 34%.|
|Estimated Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins still required: 314.|
Thirty-four percent!

He looked at his panel. It showed one in every line. The real numbers underneath flickered as they always did now, sliding between one and nine hundred and ninety-nine, telling him nothing he could hold.
But he did not need the numbers to know.

He felt it! His existence, which was his Root, which was all of him now, sat denser than it had ever sat. Packed tighter. Every Quintessential ECG had gone in and pressed the rest down, and the whole of him had settled into something so compact and so reinforced that he felt heavier standing still than he had once felt at full strength.
His diamond-jade skin had darkened a shade. The blue-gold tendrils beneath it had thickened into rivers. The crown of light above his brow burned steadier, its horns longer.
He wanted to know what that meant in practice. So he took a step.
One step, on the empty air, toward nothing in particular!
Dreams poured out of him!

Clouds of blue-gold rolled away from his foot in every direction, and behind the clouds came seas, soft shining tides of dream washing out across the frozen dark for a thousand miles. They broke over the nearest floating islands and the islands began to dream. The ice on them went hazy and slow.

The cold-filled trees on their slopes swayed as though a wind were moving through them, though there was no wind. A drifting corpse of one of the Guards, torn and aged by his arrows, rolled gently in the tide and settled, and its dead face softened into the expression of something sleeping.
Everything the dream touched, dreamed. He had not told it to. He had only moved!
So he tested the rest.

First the dreaming corpse: he chose to let its dream run forward, and it aged. Its torn edges softened, then crumbled, the whole ruined body sliding through a billion years of decay in the time it took him to breathe out, until it drifted away as dust. He turned to one of the dreaming trees and chose to run its dream backward.
The rime came off its branches. Its trunk narrowed, straightened, grew young, shrank, until a single frozen seedling hung in the air where a tree taller than a mountain had stood.
He let the seedling go, and looked at his hands.

Nothing needed to be spoken, or built, or aimed. His Provenance and his existence were one, and whatever that existence moved through fell into dream. And whatever fell into dream, he could run forward or backward, age or unmake or restore, as easily as turning a page.
It was very simple.
It was also terrifying!
Noah stretched. He rolled his shoulders, loosened his neck, flexed his hands, and felt the whole packed weight of himself move with him, and the dream-seas around him rippled with each small motion.
Then he turned to Ling.
"I am going after the one in the north,"he said. "It should be Half-Immense."
Ling said nothing!

She hung in the air beside him with her arms crossed over her chest, looking at him, and then past him, north, toward the rift and the thing coiled around it. Her face gave nothing away. For a long moment she was completely silent.

Then she stretched. Arms high over her head, back arched, one thick powerful leg pulled up and held and released, then the other, the great muscles of her thighs flexing and loosening under the blue silk, and her whole body settled into that coiled, humming readiness he had seen before the Naga.
"As long as I don’t die right away," she said. "Let’s go, Big Boy."
Noah took a deep breath.
A light of dreams rose around the two of them, blue and gold, closing over them like a curtain drawn around a bed.
And in the next instant, they were somewhere else!
The north of the Basal Floor was grand.

Everywhere else, the frozen islands floated free in the dark, turning slowly on their own. Here, they had stopped. Thousands of them lay jammed together in a vast ring, pressed edge against edge, ground and heaved and stacked into a single frozen plain that curved away around a hollow at its center.

The torn Dimensions that hung everywhere else had been pulled down here too, crushed into the ice of the plain and frozen in place, their broken seas and realms showing through the surface like things drowned under a lake. Pillars of rime rose from the plain in crooked rows. Some of them had shapes inside them. Figures. Beasts. Things that had come this way before and stopped.
At the center of the ring, the blue rift split the dark from top to bottom.
And coiled around the rift’s mouth, the thing in the north.
This close, its shape finally resolved!
It was a...panda!

A panda the size of a mountain range, and nothing about that was funny. It sat hunched at the mouth of the rift with its great round back to the dark, its fur black and white and gone hard with ages of frost, every hair of it a spine of ice. Where the white fur should have been, the ice was clear, and through it Noah could see the bones of the thing, massive and ancient and glazed in rime. Where the black fur should have been, the ice was dark as a starless sky and seemed to go down forever.

Wings rose from its shoulders. Vast, jagged, made of frost, like panes of frozen glass shattered and set back together by a hand that did not care how the pieces fit. They hung in tatters behind it, and wind that was not wind moved through them with a sound like a very old choir.

Chains of broken rime hung from its neck and its thick forearms, snapped links trailing down onto the plain, as though it had been bound here once and had simply grown too large for the binding. A mantle of frozen banners draped over its shoulders beneath the wings, stiff and cracked, each banner bearing a sigil too eroded to read. And in one enormous paw, resting across its knees, it held a great club carved from the spire of a Dimension, the stone of it still carved with the windows of the city that had once stood on it.
Over its head hung the halo of stilled snow.

Its face was the face of a panda, round, with the dark rings around its eyes. But the eyes within those rings were pale, and old, and cold beyond anything Noah had met on this Floor. Its jaw moved slowly. It was chewing on somethng. A long frozen stalk of something white that Noah realized, after a moment, was a bone.
His sight opened it, and gave him almost nothing.
|Empowered Hollow Night Lifeform.|
|VERITAS: ???. PROVENANCE: ???. POTENTIA: ???. PONDUS: ???.|
|Immensity: halfway.|
Halfway!

The aura came off it and went back into it, there and gone and there, the finished weight of Immensity pressing down on the whole frozen plain and then lifting and then pressing again. Every time it pressed, the rime pillars groaned. Every time it lifted, the air felt strangely empty.
The panda looked at him!

No rising, no spreading of wings, no lifting of the club. The panda simply turned its great round head, slowly, still chewing on its bone, and fixed its pale ringed eyes on the small figure hanging in the air at the edge of its plain.

There was no anger in that look. There was nothing in it but a deep and total boredom, the look of something vast glancing down at a bug on the arm of its chair and deciding, without much interest, whether it was worth the effort of lifting a hand.
Noah looked back at it.

He hung in the frozen air above its plain, bare-chested, dark diamond-jade, tendrils of blue-gold burning beneath his skin and a jagged crown of light above his brow. The dream-seas he had raised were still rolling off him in slow shining tides, lapping at the edge of the frozen ring. His eyes were very calm.
He did not look away.
Neither did it!
