Arms high over her head, back arched, one thick powerful leg pulled up and held and released, then the other, the great muscles of her thighs flexing and loosening under the blue silk, and her whole body settled into that coiled, humming readiness he had seen before the Naga.
"As long as I don’t die right away," she said.
"Let’s go, Big Boy."
Noah took a deep breath.
A light of dreams rose around the two of them, blue and gold, closing over them like a curtain drawn around a bed.
And in the next instant, they were somewhere else!
The north of the Basal Floor was grand.
Everywhere else, the frozen islands floated free in the dark, turning slowly on their own.
Here, they had stopped.
Thousands of them lay jammed together in a vast ring, pressed edge against edge, ground and heaved and stacked into a single frozen plain that curved away around a hollow at its center.

The torn Dimensions that hung everywhere else had been pulled down here too, crushed into the ice of the plain and frozen in place, their broken seas and realms showing through the surface like things drowned under a lake.
Pillars of rime rose from the plain in crooked rows.
Some of them had shapes inside them.
Figures.
Beasts.
Things that had come this way before and stopped.
At the center of the ring, the blue rift split the dark from top to bottom.
And coiled around the rift’s mouth, the thing in the north.
This close, its shape finally resolved!
It was a...panda!
A panda the size of a mountain range, and nothing about that was funny.
It sat hunched at the mouth of the rift with its great round back to the dark, its fur black and white and gone hard with ages of frost, every hair of it a spine of ice.
Where the white fur should have been, the ice was clear, and through it Noah could see the bones of the thing, massive and ancient and glazed in rime.
Where the black fur should have been, the ice was dark as a starless sky and seemed to go down forever.
Wings rose from its shoulders.
Vast, jagged, made of frost, like panes of frozen glass shattered and set back together by a hand that did not care how the pieces fit.
They hung in tatters behind it, and wind that was not wind moved through them with a sound like a very old choir.
Chains of broken rime hung from its neck and its thick forearms, snapped links trailing down onto the plain, as though it had been bound here once and had simply grown too large for the binding.
A mantle of frozen banners draped over its shoulders beneath the wings, stiff and cracked, each banner bearing a sigil too eroded to read.
And in one enormous paw, resting across its knees, it held a great club carved from the spire of a Dimension, the stone of it still carved with the windows of the city that had once stood on it.
Over its head hung the halo of stilled snow.
Its face was the face of a panda, round, with the dark rings around its eyes.
But the eyes within those rings were pale, and old, and cold beyond anything Noah had met on this Floor.
Its jaw moved slowly.
It was chewing on somethng.
A long frozen stalk of something white that Noah realized, after a moment, was a bone.
His sight opened it, and gave him almost nothing.
|Empowered Hollow Night Lifeform.|
|VERITAS: ???.
PROVENANCE: ???.
POTENTIA: ???.
PONDUS: ???.|
|Immensity: halfway.|
Halfway!
The aura came off it and went back into it, there and gone and there, the finished weight of Immensity pressing down on the whole frozen plain and then lifting and then pressing again.
Every time it pressed, the rime pillars groaned.
Every time it lifted, the air felt strangely empty.
The panda looked at him!
No rising, no spreading of wings, no lifting of the club.
The panda simply turned its great round head, slowly, still chewing on its bone, and fixed its pale ringed eyes on the small figure hanging in the air at the edge of its plain.
There was no anger in that look.

There was nothing in it but a deep and total boredom, the look of something vast glancing down at a bug on the arm of its chair and deciding, without much interest, whether it was worth the effort of lifting a hand.
Noah looked back at it.
He hung in the frozen air above its plain, bare-chested, dark diamond-jade, tendrils of blue-gold burning beneath his skin and a jagged crown of light above his brow.
The dream-seas he had raised were still rolling off him in slow shining tides, lapping at the edge of the frozen ring.
His eyes were very calm.
He did not look away.
Neither did it!

chapters.title: Chapter 5816: A Big, Fat, Panda! II
paragraphs: The panda only looked at him, and its gaze came down on Noah like a hand the size of a sky!

It struck his existence, all of it at once, and pressed him back hard enough that the dream-seas rolling off him caved in on themselves and the air behind him cracked. He slid backward across the frozen dark a full mile before he stopped himself, his diamond-jade skin groaning, his crown of light flickering at its tips.
One look, and it was still chewing!
|Designation: THE Warden Who Does Not Rise.|
|Empowered Hollow Night Lifeform. Keeper of the Northern Descent.|
|VERITAS: ???. PROVENANCE: ???. POTENTIA: ???. PONDUS: ???.|
|Immensity: halfway.|

The Warden Who Does Not Rise. Noah turned the name over. It had sat here since before anyone thought to write a name down. In every branch he could see where he turned back, it went on sitting here, forever, chewing its bone.
He left those branches where they lay.
|Leave, young thing.|
The voice was deep and slow and utterly unbothered, and it came from everywhere on the frozen plain at once.
|You cannot even touch me, much less get past me. And even if you did, those grander than me lie behind here.|
|This is not playtime.|
Noah rolled his neck.
Then he walked forward!

One step, and the dream-seas poured out of him again, a thousand miles of blue-gold tide rolling across the jammed islands and the rime pillars and the drowned Dimensions under the ice. Everything it touched began to dream. The pillars went soft at their edges, and the frozen figures inside them stirred in their sleep.
Then the tide reached the Warden, and broke!

The seas washed up against its great hunched body and slid away on either side, undreaming, parting around it like water around a stone that had sat in its riverbed since the river was born. Half of it was Immense, and that half stayed as solid as bedrock.
So Noah tried the other half.

He crossed the last distance in a single stride and hit it. Everything he was, every packed quark and every Quintessential ECG he had eaten, the whole dense weight of the Fiend in him, driven into the Warden’s shoulder through one closed fist!
HUUM!
The shoulder held as still as a mountain!
The Warden turned its head, slowly, and looked at the fist resting against its fur. Then it lifted the club.
It was a slow motoin, lazy and certain. The tower of Dimensions came around in a slow, bored arc, and Noah saw it coming, and it caught him anyway.
It hit him!
BOOM!
The blow stopped him entirely. His existence came apart under it so completely that nothing was left to break, and he died on the frozen plain before the club had finished its swing.
|Your Dream is Infinite. Even death will not stop it.|
Golden clouds spat him back out a mile away.

He came back already dreaming the death through, slowly, from inside. The angle of the club. Its weight and Immensity. The exact moment it found him. By the time his feet touched the ice he had learned it, and it could never kill him that way again.
The Warden watched him get up. It went back to chewing.
|You do not know Immensity.|
Noah dusted the frost off his shoulder, and kept his answer to himself. He was thinking.

Half-Immense. That was the whole puzzle, and he had been looking at it wrong. He had been trying to hurt the half that was Immense. That half stood beyond the reach of everything he currently was. But the aura kept flickering. There and gone and there. And in the moments when it was gone, the Warden was only a Hollow Night Lifeform.
A very large, very fat, very old one, carrying something Immense in its chest and the borrowed cold of the Long Night in every hair of its fur.
Borrowed.
"Ruination," he said.
|Already done, Master. The flicker is not random. It follows a rhythm. I am marking every window where the Immense half withdraws. The next opens in four heartbeats.|
Noah went forward again!

The Warden swung. He had learned the club; it passed a hand’s width from his face. It swung again, low, a new angle, and killed him. He came back. It swung a third way and killed him again. He came back, and back, each death something he would never die to twice, and every time he returned the Warden had fewer ways left to kill him.
Four heartbeats. Three. Two.
The aura went out!
Noah laid his palm on the Warden’s chest and turned its cold!

THE Kneeling Frost poured into it, and the borrowed winter packed into the Warden’s fur turned inward, freezing from the inside out, spines of ice cracking and splintering across its whole flank. The Warden grunted. It was a small sound. It was the first sound it had made besides speech.
The aura came back, and flung him away across the plain.
He landed on his feet, unhurt and interested!
|Next window in six heartbeats, Master.|

He took it. And the next. The Bow of the Ending Epoch came into his hand between windows, and he aimed its arrows past the Warden, at everything it was attached to: the broken chains trailing from its neck, the mantle of frozen banners on its shoulders, the rime pillars ringing its plain. All of them were borrowed from the Night, and all of them could age. They aged to dust under his arrows, and every link and banner and pillar that crumbled was one more piece of the Warden’s winter gone.
On the ninth window, he dreamed its bone.
The frozen stalk it had been chewing since before he arrived went soft in its mouth, and aged, and crumbled into white powder between its teeth.
The Warden Who Does Not Rise stopped chewing.
Then it rose!
Oh, it rose!
Mind you, this was a Half-Immense monstrosity!

It rose to its feet for the first time in more Ages than anything on the Basal Floor remembered, and the whole frozen plain groaned under it. Ice split for a hundred miles. Its shattered wings of frost spread wide behind it, vast and jagged, and the wind that moved through them was no longer an old choir. It was a roar. The halo of stilled snow above its head flared white, and everything under it stopped.
Time stopped. The dream-seas froze mid-wave. Noah’s own existence locked in place, pinned in a single instant, his thoughts sliding to a halt.

THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour drew that stillness into his Dreams, and a dreaming hour moved as he wished. He came loose. Slowly, then all at once, and he moved out from under the halo just as the Warden’s club came down where he had been and split the plain in half!
The Warden looked at him, and for the first time its eyes held attention!

|Dying is easy for a thing like you. A blow lands, your breath cuts out. The heart just quits. That part takes only an instant. It is over before you even have time to miss the warmth. It is the darkness that comes after which is not so easy. The dark has weight. In that quiet, there is no fire to borrow, no walls to lean on, and no one. You just sit there forever, alone with whatever small, cold thing you made of yourself. Do you fear that darkness? Is that why you try to come back?|
Its voice had changed. It was still deep, still slow, but there was attention in it now. Weight. The aura stopped flickering. It held, half-Immense and steady, pressing down on the whole plain.
Noah didn’t reply as he looked at Ling, hanging at the edge of the frozen ring with her fists clenched and her thighs coiled, a breath away from throwing herself in.
"Sit this one out," he told her.
She opened her mouth to argue. Then she looked at his face, and closed it, and stayed where she was.
Noah turned back to the Warden. He breathed in slow and deep, and let his Dream go wide.
To beat something even half Immense, he had to dream a grand dream.
He dreamed himself.

Once, at first. A second Noah stepped out of the blue-gold light at his side, diamond-jade and crowned, identical to him in every way. Then a third. Ten. A hundred, a thousand, stepping out of the dream-seas one after another, more and more, until they filled the frozen plain from edge to edge and kept going, out past the ring of jammed islands, out into the dark of the Basal Floor, versions of him stretching away in every direction without end.
|THE Waking Decree, THE Dream Without a Far Wall, and Dialetheic Infinity have been combined.|
|Formed: THE Endless Waking.|

|You dream yourself, and existence agrees that each dreamed self is you. Each one carries your full existence. Each one may die and return. Each one learns from every death any of them has ever died.|
|Their number has no end.|
The Warden Who Does Not Rise looked at the infinite sea of him, and roared!

It fought. It fought with everything it had, club and wings and halo, the steady half-Immense aura crushing down on the whole plain. Its club took a thousand of him in a single swng. Its halo froze ten thousand in place, and its wings shredded whole ranks of him into golden dust.
Every one that died came back having learned.
And behind every one that fell, there were infinitely more!

They came at it from every direction at once! A million palms on its fur turned a million lines of borrowed cold against it. Arrows of dreamed decay poured into every flicker and seam. Its wings came off pane by frozen pane, and its club broke at the grip. Up its legs and its back and its shoulders they climbed, and every step they took dreamed another piece of it away!
HUUUM!
It fell!
The Warden Who Does Not Rise toppled backward onto its own frozen plain, and the whole Basal Floor shook with the impact, and the infinite versions of Noah stood back and let it lie there.
One of him walked forward.

He climbed onto its chest, where the black fur had gone dark as a starless sky, and lay down on it, as a man lies down on a warm hillside at the end of a long day. The Warden’s great ringed eyes looked up at him.
He looked at the Panda and said lightly...
"Do not fear that endless darkness."
HUUM!
"Rage."
WAA!
"Rage."
BOOM!
Noah pressed his arms down into its chest!
They sank in. Through fur and ice and ancient bone, into the dark at the center of it, where its dream and its existence lived. He took hold of both. And pulled.
|THE Warden Who Does Not Rise has been granted death.|
|Taken: its Dream. Taken: its existence.|
|The Half-Immense core it carried is yours.|
The Warden breathed out, once, long and slow, like something very old finally being allowed to sleep.
Around them, infinite versions of Noah Osmont stood across the frozen dark, and one by one, gently, they dreamed themselves away as the one plunged into the existence of a massive Panda trembled!
The Warden lay on its back across its frozen plain, and the whole of it was treasure.

Noah could feel that from where he stood on its chest. Every spine of frozen fur carried ages of the Long Night’s cold, packed dense. Every bone under the clear ice was old enough to have watched the Basal Floor fill with Guards one by one. Its broken wings still held the shapes of stopped moments in their panes. A corpse of a Half-Immense Lifeform was worth more than a hundred beings who merely carried Roots.
He knelt, and reached further inside it!
His arms sank through fur and ice and bone, down into the dark at the center of the great chest, and found what lay waiting there.
A singularity!

It hung in the dark of the Warden’s chest, and his sight could only take half of it. One half was there, plain, a point of pale blue light so dense it bent the frozen dark around it. The other half slid away from his perception every time he reached for it, present and absent at once, flickering at the edge of seeing exactly as the Warden’s aura had flickered while it lived.
Around it, thick as the walls of a fortress, coiled weavings of Immensity.
His hand closed toward the singularity and met them. They were solid as the door he had felt at the top of his own existence. His fingers pressed and met solid Immensity at every point.
And the weavings spoke, in the voice of the panda!
|You cannot grasp Immensity if you have no Immensity.|
Noah stayed kneeling on the corpse’s chest with his hand pressed flat against the weavings, and looked at them for a while.
Then he smiled, very slightly.
"Immensity," he said.
His voice was calm.

"Everyone reaches for it. I see them. Every being that ever climbed, climbing toward the same door, as though it were the only door there is. They build their histories on the way to it. Their dreams, their hopes, all their power, poured into one shape, because they were told that shape was the top of everything."

He pressed a little harder, and the weavings held."This one sat at the door for more Ages than I can count, and got halfway through, and stayed. That was all its Immensity ever gave it. A doorway to sit in."
He looked down at the half-seen singularity in the dark.

"I reject it. All of it. Immensity is only one of the things they did. The key was never the door. The key is everything they lived on the way there. Their history. Their dreams. What they hoped for, sitting in the cold. That is the part that belongs to them. That is the part I can reach."
He let his Dream open!

Seas of it poured out of him and down into the Warden’s body. Blue-gold tides, boundless, flooding through the frozen fur and the clear ice and the ancient bones, filling every hollow of the great corpse until the whole of it glowed from inside like a lantern. The dream soaked into the Warden’s dead existence and went looking for what was still there.
It found the Warden’s dream!
Noah saw it. The whole of it, all at once, as the dream-seas carried it up to him.
"It dreamed of rising," he said softly.
The corpse beneath him glowed brighter.

"Ages at the mouth of that rift. Chained there, then too large for the chains, then too still to remember why it stayed. Guarding the way down for those grander than itself. And every Age of that watch, it dreamed of standing up and walking away, down into the dark, or out into the light, anywhere but here. It dreamed of rising for so long that the dream grew heavier than the rest of it."He breathed out. "THE Vigil That Wished to Rise."
Behind him, something began to form!

It gathered out of the blue-gold seas pouring off his shoulders, dream-stuff drawing together, taking shape. A panda. Vast, nearly the size of the Warden itself, made entirely of golden-blue light, its fur shimmering in slow drifting waves, its great round eyes ringed with gold instead of black. Wings spread from its shoulders, whole ones, unbroken, pane after pane of clear shining dream set together as neatly as the Warden’s had once been set by a careless hand. Its body was free of chains, mantle, and club alike.
It rose up behind Noah to its full height, standing tall on the frozen plain, and moved when he moved.
He lifted his hand. The dream-panda lifted its paw!

He reached forward, and it reached with him, its great shining paw sinking down past his arms into the Warden’s chest, down through the dark, to the coiled weavings of Immensity and the singularity inside them.
The weavings let it through!

They parted around the dream-panda’s paw as a mother’s arms open for her own child. It was the Warden’s dream. It was the accumulation of everything the Warden had lived and wanted across every Age of its watch. The Immensity recognized it, and gave way.
The golden paw closed around the singularity, and drew it out!
|THE Vigil That Wished to Rise has been dreamed into form.|
|The Dream of a Half-Immense Lifeform is the accumulation of its existence. What guards its Immensity recognizes its own Dream, and yields to it.|
|Loot obtained: THE Stillborn Singularity of THE Warden’s Immensity.|
|A singularity of Immensity, half-perceivable and half not, holding within it a failed Immensity: an ascent that reached the threshold and never passed through.|
|Its properties are sealed. They may be studied.|
Noah took it from the dream-panda’s paw and held it tightly.

It was cold, and heavy past anything its size had a right to be, and it flickered in his grip, there and gone and there. He could feel the whole failed ascent inside it, an Immensity that had climbed halfway through the door and frozen on the threshold. A thing that almost was. He closed his fingers around it until the flicker steadied against his palm, and put it away, deep inside himself, where nothing could reach it but him.
Then he stood, and looked down at the corpse.
The dream-panda behind him lowered its head, and sank into him.
It poured back into his shoulders in a slow golden flood, and he felt it settle somewhere deep, kept, ready to be dreamed again. The Warden’s Dream was his now.Its body was another matter.

He looked it over as a collector looks over the finest piece he has ever found. The frozen fur, every spine of it packed with the Long Night’s cold. The clear ice over ancient bones. The broken wings still full of stopped moments. All of it, whole, the corpse of a being that had sat halfway to Immensity for longer than anything on this Floor could remember.
He could swallow it right now. He could feel his existence leaning toward it, hungry, eager to press every Age of that watch into his quarks.
He kept it whole instead.

Blue-gold dream closed over the great body in a slow tide, sealing it from fur to bone, until the Warden lay wrapped in a shell of shining dream on its frozen plain. Then the shell drew inward, smaller and smaller, and the whole vast corpse went with it, down into the depths of his Dream, where it settled beside the Stillborn Singularity. Kept. Untouched.
|Consumed: the Dream of THE Warden Who Does Not Rise. THE Vigil That Wished to Rise has been kept, and may be dreamed again at your will.|
|Stored within your Dream: the corpse of THE Warden Who Does Not Rise, a Half-Immense Lifeform.|
|Held: THE Stillborn Singularity of THE Warden’s Immensity.|
|THE reach of your Dream has expanded.|
Noah stood on the frozen plain where a Half-Immense guardian had sat, alone now except for Ling watching wide-eyed at the edge of the ring and the blue rift splitting the dark before him.
A hundred deaths had brought him here. The rift behind the Warden opened downward into cold that pulled at every quark he owned, toward those grander than the Warden, waiting below.

He was hungry for them already. But first, he had to make proper use of the loot of the big, fat panda to ensure he obtained the grandest returns. Which meant giving it all away. The singularity of Immensity, and the whole Half-Immense corpse along with it, so that his Tide could give him back something even grander!
He wanted to see if that would be enough...to trigger an evolution!

Each one carries your full existence.
Each one may die and return.
Each one learns from every death any of them has ever died.|
|Their number has no end.|
The Warden Who Does Not Rise looked at the infinite sea of him, and roared!
It fought.
It fought with everything it had, club and wings and halo, the steady half-Immense aura crushing down on the whole plain.
Its club took a thousand of him in a single swng.
Its halo froze ten thousand in place, and its wings shredded whole ranks of him into golden dust.
Every one that died came back having learned.
And behind every one that fell, there were infinitely more!
They came at it from every direction at once!
A million palms on its fur turned a million lines of borrowed cold against it.
Arrows of dreamed decay poured into every flicker and seam.
Its wings came off pane by frozen pane, and its club broke at the grip.
Up its legs and its back and its shoulders they climbed, and every step they took dreamed another piece of it away!
HUUUM!
It fell!
The Warden Who Does Not Rise toppled backward onto its own frozen plain, and the whole Basal Floor shook with the impact, and the infinite versions of Noah stood back and let it lie there.
One of him walked forward.
He climbed onto its chest, where the black fur had gone dark as a starless sky, and lay down on it, as a man lies down on a warm hillside at the end of a long day.
The Warden’s great ringed eyes looked up at him.
He looked at the Panda and said lightly...
"Do not fear that endless darkness."
HUUM!
"Rage."
WAA!
"Rage."
BOOM!
Noah pressed his arms down into its chest!
They sank in.
Through fur and ice and ancient bone, into the dark at the center of it, where its dream and its existence lived.
He took hold of both.
And pulled.
|THE Warden Who Does Not Rise has been granted death.|
|Taken: its Dream.
Taken: its existence.|
|The Half-Immense core it carried is yours.|
The Warden breathed out, once, long and slow, like something very old finally being allowed to sleep.
Around them, infinite versions of Noah Osmont stood across the frozen dark, and one by one, gently, they dreamed themselves away as the one plunged into the existence of a massive Panda trembled!
The Warden lay on its back across its frozen plain, and the whole of it was treasure.
Noah could feel that from where he stood on its chest.
Every spine of frozen fur carried ages of the Long Night’s cold, packed dense.
Every bone under the clear ice was old enough to have watched the Basal Floor fill with Guards one by one.
Its broken wings still held the shapes of stopped moments in their panes.
A corpse of a Half-Immense Lifeform was worth more than a hundred beings who merely carried Roots.
He knelt, and reached further inside it!
His arms sank through fur and ice and bone, down into the dark at the center of the great chest, and found what lay waiting there.
A singularity!
It hung in the dark of the Warden’s chest, and his sight could only take half of it.
One half was there, plain, a point of pale blue light so dense it bent the frozen dark around it.
The other half slid away from his perception every time he reached for it, present and absent at once, flickering at the edge of seeing exactly as the Warden’s aura had flickered while it lived.
Around it, thick as the walls of a fortress, coiled weavings of Immensity.
His hand closed toward the singularity and met them.
They were solid as the door he had felt at the top of his own existence.
His fingers pressed and met solid Immensity at every point.
And the weavings spoke, in the voice of the panda!
|You cannot grasp Immensity if you have no Immensity.|
Noah stayed kneeling on the corpse’s chest with his hand pressed flat against the weavings, and looked at them for a while.
Then he smiled, very slightly.
"Immensity," he said.
His voice was calm.
"Everyone reaches for it.
I see them.
Every being that ever climbed, climbing toward the same door, as though it were the only door there is.
They build their histories on the way to it.
Their dreams, their hopes, all their power, poured into one shape, because they were told that shape was the top of everything."
He pressed a little harder, and the weavings held."This one sat at the door for more Ages than I can count, and got halfway through, and stayed.
That was all its Immensity ever gave it.
A doorway to sit in."
He looked down at the half-seen singularity in the dark.
"I reject it.
All of it.
Immensity is only one of the things they did.
The key was never the door.
The key is everything they lived on the way there.
Their history.
Their dreams.
What they hoped for, sitting in the cold.
That is the part that belongs to them.
That is the part I can reach."
He let his Dream open!
Seas of it poured out of him and down into the Warden’s body.
Blue-gold tides, boundless, flooding through the frozen fur and the clear ice and the ancient bones, filling every hollow of the great corpse until the whole of it glowed from inside like a lantern.
The dream soaked into the Warden’s dead existence and went looking for what was still there.
It found the Warden’s dream!
Noah saw it.
The whole of it, all at once, as the dream-seas carried it up to him.
"It dreamed of rising," he said softly.
The corpse beneath him glowed brighter.
"Ages at the mouth of that rift.
Chained there, then too large for the chains, then too still to remember why it stayed.
Guarding the way down for those grander than itself.
And every Age of that watch, it dreamed of standing up and walking away, down into the dark, or out into the light, anywhere but here.
It dreamed of rising for so long that the dream grew heavier than the rest of it."He breathed out.
"THE Vigil That Wished to Rise."
Behind him, something began to form!
It gathered out of the blue-gold seas pouring off his shoulders, dream-stuff drawing together, taking shape.
A panda.
Vast, nearly the size of the Warden itself, made entirely of golden-blue light, its fur shimmering in slow drifting waves, its great round eyes ringed with gold instead of black.
Wings spread from its shoulders, whole ones, unbroken, pane after pane of clear shining dream set together as neatly as the Warden’s had once been set by a careless hand.
Its body was free of chains, mantle, and club alike.
It rose up behind Noah to its full height, standing tall on the frozen plain, and moved when he moved.
He lifted his hand.
The dream-panda lifted its paw!

He reached forward, and it reached with him, its great shining paw sinking down past his arms into the Warden’s chest, down through the dark, to the coiled weavings of Immensity and the singularity inside them.
The weavings let it through!
They parted around the dream-panda’s paw as a mother’s arms open for her own child.
It was the Warden’s dream.
It was the accumulation of everything the Warden had lived and wanted across every Age of its watch.
The Immensity recognized it, and gave way.
The golden paw closed around the singularity, and drew it out!
|THE Vigil That Wished to Rise has been dreamed into form.|
|The Dream of a Half-Immense Lifeform is the accumulation of its existence.
What guards its Immensity recognizes its own Dream, and yields to it.|
|Loot obtained: THE Stillborn Singularity of THE Warden’s Immensity.|
|A singularity of Immensity, half-perceivable and half not, holding within it a failed Immensity: an ascent that reached the threshold and never passed through.|
|Its properties are sealed.
They may be studied.|
Noah took it from the dream-panda’s paw and held it tightly.
It was cold, and heavy past anything its size had a right to be, and it flickered in his grip, there and gone and there.
He could feel the whole failed ascent inside it, an Immensity that had climbed halfway through the door and frozen on the threshold.
A thing that almost was.
He closed his fingers around it until the flicker steadied against his palm, and put it away, deep inside himself, where nothing could reach it but him.
Then he stood, and looked down at the corpse.
The dream-panda behind him lowered its head, and sank into him.
It poured back into his shoulders in a slow golden flood, and he felt it settle somewhere deep, kept, ready to be dreamed again.
The Warden’s Dream was his now.Its body was another matter.
He looked it over as a collector looks over the finest piece he has ever found.
The frozen fur, every spine of it packed with the Long Night’s cold.
The clear ice over ancient bones.
The broken wings still full of stopped moments.
All of it, whole, the corpse of a being that had sat halfway to Immensity for longer than anything on this Floor could remember.
He could swallow it right now.
He could feel his existence leaning toward it, hungry, eager to press every Age of that watch into his quarks.
He kept it whole instead.
Blue-gold dream closed over the great body in a slow tide, sealing it from fur to bone, until the Warden lay wrapped in a shell of shining dream on its frozen plain.
Then the shell drew inward, smaller and smaller, and the whole vast corpse went with it, down into the depths of his Dream, where it settled beside the Stillborn Singularity.
Kept.
Untouched.
|Consumed: the Dream of THE Warden Who Does Not Rise.
THE Vigil That Wished to Rise has been kept, and may be dreamed again at your will.|
|Stored within your Dream: the corpse of THE Warden Who Does Not Rise, a Half-Immense Lifeform.|
|Held: THE Stillborn Singularity of THE Warden’s Immensity.|
|THE reach of your Dream has expanded.|
Noah stood on the frozen plain where a Half-Immense guardian had sat, alone now except for Ling watching wide-eyed at the edge of the ring and the blue rift splitting the dark before him.
A hundred deaths had brought him here.
The rift behind the Warden opened downward into cold that pulled at every quark he owned, toward those grander than the Warden, waiting below.
He was hungry for them already.
But first, he had to make proper use of the loot of the big, fat panda to ensure he obtained the grandest returns.
Which meant giving it all away.
The singularity of Immensity, and the whole Half-Immense corpse along with it, so that his Tide could give him back something even grander!
He wanted to see if that would be enough...to trigger an evolution!

chapters.title: Chapter 5817: Glory! I
paragraphs: Barbatos’s dream smelled of glorious death.

Noah stepped into it through the Dream Engine and found her where he always did, at the heart of a necropolis that went on forever. Tombs rose in endless terrraces under a violet sky, each one carved with names, and between them walked the dead she had raised. She sat on the steps of the tallest tomb with a book open across her knees and a thread of pale green necromancy spinning lazily between her fingers as it passed through dozens of dead Dimensions.
She looked up, saw him, and smiled.
He spared her the speech and opened his hand.

The corpse of THE Warden Who Does Not Rise came out of his Dream and settled onto the terraces of her necropolis. It filled the sky. Its frozen fur blotted out the violet light, its broken wings of stopped moments hung over whole districts of tombs, its great ringed face lay turned toward her, eyes closed, as though it had simply lain down among her dead to sleep.
Every skeleton in the necropolis stopped walking and looked at it!
Barbatos set down her book.

She asked him what it was. He told her: a Half-Immense guardian, dead, whole, carrying Ages of the Long Night’s cold in every spine of its fur. She asked him what he wanted her to do with it. He told her whatever she liked.
She walked up to it slowly and laid her palm flat against its frozen side.
"Oh," Barbatos said quietly. "Oh, you gorgeous fucking thing!"
She was talking to the corpse as he left her to it.
|Given: the corpse of THE Warden Who Does Not Rise, a Half-Immense Lifeform, to Barbatos.|
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has noted your giving. A gift of this weight, given with thought to one you hold dear, will be answered.|
He moved on!

Emotive’s dream was exactly as he had left it: THE Earliest Folds reimagined in a madwoman’s hands, woven towers of THE Loom arching overhead, and statues of him everywhere, each one carved with the devotion of someone who had never once considered being ashamed of it.
She saw him and came flying. He caught her before she could wrap herself around his feet this time.
While she clung to his chest, laughing, he thought about why he had come to her with this.

He had many people with potential. His Son. Seo-yeon. Thalia with her Root of genome alteration. Barbatos, just now, with a Half-Immense corpse to raise. Every one of them could grow into something grand.
But Emotive’s potential was the one that frightened him a little!
Her Root was Emotion, and it was Physical. Every feeling she held, she carried in her body as mass, and force, and weight. The more she felt, the heavier and stronger she became.
That alone would have been enough. It was only the beginning.

Every lifeform in existence did what it did because of how it felt. Pride built empires. Fear toppled them. Love had moved him across more domains than he could count. Emotion was the engine underneath every other engine, and Emotive’s Root was built out of that engine directly.

And emotion was always one’s own. It came from inside, every time! The Long Night froze whatever a being had taken from somewhere else, and it could find nothing in a feeling to freeze. Under the Counting, under the Sealed Door, under a winter that choked every borrowed power in existence, her Root would keep generating, because a heart that feels needs nothing from anyone.

Then there were the Seven Sins and their Virtues. She had refined them in her dream to heights that had alarmed him, stacked and packed and volatile, storm upon storm of Ego. Her Root had simply swallowed all of it and turned it into weight.

And last, the thing only she had. The link. She was tied to his emotions in an unfathomable way. Every feeling that moved through him reached her too. As he grew, she grew. As he climbed, some part of her climbed with him.
A Root that fed on the one thing in existence that could never run dry, fed further by him.
Yes. She was the one!
He set her down in front of him, and let his Dream open.
Behind him, the golden-blue panda rose!

THE Vigil That Wished to Rise gathered out of his Dream, vast and shining, its gold-ringed eyes calm, its whole unbroken wings spread wide over the woven towers. Emotive’s manic eyes went round and bright as she looked up at it. The dream-panda reached into the depths of Noah’s Dream with one great paw, and drew out THE Stillborn Singularity of THE Warden’s Immensity, half-perceivable and flickering, and lowered it gently into Emotive’s open hands.
She held it, and her hair burned in every color at once!
"For me?" she whispered.
"For you."

She stared at it, then at him, and her eyes blazed with a love so total it was very nearly frightening. Instead of asking what it was, she held it against her chest, over her Root, and he watched her existence lean toward it.
|Given: THE Stillborn Singularity of THE Warden’s Immensity, to Emotive.|
|Given this hour: a Half-Immense corpse and a singularity of failed Immensity, to two you hold dear, with thought.|
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has answered.|
HUUM!
At this time, Emotive’s figure also began to shine as an utterly euphoric blast of emotions erupted from her!
And...
|THE Tide has been made euphoric with its brilliance. The quality of your return has further increased.|
The dream around them shuddered!
|Returned, as dreamed:|
|Loot I: the corpse of an Immense One. Whole. Its Immensity settled within it, unscattered.|
|Loot II: an Immense Ergosphere. A sphere of turning Immensity, holding within it Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins. Number: unknown.|
They came out of the Tide into Emotive’s dream, and the dream strained under them at once!

The corpse came first! It hung in the sky above the woven towers, and it was vaster than the Warden had been, vaster than anything Noah had yet seen lying still. A figure like a colossal robed sovereign, its face serene and sealed, its hands crossed over its chest, a crown of pale fire still resting on its brow long after the fire had stopped burning.

Its Immensity had stayed whole through death. It sat inside the body, whole and settled and heavy, and the weight of it pressed down on the dream until the statues of Noah began to crack at their bases!
Oh!
Oh!!!
Then the Ergosphere!

It bloomed beside the corpse, a sphere of Immensity turning around a dark core, and the turning never slowed. Currents of pale gold light swept around it in bnds, faster at its equator, slower at its poles, dragging the dream-air around with them.

Inside, glimpsed through the turning bands, lay shapes. Many shapes. Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins, dozens, hundreds, more, suspended in the dark at the center, and every time Noah tried to count them, the turning carried the count away.
Emotive’s dream began to come apart!

The woven towers of THE Loom groaned and bent. Cracks raced across the sky. The statues of Noah toppled one after another, and the ground of THE Earliest Folds buckled under the weight of two things that had never been made to sit inside someone’s dream!
Noah moved at once!

He wrapped his Dream around the corpse and the Ergosphere together, sealed them in blue-gold, and pulled. The whole enormous weight of both came away out of Emotive’s dream in a single rush and went down, through him, through the Dream Engine, into THE Existential Root Domain, where there was room enough to hold them.
Emotive’s dream steadied. The cracks in the sky closed!
In THE Existential Root Domain, one part of Noah stood before a dead Immense One and a turning sphere, and looked.

The corpse lay across the blue-gold hills like a fallen range of mountains, robed and crowned, its hands crossed over its chest. Its Immensity sat inside it whole, and the weight of that pressed a shallow valley into the Domain’s soil around it. Beside it, the Immense Ergosphere turned and turned.
He was about to grasp them when his gaze changed.
Another part of him had felt something!

chapters.title: Chapter 5818: Glory! II
paragraphs: Far away, in the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity, inside a cavern of purple torches on a lone dark mountain, a sliver of Noah still sat cross-legged on a mat. He had sent the a part of himself and all of Ling down into THE Undersnow.
And now that part felt the sky come down.

Auras of Immensity pressed on the mountain from above. Several of them, heavy and foreign and moving, bearing down through the blizzard toward the Thinker’s coat of burning light. The purple torches along the cavern walls leaned sideways in their brackets as though a great wind were blowing through the stone! The cavern floor hummed.
Noah looked across at the only other being in the cavern.

THE THINKER AT THE END OF EXISTENCE sat on his prayer mat, vast and kneeling, the frost-packed gash still leaking faint threads of Immensity down his back. His great beads clicked, one by one. His pale, pupil-less eyes lifted toward the cavern ceiling and moved slowly around it, as though he could see straight through the stone to the sky beyond.
|"Adversity is always grand, and always relentless."|
His voice was calm and deep and faintly interested, the voice of a scholar noting that it had begun to rain.
|"Waves of Immensity are crashing into THE Legacy of THE Acharya. It is rare for Legacies to attack one another. But in times like these, anything is possible."|
The beads clicked.|"I have had a long time to think. And I believe I can guess what their target is, from where most of the attacking force has gathered now."|
Noah’s gaze sharpened.
"And where would that be?"
The Thinker smiled. The fierce line of his mouth widened, very slightly, beneath the weeping eyes.
|"Why, here, of course. Toward this mountain."|A slow rumble of breath. |"Which leads me to believe that their target, among other things, is you."|
The torches guttered. Somewhere far above, something heavy settled against the Thinker’s coat of Immensity, and the whole mountain shivered.
|"Have you made progress in THE Undersnow? Or in yourself?"| The Thinker tilted his great head.|"I ask because I would rather you did not worry about this end too much."|
"I made some progress," Noah said. "And I will make more."
He looked up at the humming ceiling. "But why should I not worry?"
|"THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity is extremely old."|

The Thinker’s voice held no hurry at all.|"We may have poisonous snakes among us. That is the only way anyone could have gotten in. But we are still grand. Lucy built this, after all. And Lucy is grand."|
His beads went still.
|"We have some time, for now. Let us see how things unfold."|
Noah lifted his head.

He could feel existence trembling. Beyond the stone of the mountain, beyond the Thinker’s burning coat, beyond the blizzard, something enormous was happening to the whole Legacy at once. What truly was going on out there?
He sent his perception up through the mountain to look.
The sky over THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity was broken.

Cracks ran across it from horizon to horizon, jagged and white, and through them the blizzard poured in thicker than ever. Snow buried the Elsedimension Mountains to their shoulders. The purple-gold rivers on the Legacy’s floor ran fast and dark, churning, and the Existential Conduits rising from them hummed at a pitch that set one’s teeth on edge.
And through that broken sky moved the invaders!

To his perception they looked like suns. Brilliant golden spheres, dozens of them, each one an Immensity foreign to this place, sliding through the storm in slow, deliberate lines. Some circled the mountains of the Protectors, pinning them. Some hung over the Firmament Mountain, where the Plain of Accord lay buried under snow. And the greatest number of them, a slow gathering tide of gold, were drifting toward a single lone mountain wrapped in a coat of hazy purple Immensity.
Toward the Thinker. Toward him!
Crimson gold snow fell wherever they passed.
Then the sky went dark!

It happened all at once. Across the whole broken width of the Legacy’s sky, from every horizon, a shape bloomed out of the cracks, so vast that for a moment it read as the sky itself. Obsidian, veined with gold, spreading and spreading until it covered everything above the snow.
It was a visage!

An illusory face the size of the Legacy itself, hanging over all of it. Its great head was the head of an octopus, a vast swollen mantle of obsidian skin shot through with rivers of burning gold, rising up into the broken sky past sight. Below it, where a chin should have been, hung a beard of tentacles, thousands of them, each one longer than a mountain range, coiling and uncoiling slowly in the storm.

Its skin was ridged and scaled in places, ancient, crusted with growths like coral that had been gathering since before the first Legacy was raised. Behind its head, half-seen, dark shapes that might have been vast vestigial wings stirred in the dark between the cracks.
And its eyes!

Two of them, each larger than the Firmament Mountain, burning crimson. They were enraged. They looked down at the Legacy, and at every golden sphere moving through it, with a fury so old and so total that the blizzard itself faltered under their gaze.
Somewhere in all that vastness, very small against the obsidian brow, something glinted. A pair of round lenses, perched on nothing, catching the light.
The tentacles spread!

They fell from the visage’s face and unfurled across the entire Legacy, thousands of them reaching down through the snow, curling around mountains, draping across rivers, laying themselves over every Conduit and every peak from one horizon to the other. Where they touched, the air went still.
And every golden sphere in the Legacy stopped.

All of them, from the ones circling the Protectors’ mountains to the ones over the Firmament to the great gathering tide drifting toward the Thinker’s mountain. Every foreign Immensity froze in place amid the boundless snow, pinned where it hung, as the tentacles settled over the Legacy like a net over a pond.
The visage spoke!
|This is the motherfucking Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity.|
|You all seem to forget that, so let me remind you.|
|There are levels to this shit.|
|THERE! ARE! LEVELS!|
BOOM!
Obsidian gold brilliance raged down out of the broken sky!

It poured from the visage and from every tentacle at once, black and gold and blinding, flooding the whole Legacy from its highest peak to the bottom of its rivers. Snow burned away in the light of it. The cracks in the sky filled with it. And behind it, rising out of the obsidian and the gold, came Immensity.
Unfathomable Immensity!

Noah felt it land on the Legacy, and on the frozen golden spheres, and on the mountain where he sat, and on him. It was the weight of a being who had stood at the top of existence for longer than most of existence had existed. It was the weight of a scholar who had been poisoned in his own study, and was done being polite about it.
In the purple-lit cavern, THE Thinker at the End of Existence looked up at the trembling ceiling, and his fierce almost-smile widened.
|"Ah,"| he said mildly. |"There he is."|

sentences.text: Far away, in the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity, inside a cavern of purple torches on a lone dark mountain, a sliver of Noah still sat cross-legged on a mat.
He had sent the a part of himself and all of Ling down into THE Undersnow.
And now that part felt the sky come down.
Auras of Immensity pressed on the mountain from above.
Several of them, heavy and foreign and moving, bearing down through the blizzard toward the Thinker’s coat of burning light.
The purple torches along the cavern walls leaned sideways in their brackets as though a great wind were blowing through the stone!
The cavern floor hummed.
Noah looked across at the only other being in the cavern.
THE THINKER AT THE END OF EXISTENCE sat on his prayer mat, vast and kneeling, the frost-packed gash still leaking faint threads of Immensity down his back.
His great beads clicked, one by one.
His pale, pupil-less eyes lifted toward the cavern ceiling and moved slowly around it, as though he could see straight through the stone to the sky beyond.
|"Adversity is always grand, and always relentless."|
His voice was calm and deep and faintly interested, the voice of a scholar noting that it had begun to rain.
|"Waves of Immensity are crashing into THE Legacy of THE Acharya.
It is rare for Legacies to attack one another.
But in times like these, anything is possible."|
The beads clicked.|"I have had a long time to think.
And I believe I can guess what their target is, from where most of the attacking force has gathered now."|
Noah’s gaze sharpened.
"And where would that be?"
The Thinker smiled.
The fierce line of his mouth widened, very slightly, beneath the weeping eyes.
|"Why, here, of course.
Toward this mountain."|A slow rumble of breath. |"Which leads me to believe that their target, among other things, is you."|
The torches guttered.
Somewhere far above, something heavy settled against the Thinker’s coat of Immensity, and the whole mountain shivered.
|"Have you made progress in THE Undersnow?
Or in yourself?"| The Thinker tilted his great head.|"I ask because I would rather you did not worry about this end too much."|
"I made some progress," Noah said.
"And I will make more."
He looked up at the humming ceiling.
"But why should I not worry?"
|"THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity is extremely old."|
The Thinker’s voice held no hurry at all.|"We may have poisonous snakes among us.

But we are still grand.
Lucy built this, after all.

His beads went still.

chapters.title: Chapter 5819: Glory! III
paragraphs: The tentacles had barely settled over the Legacy when the Existential Conduits began to rise.

Noah watched it happen through the sliver of himself on the Thinker’s mountain. All across the Legacy, the vast pillars of flowing authority that climbed out of the purple-gold rivers tore loose from their beds and lifted. They rose higher, and higher, until they stood like the columns of some impossible hall, and then they moved, spreading apart, drawing lines across the whole snowbound expanse, pillar beside pillar beside pillar, until the Legacy was carved into separate domains, each one walled off from the others by rings of rising light!
Golden spheres of foreign Immensity found themselves caught inside those rings, cut off, each one alone in its own partition.
Then the mist came down!

It poured out of the obsidian visage in the sky, black and gold and billowing, boundless as the blizzard and far heavier, rushing down over every carved domain at once. Mountains vanished into it, then the rivers and the Conduit walls and the frozen golden spheres pinned inside them. Everything it touched became obscure, unseeable, lost in a churning dark shot through with veins of gold.
|If you didn’t know, you’re about to know.|
|Put some respect on her name.|
|Put some respect on THE Acharya!|
BOOM!
The mists closed over the whole Legacy!

Noah’s perception went into them and came back with nothing but chaos. Immensity colliding with Immensity somewhere in the obscurity. Domains shaking. Roars that could have been anything, or anyone. The weight of beings who had stood at the top of existence for longer than most of existence had existed, all of them at war at once, hidden behind a curtain of gold and black.
His expression grew heavy!

Among all these titans, he truly fell short of every one. They held Immensity. Every one of them, the invaders and the defenders and the monstrous visage spreading its tentacles across the sky. They had walked through the door long ago, before existence shut it, and whatever they were fighting over now, they were fighting over it from a height above him.
That height was closed to him forever. Existence had made sure of that.
Yet he had something they lacked! A future away from Immensity, glorious and unwritten, that existence had denied him the old road to and so forced him to find his own.
So.
He drew his gaze back down out of the storm, and closed his eyes on the prayer mat, and turned his whole attention to the part of him standing in THE Existential Root Domain.

The dead Immense One lay across the blue-gold hills, robed and crowned, its hands crossed over its chest, its settled Immensity pressing the soil down around it into a shallow valley. Beside it, the Immense Ergosphere turned and turned, gold light sweeping around its dark core.

Ruination stood a little behind him, her crimson beams resting quietly on the corpse, reading it, keeping every detail. THE Infiniverse stood beside her in her heavy coat of many colors, still and watchful. Both of them were silent. They had come to watch their Master, and they would watch.
Noah looked at the corpse, and at the Ergosphere, for a long while.
"I generated both of you," he said.
His voice was calm and far away, and the Domain seemed to lean in to hear it.

"From my own weavings, and from what I found in existence. A Half-Immense guardian’s body. A singularity of failed Immensity. I gave them to people I love, and the Tide gave you back to me in their place. You exist because I gave."He looked at the dead sovereign’s serene face. "Now I will swallow you, to see if it will all be enough."
He opened his mouth.

Inside it lay blue-gold brilliance, endless, infinite, a light that went down and down without reaching any bottom, and at the heart of it, turning, countless points of perfect dark. Event horizons. Thousands of them. Millions. Every one of them a place where something could fall in and stay fallen.
He pulled!
The corpse moved!

It lifted off the blue-gold hills, slowly at first, the whole vast robed body of an Immense One rising from the vally it had pressed into the soil, and drifted toward him. The Ergosphere came with it, its bands of light stretching, smearing, its turning drawn out into long spirals as it fell toward his open mouth. Both of them gravitated to him as everything gravitates toward an event horizon, faster and faster, stretching as they came, the sovereign’s crown of pale fire drawing out into a long thread of light, the Ergosphere unwinding into ribbons of gold.
THE Infiniverse took a step back. Ruination’s beams flared.
The corpse reached him first, and went in!
It poured into the brilliance of his mouth in a long, stretched river of robe and flesh and crown, and fell into the countless event horizons, and his Infinite Dream took hold of it.
|Devouring: the corpse of an Immense One.|

His Dream broke it down, all of it, layer by layer, as a fire breaks down a log. The robes went first, woven of authority so old it had forgotten its own name. Then the flesh, dense beyond anything he had eaten, every cell of it saturated with settled Immensity. Then the bones, then the crown, then the serene sealed face. His Dream took each piece apart, refined it to its purest essence, and pressed that essence down into him.
His body shook!

The diamond-jade of his skin darkened, and darkened again, until it was nearly black, the tendrils of blue-gold beneath it blazing so bright they lit the Domain’s hills. His crown of light flared. His muscles locked and swelled and locked again as the Immensity of a dead sovereign packed itself into every quark of him.
|Records of an Immense One acquired. Its name has worn away. Its memories have been kept.|
|Fragment acquired: Settled Bearing. The calm of a being that stood at the top of existence has been absorbed into THE One Foundation.|
|Integrated value: equivalent to 404 Quintessential Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins.|
|THE Osmontian Culmination. Present saturation: 72%.|
Seventy-two percent!
The Ergosphere came next!
It fell into his mouth in long gold ribbons, and as its turning broke apart inside his Dream, the thing it had been hiding finally held still long enough to be counted.
|The Immense Ergosphere has been opened.|
|Contained: Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins x333.|
Three hundred and thirty-three!

They poured out of the broken Ergosphere into his Dream like a river of stars, every one of them a genuine Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin, the true thing that Lesser Kryos were only a quarter of, and his Infinite Dream took them in one after another after another. Each one went down into him and broke apart and filled him. He could feel the space inside his existence closing, every hollow packing tight, every last gap between his quarks filling with the essense of Immensity that would stay unborn.
|Devouring: Existential Chorionic Gonadotropins.|
|Present saturation: 79%.|
His existence was screaming.

It was the scream of fullness, of a vessel filled to its brim. He was packed so dense that the Domain around him had begun to bend toward him, its blue-gold hills tilting, its river of light curving in toward where he stood, as though he had become the center of everything inside it. Ruination’s beams had gone still. THE Infiniverse’s eyes were wide.
The last Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin went down.
Everything stopped!

The Domain held still around him. His Dream held still. His Root, his existence, all of him, packed to the absolute limit of what his present form could hold, held perfectly, silently still, like a breath drawn in and kept.
And then the prompts came, slow and grand, one after another.
|THE Osmontian Culmination has reached complete saturation.|
|The Absolute of your present existence has been filled.|

|Everything that made you has been gathered: your Dreams, your Records, your Actions, your Memories, every life you lived in the death of time, every gift you gave, every death you granted, every emotion you held and every one you cast out. All of it has culminated.|
|An evolutionary pathway uniquely your own has formed.|
|But your existence, your Dreams, and your history are too vast to culminate in a single shape.|
|Three pathways have formed.|
|PATHWAY I: THE Dreaming Origin.|
|A lifeform whose existence is a Dream that existence must dream along with. Your Empyros and Fiend halves carried to their end.|
|What you dream becomes true, first near you, then across Dimensions, then across whatever you can perceive. Existence itself becomes a thing you dream, and dream again, and dream differently.|
|You would stand at the source of things rather than among them. Every being you meet would be, in part, a dream you are having.|
|Born from: THE Human Dreamer, THE Waking Decree, THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour, every dream you have ever entered.|
|Cost: the farther you dream, the farther you stand from what you dream. The risk of becoming the author of a story you can no longer step inside.|
|PATHWAY II: THE Unsated Sovereign.|
|A lifeform of absolute weight and endless appetite. Your Fiend half carried to its end.|

|Your body becomes denser than any law existence can write. You devour and stay hungry. Everything you consume becomes you, and everything you become, you consume further. Even Immensity, eaten, would only make you heavier.|
|You would grow without ceiling by eating the grandest things in existence, one after another, forever.|
|Born from: THE One Foundation, THE Tide-Crowned Protagonist, THE Rendered Design, every Guard, every corpse, every Kryos you have swallowed.|
|Cost: a hunger with no end has no rest. The risk of becoming a thing that existence fears more than it can love.|
|PATHWAY III: THE Quintessential Human.|
|A lifeform that is human, entirely and infinitely. The first Letter you ever spoke carried to its end: I Am... Human.|

|You keep everything human: fear and love, doubt and hunger, the capacity to be wrong and to learn from it. And all of it becomes infinite. Your emotions generate without end. Your gifts return without end. Your people grow as you grow.|
|You would rise by what you feel and what you give, and carry everyone you hold dear upward with you.|
|Born from: THE Living Grammar, THE Sanguine Covenant, the Letter Human, every life you sheltered, every gift you gave freely, every death you refused to stay dead.|
|Cost: you would remain vulnerable in every way a human is vulnerable. Only, infinitely so.|
The last prompt came slowly.
|Every Lifeform that has ever evolved has stood where you stand now, at the edge of what it was.|
|Most chose without ever knowing they were choosing. Existence chose through them, by hunger and cold and the pressure of their days.|
|You know.|
|Three roads lie before you, and each is truly yours. Your Existence has offered them. Walking them is yours alone.|
|What you become will be decided by neither your power, nor your history, nor any prophecy of three.|
|It will be decided by a single choice. Yours.|
|Choose.|
Noah stood in the stillness of THE Existential Root Domain, packed full to the edge of everything he had ever been, and looked at the three roads.
Behind him, Ruination and THE Infiniverse waited without a sound!

chapters.title: Chapter 5820: THE Dreaming Human Origin!
paragraphs: Noah looked at the three roads.

THE Dreaming Origin, where existence would dream along with him. THE Unsated Sovereign, where he would grow heavier with everything he ate, forever. THE Quintessential Human, where everything human in him would become infinite. Each one hung before him in the stillness of THE Existential Root Domain, complete and real and waiting for him to step onto it.
He looked at them for a long time.
Then he laughed, very quietly.
"All of these are a part of me," he said.
His voice was calm.

"I am a human. I have been a human through everything, through the casting out and the death of time and every door that ever shut in my face. I am a dreamer. Everything I have built, I dreamed first. And I am a sovereign. I rule what is mine, and I take what I need, and I have yet to apologize for it once."
He looked from one road to the next. "Each of you is me. So why the hell do I have to choose?"
The stillness of the Domain trembled around him.
"I want it all," Noah said.
His voice rose.
"I WANT IT ALL!"
BOOM!
His existence shook!

It shook from the center out, every packed quark in him vibrating at once, his saturated existence lurching toward all three roads at the same time. The roads answered. They bent toward him, and toward each other, and began to bleed together, the Dreaming Origin’s gold running into the Unsated Sovereign’s dark into the Quintessential Human’s warm and living light. Something began to bloom in him!
Something enormous. His skin split along the tendrils of light and blazed. His crown of radiance flared so bright it lit the whole Domain white.
The transformation had begun!
And above him, the sky of THE Existential Root Domain split open.
It cracked from horizon to horizon in a single jagged line, and through the crack poured light that belonged nowhere in his Domain.

Obsidian gold. Black and gold together, like the mists over the Legacy, but colder. Older. It came down out of the crack in great falling shapes, and each shape was a piece of existence itself given weight and aimed at him.
He could feel what they were as they fell!
A Provenance of Ending. A Provenance of Order. A Provenance of Stillness, a Provenance of the Counted, a Provenance of the Door.
Aspects of existence, concepts as old as anything that had ever been, crashing down toward the one being in the Domain who had just tried to become something existence had forbidden!
|How dare you.|
The first one hit him!

It struck like the fall of countless Dimensons, and the blue-gold hills around him flattened into glass in a ring a hundred miles wide. The light of it was so bright that for an instant he saw nothing at all, only white, only the weight.
|How dare you.|
A heavy voice boomed out!

The second hit him. The third. They came down out of the crack one after another, an endless cascade, Ending and Order and Stillness and the Counted, each one a judgment, each one heavy enough to unmake even a certain big fat panda per strike, and every one of them aimed at him.
He raised his hands, furious, and met them!

The blasts landed on his palms, his arms, his chest, and burst. Their residue sprayed outward across the Domain in waves of obsidian gold, and where it touched, things stopped being what they had been. The river of light froze into a ribbon of crystal. The orchards went still and clear. And at the edge of the flattened ring, the residue washed over Ruination and THE Infiniverse.
Their bodies began to turn to glass!

It crept up Ruination’s legs, clear and hard, freezing her mid-step. It climbed THE Infiniverse’s coat of many colors, turning fur to frozen crystal. They roared, both of them, a sound Noah was hearing from either of them for the first time, and the glass cracked across their arms as they fought it, and kept climbing.
|Source of this Judgment: ???.|
|A portion of existence objects to your becoming.|
|You were never meant to find this road.|
|Return to what was counted.|
A portion of existence, then. Some part of it, old and obsidian and gold, reaching down through the crack in his own Domain to stop him from becoming what he was becoming. Who? What?
The blasts kept coming.
And Noah began to take them.

He felt it happen the moment he understood it. Every blast that landed on him was a Provenance. Ending, Order, Stillness, the Counted, each one a piece of existence’s own foundation, raw and pure and pouring down on him without end. THE One Foundation kept every ounce of their weight and built it into floor. His Hunger refined them as they struck, breaking them down without waste.Every judgment existence threw at him, he swallowed, and every one he swallowed made the transformation burn hotter!
|Warning: the Judgment is being consumed.|
|Provenance of Ending: integrated.|
|Provenance of Order: integrated.|
|Provenance of Stillness: integrated.|
|Your evolution is accelerating.|

The crack in the sky widened. Faster and heavier the blasts came, the obsidian gold pouring down in torrents now, enough to bury many things, while the glass crept up Ruination’s chest and THE Infiniverse’s throat, and the whole Domain groaned under it.
Noah threw his head back and bellowed.
"This is my Domain!"
His voice tore through the falling light.
"MY DOMAIN! MOVE!"
BOOM!
Dream erupted out of him!

Boundless waves of it, blue and gold and infinite, roaring up from his body in every direction at once. They hit the falling Provenances and swallowed them, and washed the residue away, and swept over Ruination and THE Infiniverse, and the glass on their bodies dreamed itself back into flesh and fur and crimson coat. And then they rose to the crack in the sky, and closed it.
The crack sealed shut with a sound like a great door slamming!
The last obsidian gold light vanished, and the Domain went quiet. His dream-seas settled over every hill and river, closed off from everything above, his and his alone.
He had withstood it.
|The Judgment has been withstood.|
|Your Domain has been sealed from within.|
|The three roads have joined.|
|Evolution: THE Osmontian, THE Dreaming Human Origin.|
|Human. Dreamer. Sovereign. All three, and more.|
Then his existence shook one final time, and Noah fell asleep!
He went down into the dream like a man sinking into deep water, slow, and easy, and complete.

Around him, everything that had ever made him rose. His Provenance came first, blue and gold, wrapping around him in long slow bands. Then his Dream, soft and endless, layer over layer, and his Infinity winding through both, the finite and the infinite at once, and through all of it, the Long Night’s cold he had carried, and the Provenances of existence he had just devoured. Every memory, every life he had lived, every death, all of it wrapped around him, tighter and tighter, until he hung in the center of the Domain inside a cocoon of everything he had ever been, and began to change.
The Domain changed with him!

Its blue-gold hills rose and rolled into new shapes, valleys deepening, ridges sharpening. The frozen river thawed and ran again, wider now, brighter, its star-pools multiplying until they spread like a second sky along its bed. Orchards bloomed with fruit that glowed.

Overhead, a single unmoving star above the Domain split into many, then hundreds, a whole new heaven of stars opening across a sky that had once held only one. Time ran differently along the edges of the Domain now, slower in some places, faster in others, a living hour breathing in and out.
Ruination and THE Infiniverse stood where his dream had freed them, and watched.
And they felt it.
A suffocation, rising out of the cocoon at the center of the Domain, so heavy and so total that the air turned thick in their throats. It pressed on them. More than the Warden’s gaze!
Oh!
And it made them happy!
Ruination’s crimson beams trembled. THE Infiniverse pressed a hand to her chest. They looked at each other, and then at the cocoon, and something lit in both their faces that was very close to joy.
Was their Master truly this strong?!
HUUM!
The cocoon opened.
It came apart slowly, bands of Provenance unwinding, Dream peeling away layer by layer, and the figure inside floated free.
He was tall. Taller than before, and leaner in some places and broader in others, his proportions shifted just past what a human body could have held.

His skin was the deep dark of a sky at night, and beneath it, slow-drifting rivers of blue-gold light moved like constellations wheeling across that sky, so that looking at him felt like looking up on a clear night far from any city. His hair hung weightless around his head, long and white-gold, drifting as though he stood underwaterr.

The crown of light had become part of him: two great curving horns of blue-gold radiance swept back from his brow, rooted in his skull. Behind his shoulders, faint and half-real, a slow ring of light turned, a halo made of time, ticking.
He was almost alien. He was also, unmistakably, grand.
Noah opened his eyes.
They were pure gold. Every part of them, white and iris alike, a single unbroken gold, with no pupils at all. They shone softly in the dark of his face, calm and bottomless and very old.
He looked down at himself.
|Evolution complete.|
|Lifeform: THE Osmontian, THE Dreaming Human Origin.|
|The first of its kind. A lifeform that exists by its own design, apart from Immensity and beyond the bounds of a Root.|
|Evolution count: 1.|
|From the Human: your emotions generate without end. Those you hold dear grow as you grow. You keep the capacity to fear, to love, to be wrong, and to learn; all of it is now infinite.|
|From the Dreamer: what you dream near you becomes true, and the reach of that truth grows as you grow. Existence near you dreams, and you hold the dream.|
|From the Sovereign: you devour without end and grow from all you devour. There is no ceiling on what you may consume or become.|
|And more: the Provenances of Ending, Order, and Stillness, taken from the Judgment, are now your own.|
|VERITAS: Uncounted. PROVENANCE: Uncounted. POTENTIA: Infinite. PONDUS: Uncounted. OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: Uncounted.|
|Existence no longer measures you in numbers it can write.|
|Eyes: THE Gold Without Pupils. You see a thing as it truly is, all of it at once.|
|Next evolution: Saturation 0%. The Absolute of your new existence is beyond present estimate.|
|Immensity: ???|
Noah read it all.
Then he read the last line again.
Immensity. A string of question marks, where every other line had an answer.
He had taken a different road, leaving Immensity ungrasped, its door unpassed, its thrones to others. Walking away from all of it, he had become something that door had no power to stop.
So what was he now?
He looked up through his new gold eyes at the sealed sky of his Domain, and wondered, compared to the Immense Ones out there in the storm, exactly what he had become!
