chapters.title: Chapter 5821: Kin! I
paragraphs: Noah touched his chest.
He did it without thinking, as a man touches the place where something has changed inside him, and the moment his fingers rested over the center of himself, he felt it.
A tree!

It stood inside his existence, where his Root had always been, grown past anything a Root could be. A trunk of blue-gold light rose up out of the deepest place in him, broad and straight and huming, and it went up. And up!

And up, past the reach of his gold eyes and his Dream and his Infinity, climbing into an endless height he could sense, its end somewhere far beyond his sight. Branches waited in the dark above. A canopy, perhaps. He could feel the weight of it hanging up there.
Only the very base of the trunk was glowing!
He had lit it. Barely! A thin band of blue-gold light around the bottom of a tree that went on forever, and everything above that band dark, waiting.

THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin had become this. His Root, the spinning mobius he had carried since the Convocation, had taken everything poured into it, every Quintessential ECG, every Kryos, a dead Immense One and grown into something measured by a different scale entirely.
He stood very still with his hand on his chest, and the prompts came.
|THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin has grown.|
|It is now THE Budding Dreaming Human Origin Tree.|
|Your evolution has lit its First Ring. The trunk above waits in the dark.|
Then the Tree laid its workings open to him, one by one!
|The Tree has unlocked your Core Weaving of THE Feast That Seals. Its details are below.|

|Predation. Devour grand beings, and your Tree drinks them. What it drinks rises through the trunk as Sap. The Tree remembers the nature of all it drinks, and may grant you an Ability, a Provenance, or an Authority born of that nature. The grander the meal, the richer the Sap and the greater the yield.|

|Auto-Fusion. Whatever the Tree holds of a kind will fuse on its own into something higher. Abilities with Abilities. Provenances with Provenances. Authorities with Authorities. And, where their natures agree, across all three.|
|Giving. What you give with thought returns through THE Tide, and what returns feeds the Tree.|
|Judgment. Grow beyond what existence allows, and existence will judge you. Survive grand Judgments of your existence, and the Tree grows a Branch. Every Branch bears a Seal or an Unsealing.|
|Kin. Those you mark with your blood, or name as your own or grant kinship in unique ways, rise when your Tree rises.|
|Rings lit: 1.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 0%.|
|When the Sap reaches the First Bough, your Tree will flower, and you will advance.|
|Judgment Debt: 1. Existence will remember.|

Noah almost laughed. He had devoured a dead Immense One and an Ergosphere and survived a Judgment from existence itself, and evolved into a lifeform no record held a name for, and the Tree looked down at him from its endless height and showed him one lit ring and an empty measure of Sap.
Fair enough. He had barely lit the base!
Then the last prompt came, larger than the others!
|Your Tree has grown its first Branch.|
|You devoured the Provenances of Ending, Order, and Stillness while existence struck you with them. They were the substance of the Severing. Your Tree has drunk them.|
|THE First Unsealing: THE Door of Immensity.|
|You may open the closed door for a being who holds a Root.|
|When they reach for Immensity, the Severing will come for them. You may stand within it beside them, and hold their Root together while it tries to cut them apart.|
|If they endure, they may establish their Immensity.|
|Existence will judge every such attempt. You must fight that Judgment each time.|
|Each attempt adds to your Judgment Debt.|
Noah went still!

Low on the trunk of the endless tree inside him, just above the thin lit band at its base, he felt it. A single Branch, newly grown, reaching out from the blue-gold wood, heavy with something that hummed in the same pitch as the closed door at the top of his old existence.
Behind him, Ruination’s crimson beams had locked onto the prompt and stopped scrolling. THE Infiniverse had taken a single step forward.
He read it again.

Minerva, on the Plain of Accord, reaching for Immensity with everything she had. The door shutting in her face. Her Root splitting down the middle with a sound like a great tree breaking, green light pouring out of her like blood, while a stranger’s voice spoke through her mouth and swore no new Immensity would rise.
He could have stood beside her in that!
He could have held her Root together while the Severing tried to cut it apart, and fought whatever came down from above, and given her a chance to stand up on the other side of the door.
His thoughts ran, fast and clear.

Thalia, with her Root of genome alteration, who could unmake and rebuild the code of anything she touched. Emotive, with a Physical Root of Emotion and a singularity of failed Immensity in her hands. Ling, who was a Root from her skin to her core. Every one of his people with Kryos sitting in their dreams right now, slowly seeding Roots of their own.
Every one of them, someday, might reach for the door.
And when they did, he could reach with them. They were Kin. When they rose, his Tree would rise with them.
Oh!
Noah breathed out slowly, his hand still resting over the endless tree in his chest.
Then he smiled!
It was a small smile, and a far from gentle one.
Noah looked at the line about Kin again.
Those you mark with your blood, or name as your own...

His Tree had risen. He could feel it inside him, the endless blue-gold trunk with its single lit ring and its first Branch humming in the dark. He had been dreamed into a new lifeform, devoured an Immense One, survived the Judgment of existence itself.
And around him, everything sat exactly as before.
Ruination stood where she had stood. THE Infiniverse stood beside her. Far away in THE Infiniverse, the Dream Engine hummed on as it always had, his people sleeping and dreaming on the golden shore.
His hand closed into a fist!
Instead of waiting for the Tree, he dreamed it.

He dreamed his family rising. All of them, every life he held dear, every person sleeping in the Dream Engine with a Kryos seeded in their dreams, every one of them climbing with him as the Tree had promised. He poured that dream down into the trunk inside his chest with everything he had, and the whole Domain trembled with it.
"I have had my transformation," Noah said.
His voice was low, and very hard.
"It is my dream to elevate my family alongside me. So why hasn’t it begun?"
The Tree answered!
|Kin recognized.|
|Your Dream has been heard. THE Feast That Seals carries it down every thread that binds you to your own.|
|Kin Evolution has begun.|
Light bloomed behind him!

Hazy cocoons of blue and gold were rising arround Ruination and THE Infiniverse, soft and shining, wrapping them in slow bands of light. Ruination’s crimson beams flickered and went quiet as the haze closed over her face. THE Infiniverse’s coat of many colors vanished into the gold. Both of them welcomed it. Both of them turned their eyes to Noah as the cocoons sealed shut, and the last thing he saw of their faces before the light swallowed them was joy.
And across THE Infiniverse, the Dream Engine began to glow!

He felt it through the threads. His people, dreaming on the golden shore, every one of them carrying a Kryos he had sent into their dreams. One after another, the light found them. His mother, sleeping beneath her blankets, wrapped in a cocoon of soft blue. Seo-yeon, curled small, glowing gold. Henry. Adelaide. Barbatos, deep in her necropolis with the Warden’s corpse beside her, cocooned in green-tinged gold while her raised dead stood around her in silent watch.
Eon. Naldine. Ul’moreth. Thalia.
And Emotive!
Her cocoon was the brightest of all!

It rose around her in the reimagined Earliest Folds, among the broken statues of him she still had yet to let him fix, and it shone in every color. Every color there was, shifting and burning at once, crimson rage and violet longing and gold joy and a deep, endless, bottomless blue of grief, all of it pouring out of her in waves as the cocoon closed.

Her Physical Root of Emotion drank in the Kin light, and the Stillborn Singularity she still held against her chest flickered in answer, there and gone and there. Her whole dream shook with the weight of what she fellt. The towers of THE Loom bent toward her. The statues of him turned their stone heads!
She was laughing as the cocoon closed. Laughing, and crying!
His fist slowly opened.
Far below, on the frozen plain at the edge of the northern rift of THE Undersnow, Ling had kept her eyes on him the whole time.
She hung in the dark beside the body of Noah that had stayed in THE Undersnow, the body that had fought the Warden and lain on its chest and taken its Dream. And she had watched that body change.

It had happened while he stood still. His diamond-jade skin had darkened to the deep black of a sky at night, constellations of blue-gold drifting slow beneath it. His hair had gone white-gold and weightless. Two great horns of radiance had swept back from his brow, rooted in his skull, and a faint ring of light had begun turning behind his shoulders. And when he had opened his eyes, they had been gold. Pure gold, all the way through, empty of pupils.
Ling had gone very quiet, watching! Her hands rested on her knees. Her mouth was a little open.
Then her existence pulsed!
It came from the very center of her, from the Root that was her whole being, a single deep throb that shook her from her skin to her core. She gasped. Her hand flew to her chest.
And in front of Noah’s gold eyes, the prompts rose.
|Among your Kin, only one has a foundation already established and ready to take a step toward Immensity.|
|Ling has been loosely designated as part of your Kin, due to your seed that remains within her.|
|Her existence is already saturated.|
|Her own evolution is beginning.|

sentences.text: Noah touched his chest.
He did it without thinking, as a man touches the place where something has changed inside him, and the moment his fingers rested over the center of himself, he felt it.
A tree!
It stood inside his existence, where his Root had always been, grown past anything a Root could be.
A trunk of blue-gold light rose up out of the deepest place in him, broad and straight and huming, and it went up.
And up!
And up, past the reach of his gold eyes and his Dream and his Infinity, climbing into an endless height he could sense, its end somewhere far beyond his sight.
Branches waited in the dark above.
A canopy, perhaps.
He could feel the weight of it hanging up there.
Only the very base of the trunk was glowing!
He had lit it.
Barely!
A thin band of blue-gold light around the bottom of a tree that went on forever, and everything above that band dark, waiting.
THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin had become this.

His Root, the spinning mobius he had carried since the Convocation, had taken everything poured into it, every Quintessential ECG, every Kryos, a dead Immense One and grown into something measured by a different scale entirely.
He stood very still with his hand on his chest, and the prompts came.
|THE Osmontian Chorionic Gonadotropin has grown.|
|It is now THE Budding Dreaming Human Origin Tree.|
|Your evolution has lit its First Ring.
The trunk above waits in the dark.|
Then the Tree laid its workings open to him, one by one!
|The Tree has unlocked your Core Weaving of THE Feast That Seals.
Its details are below.|
|Predation.
Devour grand beings, and your Tree drinks them.
What it drinks rises through the trunk as Sap.
The Tree remembers the nature of all it drinks, and may grant you an Ability, a Provenance, or an Authority born of that nature.
The grander the meal, the richer the Sap and the greater the yield.|
|Auto-Fusion.
Whatever the Tree holds of a kind will fuse on its own into something higher.
Abilities with Abilities.
Provenances with Provenances.
Authorities with Authorities.
And, where their natures agree, across all three.|
|Giving.
What you give with thought returns through THE Tide, and what returns feeds the Tree.|
|Judgment.
Grow beyond what existence allows, and existence will judge you.
Survive grand Judgments of your existence, and the Tree grows a Branch.
Every Branch bears a Seal or an Unsealing.|
|Kin.
Those you mark with your blood, or name as your own or grant kinship in unique ways, rise when your Tree rises.|
|Rings lit: 1.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 0%.|
|When the Sap reaches the First Bough, your Tree will flower, and you will advance.|
|Judgment Debt: 1.
Existence will remember.|
Noah almost laughed.

He had devoured a dead Immense One and an Ergosphere and survived a Judgment from existence itself, and evolved into a lifeform no record held a name for, and the Tree looked down at him from its endless height and showed him one lit ring and an empty measure of Sap.
Fair enough.
He had barely lit the base!
Then the last prompt came, larger than the others!
|Your Tree has grown its first Branch.|
|You devoured the Provenances of Ending, Order, and Stillness while existence struck you with them.
They were the substance of the Severing.
Your Tree has drunk them.|
|THE First Unsealing: THE Door of Immensity.|
|You may open the closed door for a being who holds a Root.|
|When they reach for Immensity, the Severing will come for them.
You may stand within it beside them, and hold their Root together while it tries to cut them apart.|
|If they endure, they may establish their Immensity.|
|Existence will judge every such attempt.
You must fight that Judgment each time.|
|Each attempt adds to your Judgment Debt.|
Noah went still!
Low on the trunk of the endless tree inside him, just above the thin lit band at its base, he felt it.
A single Branch, newly grown, reaching out from the blue-gold wood, heavy with something that hummed in the same pitch as the closed door at the top of his old existence.
Behind him, Ruination’s crimson beams had locked onto the prompt and stopped scrolling.
THE Infiniverse had taken a single step forward.
He read it again.
Minerva, on the Plain of Accord, reaching for Immensity with everything she had.
The door shutting in her face.

Her Root splitting down the middle with a sound like a great tree breaking, green light pouring out of her like blood, while a stranger’s voice spoke through her mouth and swore no new Immensity would rise.
He could have stood beside her in that!
He could have held her Root together while the Severing tried to cut it apart, and fought whatever came down from above, and given her a chance to stand up on the other side of the door.
His thoughts ran, fast and clear.
Thalia, with her Root of genome alteration, who could unmake and rebuild the code of anything she touched.
Emotive, with a Physical Root of Emotion and a singularity of failed Immensity in her hands.
Ling, who was a Root from her skin to her core.
Every one of his people with Kryos sitting in their dreams right now, slowly seeding Roots of their own.
Every one of them, someday, might reach for the door.
And when they did, he could reach with them.
They were Kin.
When they rose, his Tree would rise with them.
Oh!
Noah breathed out slowly, his hand still resting over the endless tree in his chest.
Then he smiled!
It was a small smile, and a far from gentle one.
Noah looked at the line about Kin again.
Those you mark with your blood, or name as your own...
His Tree had risen.
He could feel it inside him, the endless blue-gold trunk with its single lit ring and its first Branch humming in the dark.
He had been dreamed into a new lifeform, devoured an Immense One, survived the Judgment of existence itself.
And around him, everything sat exactly as before.
Ruination stood where she had stood.
THE Infiniverse stood beside her.
Far away in THE Infiniverse, the Dream Engine hummed on as it always had, his people sleeping and dreaming on the golden shore.
His hand closed into a fist!
Instead of waiting for the Tree, he dreamed it.
He dreamed his family rising.
All of them, every life he held dear, every person sleeping in the Dream Engine with a Kryos seeded in their dreams, every one of them climbing with him as the Tree had promised.
He poured that dream down into the trunk inside his chest with everything he had, and the whole Domain trembled with it.
"I have had my transformation," Noah said.
His voice was low, and very hard.
"It is my dream to elevate my family alongside me.
So why hasn’t it begun?"
The Tree answered!
|Kin recognized.|
|Your Dream has been heard.
THE Feast That Seals carries it down every thread that binds you to your own.|
|Kin Evolution has begun.|
Light bloomed behind him!
Hazy cocoons of blue and gold were rising arround Ruination and THE Infiniverse, soft and shining, wrapping them in slow bands of light.
Ruination’s crimson beams flickered and went quiet as the haze closed over her face.
THE Infiniverse’s coat of many colors vanished into the gold.
Both of them welcomed it.
Both of them turned their eyes to Noah as the cocoons sealed shut, and the last thing he saw of their faces before the light swallowed them was joy.
And across THE Infiniverse, the Dream Engine began to glow!
He felt it through the threads.
His people, dreaming on the golden shore, every one of them carrying a Kryos he had sent into their dreams.
One after another, the light found them.
His mother, sleeping beneath her blankets, wrapped in a cocoon of soft blue.
Seo-yeon, curled small, glowing gold.
Henry.
Adelaide.
Barbatos, deep in her necropolis with the Warden’s corpse beside her, cocooned in green-tinged gold while her raised dead stood around her in silent watch.
Eon.
Naldine.
Ul’moreth.
Thalia.
And Emotive!
Her cocoon was the brightest of all!
It rose around her in the reimagined Earliest Folds, among the broken statues of him she still had yet to let him fix, and it shone in every color.

Every color there was, shifting and burning at once, crimson rage and violet longing and gold joy and a deep, endless, bottomless blue of grief, all of it pouring out of her in waves as the cocoon closed.
Her Physical Root of Emotion drank in the Kin light, and the Stillborn Singularity she still held against her chest flickered in answer, there and gone and there.
Her whole dream shook with the weight of what she fellt.
The towers of THE Loom bent toward her.
The statues of him turned their stone heads!
She was laughing as the cocoon closed.
Laughing, and crying!
His fist slowly opened.
Far below, on the frozen plain at the edge of the northern rift of THE Undersnow, Ling had kept her eyes on him the whole time.
She hung in the dark beside the body of Noah that had stayed in THE Undersnow, the body that had fought the Warden and lain on its chest and taken its Dream.
And she had watched that body change.
It had happened while he stood still.
His diamond-jade skin had darkened to the deep black of a sky at night, constellations of blue-gold drifting slow beneath it.
His hair had gone white-gold and weightless.
Two great horns of radiance had swept back from his brow, rooted in his skull, and a faint ring of light had begun turning behind his shoulders.
And when he had opened his eyes, they had been gold.
Pure gold, all the way through, empty of pupils.
Ling had gone very quiet, watching!
Her hands rested on her knees.
Her mouth was a little open.
Then her existence pulsed!
It came from the very center of her, from the Root that was her whole being, a single deep throb that shook her from her skin to her core.
She gasped.
Her hand flew to her chest.
And in front of Noah’s gold eyes, the prompts rose.
|Among your Kin, only one has a foundation already established and ready to take a step toward Immensity.|
|Ling has been loosely designated as part of your Kin, due to your seed that remains within her.|
|Her existence is already saturated.|
|Her own evolution is beginning.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5822: Kin! II
paragraphs: Ling’s hand was still pressed to her chest when her existence began to reach.

All of her, every part of the Root that was her whole being, had begun to stretch upward, toward something far above both of them in the frozen dark. Threads of her lifted off her skin, pale and shining, rising like steam off warm water in wintter. Her ribbons, long lost in the battles, seemed to drift back into being around her wrists out of nothing. The air around her went thin and bright and very cold.
She was reaching for Immensity.
And she knew it!

Her face went white. She clutched at her chest with both hands as though she could hold herself down, and the threads kept rising regardless, pulling at her, drawing her upward toward the door she had watched slam shut on the Plain of Accord.
In a rush of half-sentences, she told him what she was feeling. Terror, first!

The door was shut. Everyone knew it was shut. She had watched Minerva’s Root break in half on the snow, watched the green light pour out of her like blood. And now her own existence was reaching for that same door, by itself, without asking her, and she was helpless to stop it!
"I’m not doing this," Ling said. Her voice was heavy! "I’m not, it’s just, it’s going on its own, and if it reaches the door I’m going to, I’ll be just like her, I’ll be..."
Noah floated down to her.
He put a hand on her shoulder. His fingers rested on the blue silk, and through them she could feel the weight of him.
"It’s okay," he said.
She stared at him.
"Your existence is reaching because it is ready. Reach. When the door comes for you, I will be standing in it with you."
She looked at him for a long, trembling moment.
Then the fear in them changed.
It hardened. Her hands came away from her chest and closed into fists, and her powerful thighs coiled under her, and her whole body began to hum!
WUU!
"Fine," Ling said.
She threw back her head and roared.
"Fine! FINE! You want to cut me apart? You want to tell me no? Fuck you! Fuck the door, fuck the cold, fuck every voice that ever said no new Immensity! Come and get me, then!"
BOOM!
And she gathered herself!

Every thread of her that had been drifting upward, she took hold of. She pulled them in, wound them tight, drew every scrap of her existence into a single burning point at the center of her body, and then she flung it all upward at once. Toward Immensity. Toward everything that had been shut against her.
The Basal Floor went white!
Far above them, in the frozen dark, a hazy door appeared.
It hung above Ling, vast and pale and sealed, and as she reached for it, the cold came down.

It fell from the door like a blade of blue-white winter, long and thin and absolute, the same color as the eyes that had looked out of Minerva’s face. It came down straight toward the center of Ling’s Root, meaning to split her in two, exactly as it had split the Progeny on the Plain of Accord.
Noah rose to meet it.
The Branch on his Tree hummed!
|THE First Unsealing: THE Door of Immensity.|
|A Kin reaches for Immensity. You may stand within the Severing beside her.|
He stood above Ling, between her and the falling blade, and opened his hand.
The Severing struck his palm!

It cut. It was made to cut Roots, and it found the Tree that stood where his Root had been, and it bit into him like the edge of the whole Long Night at once. Pain went through him from his hand to his core. His skin split along his palm and blue-gold light poured out. But his hand held its place, and the blade stayed above Ling.

Below him, she kept reaching. Her existence was climbing, burning, pulling upward toward the door, and the Severing kept trying to find a way past him to her Root, and every time it slid, he moved, and every time it pressed, he held.
He reached down with his other hand, past the blade, and laid it over the center of her Root.
He held it together.

The Severing pressed down on her Root through his hand, trying to find the seam that would let it split her, and he gave it none. His Dream poured into her Root and wrapped it, held it, pressed every part of it close, until the only thing left for the blade to cut was him!
And then the Judgment came!
Obsidian gold. It tore open the sky above the door, the same cold old light that had crashed into his Domain, and it fell on him with all its weight.
|HOW DARE YOU.|

It landed on his shoulders like a mountain range. His knees bent. His crown of radiance flared. The obsidian gold pressed down on him from above while the Severing pressed up against his palm from below, and between the two of them, his whole existence groaned.
It smashed down with the same Provenances he had devoured before!
He held on!
Below his hands, Ling reached the door.
It opened in silence!
And Noah did something new under the whole of existence. He let her go through it inside his Dream.

Blue-gold light poured down out of his hand into the center of her, out of the endless Tree in his chest, out of every dream he had ever dreamed. Its source was him; the door merely stood open above them. Ling passed through it wrapped entirely in his Dream, and on the other side of it, what took shape in her was something the door had given no one before her.
Immensity, dreamed.

It came into her slowly, solemnly, like something sacred being set into place. Her Root, already her whole existence, began to unfurl. It grew in depth rather than size. Layer upon layer of her opened, each one revealing another beneath it, and each layer filled with blue-gold dream and kept it.

Threads ran from the deepest of those layers up into Noah’s hand, and through his hand to the Tree in his chest, binding her new Immensity to the place it had been dreamed from. Her existence stretched outward from the small round-faced girl in blue silk into something vast, something that pressed against the frozen dark of the Basal Floor and kept pressing, until the dark gave way.
She rose.

Her silk dress darkened into the deep blue of the sky at dusk, embroidered now with burning lines of light in place of gold thread, lines that ran and shifted across it. Loose from its buns, her hair spread around her in a great dark cloud, and through it wound ribbons of white flame, long and slow and living. Her powerful legs blazed with blue-gold dream-light from hip to heel, every line of muscle lit from within, so bright they were hard to look at. Behind her, purple fire bloomed, the same deep violet as the torches in her father’s cavern, wreathing her shoulders in a slow, steady burn.
And her eyes opened.
They were white. Pure white, all the way through, without a pupil anywhere in them. Exactly like her father’s.
The Severing shattered against Noah’s palm!

It broke into a thousand blue-white shards and faded into nothing. Above him, the obsidian gold Judgment shuddered, and pressed down one last time, and withdrew into the sky, and the sky closed behind it.
|The Severing has been withstood.|
|The Judgment has been withstood.|
|Judgment Debt: 2. Existence will remember.|
|Kin Evolution: Ling has established a Dream Immensity.|
|A Dream Immensity is formed within your Dream, and rooted in it. It is Immensity, true and whole, yet it answers to the Dream that bore it rather than to the door.|
|It grows as your Tree grows. Its threads are bound to you.|
|Your Tree drinks from the rising of its Kin.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 14%.|
The door above them faded. The Basal Floor’s frozen dark rushed back in around them, and Ling hung in the middle of it, vast and shining, her white eyes fixed on Noah.
She spoke, and existence carried it.
|I am THE Dancer in the Boundless Dream.|
|I am lucky enough to attain Immensity when I had absolutely no reason to.|
|I am...grateful.|
A pause, and her white eyes narrowed with something very like her old cheerful grin.
|So let me thank you properly, Big Boy.|
She moved!

With no wind-up at all, one moment she hung before him, and the next her leg was already swinging, thick and powerful and blazing with dreamed Immensity, coming at him with the whole weight of something newly risen behind it!
Noah raised his hand.
That was all. One open hand, lifted calmly into the path of her kick.
Boundless dream unfurled from it!

Blue-gold light poured out of his palm in an endless tide, wave after wave of it, soft and infinite, rolling out to meet her leg. Her Immensity crashed into it. And the dream took it. All of it. The whole weight of a kick carrying Dream Immensity, absorbed into a tide of dream with no far wall, held in his single open hand.
Her leg stopped a hand’s width from his palm.
The force of it went on.
BOOOOM!

Out around them it went, in every direction at once, a ring of pure released Immensity tearing out across the Basal Floor, and everything it touched broke. Floating islands cracked in half and spun away. Torn Dimensions shattered like dropped glass. The jammed frozen plain around the northern rift split into a thousand peices and fell apart into the dark, and the cold-filled trees snapped and toppled, and the crack ran on and on, out past anything One’s eyes could follow, until half of the Basal Floor lay in ruin around them, broken and drifting, destroyed by a single kick that had stopped short of its target.
And in the middle of all of it, Noah stood with his hand raised and his gold eyes calm, holding back the leg of a Dream Immensity with nothing but his palm and the Dream it had risen from.
Ling looked at him over her own blazing knee.
Her white eyes went wide!
Noah held his hand where it was, open in the frozen dark, Ling’s blazing leg resting a hand’s width from his palm.
He looked at it.

His hand. The same hand that had once thrown fireballs in a dilapidated city, the hand that had killed apes and bears and turtles and dragons, the hand that had grasped Beasts and Demons and Celestials!

The hand that had shaken under the weight of a stone in a dead domain, that had held a dying Steed’s haed and pressed a cure into an ancient line of script. Night-dark now, constellations drifting under the skin, a split still healing across the palm where the Severing had bitten him.
And it had just stopped the full weight of an Immensity!
Something rose in his chest!

It came up from the part of him the evolution had kept human and made infinite. It was warm, and loud, and it shook, far removed from the cold, far-away clarity of the infinite dream where every path was already walked.
He had done it!

All those years. The apocalypses, and the fear, and the first clumsy skills. Every time he had looked up at something vast and known in his bones that it could end him with a glance. Every time he had told himself he would get there, someday, somehow.
Today, an Immense One had kicked him with everything she had.
And he had stopped it with one hand!

His eyes stung. He had gold eyes now, pupil-less, eyes that saw everything as it truly was, and they were burning at the edges like any man’s. His throat had gone tight. He was laughing, a little, under his breath! He felt like he was laughing and crying at the emotions infinitely stretching across him!
So this was it. The human side of what he had become. The part that would always feel everything, infinitely.
It felt like this as it was glorious!
Ling was still staring at him over her knee, white eyes wide.
Noah let the feeling run all the way through him. He let it rise and rise until it filled him from his crown to his heels.
Then he moved!
His hand left her leg and came up, and came down. Straight down, swung like a hammer, toward the center of Ling’s forehead!
It was fast. So fast that the frozen dark between them seemed to skip. And it carried something with it, riding on the edge of the swing, a dream he was dreaming for the first time: extinction.
Ending without remainder, without return, the dream of a thing simply ceasing to have ever been.
Ling’s entire existence buzzed!
Her new Dream Immensity screamed alarm through every layer of her at once, and her white eyes flew wider, and her body was still deciding which way to move when the hand arrived.
It stopped!

A finger’s breadth from her forehead, his palm hung perfectly still. The dream of extinction riding on it went quiet and drew back into him, tucked away, gone. The wind of the swing caught up a moment later and blew her hair back from her face in one great dark rush.
She forgot to breathe as only now did she begin heaving as if she had escaped death.
For a long moment, both of them stayed perfectly still. She stared at his hand. He stared at her face. Her lips had parted. Her white eyes were enormous.
Then his hand turned.

Slowly, gently, it moved from her forehead to the side of her face, and rested there, his palm warm against her cheek, his thumb under the curve of her jaw. She leaned into it before she seemed to know she was doign it.
He pulled her in, and kissed her!

Ling made a small, startled sound against his mouth. Then her hands found the back of his neck and gripped hard, her fingers sinking into his weightless white-gold hair, and she kissed him back with the whole fierce, cheerful, foul-mouthed force of her, a newly risen Dream Immensity wrapped around him in the ruins of half the Basal Floor.
Golden clouds bloomed around them.

They rose out of Noah on their own, soft and thick and shining, rolling up over the two of them and closing like curtains around a bed. The ruined islands vanished, and the drifting shards of shattered Dimensions, and the frozen dark. There was only gold, and warmth, and the two of them inside it.
His human side wanted much more for the sake of...research.
He let it have its way!

|Kin Evolution: Ling has established a Dream Immensity.|
|A Dream Immensity is formed within your Dream, and rooted in it.
It is Immensity, true and whole, yet it answers to the Dream that bore it rather than to the door.|
|It grows as your Tree grows.
Its threads are bound to you.|
|Your Tree drinks from the rising of its Kin.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 14%.|
The door above them faded.
The Basal Floor’s frozen dark rushed back in around them, and Ling hung in the middle of it, vast and shining, her white eyes fixed on Noah.
She spoke, and existence carried it.
|I am THE Dancer in the Boundless Dream.|
|I am lucky enough to attain Immensity when I had absolutely no reason to.|
|I am...grateful.|
A pause, and her white eyes narrowed with something very like her old cheerful grin.
|So let me thank you properly, Big Boy.|
She moved!

With no wind-up at all, one moment she hung before him, and the next her leg was already swinging, thick and powerful and blazing with dreamed Immensity, coming at him with the whole weight of something newly risen behind it!
Noah raised his hand.
That was all.
One open hand, lifted calmly into the path of her kick.
Boundless dream unfurled from it!
Blue-gold light poured out of his palm in an endless tide, wave after wave of it, soft and infinite, rolling out to meet her leg.
Her Immensity crashed into it.
And the dream took it.
All of it.
The whole weight of a kick carrying Dream Immensity, absorbed into a tide of dream with no far wall, held in his single open hand.
Her leg stopped a hand’s width from his palm.
The force of it went on.
BOOOOM!
Out around them it went, in every direction at once, a ring of pure released Immensity tearing out across the Basal Floor, and everything it touched broke.
Floating islands cracked in half and spun away.
Torn Dimensions shattered like dropped glass.

The jammed frozen plain around the northern rift split into a thousand peices and fell apart into the dark, and the cold-filled trees snapped and toppled, and the crack ran on and on, out past anything One’s eyes could follow, until half of the Basal Floor lay in ruin around them, broken and drifting, destroyed by a single kick that had stopped short of its target.
And in the middle of all of it, Noah stood with his hand raised and his gold eyes calm, holding back the leg of a Dream Immensity with nothing but his palm and the Dream it had risen from.
Ling looked at him over her own blazing knee.
Her white eyes went wide!
Noah held his hand where it was, open in the frozen dark, Ling’s blazing leg resting a hand’s width from his palm.
He looked at it.
His hand.
The same hand that had once thrown fireballs in a dilapidated city, the hand that had killed apes and bears and turtles and dragons, the hand that had grasped Beasts and Demons and Celestials!
The hand that had shaken under the weight of a stone in a dead domain, that had held a dying Steed’s haed and pressed a cure into an ancient line of script.
Night-dark now, constellations drifting under the skin, a split still healing across the palm where the Severing had bitten him.
And it had just stopped the full weight of an Immensity!
Something rose in his chest!
It came up from the part of him the evolution had kept human and made infinite.
It was warm, and loud, and it shook, far removed from the cold, far-away clarity of the infinite dream where every path was already walked.
He had done it!
All those years.
The apocalypses, and the fear, and the first clumsy skills.
Every time he had looked up at something vast and known in his bones that it could end him with a glance.
Every time he had told himself he would get there, someday, somehow.
Today, an Immense One had kicked him with everything she had.
And he had stopped it with one hand!
His eyes stung.
He had gold eyes now, pupil-less, eyes that saw everything as it truly was, and they were burning at the edges like any man’s.
His throat had gone tight.
He was laughing, a little, under his breath!
He felt like he was laughing and crying at the emotions infinitely stretching across him!
So this was it.
The human side of what he had become.
The part that would always feel everything, infinitely.
It felt like this as it was glorious!
Ling was still staring at him over her knee, white eyes wide.
Noah let the feeling run all the way through him.
He let it rise and rise until it filled him from his crown to his heels.
Then he moved!
His hand left her leg and came up, and came down.
Straight down, swung like a hammer, toward the center of Ling’s forehead!
It was fast.
So fast that the frozen dark between them seemed to skip.
And it carried something with it, riding on the edge of the swing, a dream he was dreaming for the first time: extinction.
Ending without remainder, without return, the dream of a thing simply ceasing to have ever been.
Ling’s entire existence buzzed!
Her new Dream Immensity screamed alarm through every layer of her at once, and her white eyes flew wider, and her body was still deciding which way to move when the hand arrived.
It stopped!
A finger’s breadth from her forehead, his palm hung perfectly still.
The dream of extinction riding on it went quiet and drew back into him, tucked away, gone.
The wind of the swing caught up a moment later and blew her hair back from her face in one great dark rush.
She forgot to breathe as only now did she begin heaving as if she had escaped death.
For a long moment, both of them stayed perfectly still.
She stared at his hand.
He stared at her face.
Her lips had parted.
Her white eyes were enormous.
Then his hand turned.
Slowly, gently, it moved from her forehead to the side of her face, and rested there, his palm warm against her cheek, his thumb under the curve of her jaw.
She leaned into it before she seemed to know she was doign it.
He pulled her in, and kissed her!
Ling made a small, startled sound against his mouth.

Then her hands found the back of his neck and gripped hard, her fingers sinking into his weightless white-gold hair, and she kissed him back with the whole fierce, cheerful, foul-mouthed force of her, a newly risen Dream Immensity wrapped around him in the ruins of half the Basal Floor.
Golden clouds bloomed around them.
They rose out of Noah on their own, soft and thick and shining, rolling up over the two of them and closing like curtains around a bed.
The ruined islands vanished, and the drifting shards of shattered Dimensions, and the frozen dark.
There was only gold, and warmth, and the two of them inside it.
His human side wanted much more for the sake of...research.
He let it have its way!

chapters.title: Chapter 5823: Immensity! I
paragraphs: The golden clouds thinned a long while later, and the frozen dark of the Basal Floor came back in pieces.
Noah lay on his back on a drift of dream with Ling asleep against his chest, her dark hair spread across both of them, one blazing leg hooked over his.
He might have been a bit...relentless.

Above them, half of a destroyed Floor drifted in silence. Islands split down their middles turned slowly in the cold. Shards of shattered Dimensions hung like broken windows, each one still holding a sliver of whatever sky it had once looked out on. Snow fell through all of it, unhurrid, as though nothing at all had happened here.
The Tree in his chest hummed.

He listened to it for a while. One lit ring at the base of an endless trunk. A single Branch with the Unsealing hanging from it. Sap sitting low in the wood, waiting. He had evolved into a lifeform no record held a name for, and he understood...only a little about what that meant.
That had to change!
So he began to test!

He started with the part of him that was human, and let himself worry, on purpose. He thought of the cocoons in the Dream Engine, of his mother and Seo-yeon and Henry sealed in light, of Emotive burning in every color with a stolen singularity against her chest. The worry rose, as worry does. And then it kept rising. It fed itself. It generated more of itself without end, and every bit of it poured into him as strength, a slow warm pressure filling his limbs.
He let it run for a full minute, then tried to set it down.
It went quiet when he asked, and stayed, a low warmth under everything.

Results showed that... his emotions were fuel, endless, a well that would keep giving forever. They would also keep speaking forever, under everything. He would have to carry every feeling he had for the rest of his existence, and carry it well.
Next, the Dreamer.

He turned his gold eyes on the nearest broken island, a slab of ice split clean in two with a frozen forest on each half, and dreamed it whole. The halves drifted together, and the crack sealed from the bottom up, ice knitting to ice, roots finding roots across the seam, until the forest stood! He stopped dreaming, and it stayed. It was simply an island again, real, as though the kick had passed it by.

He widened the dream. Ten islands came together around him. Then a hundred, a whole archipelgo of frozen land reassembling itself in the dark, cold-filled trees righting themselves, shattered Dimensions folding their broken skies back into frames for Gigaparsecs.
At the edge, the truth began to thin. The farthest islands held together, but loosely, their seams faint, as though they might remember being broken if anything struck them hard enough.
So...what he dreamed near him became true, and the reach grew with his attention. Spread it too far and the truth wore thin at the edges.
Then the Sovereign.

He opened his mouth, and the blue-gold brilliance inside it looked out onto the ruin, and he pulled. Everything that remained of the destruction came to him: Dimensional shards too broken to dream back, the lingering cold of the Warden soaked into the drifting ice, the faint residue of fifty-five Guards’ patrols still hanging in the dark like old footprints. It all streamed into the event horizons inside him and went down as he literally devoured nearly a forth of THE Basal Floor of THE Undersnow.
The Tree drank!
|Predation: residue of THE Basal Floor.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 17%.|
|Auto-Fusion: Provenance of Stillness + the lingering cold of THE Warden Who Does Not Rise.|
|Formed: Authority of the Held Breath (Minor). Whatever you hold in your gaze, you may still for a moment.|
He tried it at once. He looked at a falling snowflake and held it. It stopped in the air, perfectly still, for the space of a breath. Then it fell on.
A bit useless, but okay!
Last, his eyes.
He looked down at Ling!

The Gold Without Pupils showed her as she truly was. A girl asleep, round-faced, her lips parted. And beneath that, her Dream Immensity, deep and shining, layer on layer, every layer bound by fine bright threads that ran up out of her chest and into his Tree.
She looked like a pulsing nervous system that rapidly circulated golden pulses of Immensity as her entire body buzzed.

Deep, compared to anything he had been a day ago. Shallow, compared to the depth he could feel in the Thinker even from here, a pressure at the very edge of his senses, like the pull of a sea far below a cliff.

He checked the Kin next, through the Dream Engine. Every cocoon still closed, still glowing. Ruination and THE Infiniverse in their bands of blue-gold haze in the Root Domain. His mother in soft blue. Seo-yeon curled small in gold. And Emotive’s cocoon, brightest of all, burning every color at once, the Singularity flickering against her chest like a heartbeat.
Then the sliver he had left on the Thinker’s mountain screamed at him!

The pressure on it spiked. Through it, Noah felt the purple coat of Immensity around the mountain buckle inward, as though something enormous had leaned its whole weight against it, and the coat had bent.
Ling woke!
She opened her white eyes and looked at his face, and whatever she saw there brought her upright in an instant. She asked what was wrong.
"Some invaders into the Legacy. Something is pressing on your father’s Immensity hard enough to bend it."
She was on her feet before he finished.
Her father’s mountain was her home!
But...
"Don’t worry."
He told her calmly, his endlessly gold eyes without pupils calming her down completely!!
He gathered himself, and the Basal Floor fell away!

In the cavern, the sliver filled. It swelled from a thread of attention into the whole of him, night-dark and crowned, constellations drifting under his skin, his white-gold hair lifting off his shoulders.
Noah opened his gold eyes on the prayer mat.
Across from him, the Thinker’s great beads stopped clicking. The kneeling giant turned his weeping, pupil-less eyes toward him and regarded him for a long moment.
|"You seem a bit...different,"|the Thinker said mildly.
Noah didn’t reply to these words as he looked up through the stone of the mountain, and for the first time in his existence, he saw the Immense as they truly were.

Before, they had been hazes. Thrones on golden clouds with shapes too deep to resolve, auras that pressed and loomed and gave him nothing to hold. Now his gold eyes went through the cavern ceiling and the mountain’s peak and the torn purple coat above it, out into the sky of THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity, and the hazes were gone.
The Legacy was at war, and he could see every one of its warriors!
First, he saw Sir Moriarty!

The octopus-headed visage still hung across the sky, obsidian veined with gold, crimson eyes blazing over the walled domains. But the visage was only the part that showed. Beneath it, Noah’s eyes followed the rest of Moriarty down, and down. The great body coiled through the foundations of the Legacy itself.

Its tentacles ran through every Existential Conduit as roots run through soil, threaded under the purple-gold rivers, wrapped around the bases of the thousand mountains, braided through the snow-buried floor. Some of those tentacles were older than the mountains they held up.
The Legacy was defended by Moriarty. In places, the Legacy was Moriarty.
And all through that vast coiled body, faint and sick, ran threads of poisonous green!
Noah let his gaze move across the walled domains.

On one mountain, THE Ashen Cantor stood in a robe of grey cinders with his mouth open, singing. Each note struck a golden sphere of foreign Immensity and unwrote a piece of it, gold peeling away from the sphere in long flakes and drifting off into nothing.

On a peak to the east, THE Keeper of the Unbroken Vow stood with a chain wrapped three times around an invader, and the chain was made of oaths, every promise ever kept in the Legacy hammered link by link into iron. The invader strained against it, and every link held!

Farther off, THE Lantern of the Last Shore, a tall robed figure with no face beneath the hood, lifted a lamp whose light showed the dead where to go, and the invaders it touched turned and began to walk that way, slowly, as though they had remembered somewhere they were meant to be. And over the Firmament, THE Hollow Choir hung in a ring of hollow faces, and their silence fell on the enemies below like a crushing tide.
Every one of them was deep. Deeper than anything Noah could measure!
And every one of them was different!
He turned to the Thinker.
"Why do some burn brighter than others?"he asked.
The Thinker considered the question as though it were a stone he had been handed, turning it over between his great fingers.
|"Oh? Can you actually see Immensity at this time? Hmm...Well, what makes a well deep?"| he asked in return.
Noah waited.

|"Immensity is depth,"| THE Thinker said at last, |"not height. Everyone who first reaches it believes they have climbed. They have dug. And depth is measured in what one has carried through the Ages. A young Immensity is shallow, and loud, because it has carried little and wishes everyone to know it has carried anything at all. An old one is quiet."|
His beads clicked once. |"There is more to it than that. As the big guy said, there are levels to this."|
Noah looked back out at the war.

Now that he knew what to look for, he could see it. The invading spheres were not all alike. Some blazed and roared, gold flaring, straining loudly against their walls: young, he guessed, only a few Ages into their Immensity. Others hung almost still, dim and patient, and those seemed far too heavy.
"A war between the depths of wells," Noah said quietly.
"Each one deeper than the last. Each one sure it holds the water that matters. And I am standing at the edge of all of them with a Tree whose roots have only just reached the water."
He watched a golden sphere flake apart under the Cantor’s song."It is a strange thing, to finally see the size of the sky and know you cannot touch it yet."
The Thinker said nothing to that. But his beads went still for a moment, and then resumed.
Then Noah turned his gold eyes on his host.

For a while he had sat across from THE Thinker. He had seen the kneeling giant, the boulder beads, the weeping eyes and the fierce almost-smile and the purple torches along the walls. He had felt the depth of him at the edge of his senses, as one feels the drop beyond the edge of a cliff in the dark.
Now he saw it!

The kneeling giant was a fraction, the smallest part, a single bead on a much longer string. Behind him, the mountain was him; every stone of it carried his Immensity, every vein of ore, every torch. And behind the mountain, beneath it, around it, ran a depth that went down in every direction at onec, purple fire burning along it like torches lit at intervals down a shaft whose floor lay past any sight. Noah looked, and looked, and found no bottom.

The gash on the Thinker’s back leaked Immensity in a slow, steady river. Noah had thought of it as a wound. Through his new eyes it was a river wide enough to drown the Legacy’s largest Conduit, and it was still only the trickle escaping from a sea.
That trickle held more Immensity than multiple invading sphere in the sky combined!
Holy fucking shit.These beings were actually monsters!
Noah very nearly looked away!
|THE Thinker at the End of Existence.|
|Depth: beyond perception.|
The Thinker turned his great head and looked back at him, and the fierce line of his mouth softened, very slightly.
Then the Thinker’s gaze moved past Noah, to the mouth of the cavern, and beyond it, to the sky.
Noah followed it!

At the edge of the walled domain that held the mountain, Moriarty’s obsidian-gold mist had thinned. In one small place only. Something green was threading through it from the inside, fine and patient, a single living tendril finding its way along a seam in the wall that nobody else would have known was there. And it was coming straight at them!
The Thinker’s beads clicked once.
|"You...get to see me stretch my muscles it seems."|

chapters.title: Chapter 5824: Immensity! II
paragraphs: The green tendril reached the purple coat around the mountain, found a seam in it hidden from everyone but her, and pulled!
The coat opened like a curtain!

Snow blew in through the gap, and with the snow came the scent of spring. Wet earth, new leaves, flowers that had bloomed and fallen and bloomed again for Ages. The torches along the cavern walls leaned toward the opening, then away from it.
THE Verdant Regard stepped through!

She came as a tall figure of soft green light. The body walking into the cavern was one of several. Far away, in her ever-spring domain, the rest of her sat on a bed of moss with her daughter’s head in her lap, and this body was a branch she had sent out from that place, as a tree sends out a root toward water. Even so, its depth went down past his sight.
Green below green below green, spring after spring after spring, an Immensity built from every season that had ever ended and come back.
She knew every path in this Legacy. She had walked them as a friend for longer than most Legacies had stood.
Three more came through behind her!

The first was a woman, tall and stooped, her body corroded bronze from crown to heel, her robe a single sheet of flaking verdicts that rustled when she moved. Where she passed, the stone at the cavern’s mouth went brown and crumbled. The torchlight that touched her came away dull, aged, its color rusted out of it. She walked slowly, with the patience of something that had outlved every enemy it had ever made and expected to outlive a few more.
|THE Rusted Matriarch.|

The second was a beast. Lean and grey, the size of a range of hills pressed down into the cavern’s mouth, its shoulders hunched as it squeezed through. Its eyes were two open doorways with nothing behind them. It stopped just inside the entrance and sniffed at the air, at the walls, at the torn coat behind it, with the deep pleased interest of a hound that has found the most interesting door in existence.
|THE Hound of Thresholds.|

The third was a young man in gilded armor, handsome, golden-haired, his Immensity glittering on him like fresh gold leaf. He swept in with a smile already on his face and looked around the cavern as though he had come to inspect a property he was thinking of buying.
|THE Gilt Heir.|

Noah read them with his gold eyes, one after another. The Gilt Heir was the shallowest, and the loudest; only a few Ages deep, and still more depth than Noah could reach the bottom of. The Hound went deeper, far deeper. Deepest of the three, the Rusted Matriarch’s depth slid away from him entirely, rust on rust on rust, down into a dark beyond his following.
Then the fifth one came, and the cavern changed!

It began before he finished arriving. The purple torches along the walls flickered, and their fire turned crimson gold. The prayer mats darkened at their edges into his colors. Even the snow drifting in through the torn coat stopped in the air, every flake of it, and each one turned slowly to face the entrance.

Noah felt why. Wherever this one’s attention rested, existence began to become his, owned rather than destroyed. The torches still burned, but they burned for him now! The mats still lay on the floor, but they were his mats. He owned what he touched, and he owned a little of whatever he simply looked at.
THE Sleepless Fiend stepped into the cavern!

He came as a tall figure in dark robes, his face barely perceptible, his presence a weight that made the mountain groan. Noah could see more than that now. A great deal more. But the Fiend kept all of that turned away from him so far.
The five of them spread out around the Thinker.

The Thinker stayed on his knees. He knelt on his prayer mat exactly as he had knelt for Ages, his beads clicking slowly through his fingers, his weeping eyes half closed. Behind him, Noah sat on his own mat, his gold eyes calm.
He felt them read him!
He felt each of them look at him and see what he had let them see: a dream of a lifeform whose Root, by every account in the Legacy, had formed days ago.
The Gilt Heir laughed out loud! The Hound sniffed in his direction once and lost interest, and the Rusted Matriarch kept her eyes elsewhere entirely.
THE Sleepless Fiend smiled!
"Old friend," he said to THE Thinker.
His voice was warm. Reasonable. It was the voice of a man arriving late to dinner, sorry to have kept everyone waiting.

"It has been a very long time. I wish we were meeting over something gentler."He spread his hands."I regret the method. Truly. The coat, the Legacy, poor Moriarty. None of it was what I would have chosen. But the snow is deep, and getting deeper. The door is shut. You know what that means for all of us who still breathe. Keys must be found, and kept, and used. For the good of everyone."
His gaze settled on THE Thinker, gently.
"Step aside. Let us take the boy. You will not lose anything you cannot afford."
THE Thinker’s beads clicked once.

|"I have thought through a great many probabilities,"|he said, without opening his eyes. |"Across a great many Ages. In none of them is a gift from THE Sleepless Fiend paid for by the one who receives it."|
|"I decline."|
The Fiend sighed.
THE Verdant Regard took a step forward.
Her soft green light dimmed as she moved, and when she spoke, her voice was nothing like the Fiend’s. It was tired, and raw, and grieving.
"My daughter has not woken," she said to the Thinker. "Her Root lies frozen on the moss beside her. The snow falls on her face and I cannot keep it off."
She looked at him, and her green eyes were wet. "You have a daughter. You know. Please. Understand."
The Thinker opened his weeping eyes and looked at her for a long moment.
|"I do understand,"| he said gently. |"And I am sorry. Truly."|
His beads stilled. |"Understanding changes nothing though."|
Her face closed!
The Fiend let out a long breath, the sigh of a father over a stubborn child, and lifted one hand.
"Then," THE Sleepless Fiend said,"we will simply take the boy."
HUUM!
Five depths of Immensity rose inside the cavern at once!

They rose out of the five invaders like tides coming in from five different seas. The Gilt Heir’s gold flared bright and brash. The Hound’s grey Immensity poured out low along the floor, sniffing. Rust spread from the Matriarch in a slow brown wave, aging the air itself. The Verdant Regard’s spring rolled outward, green and overwhelming, flowers bursting from the stone wherever it touched. And the Fiend’s ownership spread from him in every direction, quiet, total, claiming everything it reached.
All five came for the Thinker, and for the man behind him.
The Thinker stayed kneeling!
He opened his great hands, and the beads left them.

They rose into the air, one after another, boulders of dark stone the size of hills, and as they rose, each one caught purple fire. They began to orbit him. Slowly at first, then faster, a ring of burning moons wheeling around a kneeling giant in the heart of his mountain.

One moon swung out and met the Rusted Matriarch’s rust. The corrosion washed against it, and the bead’s purple fire held it, rust and fire grinding against each other in a slow, endless push. Another swung out against the Gilt Heir’s gold and stopped it dead, the young lord’s Immensity flaring and straining and going nowhere. A third met the Verdant Regard’s spring, flowers blooming and withering against its burning surface. A fourth swung out to the Fiend, and the Fiend’s ownership spread across it, and the bead stayed the Thinker’s own.
Four Immense Ones. Four beads. The Thinker held all of them at once without rising from his mat.
The cavern should have collapsed!

Noah could feel the weight in it, five depths of Immensity grinding against one another in a space of stone. The mountain stood because the Thinker had decided it would stand. His weeping eyes stayed half closed. His fierce almost-smile held perfectly still.
This was what depth looked like when it chose to act!
And the Hound found the gap!
It slipped between the orbiting moons at the one instant when two of them crossed, low and grey and quick, its doorway eyes fixed on Noah. Its Immensity poured toward him in a rush.
Out of that rush, a hand formed.

Vast and grey, woven out of the Hound’s Immensity, large enough to close around a mountain. It came down over Noah where he sat on his prayer mat and wrapped around him, fingers curling, and began to close.
The pressure was beyond anything in his life!
The Warden’s half-Immensity had been heavy, flickering, half there. This was whole. Finished. Deep. The grasp of a being that had pased through the door Ages ago and carried every Age since.
It pressed on every part of him at once, and the Tree in his chest shuddred under it, and for an instant he felt how small he was inside that hand.
Then his body answered!

The constellations under his night-dark skin began to move outward. Off his chest, off his arms, off his face, drifting into the air around him, spreading until he sat inside a moving sky of his own, stars of blue and gold wheeling slowly in the space between his skin and the Hound’s closing fingers.
The halo of time behind his shoulders turned faster, ticking. His horns of radiance flared bright enough to throw shadows across the whole cavern.
And his Dreaming Origin side surged forward.
Inside the reach of his dream, things became what he dreamed them to be. And he dreamed that the hand closing on him was closing on a dream of him.
The Hound’s fingers closed, gripping, squeezing with all the weight of an established Immensity.
They were holding a sky!
Noah stood up inside it.
He lifted his own hand, slowly, laid his palm flat against the inside of the Hound’s grey fingers, and pushed.
The Immensity moved!

It moved away from him a hand’s width. Then an arm’s length. The grey fingers bent back, and opened, and the Hound’s whole Immensity slid back from him across the cavern floor like a tide going out, and Noah stood alone on his prayer mat inside his sky of drifting stars with his hand still raised.
The cavern went silent!
Every Immense One in it was looking at him.

The Gilt Heir’s smile had gone, and the Hound had frozen mid-step, its doorway eyes narrowed to slits, and the Rusted Matriarch had finally turned her head, and her rusted face held something that might have been interest. Even THE Verdant Regard had gone still, her green light flickering.
The Gilt Heir spoke first, and his voice cracked on it.
"The fuck?"
How...could something so unfathomably weak rebuff an Immensity? This was the singular question orbiting all beings here!
The Thinker’s orbiting beads paused for exactly one heartbeat.
Then they moved on!
|An Immense grasp has been rebuffed.|
|Predation: residue of an Immense One’s reach.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 20%.|
Noah lowered his hand.
His arms were trembling, he noticed. Faintly. The push had cost him: the lit ring at the base of his Tree had dimmed a shade, and it would take a few nanoseconds to burn bright again.
The enemy’s Immensity was many times more powerful than Ling!
Inside his dream, an Immense grasp became a grasp on a dream of him, and he could open it. Holding one off for long would drain him. Holding off two at once, he had no wish to test yet.
And THE Sleepless Fiend, for the first time since he had entered the cavern, turned and looked directly at him.
Every torch in the mountain burned crimson gold at once!

chapters.title: Chapter 5825: Immensity! III
paragraphs: The Fiend’s gaze rested on Noah for a long, quiet moment.
He smiled a little, and turned back to the Thinker’s burning bead, as though he had decided to save Noah for later.
The Hound had decided otherwise!

It came again, harder, and this time the Gilt Heir tore himself free of the Thinker’s bead and came with it, gold blazing, sword drawn, a young lord’s face twisted with the humiliaton of having laughed too soon. Two Immense Ones, coming for Noah at once!
Noah opened his dream.
Ling came out of it!

She burst from the blue-gold light like a thrown spear, white eyes blazing, legs lit from hip to heel with dream-light, purple fire roaring off her shoulders. The Gilt Heir saw her a heartbeat too late.
Her kick took him across the chest!
BOOM!
He flew across the cavern and slammed into the far wall, and the wall held, because it was the Thinker’s wall. The Gilt Heir peeled himself off it, gold armor dented, his face white with calm shock.
"You..." he said. "You’re the old man’s brat?"
"And you’re a dumb motherfucker," Ling said. She rolled her neck. "Come here."
He came. She met him!
Newly risen against a somewhat established Immensity, gold against dream, his sword against her legs, and every exchange shook the mountain!
Oh!

She was shallower than he was, a Dream Immensity only an hour old against a few Ages of gold, and she held him anyway, laughing and cursing and kicking until his armor rang like a struck bell. He fought like a man more surprised than serious.
Which left Noah, and the Hound!
It came at him across the cavern floor, and Noah decided to experiment. He let himself be afraid.

The fear rose and fed itself and poured into him as strength. Anger followed, hot and steady: at the Fiend for walking into his host’s home, at the Verdant Regard for her betrayal, at all of them for coming to take him like a parcel. It fed itself too. The more he felt, the more of him there was!
That was the Human in him!
The Hound’s jaws came down where he stood, and closed on an echo.

Noah had dreamed the space around himself into his own. Inside it, the Hound’s lunge arrived already spent, its jaws snapping shut on the place he had been a dream ago. Its paw landed slow and dull, its force bleeding away into the dream. Its Immensity tried to close on him again, and slid off a sky.
That was the Dreamer!
And every blow that broke against his dream shed fine grey residue, like sparks off a whetstone. Noah opened his mouth and drank it.
That was the Sovereign!
|Predation: residue of THE Hound of Thresholds.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 26%.|
|Auto-Fusion: Authority of the Held Breath + Provenance of Order + residue of an Immense One’s reach.|
|Formed: Authority of the Unclosing Hand. That which tries to close upon you finds itself held open.|
The Hound lunged again, and its jaws locked wide open in mid-bite, held by nothing. It wrenched free and backed away, its eyes narow.
Noah decided to test something else.
The Bow of the Ending Epoch dreamed itself into his hand. He drew, an arrow of compressed Epochs forming along the string, and loosed it into the Hound’s grey chest from ten paces.
It went in!
The hide around the wound withered, cracked, wore toward bone through a thousand Ages in an instant.
Then the Hound’s Immensity swallowed the Ages whole, as a calm sea swallows a stone. The hide filled back in, the scratch closed, and the Hound shook itself once and smiled with marvel!
|"Wow! He might be the real deal! He is a bit weak, but this is definitely Immensity! How the hell is he displaying Immensity? I see why we want to kidnap him!"|
The words were heavy.
Noah lowered the bow. Killing it lay beyond him, for today.

"It seems that Immensity is deep," he said. His voice boomed out grandly."I can see how deep. My eyes go down through you, Age after Age, and I can see that your bottom is very far, and that I cannot reach it."
He let the bow fade from his hand.
"I do not need to reach it today. I only need you to understand that you cannot reach me either. And someday, your bottom will be in reach."
The Hound of Thresholds, which had hunted every opening in existence for longer than Noah’s whole species had existed, pulsed with wonder.
The Fiend stepped off the Thinker’s bead.

Immensity raged as the Thinker was swarmed on all sides, the Hound turning its attacks on him to keep him busy, and THE Sleepless Fiend walked toward Noah. With every step, the stone under his feet darkened into crimson gold, and the air he passed through grew warm and faintly sweet, as air does in a room that belongs to someone else.
Across the cavern, Ling and the Gilt Heir broke apart to watch.
Noah looked at the Fiend with his gold eyes, and this time, he looked all the way!

The tall figure in dark robes was only a skin on something enormous. Beneath it, the Fiend went down and out in every direction, a vastnes built entirely of eyes that had stayed open since their making. Each one watched a different place the Fiend had touched once and so owned forever: a city, a sea, a Dimension, a child asleep in a cot.

From the vastness ran threads, hundreds of thousands of them, each one down a lineage the Fiend had sired across the Ages, Descendants hanging from them like fruit from a vine. One ran toward the Krazhor-Nul. One had been cut, recently, its end hanging loose and bleeding.
Around his head rested a crown of chains, every link a promise someone had made to him and was bound to keep.
And everything near him, stone and air and light, was being rewritten into what he wished it to be, all the way down to what each thing was!
|THE Sleepless Fiend.|
|Profundity: Unknown.|
The Fiend stopped an arm’s length away.
"Osmont," he said. "That is what they call you, yes?"
His voice was warm and pleased.
"That was very well done. I may even change the course of plans and mission we were given here today."
He clasped his hands behind his back.

"The Keepers of Existence have a seat open. I would like you to take it. You would have protection beyond anything this Legacy can offer, beyond anything the old man there can offer, dying as he is. You would have resources. Teachers. Every Gu and every Immense corpse you could wish to eat. And when the one who will open the door finally stands before it, you would stand at his side."
His countless eyes all turned toward Noah at once. "You would be valued. Kept. Fed. You would be made grand. You may just have to...offer your heart."
Noah looked at him.
"No," he said.
That was all.
The Fiend’s smile warmed.
"Of course,"he said.
He lifted a single finger and laid it, almost gently, on the edge of Noah’s dream.
Ownership flowed out of it!

Crimson gold bloomed outward from that one point like ink in still water. Star after star in Noah’s dream changed color, and he felt each one stop being his. The sky that had held the Hound’s hand and dreamed islands back together was becoming someone else’s, one light at a time!
HUUM!
Noah poured everything he had into that single point!

The Tree in his chest blazed, every ring and Branch and drop of Sap lit at once, and dream rushed out of him to meet the Fiend’s finger, tide against tide. A crimson gold star went blue-gold again. Another went crimson. Then back.
It was terrifying. He felt he could slip at any moment!
He held for an instant. Just an instant. Any longer, and he knew he would be crushed, and face his first death since his evolution!
A bead of purple fire slid between them!
It drifted into the space between the Fiend’s finger and Noah’s dream, burning steadily. The Thinker had still not risen. His eyes were still closed. One of his moons had simply decided to be there.
The Fiend withdrew his finger, unhurried, and regarded the bead with mild amusement, then the old man on his mat, then Noah.
The crimson gold drained out of the stars, and every one of them went blue-gold again.
Noah stood inside his dream, chest heaving, infinite emotions burning all through him.
He looked into the Fiend’s countless eyes, every one of them watchng him.
And he smiled!
It was an affirmation he wanted to make, that he could at leasy defend himself! Even if only for an instant!
At this time, far above them, through the mountain and the torn coat and Moriarty’s mist, the whole Legacy began to hum, and a brilliant light began heading their way!
The Thinker opened his weeping eyes and breathed out a calm sigh.
Finally, the help would be arriving!

He smiled a little, and turned back to the Thinker’s burning bead, as though he had decided to save Noah for later.
