It came again, harder, and this time the Gilt Heir tore himself free of the Thinker’s bead and came with it, gold blazing, sword drawn, a young lord’s face twisted with the humiliaton of having laughed too soon.
Two Immense Ones, coming for Noah at once!
Noah opened his dream.
Ling came out of it!
She burst from the blue-gold light like a thrown spear, white eyes blazing, legs lit from hip to heel with dream-light, purple fire roaring off her shoulders.
The Gilt Heir saw her a heartbeat too late.
Her kick took him across the chest!
BOOM!
He flew across the cavern and slammed into the far wall, and the wall held, because it was the Thinker’s wall.
The Gilt Heir peeled himself off it, gold armor dented, his face white with calm shock.
"You..." he said.
"You’re the old man’s brat?"
"And you’re a dumb motherfucker," Ling said.
She rolled her neck.
"Come here."
He came.
She met him!
Newly risen against a somewhat established Immensity, gold against dream, his sword against her legs, and every exchange shook the mountain!
Oh!
She was shallower than he was, a Dream Immensity only an hour old against a few Ages of gold, and she held him anyway, laughing and cursing and kicking until his armor rang like a struck bell.
He fought like a man more surprised than serious.
Which left Noah, and the Hound!
It came at him across the cavern floor, and Noah decided to experiment.
He let himself be afraid.
The fear rose and fed itself and poured into him as strength.
Anger followed, hot and steady: at the Fiend for walking into his host’s home, at the Verdant Regard for her betrayal, at all of them for coming to take him like a parcel.
It fed itself too.
The more he felt, the more of him there was!
That was the Human in him!
The Hound’s jaws came down where he stood, and closed on an echo.
Noah had dreamed the space around himself into his own.
Inside it, the Hound’s lunge arrived already spent, its jaws snapping shut on the place he had been a dream ago.
Its paw landed slow and dull, its force bleeding away into the dream.
Its Immensity tried to close on him again, and slid off a sky.
That was the Dreamer!
And every blow that broke against his dream shed fine grey residue, like sparks off a whetstone.
Noah opened his mouth and drank it.
That was the Sovereign!
|Predation: residue of THE Hound of Thresholds.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 26%.|
|Auto-Fusion: Authority of the Held Breath + Provenance of Order + residue of an Immense One’s reach.|
|Formed: Authority of the Unclosing Hand.
That which tries to close upon you finds itself held open.|
The Hound lunged again, and its jaws locked wide open in mid-bite, held by nothing.
It wrenched free and backed away, its eyes narow.
Noah decided to test something else.
The Bow of the Ending Epoch dreamed itself into his hand.
He drew, an arrow of compressed Epochs forming along the string, and loosed it into the Hound’s grey chest from ten paces.
It went in!
The hide around the wound withered, cracked, wore toward bone through a thousand Ages in an instant.
Then the Hound’s Immensity swallowed the Ages whole, as a calm sea swallows a stone.
The hide filled back in, the scratch closed, and the Hound shook itself once and smiled with marvel!
|"Wow!
He might be the real deal!
He is a bit weak, but this is definitely Immensity!
How the hell is he displaying Immensity?
I see why we want to kidnap him!"|
The words were heavy.
Noah lowered the bow.
Killing it lay beyond him, for today.
"It seems that Immensity is deep," he said.
His voice boomed out grandly."I can see how deep.
My eyes go down through you, Age after Age, and I can see that your bottom is very far, and that I cannot reach it."
He let the bow fade from his hand.
"I do not need to reach it today.
I only need you to understand that you cannot reach me either.
And someday, your bottom will be in reach."
The Hound of Thresholds, which had hunted every opening in existence for longer than Noah’s whole species had existed, pulsed with wonder.
The Fiend stepped off the Thinker’s bead.
Immensity raged as the Thinker was swarmed on all sides, the Hound turning its attacks on him to keep him busy, and THE Sleepless Fiend walked toward Noah.
With every step, the stone under his feet darkened into crimson gold, and the air he passed through grew warm and faintly sweet, as air does in a room that belongs to someone else.
Across the cavern, Ling and the Gilt Heir broke apart to watch.
Noah looked at the Fiend with his gold eyes, and this time, he looked all the way!
The tall figure in dark robes was only a skin on something enormous.
Beneath it, the Fiend went down and out in every direction, a vastnes built entirely of eyes that had stayed open since their making.
Each one watched a different place the Fiend had touched once and so owned forever: a city, a sea, a Dimension, a child asleep in a cot.
From the vastness ran threads, hundreds of thousands of them, each one down a lineage the Fiend had sired across the Ages, Descendants hanging from them like fruit from a vine.
One ran toward the Krazhor-Nul.
One had been cut, recently, its end hanging loose and bleeding.
Around his head rested a crown of chains, every link a promise someone had made to him and was bound to keep.
And everything near him, stone and air and light, was being rewritten into what he wished it to be, all the way down to what each thing was!
|THE Sleepless Fiend.|
|Profundity: Unknown.|
The Fiend stopped an arm’s length away.
"Osmont," he said.
"That is what they call you, yes?"
His voice was warm and pleased.
"That was very well done.
I may even change the course of plans and mission we were given here today."
He clasped his hands behind his back.
"The Keepers of Existence have a seat open.
I would like you to take it.
You would have protection beyond anything this Legacy can offer, beyond anything the old man there can offer, dying as he is.
You would have resources.
Teachers.
Every Gu and every Immense corpse you could wish to eat.
And when the one who will open the door finally stands before it, you would stand at his side."
His countless eyes all turned toward Noah at once.
"You would be valued.
Kept.
Fed.
You would be made grand.
You may just have to...offer your heart."
Noah looked at him.
"No," he said.
That was all.
The Fiend’s smile warmed.
"Of course,"he said.
He lifted a single finger and laid it, almost gently, on the edge of Noah’s dream.
Ownership flowed out of it!
Crimson gold bloomed outward from that one point like ink in still water.
Star after star in Noah’s dream changed color, and he felt each one stop being his.
The sky that had held the Hound’s hand and dreamed islands back together was becoming someone else’s, one light at a time!
HUUM!
Noah poured everything he had into that single point!
The Tree in his chest blazed, every ring and Branch and drop of Sap lit at once, and dream rushed out of him to meet the Fiend’s finger, tide against tide.
A crimson gold star went blue-gold again.
Another went crimson.
Then back.
It was terrifying.
He felt he could slip at any moment!
He held for an instant.
Just an instant.
Any longer, and he knew he would be crushed, and face his first death since his evolution!
A bead of purple fire slid between them!
It drifted into the space between the Fiend’s finger and Noah’s dream, burning steadily.
The Thinker had still not risen.
His eyes were still closed.
One of his moons had simply decided to be there.
The Fiend withdrew his finger, unhurried, and regarded the bead with mild amusement, then the old man on his mat, then Noah.
The crimson gold drained out of the stars, and every one of them went blue-gold again.
Noah stood inside his dream, chest heaving, infinite emotions burning all through him.
He looked into the Fiend’s countless eyes, every one of them watchng him.
And he smiled!
It was an affirmation he wanted to make, that he could at leasy defend himself!
Even if only for an instant!
At this time, far above them, through the mountain and the torn coat and Moriarty’s mist, the whole Legacy began to hum, and a brilliant light began heading their way!
The Thinker opened his weeping eyes and breathed out a calm sigh.
Finally, the help would be arriving!

chapters.title: Chapter 5826: Immensity! IV
paragraphs: The note rose, and rose, and THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity woke.

Noah felt it through the soles of his feet first. A deep vibration climbing up out of the mountain’s roots, out of the rivers below, out of the snow-buried floor of the whole Legacy. Then his gold eyes caught it, and he saw what Lucy had built.
It was a single thing!

The purple-gold rivers and the Existential Conduits rising out of them, the thousand Elsedimension Mountains with their monasteries and thrones and caverns, the Plain of Accord, the Firmament, the Keepers’ Roads winding between the peaks, the floor of snow beneath it all.

He had always seen them as parts of a place. They were parts of one body. An Immensity, woven into the shape of a home and laid down to sleep, so long ago that even the Immense who lived inside it had forgotten it was alive.
It had slept for Ages.
Now it was awake, and Noah could see who had woken it!

Deep in the Legacy’s heart, where every river and Conduit met, Sir Moriarty coiled around the center of everything with every tentacle he had. Green poison bled from every seam of him. His spectacles were cracked. He was hurt badly, in ways an Immense One should be spared. And he had reached the heart anyway, and laid himself across it, and called the Legacy up out of its sleep.
The Legacy answered him!
Obsidian gold came down on the Thinker’s mountain!

It poured out of every Conduit in the Legacy at once, all of them turning their light toward the mountain, and it came down through the torn purple coat in a single crushing tide. And it fell only on those who were strangers here!

The Rusted Matriarch’s rust peeled off her in long brown sheets, her bronze body groaning under the weight. The Gilt Heir dropped to one knee, his gold dimming to brass, his face slack with shock. And the Hound of Thresholds was hurled backward out of the cavern entirely, out through the torn coat and into the blizzard, its doorway eyes wide.
THE Verdant Regard’s body cracked down its whole length like dry bark splitting in a frost, green light bleeding from the seam.
On Noah, it fell like warm rain!
The Legacy’s waking Immensity had looked at him and counted him among its own.
On Ling, it fell like a hand on her hair. On the Thinker, it fell and was welcomed, and the purple fire on his orbiting beads flared brighter.
The Fiend stayed exactly where he stood.
He stood in the middle of the obsidian gold tide as it crashed down on him. He studied the light pouring through the torn coat!

The pressure on him was enough to grind mountains, and yet he stood as this fucker’s immensity was unfathomable! How the hell had Noah escaped his grasp before when Poona threatened them just with the Legacy behind her?!
He had been cautious enough that the name of THE Legacy of THE Acharya made him hesitate then, but here he was among those leading in its invasion. What changed?
As he thought about this...
The thrones descended!
They came down through the torn coat one after another, out of the obsidian gold, and each took a place around the cavern without a word.
Sir Moriarty came first, in person. Well, in octupus.

The octopus-headed visage had drawn down into a body Noah had seen before: tentacles, spectacles, a long dark coat. But the coat was soaked through with green, the tentacles trailed poison in long glowing threads, and one lens of his spectacels was split clean across. He was breathng hard. His crimson eyes were steady.

THE Ashen Cantor came behind him, cinders drifting off his robe, his mouth closed for once. THE Keeper of the Unbroken Vow, the chain of oaths coiled over one shoulder. THE Lantern of the Last Shore, faceless, his lamp held low. THE Hollow Choir, their ring of hollow faces drifting into place along the cavern’s ceiling, silent.
They took their places around the five invaders.
And then, one by one, they turned and looked at Noah.
Thry had sensed or seen the power Noah had displayed to rebuff an Immense One and even not crumbled completely under THE SLEEPLESS FIEND as they had questions!
Their eyes shone!
Moriarty’s shone most of all. Behind his cracked spectacles, the crimson eyes held something new to Noah: hope... and it was enormous!

Noah understood what Moriarty thought he was seeing. They were looking at him and seeing an answer to the shut door. A key. Something beyond the winter’s grip. Every one of them was more certain of it than they had been an hour ago.
The Thinker spoke quietly, for Noah’s ears alone.

|"They see a key,"| he said, |"because they have spent a long looking for one. Long before this Winter. All of us are immense, but we remain. Ultimately, we have been waiting for things that will never arrive because we needed to save ourselves and find our own way...not find someone else to open the door for us."|
WAA!
His beads drifted slowly around him, burning.

|"As grand as you seem right, I still see a man who chose. It is the larger thing. And the rarer. The choice to choose...that is existence. All Civilizations chose. All ways choose. Existence is a series of...choices."|
Noah looked around the circle of thrones. Moriarty, the Cantor, the Keeper, the Lantern, the Choir.
He counted them again.
Where was Poona?
He always expected her to be with Moriarty!
Moriarty’s crimson eyes moved away from his, toward the torn coat and the blizzard beyond it.
In the middle of the cavern, THE Sleepless Fiend lifted one hand to his brow in a small, courtly salute. To the Thinker first. Then to Moriarty. And last of all, unhurried, to Noah.
The Fiend lowered his hand from his brow, and smiled at the circle of thrones as though they had all just shared a good meal.

"Well," he said. "Things did not go entirely according to plan, but I have learned a great deal that I can now report. It seems that what the great Lucy left behind...is not so untouchable as you all had everyone believe. I felt a sense of shame after this name alone made me not act not long ago, and I can be considered responsible for letting something slip past me."
HUUM!
He turned his face toward Moriarty. The obsidian gold was still pouring down on him, grinding, endless, and he stood in it with his robes perfectly still.
"I will come back when the snow is deeper, old friend. It will not be long now. And when I do, I think you will be more reasonable."

His countless eyes, behind his face, all seemed to settle on the split lens of Moriarty’s spectacles."I left you something on one of your mountains. Where my daughter was broken. A small gift, for old times’ sake."
He paused.
"I hope you will remember the taste of the Verdant Regard’s tea every time you look at it."
Moriarty’s tentacles went perfectly still.
The Fiend withdrew.

He simply stepped backward through the torn purple coat, and the cavern’s stone and air and light, one by one, went back to being what they had been. The torches lost their crimson gold and burned purple again. The prayer mats faded to their old dull color. Even the snow that had turned to face him turned away and fell.

THE Verdant Regard went with him. Her cracked body bled green as she backed toward the gap, and her eyes stayed on the Thinker to the very last, wet and furious and full of a grief that had nowhere left to go as she blamed him for the fact that they weren’t able to get Noah.
She also gazed hatefully at Noah as she sent him a message...

|"Why the fuck do you portray Immensity now? You were simply playing along this whole time? This power could have entirely crushed my daughter- why push her to form Immensity for her to simply be severed?! Why?!"|
Noah’s eyes remained cold as he didn’t even spare this woman a reply.
How the fuck was he to blame?
He ignored her as she disappeared!

The Rusted Matriarch followed, rust trailing from her. The Gilt Heir dragged himself up off his knee, glared once at Ling, and went. Out in the blizard, the Hound of Thresholds was already loping away across the Legacy, grey and fast, without looking back.
Then they were gone alongside all Immense Ones who had invaded as if they all had received a collective order to withdraw!
The Legacy breathed out!

Noah felt it everywhere at once through his gold eyes. The walled domains came down. The Existential Conduits that had risen into pillars sank slowly back into their rivers, light dimming to its usual purple-gold.

Moriarty’s obsidian-gold mist lifted from the mountains in long drifting curtains, and the golden spheres of foreign Immensity that had been frozen inside those walls truly tore loose all at once and fled. Dozens of them, streaking up through the cracked sky and out of the Legacy like sparks leaving a fire!
The cracks in the sky remained!
Snow fell through them, heavier than before.
|The incursion into THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity has ended.|
|Immense grasps rebuffed: 2.|
|Immense residue devoured: 4.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 29%.|
|Judgment Debt: 2.|
Twenty-nine percent!

The Hound’s residue, the Immense grasps turned aside, the Fiend’s own finger held off at the edge of his dream: the Tree had drunk all of it and grown. He had come out of a cavern full of Immense Ones stronger than he went in!
And beside him, the Thinker was looking at the cracks in the sky with his weeping eyes open.
|"I truly dislike the Fiend. He leaves gifts,"| the Thinker said quietly, |"as other beings leave footprints. Wherever he has walked, something is left behind for someone to find."|
His beads hung still.|"It is never kind."|
Ling looked from her father to Noah and back, her white eyes narrowing. She asked what gift. The Thinker gave her no answer.
He was looking at Moriarty.

The old scholar had stood frozen since the Fiend spoke. He stood among the other thrones with his tentacles hanging limp, green poison dripping slowly from them onto the stone, and his crimson eyes fixed on the place in the coat where the Fiend had gone.
Footsteps came up the mountain path outside!

Quick, uneven, a little too fast for an old man’s knees. Verys came in through the cavern mouth with snow on his shoulders and his face grey. He bowed to the Thinker. He bowed to the thrones. Then he came straight to Noah, and Noah saw his hands were shakng.
The Keepers’ network had carried it, Verys told him.
Every servant in the Legacy had it now, passed mountain to mountain through the Conduits while the war was still going. What had happened in Moriarty’s study.
When the Fiend had opened the Verdant Regard’s dome, when the poison had come blooming out of Moriarty and the two of them had moved to finish him, Poona had stepped between them.

She had already taken her true form. The vast slime of every color, filling half the study, her one great eye open. She had put herself between Moriarty and the two oldest enemies in the room, and she had burned her own Immensity to hold them. All of it. Every Age of it.

She had poured it out into a wall of living color that neither the Fiend nor the Verdant Regard could get through, and she had held that wall while Moriarty fought the poison off and dragged himself down into the heart of the Legacy to wake it.
She had held it for exactly as long as it took.

Beside Noah, Ling had gone white. Her hands came up over her mouth, and her white eyes went to her father. The Thinker’s beads hung motionless in the air around him, every one of them dark, their purple fire banked low for the first time since the Fiend had walked into the cavern.
Verys stopped there. The rest needed no saying.
Across the cavern, Moriarty reached up with one trembling tentacle and took off his cracked spectacles.
Noah stood.
The Tree in his chest had gone very quiet. The Human in him roared!
"Where is she?" he asked.
Verys looked at him as he answered in a low voice.
"The Fiend moved her corpse to The Firmament, Sir,"he said. "On the Plain of Accord."

When the Fiend had opened the Verdant Regard’s dome, when the poison had come blooming out of Moriarty and the two of them had moved to finish him, Poona had stepped between them.
She had already taken her true form.
The vast slime of every color, filling half the study, her one great eye open.
She had put herself between Moriarty and the two oldest enemies in the room, and she had burned her own Immensity to hold them.
All of it.
Every Age of it.

She had poured it out into a wall of living color that neither the Fiend nor the Verdant Regard could get through, and she had held that wall while Moriarty fought the poison off and dragged himself down into the heart of the Legacy to wake it.
She had held it for exactly as long as it took.
Beside Noah, Ling had gone white.
Her hands came up over her mouth, and her white eyes went to her father.
The Thinker’s beads hung motionless in the air around him, every one of them dark, their purple fire banked low for the first time since the Fiend had walked into the cavern.
Verys stopped there.
The rest needed no saying.
Across the cavern, Moriarty reached up with one trembling tentacle and took off his cracked spectacles.
Noah stood.
The Tree in his chest had gone very quiet.
The Human in him roared!
"Where is she?" he asked.
Verys looked at him as he answered in a low voice.
"The Fiend moved her corpse to The Firmament, Sir,"he said.
"On the Plain of Accord."

chapters.title: Chapter 5827: Legacy’s Son!
paragraphs: The Plain of Accord lay under a deep fresh fall of snow, and in its center, the snow was grey.

Noah came down onto the Firmament’s broad shoulder with Ling at his side and the Thinker’s great kneeling shape descending behind them. Golden clouds still hung in their ring above the Plain, every throne on them vacant, snow gathering on the seats.
And at the Plain’s center lay Poona.

What was left of her filled a hollow in the snow as wide as a village. The vast gleaming slime of every color that had sat on Moriarty’s table eating his pastries had been torn open, long ragged rips running through her from edge to edge, and along every one of them, crimson and violet and gold and blue had gone to grey, as though someone had dragged claws through a painting and taken the paint with them. Her one enormous eye was dimmed to the color of old ice and cracked straight down its middle.
The Fiend had taken his time over killing her!

Many had already gathered. Moriarty stood at the edge of the hollow with his cracked spectacles in one tentacle, green still bleeding from his seams, the Legacy’s Immense Ones around him. Beyond them, in widening rings, stood Progeny and Provenance Lifeforms from every mountain, Keepers in their simple robes, Achilles with Rose wrapped in his cloak and the frost on his shoulders staying frozen, and hundreds more Noah did not know, all looking at the grey thing at the center of everything.
Behind him, the Thinker set his great knees down at the edge of the Plain and bowed his head. The last time he had truly left his mountain was a long time ago. He had left it now, for this.
And in the periphery, the auras of other Immense Ones watched with heavy eyes. A few of them turned toward Noah as he came down, and a few of them were hard!
Then a voice from somewhere in the skies.
|"Was he not their focus?"|
Another voice. |"The Fiend and others walked into the old man’s mountain for him. Poona was merely collateral for their plans."|
Noah heard every word calmly.
He walked to the edge of the hollow, passing close by Moriarty, and looked down at Poona. She had saved him once before. He felt it, sharp and sentimental!
With the Gold Without Pupils, he looked at her across every branch his eyes could follow, every way the ambush in Moriarty’s study might have gone.
He dreamt!
In some, the dome held longer. In some, the poison bloomed faster. In some, Moriarty moved first, or the Fiend did, or the Verdant Regard hesitated at the last.
In every one, Poona stepped forward!
She took her true form, filled half the study, and burned her Immensity to a wall of living color. And in every single one, as the wall went up, she was smiling!
On the outside, Noah’s face stayed still. His gold eyes stayed calm. But the Human in him pulsed as anger and grief came pouring up through the crack, and kept pouring.

|You have better understood the emotion side of your humanity as with your evolution, your emotions grow infinitely as the happier, loving, angry, lustful, fearful...any extreme of emotions you experience will experience infinite growth and only further elevate your power.|
Noah’s eyes pulsed as he looked closer, past the drained colors and the cracked eye, down into the deepest place in what was left of her, as he had once looked into the Warden’s chest.
Something was still there!
It was faint, almost nothing, a flicker far down in the grey. Every Age of her Immensity had been burned to hold that wall. But at the very bottom, something was still unfinished.
A dream.
Poona was dead. Her dream lingered, faint, and still alive!
Noah walked down into the hollow, past the torn grey edges of the slime, while the whole Legacy watched in silence. Moriarty lifted his head. The Thinker’s beads went still.
He knelt beside her, laid his stellar dark hand flat on the grey, torn surface, and closed his gold eyes.
Under his palm, the slime was cold, and still, and far heavier than it looked.

His dream went down first, soft and blue-gold, sinking into the grey mass as warm water sinks into snow. It found every place where her Immensity had been burned out and scorched clean. And at the very bottom, where the last flicker waited, it closed around it, gently, and drew it up.
Poona’s dream came into his hand!
A kitchen. Warm, cluttered, bright with lamplight, somewhere deep inside the Legacy in an Age long past.

Pastries cooling on every surface, on the shelves, on the windowsill, piled on plates along a table far too long for any kitchen to hold. Flour in the air. Noise everywhere. Every Immense One she had ever talked to sat around that table at once, arguing and laughing and reaching across one another for the last of the honey cakes that burned with Immensity.

Moriarty, younger, his spectacles whole, trying to read at the table and failing. The Ashen Cantor singing badly on purpose. The Keeper of the Unbroken Vow pretending not to eat. And at the head of the table, an empty chair, carved and plain, with a cup of tea set in front of it, still steaming, waiting for someone to come home and sit down.
Lucy’s chair!
That was what Poona had dreamed. All of them, at one table, fed and loud and safe, and the chair kept ready.

Noah held the dream against his chest and carried it down past his skin and his constellations of dreams, down to the Tree. He laid the kitchen at the base of the endless trunk, where the first ring glowed, and dreamed it into...Immensity. As he had dreamed Ling’s. Through his own Dream, past the door, without asking the door’s permission.
The dream began to grow. Its lamplight deepened. Its warmth went down, layer under layer, Immensity filling it from below like a well filling with water.
The sky over the Plain of Accord split open!
BOOM!

Obsidian gold poured through a crack that ran from one horizon to the other, straight through the ring of empty thrones, down onto the snow, onto Noah kneeling in the hollow with his hand on a corpse and a dream cupped against his chest.
A voice only he could hear boomed out!
|How dare you.|
|The dead are counted. The dead stay counted.|
|You would dare to dream what existence has ended?|
It landed on his back like the weight of every Age at once!

His knees drove into the snow. His crown of radiance flared, guttered, flared again. The constellations of dreams under his skin blazed and dimmed and blazed, and the obsidian gold ground down on him, searching for the place where he would let go.
He held the dream!

Bent over it as a man holds a child in a burning house, his whole body a roof, he let every ounce of the Judgment fall on him, and THE One Foundation took it and built it into floor beneath him. He kept it from the kitchen. He kept it from the chair!
Around the Plain, nobody moved, for what they perceived was different from what Noah percieved!
The Judgment pressed down one last time, then withdrew, and the sky closed behind it.
|The Judgment has been withstood.|
|Judgment Debt: 3. Existence will remember.|

Noah raised his head, snow settled on his white-gold hair, and laid the dream back at the bottom of the torn slime, where he had found it. It sank out of his hand and settled into the place where her Immensity had burned out.
Then he spoke to her. His voice was quiet. It carried across the whole Plain anyway!
"Dream once more," Noah said.
He kept his hand on her.
"Under my gaze and brilliance... dream."
The corpse buzzed!
A single deep vibration rose from the bottom, where the dream had settled, and then the color came back, one slow wave of it rolling outward through every drained stripe and every torn edge.
At the center, the great eye shudderd.

The crack down its middle sealed from the bottom up. The dull ice warmed. And the eye opened, clear and bright and fully awake, and fine glowing threads ran out of the depths behind it, across the snow, into Noah’s chest, into his Tree.
A new Immensity rose out of Poona!
It rose over the Plain, smelling faintly of honey cakes and lamplight, and every Immense One on the Plain of Accord felt it!
|Kin Evolution: Poona has established a Dream Immensity.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 38%.|
The slime gathered itself and shrank, until a small round shape sat in the snow in front of Noah, gleaming with every color, its one great eye blinking up at the gathered Legacy.
Moriarty and others showed extremely complex expressions as many eyes turned over and locked onto Noah!
What had he just done?! He revived...an Immensity?
Who among them could do this?!
As for Poona, she turned to Noah and smiled brilliantly, and through her Dream Immensity he sensed her about to kneel to him before everyone. He quickly and sternly sent her a command not to!
She went very quiet.

Moriarty bent and looked at Poona with wonder. He then looked at Noah for a long time across the snow as he also sensed the somber gazes of many others, with other Immense ones showing hungry and interested looks by the dozens!
So he raised his voice, and spoke to the whole Plain.

"THE Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity,"Moriarty said, "has never named a Son. Not once, since Lucy founded it. She left directions that if and when the time came when the nights grew long and all doors closed, someone would have to be named THE Legacy’s Son. Someone who may be able to gaze past the treachery of the long cold and ensure the Legacy shines bright...till the doors are open once more!"
HUUM!
His crimson eyes stayed on Noah. "Before this winter grows any longer, I would like to propose THE Legacy’s Son."
THE Legacy’s Son!
Nobody on the Plain spoke.
At its edge, THE Thinker at the End of Existence knelt in the snow with his beads still, and smiled his fierce almost-smile, and said nothing at all.

The snow fell on the Plain of Accord, heavier than before. It fell on the empty thrones and the gathered Legacy, on a small bright slime blinking in the hollow, on a Legacy beginning to prepare for the long winter ahead.
And it fell on the man its oldest scholar had just proposed to name THE Legacy’s Son as he was feeling his rising dream after doing the unthinkable!

chapters.title: Chapter 5828: Order! I
paragraphs: The silence on the Plain of Accord lasted until Moriarty’s Immensity pulsed.
His voice carried to every one of them. They were to return to their mountains. The Immense Ones of the Legacy would hold a council, and what came next would be decided there.
The crowd broke apart at once, and Achilles lifted a hand to Noah across the snow before leading Rose away. Overhead, the thrones began to fill!
Poona looked at him before the eyes of other Immense Ones as she said...
"I have to thank someone for my return! No worries, I will keep him safe."
Her golden brilliance flared and wrapped around her and Noah as they both disappeared, seemingly to Poona’s Existential Immense Domain.
But that was not the case!
THE Existential Dreaming Origin Domain had kept growing since the evolution. New ridges, new valleys, Gigaparsecs of golden blue brilliance.
On a hill above the river, Ruination’s and THE Infiniverse’s cocoons still glowed, still closed.
Noah gazed at Poona on the grass.

She had shrunk into a little golden slime, round and bubbly, flecked with every color. She wobbled a few times to find her balance, then bowed so deeply her eye nearly touched the ground, and thanked him for resuscitating her dream.
She had saved him a few days ago, she pointed out, and now he had saved her, and held her Immensity in his hands besides. As his senior, no less!
"Now I feel like a baby Immense One again, wow!" she added, mostly to herself.
Noah let her bounce for a moment.
Then he sat down cross-legged in front of her and started asking questions!
He had plenty. A whole Legacy of Immense Ones had just fought a small war, and he understood almost nothing about what they actually were. Poona was the first of them who looked happy to explain.
First, he asked her how Immense Ones differed from one another.
According to Poona, they differed in almost every way that mattered. Immensity took the shape of whatever a being had been carrying when it went through the door.
Next, he asked her how to measure them. His gold eyes could look down into an Immense One, but past a certain point, they simply found no bottom.

Poona told him the Immense had a word for that: Profundity. How far down a being’s Immensity went, rather than how high it had climbed, and how much it had carried through the Ages to get there. She explained it in her own cheerful, rambling way as...she loved talking a bit too much.
As she talked, Noah’s eyes worked. He laid her words over everything he had seen in the Thinker’s cavern, every Immense One he had read, every bottom he had failed to find.
And his existence answered with prompts that simplified her convoluted explanations!
|Profundity of Immensity.|
|The measure of what an Immense One has carried, and how far down its Immensity reaches.|
|Newly Risen. Immensity freshly established. Shallow, loud, and still learning its own shape. A Newly Risen One can be read to the bottom by a keen enough eye.|
|Known to you: Ling, THE Dancer in the Boundless Dream. Poona, reborn.|
|Established. Immensity that has carried Ages. Its bottom can be glimpsed, but lies far below. Most who sit on thrones are Established.|
|Known to you: THE Gilt Heir. THE Hound of Thresholds. Many of the Legacy’s thrones.|
|Ancient. Immensity that has carried more Ages than most lifeforms can imagine. Its bottom cannot be seen. Its presence alone changes existence nearby.|
|Known to you: Sir Moriarty. THE Sleepless Fiend. THE Thinker at the End of Existence. THE Verdant Regard. THE Rusted Matriarch.|
|Unfathomable. Immensity whose Profundity cannot be measured, even by the Ancient.|
|Known to you: none.|
|Beyond. ???|
Noah read the list twice.
The Thinker, who had held four Immense Ones at bay without standing up, was Ancient. The Fiend, whose single finger had nearly stolen his dream, was Ancient.
And above them sat a whole tier he had yet to meet.
Unfathomable. Then Beyond, with nothing written under it at all!
|Your own Profundity: ???|
|Others perceive in you the Immensity of a weak Newly Risen One.|
To the Immense, he looked like a fresh, weak Immense One standing where a days-old Root should have been. Wrong, but useful. He would let them keep thinking it!
Then he asked Poona about THE Legacy’s Son.
Here she went serious, briefly.

According to her, the title was a spiritual pillar for the whole Legacy: the successor to everything Lucy had left behind. Lucy had named no one. She had left directions, sealed for Ages, about when one should be named. And whoever became THE Legacy’s Son gained access to an Immense Domain that nobody had ever entered, left by Lucy specifically for them. Even Moriarty had yet to set foot inside.
Then she squinted up at him.
"Do I have to call you Master now, since you hold my Dream Immensity?"Poona asked. She thought about it for exactly one heartbeat. "Well, I don’t care! Master, then."
Since his power showed itself at the level of a weak Immense One when he was supposed to have only just formed his Root, she went on, most of the Legacy’s Immense would likely accept him.
"We will see!" she finished, and smiled brilliantly.
Noah looked at her truly.

Her Dream Immensity was shallow, a single warm layer of lamplight with only the beginnings of Profundity beneath its floor. Under it ran the faint memory of everything she had once been, Ages of old quiet Immensity, burned away and remembered. Bright threads ran from the bottom of her into his Tree.
|Poona.|
|THE Dreaming Hearth.|
|Dream Immensity. Kin.|
|Profundity: Newly Risen. It remembers being Ancient.|
THE Dreaming Hearth. It suited her!
Noah stood up and looked out over his Domain as he sensed his own existence.
The gain were Sap from 14% to 38%. Two new Authorities, the Held Breath and the Unclosing Hand. One Immense grasp rebuffed outright, one held at bay. Poona revived as Kin. A proposed title.
The negatives of it all were Judgment Debt up to 3. The Fiend’s full attention. The Verdant Regard’s hatred.
And the most importantly...without the Thinker, Moriarty, and Poona, he would have been captured today. Plainly and simply captured.
He disliked that intensely!
Being saved was a fine thing when it came. Planning on it was another matter. So the answer was simple. Grow until nobody needed to protect him.

He was a dreamer, a sovereign, and a human. The sovereign in him would take this Legacy’s Son title grandly, walk into Lucy’s sealed Domain, and see exactly what she had left behind. If it could be learned, he would learn it. If it could be eaten, he would eat it.
But titles alone would leave his Tree hungry.
What had carried him to his first evolution? A dead Immense One’s corpse and an Ergosphere full of Roots. So where would he find more things like that?
The answer came at once!
THE Undersnow!

Dead Immense Ones. Kept First Lifeforms. Beings at Immensity, in abundance. A Floor already cleared, and a rift north of it standing open and unguarded, leading down into THE Evergrave. Down there were the Caretaker in her chains, the secrets of the Long Night, and things old enough to remember the First Sundering.
And, quite possibly, a great deal to eat!
He turned his gold eyes toward the far edge of his Domain, toward the cold waiting beyond it.
"Existence is vast,"Noah said, "and full of terrors..."
It truly was as to prepare, he had to properly understand himself!
So he sat down cross-legged on a hill in THE Existential Dreaming Origin Domain, with Poona bouncing on the grass beside him, and turned his gold eyes inward.
The first question was simple. Could his own Tree count what existence had given up on?
He dreamed that it could, and his existence began to buzz!
|Existence counts what it can write. Its count of you broke at nine hundred and ninety-nine.|
|Your Tree measures you differently: by how far your Dream can reach, and how much of that reach it can command.|
|These are the Orders of the Dream.|
Noah leaned forward.
|Order I. Your Dream reaches across many Dimensions and facets of existence at once, and commands the power within them.|

|Order II. Your Dream can reach across the whole domain of a Legacy and Dream without other’s knowledge: countless Dimensions, and every space between them. All of Order I becomes a single grain within it.|
|Order III. Your Dream gains the capability to reach across an entire stratum of existence, Undefined Gaps, the whole of THE Infinite Carcosa, or the whole of THE Source Lands.|
|Order IV. Your Dream reaches across every stratum existence can perceive, layered together as one.|
|Order V. Your Dream reaches beneath existence: THE Undersnow, THE Evergrave, and the layers of cold beneath the cold further underneath.|
|Order VI. Your Dream reaches across every cycle of existence, back past THE First Sundering.|
|Order VII. Your Dream reaches outside existence.|
|Order ???|

|Within each Order, the measure after the point is how fully you command it. At I.0, an attribute has only just entered the first Order. At I.9, it presses against the second. Every tenth is a true step in what you can do.|

"I have to thank someone for my return!

Her golden brilliance flared and wrapped around her and Noah as they both disappeared, seemingly to Poona’s Existential Immense Domain.
But that was not the case!
THE Existential Dreaming Origin Domain had kept growing since the evolution.
New ridges, new valleys, Gigaparsecs of golden blue brilliance.
On a hill above the river, Ruination’s and THE Infiniverse’s cocoons still glowed, still closed.
Noah gazed at Poona on the grass.
She had shrunk into a little golden slime, round and bubbly, flecked with every color.
She wobbled a few times to find her balance, then bowed so deeply her eye nearly touched the ground, and thanked him for resuscitating her dream.
She had saved him a few days ago, she pointed out, and now he had saved her, and held her Immensity in his hands besides.
As his senior, no less!
"Now I feel like a baby Immense One again, wow!" she added, mostly to herself.
Noah let her bounce for a moment.
Then he sat down cross-legged in front of her and started asking questions!
He had plenty.
A whole Legacy of Immense Ones had just fought a small war, and he understood almost nothing about what they actually were.
Poona was the first of them who looked happy to explain.
First, he asked her how Immense Ones differed from one another.
According to Poona, they differed in almost every way that mattered.
Immensity took the shape of whatever a being had been carrying when it went through the door.
Next, he asked her how to measure them.
His gold eyes could look down into an Immense One, but past a certain point, they simply found no bottom.
Poona told him the Immense had a word for that: Profundity.
How far down a being’s Immensity went, rather than how high it had climbed, and how much it had carried through the Ages to get there.
She explained it in her own cheerful, rambling way as...she loved talking a bit too much.
As she talked, Noah’s eyes worked.
He laid her words over everything he had seen in the Thinker’s cavern, every Immense One he had read, every bottom he had failed to find.
And his existence answered with prompts that simplified her convoluted explanations!
|Profundity of Immensity.|
|The measure of what an Immense One has carried, and how far down its Immensity reaches.|
|Newly Risen.
Immensity freshly established.
Shallow, loud, and still learning its own shape.
A Newly Risen One can be read to the bottom by a keen enough eye.|
|Known to you: Ling, THE Dancer in the Boundless Dream.
Poona, reborn.|
|Established.
Immensity that has carried Ages.
Its bottom can be glimpsed, but lies far below.
Most who sit on thrones are Established.|
|Known to you: THE Gilt Heir.
THE Hound of Thresholds.
Many of the Legacy’s thrones.|
|Ancient.
Immensity that has carried more Ages than most lifeforms can imagine.
Its bottom cannot be seen.
Its presence alone changes existence nearby.|
|Known to you: Sir Moriarty.
THE Sleepless Fiend.
THE Thinker at the End of Existence.
THE Verdant Regard.
THE Rusted Matriarch.|
|Unfathomable.
Immensity whose Profundity cannot be measured, even by the Ancient.|
|Known to you: none.|
|Beyond. ???|
Noah read the list twice.
The Thinker, who had held four Immense Ones at bay without standing up, was Ancient.
The Fiend, whose single finger had nearly stolen his dream, was Ancient.
And above them sat a whole tier he had yet to meet.
Unfathomable.
Then Beyond, with nothing written under it at all!
|Your own Profundity: ???|
|Others perceive in you the Immensity of a weak Newly Risen One.|
To the Immense, he looked like a fresh, weak Immense One standing where a days-old Root should have been.
Wrong, but useful.
He would let them keep thinking it!
Then he asked Poona about THE Legacy’s Son.
Here she went serious, briefly.
According to her, the title was a spiritual pillar for the whole Legacy: the successor to everything Lucy had left behind.
Lucy had named no one.
She had left directions, sealed for Ages, about when one should be named.
And whoever became THE Legacy’s Son gained access to an Immense Domain that nobody had ever entered, left by Lucy specifically for them.
Even Moriarty had yet to set foot inside.
Then she squinted up at him.
"Do I have to call you Master now, since you hold my Dream Immensity?"Poona asked.
She thought about it for exactly one heartbeat.
"Well, I don’t care!
Master, then."
Since his power showed itself at the level of a weak Immense One when he was supposed to have only just formed his Root, she went on, most of the Legacy’s Immense would likely accept him.
"We will see!" she finished, and smiled brilliantly.
Noah looked at her truly.
Her Dream Immensity was shallow, a single warm layer of lamplight with only the beginnings of Profundity beneath its floor.
Under it ran the faint memory of everything she had once been, Ages of old quiet Immensity, burned away and remembered.
Bright threads ran from the bottom of her into his Tree.
|Poona.|
|THE Dreaming Hearth.|
|Dream Immensity.
Kin.|
|Profundity: Newly Risen.
It remembers being Ancient.|
THE Dreaming Hearth.
It suited her!
Noah stood up and looked out over his Domain as he sensed his own existence.
The gain were Sap from 14% to 38%.
Two new Authorities, the Held Breath and the Unclosing Hand.
One Immense grasp rebuffed outright, one held at bay.
Poona revived as Kin.
A proposed title.
The negatives of it all were Judgment Debt up to 3.
The Fiend’s full attention.
The Verdant Regard’s hatred.
And the most importantly...without the Thinker, Moriarty, and Poona, he would have been captured today.
Plainly and simply captured.
He disliked that intensely!
Being saved was a fine thing when it came.
Planning on it was another matter.
So the answer was simple.
Grow until nobody needed to protect him.
He was a dreamer, a sovereign, and a human.
The sovereign in him would take this Legacy’s Son title grandly, walk into Lucy’s sealed Domain, and see exactly what she had left behind.
If it could be learned, he would learn it.
If it could be eaten, he would eat it.
But titles alone would leave his Tree hungry.
What had carried him to his first evolution?
A dead Immense One’s corpse and an Ergosphere full of Roots.
So where would he find more things like that?
The answer came at once!
THE Undersnow!
Dead Immense Ones.
Kept First Lifeforms.
Beings at Immensity, in abundance.
A Floor already cleared, and a rift north of it standing open and unguarded, leading down into THE Evergrave.
Down there were the Caretaker in her chains, the secrets of the Long Night, and things old enough to remember the First Sundering.
And, quite possibly, a great deal to eat!
He turned his gold eyes toward the far edge of his Domain, toward the cold waiting beyond it.
"Existence is vast,"Noah said, "and full of terrors..."
It truly was as to prepare, he had to properly understand himself!
So he sat down cross-legged on a hill in THE Existential Dreaming Origin Domain, with Poona bouncing on the grass beside him, and turned his gold eyes inward.
The first question was simple.
Could his own Tree count what existence had given up on?
He dreamed that it could, and his existence began to buzz!
|Existence counts what it can write.
Its count of you broke at nine hundred and ninety-nine.|
|Your Tree measures you differently: by how far your Dream can reach, and how much of that reach it can command.|
|These are the Orders of the Dream.|
Noah leaned forward.
|Order I.
Your Dream reaches across many Dimensions and facets of existence at once, and commands the power within them.|
|Order II.
Your Dream can reach across the whole domain of a Legacy and Dream without other’s knowledge: countless Dimensions, and every space between them.
All of Order I becomes a single grain within it.|
|Order III.
Your Dream gains the capability to reach across an entire stratum of existence, Undefined Gaps, the whole of THE Infinite Carcosa, or the whole of THE Source Lands.|
|Order IV.
Your Dream reaches across every stratum existence can perceive, layered together as one.|
|Order V.
Your Dream reaches beneath existence: THE Undersnow, THE Evergrave, and the layers of cold beneath the cold further underneath.|
|Order VI.
Your Dream reaches across every cycle of existence, back past THE First Sundering.|
|Order VII.
Your Dream reaches outside existence.|
|Order ???|
|Within each Order, the measure after the point is how fully you command it.
At I.0, an attribute has only just entered the first Order.
At I.9, it presses against the second.
Every tenth is a true step in what you can do.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5829: Order! II
paragraphs: Noah looked over everything thoroughly!
Each rung swallowed the one beneath it whole, and above all of them sat the undersides of existence, the cycles of the Ages, and the outside.
He smiled.
Then the Tree measured him.
|Noah Osmont. THE True Human Emperor. THE Osmontian, THE Dreaming Human Origin.|
|VERITAS: Order I.4. What you dream holds true across many Dimensions near you, and thins toward the far edges of your reach.|
|PROVENANCE: Order I.6. What you make of yourself draws on more than half the power your Order can command, and owes nothing for it.|
|POTENTIA: Infinite. No Order contains it.|
|PONDUS: Order I.3. Your weight bends a third of your reach around you.|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: Order I.1. Your hold on fate and narrative has barely entered the first Order.|
|Profundity: ???|
First Order, every one of them!
So where did the Immense sit on this ladder?
He looked at Poona, and his existence answered.

|Measured against the Orders: a Newly Risen Immensity commonly reaches upper bounds of Order I in its strongest attribute. The Ancient reach far higher. Their full measure lies beyond your present sight.|
"Hmm..."He nodddd at this.
Then he looked at everything else!
Over his existence he had gathered a great deal: Core Capabilities, Authorities, Provenances, techniques, Records, a whole system in his Tree. It worked, but it was cluttered.
He was THE Dreaming Human Origin now. Human, Dreamer, Sovereign.
So everything he had should belong to one of the three.
He reached into himself and began to sort!
It was strange work and very satsifying. Each capability, when he touched it, leaned toward one of the three parts of him as naturally as water runs downhill.
His existence logged it as he went.
|Streamlining your existence.|
|THE Human.|
|What you feel, what you speak, and whom you hold.|
|Your emotions: endless, every extreme growing without limit and feeding your power.|
|Core Capability IV: THE Living Grammar. Core Capability VIII: THE Sanguine Covenant. Egos.|
|Kin: Ling, THE Dancer in the Boundless Dream. Poona, THE Dreaming Hearth. Cocoons yet to open.|
|THE Dreaming Origin.|
|What you dream becomes true.|

|Core Capability I: THE Dream Without a Far Wall. Core Capability II: THE Sovereign of the Lived Hour. Core Capability III: THE Waking Decree. THE Gold Without Pupils. THE Endless Waking. THE Vigil That Wished to Rise.|
|THE Sovereign.|
|What you take, what you build, and what you rule.|

|Core Capability V: THE Rendered Design. Core Capability VI: THE Tide-Crowned Protagonist. Core Capability VII: THE Unkneeling Chill. THE Bow of the Ending Epoch. Authority of the Held Breath. Authority of the Unclosing Hand. Provenances of Ending, Order, and Stillness. Records of an Immense One. THE Feast That Seals: Predation, Auto-Fusion, Judgment, and the Branches of your Tree.|
|Beneath all three: THE One Foundation, Dialetheic Infinity.|
|Streamlining complete. What was many is arranged as one.|
Noah let out a long breath.
Every power he owned now sat in its propper room, ready to his hand.
That left one thing unfinished.

He had given two great gifts on this road: Ling, carried through a sealed door inside his own Dream and made a Dream Immensity, and Poona, drawn out of her own corpse as a last flicker and dreamed back to life. Through all of it, THE Tide That Owes Nothing had not given.
It held weight sitting in the deepest part of THE Tide-Crowned Protagonist, waiting for him to ask.
So he asked!
|THE Tide That Owes Nothing has kept count of your giving.|
|Given: a Dream Immensity, to Ling. Given: a Dream Immensity and a second life, to Poona.|
|These were gifts no lifeform has given before. They were given with thought, at great cost, to those you hold dear.|
|THE Tide answers in full, and its answer exceeds your Order.|
Exceeds his Order?
The sky of the Domain darkened, and the first one rose over the hills!

It came up slowly, as a sun comes up, vast and round and gold. As it climbed, Noah saw that it was a shell. A great hollow sphere woven of dream, thread over thread, shining blue and gold, and inside it, at its heart, something burned.

Dreams. Countless dreams, every one a light, gathered into a single blazing core: the dreams of a whole civilization, then another, then thousands, peoples across countless Dimensions all sleeping at once and dreaming into this one place. A child dreaming of the sea. A smith dreaming of the perfect blade.
A city dreaming of its own tomorrow. All of it pouring into the core, and the shell around it catching every scrap of their light and holding it, harnessing it, turning it into power.
A sun made of a civilization’s sleep, and a shell built to drink it.
|Loot obtained: THE Dreaming Shell of Countless Sleeping Peoples.|
|A sphere woven around the gathered dreams of countless civilizations, harnessing the whole of their dreaming as power.|
|Born of the dream you carried through a sealed door. What opened for one, now gathers from countless.|
|Its reach spans the whole weavings of a Legacy. It is of the second Order.|
Second Order!
His whole existence leaned toward it. Every attribute he had sat on the first rung, and this reached a whole Legacy’s breadth.
The second one rose beside it.

This one rose out of warmth. Lamplight first, spilling across the river of light, gold and steady, and the smell of honey and baking bread rolling over the hills so thick that Poona’s eye went wide and wet. The lamplight gathered, and rose, and became a second sun beside the first.
But this sun was made of hearths.

Noah could see them in it, millions of them: the fire under every family’s pot, the lamp left burning in every window for someone coming late, every table where people gathered to eat and argue and be safe. All that warmth burned in a single sphere, and around it turned a shell of woven dream, keeping it.
A whole people’s dream of home, harnessed.
|Loot obtained: THE Hearth-Sun of the Kept Tables.|
|A sun formed of the warmth of every hearth across a civilization’s countless homes, and the dream of a home that waits for each who has not yet returned.|
|Born of the life you dreamed back from death. What returned to one table, now burns at a million.|
|Its reach spans the whole weavings of a Legacy. It is of the second Order.|
Noah stood up.
Two Second Order suns hung over his Domain, and every star in his sky had dimmed around them.
He felt something rise in his chest.

Greed, first. Pure and bright and shameless. He wanted them! He wanted both of them, and everything like them, every sleeping people’s dreams and every hearth’s warmth in every civilization across existence!
His Tyranny and his Quintessence also rose. The core of him. They looked at the two suns and knew, plainly, that they belonged inside him.
|Greed: risen, without end.|
|Tyranny: risen, without end.|
|Quintessence: risen, without end.|
|Your emotions elevate your power.|
He opened his mouth.

The blue-gold brilliance inside it looked up at the two suns, and the event horizons turned, and he pulled. The Dreaming Shell came down first, its woven threads stretching into long ribbons, the blazing dreams of countless peoples streaming after them like a river of sparks. Then the Hearth-Sun, unwinding into lamplight, the warmth of a million homes pouring down out of the sky and into him in a long gold flood.
His Tree drank!

The dreams of the sleeping peoples went into the truth of him and the weave of his fate. The hearths went into his weight and the part of him that generated from itself. His constellations blazed until they lit the whole hill, and the sky of the Domain, emptied of its two suns, burned brighter than before.
|Devoured: THE Dreaming Shell of a Thousand Sleeping Peoples.|
|Devoured: THE Hearth-Sun of the Kept Tables.|
|Second Order loot integrated by a first Order existence. Your attributes surge toward the second rung.|
|Sap risen toward the First Bough: 53%.|
|VERITAS: Order I.4 to Order I.8.|
|PROVENANCE: Order I.6 to Order I.9. Knocking on the doors of Order II|
|PONDUS: Order I.3 to Order I.8.|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: Order I.1 to Order I.5.|
|POTENTIA: Infinite.|
Noah read the numbers, and laughed out loud.
Provenance at I.9, pressing against the second rung, with Veritas and Pondus close behind. He could feel the next Order above him now, close enough to touch.
He wanted it. He wanted all of it!
Poona was staring at him with her one great eye very round.
"Master," she said slowly, "Were you a slime before? Your hunger and devouring almost seems grander than mine. We can test this by seeing who can devour Dimensions the fastest..."
She said some ridiculous things as he didn’t reply.
His existence only buzzed as he probed regarding The Judgments and the capability that called forth what looked like a tribulation from existence everytime he used it.
|A clarification, on the Branches of your Tree.|
|A Branch grows only when your Tree itself grows beyond what existence allows, and survives the Judgment for it.|
|When you stand within a Judgment for another, as for Ling’s rising or Poona’s return, the Judgment falls on you and is counted in your Debt. The growth is theirs. No Branch of yours grows from it.|
Okay! It didn’t answer too much, but okay!
He looked at the whole of himself one last time, sorted and counted.
First Order, every attribute, Potentia aside. Three umbrellas. One Tree, one ring lit, Sap at fifty-three percent, a single Branch with an Unsealing on it, and a Judgment Debt of three.
It was a beginning, and only that. The Ancient Ones he had met sat a little above. They had lived longer than him as that was fine.
That meant there was a great deal left to eat!
Noah stood and brushed the dream-grass off his knees. Beside him, Poona stopped bouncing and looked up.
Noah turned toward the far edge of his Domain, toward the threads that ran down out of him into THE Undersnow, toward the frozen dark of the Basal Floor and the rift that split it open in the north.
There was much to be done!
